title: Todd Monken: Deshaun Watson not ruled out yet, but Shedeur Sanders preparing to start
summary: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday.
full_text: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday. Head coach Todd Monken told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that Watson hasn’t necessarily been ruled out for Sunday’s game against New Orleans. But the club is preparing Shedeur Sanders to start. “What I would say is, credit to Deshaun — after the game, [he] felt fine. Monday night, started feeling a little bit, little bit of a headache, and came in Tuesday and, you know, reported,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “So, credit to him for someone who really loves playing the game. And so, he is in the protocol. And Shedeur will take the reps today with the ones.” Monken admitted that it’s “a little more difficult” for a quarterback to play on Sunday after missing practice due to a concussion. But Monken and the team will let the process play out. “I mean, there’s a long time between now and then, right? I mean, look where the Ravens are at. And you don’t know as the week goes on what could happen,” Monken said. “It’s not ideal, right? It’s not ideal for any player to go through a week and not practice and then play. We know that. But every situation is different.” Monken noted that Watson can participate in the team’s meetings to help him stay prepared in the event that he gets cleared. The team has been game-planning with the idea that Sanders will start. But Monken said the game plan won’t change much if it’s Sanders or Watson behind center. “I don’t see the way [it would change], because the rest of the guys are the same, and they’re similar in some ways,” Monken said. “Some things, you know, Shedeur’s skill set is different than Deshaun’s, but still very similar in terms of what we do. We can’t change that dramatically.” Either way, Watson is expected to still be the starter when he is cleared. “Yeah, I didn’t assume I’d get that question. Yeah, he’s been our starter for eight games. I would assume he’s still our starter,” Monken said. “I don’t — I’m thinking about Wednesday. But I’m not — I’m really thinking about today and watching Shedeur play today.” So far this season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s been sacked a league-high 33 times. His eight games this season are the most he’s played in a year for the Browns since arriving on the club in 2022. Last season, Sanders completed 56.6 percent of his throws for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games with seven starts.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Ravens finalizing trade for Jacoby Brissett
summary: Brissett is on his way to Baltimore after being benched by the Cardinals.
full_text: The Ravens will be starting Joe Fagnano at quarterback against the Jaguars on Thursday night, but it looks like they will have a more experienced option available for Week 10 and beyond. ESPN reports that they are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett. The deal will not be done by Thursday night's game, but it is expected to be completed over the weekend. Brissett started the first eight games of the season for Arizona, but was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew last Sunday and demoted to the No. 3 spot on the depth chart this week. Brissett signed a revised contract with the Cardinals after a protracted absence from the team this offseason, but most of the money has been paid out already and the Ravens will be responsible for the remainder of his base salary. The move to No. 3 made Brissett an obvious trade candidate and the Ravens were a logical destination. Lamar Jackson could be out for the rest of the season with a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley will miss the rest of the year with turf toe, which left the undrafted Fagnano and other inexperienced players as the in-house options for Baltimore.
author: Josh Alper

title: Matthew Stafford has full participation with elbow injury; Myles Garrett limited in return
summary: Rams coach Sean McVay wouldn't allow much about the ice pack on quarterback Matthew Stafford's arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers other than to say it was soreness.
full_text: Rams coach Sean McVay wouldn’t allow much about the ice pack on quarterback Matthew Stafford's arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers other than to say it was soreness. The injury report said it isn't serious, and Stafford agreed. Stafford was a full participant, listed with an elbow injury. " I’m 38 years old , trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year," Stafford said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times . "Haven't missed a rep. Feel good. So I'm not too worried about it." Stafford underwent surgery on his elbow during the 2022 offseason. He threw only 25 passes on Sunday. The Rams got more good news when outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) returned to practice as a limited participant. It was the first practice Garrett and Aaron Donald have had together. Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after playing 40 snaps in the season opener. He was given a six-week prognosis and has missed seven games. The Rams practiced without cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and safety Kam Curl (foot) on Wednesday. Inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sam Darnold out Week 9 with quad injury, Drew Lock in line to start
summary: HC Mike Macdonald said Darnold also suffered a cracked rib early in Monday's loss to the Bears.
full_text: Seattle's QB1 for Week 9 is in flux. Quarterback Sam Darnold will not play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals after suffering a quad injury late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald announced in his Wednesday press conference. " It’ll be week-to-week for Sam ," Macdonald said. "He’s not going to go on IR." Macdonald noted the club intends to start Drew Lock on Sunday, but he's also working through an injury. "The plan is for Drew to start. Jalen [Milroe] will be ready to back up," Macdonald said. "Drew’s still working back from his elbow, so we’ll work through that process this week. So we’ll be getting both guys ready to play. Have full confidence in those guys and we have a plan in place and we’ll go execute." Lock finished the Week 1 win over the Patriots and started Week 2 when the Seahawks beat the Cardinals in Arizona. He’s completed 35-of-48 passes this year for 422 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions. “He’s able to throw. How much, we’re working through that right now. That’s the best way to put it,” Macdonald said of Lock’s elbow injury. “He’s going to throw the ball throughout the week, but we’re just going to manage it. He’s not going to take 8,000 throws.” Lock and Milroe are set to split reps at least early in the practice week. “I think we just have to take it day-by-day at this point,” Macdonald said. While Macdonald characterized Darnold as week-to-week with the quad injury, the quarterback is also dealing with another issue. “In terms of Sam, this guy, he’s tough as nails,” Macdonald said. “I think the second play of the game, I just asked if I could share this, but he cracked his rib on the second play of the game. So, playing the whole game without even making a name of it, and playing his tail off, and competing, it’s worth noting how tough this guy is. He’ll be back sooner than later, I’m sure.” Darnold has completed 60.2 percent of his passes this season for 1,478 yards with 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions so far this season. Seattle’s first injury report of the week will be out later on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Nick Sirianni: I've always felt complete support from Jeffrey Lurie
summary: Nick Sirianni has never missed the playoffs since becoming the Eagles' head coach and he's won one of the two Super Bowls the team has played in during his tenure, but the waters have gotten rockier for him over the last 12 months.
full_text: Nick Sirianni has never missed the playoffs since becoming the Eagles' head coach and he's won one of the two Super Bowls the team has played in during his tenure, but the waters have gotten rockier for him over the last 12 months. The Eagles will bring a six-game losing streak into Sunday's game against the Giants and the team is 5-11 since an 8-2 start to the 2025 season. While his overall history and the overall circumstances of this season would say that he's earned a chance to turn things around, Eagles history says that team owner Jeffrey Lurie hasn't shied away from making changes after a season goes awry. Doug Pederson also won a Super Bowl for the Eagles, but was dismissed after snapping a three-year postseason run by going 4-11-1 in 2020. That may have factored into a question for Sirianni on Wednesday about his communications with Lurie during the team's current difficulties. "I've always felt nothing but complete support from Mr. Lurie in everything, through good times, through bad times," Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. "That's huge. That's huge to be able to know that the owner has your back in all situations. We've been high of highs, we've been low, and I've felt nothing but support and my communication remains the same with him as it has [been] whether we're on a winning streak or whether we're on a losing streak. I love that steadiness, and I'm trying to give that same thing to the guys: the consistency, the steadiness, because I know I'm receiving it from the very top." Sirianni spoke before word broke that the Eagles will veer away from steadiness at quarterback this week. They'll give Joe Milton a chance to run the offense well enough to snap a skid that will certainly impact Sirianni's job security if it doesn't come to an end relatively soon.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saints WR Jordyn Tyson feels "more explosive than I ever have" in return from hamstring injury
summary: The Saints can use all the help they can get after a 2-5 start to the season and one ray of hope is the return of rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson to the practice field this week.
full_text: The Saints can use all the help they can get after a 2-5 start to the season and one ray of hope is the return of rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson to the practice field this week. Tyson has been out since injuring his hamstring during a joint practice with the Jaguars in August, but the first-round pick was designated for return from injured reserve this week and he gave a very positive assessment of his health while speaking with reporters on Wednesday. “I ran the fastest I ran since I been here in rehab. I feel more explosive than I ever have," Tyson said. "So I think I'm doing pretty good. I think I'm doing just fine." The Saints haven't said if Tyson will play against the Browns this Sunday, but he said he's "pretty anxious" to make his NFL debut and start providing the big plays that the team envisioned when they took him eighth overall in April. That would be a positive way to head into the second half of a season that has not gone as hoped in New Orleans.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lamar Jackson's latest injury raises obvious questions about his future in Baltimore
summary: The Ravens wanted to re-sign him in 2026, and there's no reason to think they won't want to in 2027.
full_text: With quarterback Lamar Jackson's ninth NFL season possibly over after three full games and two first-half exits, obvious questions have emerged regarding his future in Baltimore. The facts fuel the speculation. He's under contract for one more season, and the Ravens can't use the franchise tag or the transition tag to limit his ability to become an unrestricted free agent in March 2028, which is only 16 months away. If Jackson wants a fresh start at age 31, he'll be able to have one. The Ravens made it clear in January that they wanted to extend his contract by the start of the new league year in March 2026. It didn't happen, for reasons that never became clear because neither Jackson nor the Ravens (at Jackson's behest) share information about the negotiations. Before the season began, it seemed that a new contract wa just a matter of time. The Ravens surely would like to do it before the start of the new league year in March, when Jackson's cap number spikes to $84.34 million. Although the team has the right to do another restructuring that would reduce the 2027 cap number, that would make the dead-cap reckoning even larger as of 2028. A trade would avoid the final $52 million in cash and cap charges, but the cap realities would make a post-June 1 move the far better option. And there have been whispers of at least one team doing advance homework on a potential pursuit of Jackson in 2027. The overriding question is whether Jackson's lingering availability issue changes things for the Ravens. For now, there's no reason to think it has. When the dust settles on the season, the Ravens will have to revisit that question. But that will lead to another question. What would they do at quarterback without Lamar Jackson? That simple reality prompted them to give him a market-level deal in 2023, and to want to do it again. As long as that desire to avoid a future without Lamar Jackson remains, there's no reason to think he won't be back in Baltimore in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos proactively replace entire surface at Mile High Stadium, again
summary: With four regular-season home games played and four to go, the Broncos are being proactive — again — about the quality of the playing surface at Mile High Stadium.
full_text: With four regular-season home games played and four to go, the Broncos are being proactive — again — about the quality of the playing surface at Mile High Stadium. The entire field is being ripped up and replaced, despite the absence of any complaints about the quality of the grass there. For the fifth straight year, the Broncos are spending the money to ensure that the players will be performing on the highest-quality surface, emphasizing that "the Walton Penner Family Ownership Group’s commitment to player safety and a best-in-class playing surface throughout the season." At a time when the debate regarding real grass vs. fake grass continues, with the situation boiling down to whether the owners are willing to write the check to ensure the best and safest surfaces for players, the statement made by the Broncos makes their ownership look good and, in comparison, owners who cling to artificial turf look bad. Beyond caring about player safety, having the best playing surface provides the best protection of the investment the owners have made in their rosters. Which would be a sensible position for any owner — especially the cheap ones. Now that it has morphed into a matter of collective bargaining, those who choose to be pennywise have even more cover for their pound foolishness. Which makes it even more important that the NFL Players Association apply not general public pressure to the league but specific scrutiny to the owners who won't ditch artificial turf for grass, or who won't replace low-quality grass with high-quality grass.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean Payton says J.K. Dobbins remains "a huge part of what we're doing"
summary: It's been a somewhat strange second year in Denver for veteran running back J.K.
full_text: It's been a somewhat strange second year in Denver for veteran running back J.K. Dobbins. As coach Sean Payton tells it, however, everything is going as planned. “He’s a huge part of what we’re doing," Payton told reporters on Wednesday regarding whether the team is managing Dobbins's workload. "So each week we look at — a lot of times who’s the back that’s in there with the hot hand. But he’s been fantastic. So to answer your question: No, that’s not a hot button topic with us here. It might be with you guys, but not with us. So we’re good. We’re good with the rotation.” Payton is generally using a three-back rotation, with Dobbins joining R.J. Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman. Still, with Harvey on injured reserve for Sunday's showdown against the Chiefs, Dobbins got fewer chances than Coleman. Coleman, who was on the field for 41 offensive plays, had 11 carries for 41 yards and four catches for 63. Dobbins played 13 snaps, getting seven carries for 13 yards and no targets in the passing game. " Look, it’s always easy to work two [running backs] and it becomes more challenging when you’re trying to work three, but he’s doing a great job," Payton said of Dobbins. For the year, Dobbins has 94 carries for 306 yards in eight games, with eight catches for 27 yards. That's 333 yards from scrimmage — an average of 41.6 per game. In 10 games last year, before he suffered a season-ending foot injury during a Thursday night game against the Raiders, Dobbins was averaging nearly twice that amount, at 80.9 yards from scrimmage per game. Through it all, the Broncos have been linked to a potential trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. While the prospect of acquiring a workhorse would cut against Payton's longstanding approach to use multiple running backs, Taylor's arrival would surely result in even fewer chances for Dobbins.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Allen and James Cook can both top 5,000 career rushing yards on Monday night
summary: Allen currently has 4,991 career rushing yards, and Cook currently has 4,966.
full_text: Bills quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook can both reach a big career milestone on Monday night against the Vikings. Allen and Cook may both reach 5,000 career rushing yards: Allen currently has 4,991 rushing yards in his career, and Cook currently has 4,966, so Allen needs nine yards against the Vikings and Cook needs 34 yards to reach 5,000. Allen is averaging 39 rushing yards per game this season and Cook is averaging 101, so it's likely that they'll both reach the 5,000-yard milestone on Monday night. Allen would be the fifth quarterback in NFL history with 5,000 career rushing yards. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is the NFL’s all-time quarterback leader with 6,666 career rushing yards. Behind Jackson are Michael Vick with 6,109, Cam Newton with 5,628 and Russell Wilson with 5,568. Allen probably won't catch Jackson, who, though currently injured, is a year younger and will keep adding to his yardage total. But the 30-year-old Allen has a great chance of continuing to rack up rushing yards long enough to move ahead of Vick into No. 2 in rushing yardage among quarterbacks in NFL history. Cook is in his fifth year in the NFL and is on closing in on his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard season. He ranks 15th among active NFL players in career rushing yards, and Allen ranks 14th.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kyle Shanahan confirms Jauan Jennings decided not to pursue trade back to 49ers
summary: Yes, the 49ers tried to arrange a reunion with receiver Jauan Jennings.
full_text: Yes, the 49ers tried to arrange a reunion with receiver Jauan Jennings. Over the weekend, Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported that the 49ers and Vikings had a deal in place, but that Jennings eventually decided to stay in Minnesota. On Wednesday, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed it. " The report was accurate, just not totally exactly detailed up," Shanahan told reporters. "I mean, you can't talk to other players on other teams. You're not allowed to. We love Jauan. We have such a good relationship with Jauan and know him really well and we didn't want to do it without talking to him first. So, we had to agree on some things to at least make it close enough to be able to talk to him. "Then when we got on a FaceTime with J.J., it went well. It was awesome. We talked about a lot of stuff, and he ended up saying that he was happy with where he was. It wasn't just like a definite 'no' first, but he was like, ‘Man, Kyle, I'm pretty happy here and liking stuff.’ And when I heard the way he talked and where we're at, I agreed with him. So, it was a good conversation and something that was possible, but that's why it didn't go down.” Jennings still hasn't done much for the Vikings. In six games, he has six catches for 54 yards. The fact that the Vikings allowed Jennings to talk to the 49ers shows that the Vikings were willing to move on. The fact that Jennings stayed has kept receiver Odell Beckham Jr. parked on the Minnesota practice squad.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bryce Young a full participant but with an ankle injury
summary: Bryce Young was listed with a knee injury on the Panthers' practice reports over the past four weeks.
full_text: Bryce Young was listed with a knee injury on the Panthers' practice reports over the past four weeks. The quarterback was listed with an ankle injury Wednesday. Young, though, was estimated as a full participant. The Panthers did not practice Wednesday. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), left guard Damien Lewis (knee), linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and rookie cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring) were listed as non-participants. Phillips has missed the past two games, and Lewis missed last week's game against the Packers. Offensive linemen Corey Bullock (quad) and Torricelli Simpkins III (ankle) were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Nick Bosa returns to practice with limited work
summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa returned to practice Wednesday after missing the team's past five games with a calf injury.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa returned to practice Wednesday after missing the team's past five games with a calf injury. Bosa was a limited participant. “ It’s a long year , and I kind of just reminded myself that I need to be ready for the long haul," Bosa said, via Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle . Bosa tore his right ACL in a Sept. 21, 2025, game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery five days later. As he was coming back this summer, Bosa experienced soreness and tendinitis in his right knee, and the 49ers backed him down until Sept. 2 when he returned to practice. He injured his left calf while warming up in practice for Week 3. “I must have had some type of compensation going on, especially in that first week back," Bosa said. "I was kind of trying to push it back with the [right knee] tendinitis, so I may have been favoring [the left calf] a little bit. I was just doing my normal warm-up drills one day, and I tweaked it. Calves are a pretty long process. I've never had one, so it took a little longer than I expected, but I don't even think about it anymore.” Wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) remained out of practice, and running back Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) also didn't practice. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring), safety Siran Neal (knee/foot) and offensive tackle Trent Williams (rest) were the other players who sat out Wednesday's session. Linebacker Luke Gifford (groin), cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor), wide receiver Christian Kirk (knee), wide receiver Demarcus Robinson (ankle), safety Marques Sigle (ankle), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) and linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring) were limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Jalen Hurts makes an appearance at team facility
summary: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made an appearance at the team's practice facility on Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN reports.
full_text: '' Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made an appearance at the team's practice facility on Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN reports. It is the first time some players had seen Hurts since he went on injured reserve with blood clots in his lungs. Hurts sat in on the team meeting and additional meetings, but he did not address the team. Coach Nick Sirianni did not address a question Wednesday about whether the quarterback had been at the facility. "I've talked to him and am in constant communication with him and know he's resting and recovering," Sirianni said. "I miss him like crazy. But nothing new on that front. I know he's resting and recovering, and we're all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery." Hurts, 28, went on injured reserve on Oct. 17 and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Tanner McKee went 0-3 in Hurts' absence before being benched for Joe Milton this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Jacobs: "There's a lot of stuff being said about me that's completely false"
summary: On Friday, Wisconsin authorities released documents in the Josh Jacobs criminal case that included three allegations against him from other women.
full_text: '' On Friday, Wisconsin authorities released documents in the Josh Jacobs criminal case that included three allegations against him from other women. On Wednesday, Jacobs spoke directly to reporters for the first time since the material became public. "It's one of those things for me where it's like, it really feels like an attack on me and who I am and my character ," Jacobs said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. "And at the end of the day, there's a lot of stuff being said about me that's completely false -- like, completely made up, and it's like people just run with it. And I can't change that. "It's just one of those things where it's like, OK, all I can do is try to be who I am and try not to let the negative moments change who I am. And that was the biggest thing for me throughout this whole process. I didn't want to go to a place where I felt like I was closed off and I'm angry all the time because of what's going on in my life." The situation would be very different if Jacobs hadn't pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor battery charge arising from an incident in May 2026. Admitting to an incident of violence against a woman makes it harder for him to credibly claim that three other women who contacted authorities about Jacobs doing the same thing are making it all up. Still, Jacobs believes the newly-surfaced allegations won't result in more missed time, following the six-game stint on paid leave arising from the most recent incident. "With all the evidence that we have and that they have at this point, it's not one of those things where I'm sitting back on my hands like, 'OK, am I going to play this week?'" Jacobs said. "It's like, I kind of already know what it is, so it's like . . . it's really just up to them to make their final decision. But like I'm not worried about feeling like I'm going to miss any more time than I already have." The league continues to investigate Jacobs, and it's investigating the recent allegations, too. Through it all, the Packers have been linked on multiple occasions to a potential trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. If the Packers land Taylor, it could mean that they'll move on from Jacobs.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jack Campbell: I have full movement in my lower body, and am making progress with movement in my upper body
summary: The Lions released a statement from Campbell on Wednesday providing an update on his condition after he suffered a significant neck injury on Sunday.
full_text: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has issued a statement on Wednesday after suffering a serious neck injury on Sunday, saying that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. This is the first definitive update on Campbell's condition since he was transported to the hospital on Sunday. "I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time," Campbell's statement reads, in part. "I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." Campbell went on to thank those who have helped take care of him since Sunday. “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” Campbell said. "I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. “I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.” Campbell added, “To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. “One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. “Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jim Harbaugh, Justin Herbert respond to Quentin Lake's "seeing ghosts" critique
summary: As the football-following world tries to figure out the problem(s) with Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, Rams safety Quentin Lake provided a scathing critique of Herbert's most recent performance, in a 24-9 loss to the Rams.
full_text: As the football-following world tries to figure out the problem(s) with Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, Rams safety Quentin Lake provided a scathing critique of Herbert's most recent performance, in a 24-9 loss to the Rams. “He was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said. “He’s seeing ghosts . I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one.” They got two. On Wednesday, both Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert himself were asked about Lake's remarks. "As far as anybody's opinion I don’t see that ," Harbaugh told reporters. "Everybody's entitled to their opinion. Not what I see." So what did Harbaugh see in the latest loss? "I thought he played — did his job exceptionally well," Harbaugh said. "You know, two throws he would have liked to have back." Herbert said he wasn't aware of Lake's comments. " I haven’t looked into it , haven't heard anything about it, so I can't really make a comment about it," Herbert told reporters. "We're really just focused on what's going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that's all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control." Still, it's jarring to hear an NFL defender make comments about a supposed franchise quarterback that make him seem like a Jets first-round draft pick who has yet to have the game slow down. Herbert is in the seventh year of his career. He's making $52.5 million per year. Something has happened this year. It's still not clear what it is, or whether it will change. Before it can change, the Chargers need to realize there's a problem. And that's the most confounding part of all of it. They've lost seven and won none; at times, they sound like they've won seven and lost none.
author: Mike Florio

title: Christian McCaffrey says "I feel great" after hamstring injury, but he didn't practice on Wednesday
summary: Thigh injury that became hamstring problem keeps McCaffrey out of practice.
full_text: 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey missed part of the Week 7 loss to the Falcons with what had been called a thigh injury during the game. By Monday, it had been revised to a hamstring injury . Nine days later, McCaffrey wasn't able to practice because of it. In the first official injury report issued by the 49ers since they said he had a thigh injury during the Week 7 loss, the 49ers say that McCaffrey missed practice due to a hamstring injury. After the game in Atlanta, McCaffrey said it felt like his leg " just died on me ." On Wednesday, McCaffrey expressed optimism that he'll play on Sunday against the Raiders. “I had no idea [it was a hamstring injury],” McCaffrey said Wednesday, via Vic Tafur of The Athletic . “Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you. . . . It wasn’t too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great .” Still, not great enough to practice. Which creates the kind of mixed signals that conjure memories of the strange way in which the team handled McCaffrey's 2024 Achilles injury, which resulted in his unexpected scratch for the regular-season opener. Here's the basic reality. He had a career-high 413 touches in 2025. He has 118 in seven games this year. Now 30, the workload can take a toll — especially in a 17-game season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks miss Wednesday's practice
summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley missed practice Wednesday with his hamstring and back injuries.
full_text: '' Eagles running back Saquon Barkley missed practice Wednesday with his hamstring and back injuries. Barkley practiced only once last week, getting limited work Friday, before playing 22 snaps on Sunday against the Commanders. He played 10 snaps the week before against the Cowboys. Wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) remained out of practice, with both on track to miss a third consecutive game. title: Eagles-Commanders somehow breaks 19 million viewers
summary: When George Costanza pitched the show about nothing to NBC president Russell Dalrymple, Dalrymple asked, "Well, why am I watching it?"
full_text: When George Costanza pitched the show about nothing to NBC president Russell Dalrymple, Dalrymple asked, " Well, why am I watching it? " "Because it's on TV," Costanza said. More than 30 years later, that sentiment still applies. As evidenced by the fact that, per Nielsen, 19.015 million (on average) watched Sunday night's snoozefest between the Eagles and Commanders on the network that Dalrymple once ran. It's an amazing number, given that it was the 2-5 Eagles against the 1-4-1 Commanders. The game itself wasn't particularly compelling, and it followed afternoon windows that culminated in a down-to-the-wire showdown between the Chiefs and the Broncos. The league could have flexed the game out of the evening window. It chose not to. In the end, the not-ready-for-prime-time game managed to attract far more viewers than anyone would have expected. It helped that there wasn't a 9:30 a.m. ET game in Week 8. Fourteen straight hours of football is a lot, even for the most ardent fan. Then again, Commanders-Eagles was a lot. Even for the most ardent fan. And more than 19 million nevertheless watched the game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Maxx Crosby: I love being a Raider, and this is where I want to be
summary: A report this week indicated the Raiders have no plans to trade Crosby, who wants to stay with the team.
full_text: The Raiders have traded Maxx Crosby once, but the Ravens reneged on the deal. A report this week indicated that the Raiders have " no plans " to trade the edge rusher again, and he doesn't want them to. " I love being a Raider . I've said that a million times," Crosby said Wednesday, via video from Raider Nation Radio. "This is where I want to be. Super excited, obviously for the present, but also for what's to come." The Ravens sent two first-round picks to the Raiders for Crosby. The Ravens, though, failed him on his physical and sent him back to Las Vegas, because of long-term concerns about Crosby's surgically repaired left knee. Crosby, 29, likely could still bring two first-round picks to the Raiders. He has 22 tackles, three sacks, a forced fumble, a pass defensed and 18 quarterback hits this season. Crosby has played 88 percent of the team's defensive snaps. He expressed optimism at where the Raiders are headed short term and long term. "I'm not thinking too far down the road. I'm being present," Crosby said. "We're 4-4. We've got a really good football team. I love this locker room. I love the guys. We have great leadership. Klint [Kubiak] is a really good coach. We have Robby [Leonard], who is a first time being a DC. He's doing a hell of a job. We've got a lot of new faces, new pieces, a lot of young guys as well. "I love where we're going. We've got a lot of work to do. We know that. That's the beauty in it. Everyone can say whatever they want. We had this conversation last week [after a 35-21 loss to the Rams], and it was like the world is ending, and now it's all these positive vibes. For us, it's about focus about this week, today, getting better. That's the mindset of this whole team. I'm excited about everything."

title: Micah Parsons won't "pinpoint a day" I'll be back in the lineup
summary: Parsons practiced with the team on Wednesday for the first time since tearing his ACL.
full_text: ' Packers defensive end Micah Parsons took a big step back toward the lineup on Wednesday when he participated in practice for the first time since tearing his ACL last December. Parsons was limited to individual work on his first day back and head coach Matt LaFleur said that the team will take it " one day at a time " as Parsons ramps back up. LaFleur added that he hopes Parsons is ready for game action sooner rather than later and reports have indicated that the team's Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve game against the Rams is the target, but Parsons isn't looking at a specific date at this point. "I won't say too much because even if I did play, I don't want them to game plan for it," Parsons said in a post-practice media session. "I just want it to be a surprise. I just want it to be a fulfilling moment for myself, the staff — just to enjoy that day and not put too much pressure on that day. My family even been asking me, 'You going to play? Should we buy flights to come out there?'" . . . It is what it is. You can buy your flight and cancel last minute, that's up to you, but I'm not going to pinpoint a day to disappoint anyone or get people expectations that I can't meet.' I gotta stack 20 days and hopefully on that 21st day I feel incredible." Parsons said he's looking forward to upping his practice participation next week and that he understands that he needs to "get into more of a football shape" because his conditioning is not where he needs it to be. That should improve over the next couple of weeks and that should put Parsons in a good spot for the Rams game if everything continues to play out the right way.

title: Kellen Moore confirms Charlie Smyth will kick for the Saints this week

Just felt like this was the best thing for our football team moving forward. These things are never easy, but Charlie's done this for us back in the last year, so he'll be ready to go." title: Dianna Russini gets out the word that she's coming back to work next week
summary: The halfway point of the 2026 NFL season arrives this weekend.
full_text: The halfway point of the 2026 NFL season arrives this weekend. Next week, Dianna Russini apparently will return to sports media. Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she'll be returning to work "next week." It's unclear where she'll be working, or what she'll be doing. She resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after photos were published by the New York Post of Russini and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel at a resort in Arizona. In both her comments to the Post and her resignation letter to The Athletic, she denied that there was any type of impropriety. The Athletic conducted a review of her work. Its findings were released in early September. “Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards,” wrote Mike Semel of The Athletic , who conducted the investigation. “Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed.” Beyond the relationship was the manner in which she handled the emergence of the controversy. "[W]hen first confronted with the photos by The New York Post ,” Semel wrote, “Russini waited two days before telling her editors and managers. She then told a story to explain the photos that did not align with facts, raising issues of trust.” Along the way, a strange story emerged regarding Russini being pulled over for texting while driving — made stranger by her decision to tell the story publicly and embellish the notion that she FaceTimed a head coach for help in getting out of the ticket. So if she'll be reporting again, she'll need to restore her own credibility. Especially given the unique set of facts that resulted in her departure from The Athletic .

title: Ravens vs. Jaguars: Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup?
summary: How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9
full_text:
In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars .
Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first offensive play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game.
Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year.
Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score.
Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision.
The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season.
The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler.
Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot.
The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented.
Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.)
The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone.
You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night.
Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once.
Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football.
Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night.
The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease.
Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6
author: Jared Dubin

title: NFL Week 9 picks: Our experts face off on Jaguars at Ravens, Bengals vs. Falcons and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons .
This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears.
Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work.
Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home.
Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13
Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease.  … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6
Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23
Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow.  … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20
Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500.  … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17
Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense.  … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16
Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters.
This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20
Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road.  … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17
Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game,  which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five.   … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24
Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield.  … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20

title: NFL Week 9 upset alert: Texans allow Chargers their first win, Vikings overtake Josh Allen's Bills
summary: Plus, Denver is a road favorite that could be due for a letdown
full_text:
As remarkable as it sounds, we've reached the midway point of the 2026 regular season now that Week 9 is on our doorstep. The first half of the year has heard underdogs bark loudly, and there's no reason to think that'll subside as we barrel down this second leg of the season.
That's especially true this week as there are eight home underdogs on the Week 9 slate. Normally, this is a recipe for the league to flip on its head, particularly after a Week 8 schedule that was mostly chalk. Last week, we correctly identified the Raiders as a live road underdog as they came out with the outright win over the Jets , but favorites largely owned the rest of the schedule.
Water may find its level in Week 9, however, which is why we have three road favorites firmly on upset alert as we look forward to another week in the NFL .
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
Green Bay and New England have sort of mirrored each other to this point in the season. They both started the year 1-2 and have since surged back into playoff contention with 4-1 records over the past five weeks. Jordan Love leads the NFL in passing yards entering Week 8, while Drake Maye leads the league in total yards and touchdowns from Weeks 4-8. So, both of these teams are quite hot heading into this Week 9 matchup in Foxborough.
That said, injuries have plagued the Patriots offense, with wideout A.J. Brown missing Week 8 with a knee injury and tight end Hunter Henry leaving last week's win over Miami with a foot injury. Those are two pivotal outlets for Maye in the passing game that he may not have when he goes up against an emerging Packers defense.
Over the last five games, the Packers have given up 14.6 points per game, which ranks third in the NFL. With a potentially limited cast around Maye, Green Bay's strength could end up winning the day and the game.
Most of the attention for this game will go to the best-on-best matchup between the Bills offense and the Vikings defense. After all, Buffalo is averaging a league-best 33.3 points per game entering Week 9, while Minnesota is holding opponents to a league-low 13.3 points per game. Something will need to give there, and it could be the Vikings' blitz-heavy defense that has the advantage.
Coming into Week 9, Minnesota leads the NFL with a 69.1% blitz rate. Against the blitz this season, Allen ranks 20th among 31 qualified quarterbacks in passer rating (88.2) and is tied for the second-most interceptions (3). Of course, Allen's rushing ability can help negate Minnesota's pass rush, but his passing numbers against the blitz are noteworthy.
Meanwhile, this could be a solid spot for Minnesota's offense to find its footing. Kyler Murray hasn't been as dynamic under center as the Vikings hoped when they acquired him this offseason, and the team has largely won in spite of the offense. That said, Buffalo's defense is allowing 25.9 points per game this season, which is tied for 24th in the NFL entering Week 9. Playing in one of the better home-field environments also helps Minnesota's chances.
The Chargers have to win a game at some point, right? Right?! So far, nothing has worked for Los Angeles, as it is 0-7 this season and ranks last in the NFL in points per game (14.1) while leading the league in turnovers (17). The Chargers also haven't scored a touchdown since the third quarter of Week 5. It's been an unmitigated disaster.
While it's hard to imagine the tide turning, there's at least a glimmer of hope this week against a surprisingly shaky Texans defense. Maybe the bye week was enough for them to take a breather and get right, but what we've seen on the field so far hasn't been anything like what they were in 2025. The Texans have allowed 30-plus points three times this season after doing so once last year. They've also had three 300-yard passing games allowed, after none in 2025.
If they continue to look sluggish defensively, maybe the Texans open the door for the Chargers to catch lightning in a bottle at home.
Under Dave Canales (since 2024), the Panthers are a respectable 8-9 as a home underdog (11-6 ATS). If you cut it to the start of last season, Carolina is 6-4 as a home underdog, so this is not only a spot it is familiar with, but it's also come out on top with straight-up wins more often than one would think.
Yes, this matchup against Denver comes at a bad time for Bryce Young and the offensive line. Carolina's offensive line is banged up, which has led to Bryce Young enduring 11 sacks over the past two games. With the Broncos tied for the fourth-most sacks (23) in the NFL through Week 8, this, on paper, has the possibility of getting ugly.
That said, I wonder if the Panthers continue to find success as an overlooked team at home, especially having the rest advantage after playing last Thursday. Meanwhile, don't sleep on Denver having a bit of a letdown in Week 9 after pulling off a marquee win over the Chiefs last Sunday.
The NFL heads back out into international waters as the Bengals and Falcons square off in Madrid.
After watching both of these offenses last week, it's hard to see the Falcons keeping pace with the Bengals. That said, lost in Joe Burrow 's six-touchdown performance was that Tennessee dropped 36 points against Cincinnati's defense. Cam Ward , who has had an up-and-down start to his career, threw for 304 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 41 yards against a Bengals defense that is starting to get dinged up. The Bengals lost Cashius Howell (fractured wrist), corner DJ Turner (heel), and defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle), all of whom suffered injuries against the Titans. Turner and Johnson could play this week, but the unit isn't 100%.
As for the Falcons, they are getting a boost defensively as top edge rusher James Pearce Jr . is back after serving his eight-game suspension to begin the year.
Cincinnati is also giving up 4.8 yards per rush this season, which is tied for the fourth-highest in the NFL. That suggests Bijan Robinson could dazzle on the international stage, especially after seeing Tony Pollard total 117 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns against the Bengals last week. If it's a ground-controlled game for Atlanta, that could be the avenue to pulling off the win.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: It wouldn't shock me if ... NFL Week 9: Chargers fire Mike McDaniel, another QB change in Arizona
summary: Is it finally over for Mike McDaniel in Los Angeles?
full_text:
This is about the time on the NFL calendar when teams begin taking a hard look at themselves. With the arrival of Week 9, we're halfway through the regular season, and the Nov. 10 trade deadline is on the league's doorstep.
That leaves every franchise facing the same question: What are we in 2026? Should we invest in the club we have or sell off pieces and begin building for a brighter tomorrow? The answer, of course, will vary from team to team.
We could, however, start seeing some early indications of which way these clubs are leaning in response to that question as Week 9 unfolds. In our five predictions this week, three of them center around the trade deadline and/or facing the reality that 2026 is not their year and need to make moves to better themselves for 2027 and beyond. Meanwhile, there are a couple of other less existential developments that we wouldn't be shocked to see, including a rough showing from Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels .
We'll look to carry the momentum from a strong selection last week, where we accurately pinpointed a reduced snap share from Jonathan Taylor amid trade rumors and a strong performance from T.J. Hockenson . Below, you can find five storylines and/or individual performances that we wouldn't be shocked to see happen over the course of Week 9.
The Broncos have been in the thick of trade rumors leading up to the Nov. 10 deadline as they've been a team eyed as a potential landing spot for some of the top available running backs.
When you look at their 92.6 rushing yards per game average on the season, it makes sense why they'd possibly pursue the likes of Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis, especially with the club sitting atop the AFC West and hoping to make another deep playoff run. However, that's a 10,000 ft. view of the situation in the backfield. If you zoom in, there's a possibility that the answer to their rushing woes is already on the roster.
Rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a mini breakout performance in the win over Kansas City last week. In just his second game back from returning off injured reserve due to an ankle injury, Coleman saw a team-high 11 carries and rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown. He also caught four of his five targets for 63 yards, which included a pivotal 51-yard catch-and-run on the go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter.
That flash could just be the beginning for Coleman, who should continue to break out this week against Carolina. The Panthers are surrendering 4.8 yards per carry so far this season, which is tied for the fourth-highest in the NFL. Their 140.7 rushing yards per game allowed is third-highest in the league, so this is quite the matchup for Coleman. If he takes advantage of it, he'd silence any need for the Broncos to make a move for a back before the deadline.
The Cardinals made an in-game switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew last week, which helped springboard them to a win over the Cowboys . Minshew threw three touchdowns in the comeback win, which helped him be named the starter for Week 9 against Seattle. It also paved the way for the organization to trade Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens . All of those moves have seen rookie quarterback Carson Beck quietly move up the depth chart. After initially serving as the emergency third quarterback, he's now the primary backup for Arizona.
At some point, this ascension up the depth chart will continue for Beck to the point where he starts games for the Cardinals this season. After taking him atop the third round last spring, the organization has to see what it has in him before embarking on the offseason and possibly searching for another option under center. I wonder if Beck's debut could come as soon as this week during Sunday's divisional matchup with Seattle.
Minshew slicing up a poor Cowboys defense is one thing, but he'll have a much more difficult challenge against a Seattle defense allowing the fewest total yards per game (250.0) through eight contests in team history. Their 4.2 yards per play allowed is also the fourth-fewest by any NFL team through eight games in the last 20 years.
The Seahawks defense is also tied for the third-most takeaways in the NFL this season, so there's the possibility of things getting ugly for Minshew and the Cardinals offense. Does it get so ugly that Matt LaFleur makes another change in favor of Beck? I wouldn't rule it out.
One of the underrated pieces of Washington's win over the Eagles in Week 8 was just how erratic Jayden Daniels was throwing the football. On the night, Daniels registered a 17.2% off-target throw rate, which is the third-highest single-game mark in his career (including playoffs). If that persists in this matchup against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Daniels' currently immaculate interception rate could shatter.
Coming into Week 9, Daniels, who has been limited to five games due to an elbow injury, has yet to throw an interception. He's just the sixth player in NFL history to have at least 240 yards of total offense per game and zero interceptions through five starts. In fact, Daniels hasn't even lost a fumble, so he has no turnovers whatsoever so far in 2026. Something tells me that changes in Week 9.
The Rams are tied for the fifth-most interceptions (7) on the season and are coming off a Week 8 win over the Chargers , where they picked off Justin Herbert twice and forced a fumble (recovered). Oftentimes, turnovers come in bunches, and if Daniels' throws continue to be all over the place, it could cost him. If the Rams, who are a 5.5-point road favorite, build a lead and force Daniels and the Commanders into a pass-heavy game script, it only adds more opportunity for the secondary to create multiple turnovers and stain his currently pristine record.
Bijan Robinson enters Week 9 as the NFL rushing leader with 780 yards on the ground thus far. However, by looking at him over the last four weeks, you wouldn't really know it. Over the past four games, Robinson's rushing totals have taken a precipitous fall, averaging 4.4 yards per carry and 71.5 rushing yards per game. Those figures are well off the otherworldly pace he was on over the first four weeks of the year.
Week 9 presents a great opportunity for Robinson to get back to something closer to the production we saw over the opening month. Entering this international matchup in Madrid, Cincinnati is allowing 122.3 rushing yards per game, which is just outside the top-10 in the NFL. When you dig a bit deeper into the numbers, however, they're even more advantageous for Robinson, with the Bengals allowing 4.8 yards per carry (tied for the fourth-highest in the league). In a surprisingly tight win over the Titans last week, Cincinnati let Tony Pollard rush for 117 yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries.
Joe Burrow has been one of the hottest quarterbacks in the NFL over the past few weeks, and one of the ways the Falcons could look to cool him off is by taking a ground-and-pound approach to this game. They have a back capable of taking over in Robinson, and this matchup is the perfect opportunity to take that approach. Expect a huge day for No. 7.
Sunday goes one of two ways for the Los Angeles Chargers. I don't think it's out of the realm of possibility that they pull out their first win in this home matchup against the Texans , especially if Houston's defense continues to struggle. However, if it continues the way it has for LA and the offense can't muster anything close to a respectable unit, I think we've reached the point where McDaniel is let go. Yes, there were cases to make this move weeks ago, particularly during the club's Week 7 bye, but Jim Harbaugh elected to stick with his offensive coordinator.
Coming out of the break, things didn't look improved whatsoever. In the Week 8 loss to the Rams, the offense continued to sputter. The unit ranks last in the NFL in points per game (14.1) and has the most total turnovers (17). They've also not scored a touchdown since the…
