title: Ravens trade candidates: Three quarterbacks Baltimore should consider amid injury crisis
summary: With Lamar Jackson sidelined and Tyler Huntley out for the year, Baltimore could look to Jacoby Brissett or Anthony Richardson before the trade deadline to keep its 4-4 season alive
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens sit in a dangerous position, as they lost their top two quarterbacks to injury, and their third option is also questionable. On his first passing attempt in the eventual 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery, landed him on injured reserve and could end his season. Then, Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury as well.
That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into the lineup, who completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception vs. Buffalo. However, he's nursing an ankle injury and is considered questionable for the Ravens' Week 9 matchup vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. That led Baltimore to add Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed to its roster.
While Fagnano will likely join Anthony Brown as the only undrafted rookie quarterbacks to start a game for the Ravens, should the team consider chasing a legitimate starter prior to next Tuesday's trade deadline? While Baltimore does reside in last place in the division with a 4-4 record, the season isn't over yet. Let's examine three quarterback options for the Ravens to consider.
The Arizona Cardinals demoted Jacoby Brissett from starter to third-stringer this week, as Mike LaFleur is moving forward with Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck as his new No. 2. Brissett was benched for Minshew in the third quarter of the Cardinals' Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys , who sparked the offense with three touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to get the game to overtime. The Cardinals won that game in the extra period, leading LaFleur to make the decision he did.
Brissett has not been terrible this season. He's completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight games. His 75.6 yards per game to Trey McBride entering Week 8 were the most by a QB-TE combo since 1970 (min. 15 games). Brissett isn't going to be raking in Pro Bowl votes, but he's a borderline starter in this league that would be an upgrade over an undrafted rookie or career third-stringer.
This would be the most intriguing swing of the bat for general manager Eric DeCosta, as Anthony Richardson is the option that offers the most upside. The former No. 4 overall pick out of Florida hasn't made a start since 2024, but he's one of the most athletic quarterback prospects we've ever seen. Obviously, it hasn't gone according to plan for him with the Indianapolis Colts . The 24-year-old quarterback is 8-7 as a starter, having completed 50.9% of his passes with 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions in 18 total games played. Availability and consistency have been major issues for Richardson, but a change of scenery could do wonders for him.
Before you write Richardson off as a complete bust, consider the impact J.J. McCarthy is having early on for the New York Giants . Why couldn't Richardson thrive after his long-awaited trade? Plus, Richardson is a dual-threat athlete who could pair well with Derrick Henry . He averaged 40 rushing yards per game in his first two seasons, and scored 10 touchdowns on the ground as well. Give me the read option every play.
Tyson Bagent of the Chicago Bears has been floated as a trade candidate for the Ravens given his familiarity with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Bagent has truly been one of the most fascinating stories we've seen in the NFL over the past couple of seasons. Undrafted in 2023 out of Shepherd University -- a Division II school in Shepherdstown, West Virginia, Bagent did enough with Chicago in his first preseason to earn a spot on the final 53-man roster. As a rookie, he was called upon to make four starts, and even defeated No. 1 overall pick Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers in prime time.
Bagent signed a two-year, $10 million extension in 2025, but has struggled this season. He threw for 268 yards and one interception in the Week 4, 23-12 win against the New York Jets , then threw for just 87 yards and two interceptions in the 31-7 blowout loss suffered at the hands of the Green Bay Packers the following week. Bagent's struggles look even worse considering that 38-year-old Case Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns in a primetime upset of the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3. If Caleb Williams had to miss another start at some point, you have to wonder who Ben Johnson would start at quarterback this time around.
One question to consider is what would the Bears want for Bagent? If Ryan Poles wants a fourth-round pick for him,it should be "thanks but no thanks."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Jadeveon Clowney mock trades: Cowboys reunion headlines four deals Texans can make before NFL trade deadline
summary: Clowney's name has surfaced in trade discussions this week
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline less than a week away, the hot stove is officially boiling. More and more names are being bandied about with each passing day. Some of them are big and some are smaller, but it seems like things could get pretty wild ahead of Nov. 10.
One name that has been floated in recent days is Houston Texans edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney . ESPN reported earlier this week that the former No. 1 overall pick's name has surfaced in trade discussions.
The Texans are sitting at 2-3, three full games back of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC South and 2.5 games back of the final wild card spot. Clowney himself has played sparingly, appearing on only 37% of Houston's defensive snaps so far this season. He's also been fairly unproductive, recording just 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.
His pressure rate of 13.0%, though, indicates he's been a bit more effective than his counting stats, as he ranks 58th out of 262 players who have rushed the passer at least 50 times so far this season, according to Tru Media. The sample is very small, as Clowney has just 69 pass-rush snaps.
Still, given Clowney's age (33 years old) and relative lack of production, it's hard to see him generating much in the way of a trade return for the Texans. It's most likely that he would net a late-round pick at most, and perhaps only a swap of picks. The Texans sent one of their 2027 seventh-round picks to Cleveland in 2025 and another to Detroit this past offseason in the David Montgomery deal, but have one incoming from the Chargers, so that is the pick we have them sending out in each deal.
As for a few teams that could make sense for Clowney, here's a list.
The Niners have already given their defensive line a boost by trading for DeForest Buckner , and they should welcome Nick Bosa back into the fold soon, if not this week coming off their bye. But they're still just 21st in the NFL in pressure rate, according to Tru Media, and they have been dealing with injuries along the defensive front all season. Adding another capable rotational player off the edge could give them an extra boost ahead of a potential playoff run.
The Chiefs have bigger needs, with the most obvious one being wide receiver, but that doesn't mean they can't use at least some help in the pass rush department. George Karlaftis has 34 pressures this season, but R Mason Thomas , Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Ashton Gillotte have combined for only 42, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding another body to the mix could have some merit. The Chiefs have a 2027 sixth-round pick incoming from the 49ers, likely very late in the round, which they can send out here.
To be clear, the Cowboys should almost certainly not be buyers ahead of the deadline. They are 3-5 and going nowhere fast. But we know that Jerry Jones doesn't operate that way. He fears irrelevance more than anything else, and the Cowboys are in danger of becoming irrelevant this season. Clowney was in Dallas last year and racked up 8.5 sacks but the team elected not to re-sign him because of scheme fit concerns, but with the pass rush mostly not getting home, perhaps the Cowboys would bring him back. Dallas sends out a 2028 pick here because the 2027 sixth-rounder is headed to Pittsburgh in the Joey Porter Jr. trade.
The Giants are in first place in the NFC East and apparently going hunting for all kinds of players at the deadline. With Brian Burns out for the year, the Giants check in 31st in pressure rate, per Tru Media, and they could use some help for Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux coming off the edge. If they allocate more resources to other positions, it could make sense to go for a cheaper option on the defensive front. The Giants have an incoming sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft from the Jacksonville Jaguars, and that's likely to land pretty late in the round.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Browns' Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol: Shedeur Sanders potentially in line to start Week 9 at Saints
summary: Watson cleared evaluation Sunday but started having symptoms Monday night
full_text:
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson entered the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday morning, the Browns announced . Watson, who passed concussion evaluation after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday's loss to the Steelers , told team doctors he started feeling concussion-like symptoms Monday night.
Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol pic.twitter.com/ViiyRHMct8
Should Watson be unable to play in Week 9 against the Saints , the Browns would likely turn to second-year pro Shedeur Sanders .
Watson briefly left Sunday's contest in Pittsburgh after a spotter called down to the sideline for Watson to be checked out after Jaquan Brisker's helmet-to-helmet hit (which was flagged). Sanders entered the game briefly before Watson returned. Watson finished the 27-6 loss with 324 passing yards but also eight sacks and zero touchdowns.
Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA
The Browns say they also evaluated Watson for a concussion after the game and again Monday morning, per league rules. However, when Watson reported his symptoms to the team on Tuesday morning, Cleveland immediately put him in the protocol.
Sanders, 24, could start Sunday in a crucial game for the Browns, who are 5-3 this season. He has appeared in two games this year, but only for five snaps. He has completed all three of his passes for 2 yards.
Sanders did get considerable playing time as part of Cleveland's quarterback carousel last year, appearing in eight games (seven starts). He threw seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions while completing 56.6% of his passes. He had some impressive performances, including a three-touchdown day against the Titans , but struggled overall. Out of 36 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts, he was last in completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception rate and passer rating.
Sanders lost the quarterback battle to Watson this offseason, but should he be called upon to start, he'd be in a much better offensive ecosystem than he was in last year. The Browns have upgraded their offensive line and wide receivers, with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion impressing. The Saints could potentially provide a soft landing spot, too: New Orleans' defense ranks 28th in both yards per play and yards per game.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Brandon Aiyuk files to be reinstated, will report to 49ers facility this week, per report
summary: San Francisco now has the option to trade or release the disgruntled wide receiver, with an outright cut viewed as the most likely outcome after a turbulent year away from the team
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is taking the steps necessary to return to the field. This week, ESPN reported he had hired agent Drew Rosenhaus to represent him, and now, he has reportedly turned in paperwork filing to be reinstated . Adam Schefter says Aiyuk will report to the 49ers' facilities on Friday.
"Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field," Rosenhaus said.
If Aiyuk is reinstated, the 49ers could trade or release him. General manager John Lynch said 10 months ago it was safe to say the wide receiver had played his last snap for the 49ers. The franchise would like to pick up some compensation in parting ways with their two-year-old headache, but it remains to be seen if any team would offer anything for him. ESPN reported that if Aiyuk is reinstated, the most likely outcome is the franchise releasing him.
This strange saga began when Aiyuk tore his ACL in October 2024. He was placed on the PUP list prior to the 2025 season as he continued to rehab, but 13 months after his injury, it was reported that the 49ers had voided the $27 million of 2026 salary guarantees in his contract. Aiyuk apparently had not been checking in with the team, sticking to his rehab schedule or doing what his contract required of him. Aiyuk was placed on the reserve/left squad list in December.
Aiyuk spent this past offseason taking shots at the 49ers on social media, and acting as if he were going to reunite with his college quarterback in Jayden Daniels and sign with the Washington Commanders . However, the 49ers still owned his rights, so Aiyuk had to file for reinstatement and then be acquired via trade if his Washington dream were to come true. Aiyuk refused to complete these steps in the offseason, but now, he's playing ball.
Aiyuk established himself as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL in 2023, as he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on the way to Super Bowl LVIII. His 3.1 yards per route run that year ranked No. 3 behind Tyreek Hill and Nico Collins , and his 81.3% of receptions going for a first down or a touchdown ranked first in the NFL.
The offseason following the Super Bowl appearance, Aiyuk orchestrated a "hold-in" during training camp, which eventually led to the four-year, $120 million extension he was after. That 2024 season, Aiyuk reached 50 yards receiving in just one of the seven games he played in before tearing his ACL.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Midseason All-Rookie Team: QB Jalon Daniels leads team filled with multiple Browns, Jets
summary: A dynamic Browns wide receiver duo and Titans standout Carnell Tate highlight the offensive playmakers making an immediate impact through the first eight weeks
full_text:
The departure from a 16-game regular season eliminated a clean midway point to the NFL regular season, but there is a large enough sample size to assess the contributions of the rookie class through Week 8.
Reflecting upon the 2026 NFL Draft , there were 19 offensive and 13 defensive prospects taken in the first round. Although the No. 1 overall selection has yet to make his first start, several others are making a meaningful impact on their respective teams.
Here is the Midseason All-Rookie team:
Daniels is the selection by default. He is the only rookie quarterback to appear in more than one game and the only quarterback with more than 36 dropbacks.
The undrafted free agent out of Kansas had some good moments. He looked crisp in three quarters against the Steelers , but accuracy waned in the game's most critical moments. His comfort is throwing to the boundary rather than attacking the middle of the field, but he would lock onto his first read, and defenders began breaking on it once they picked up on the tendency. When the sea parted before him, Daniels showed the foot speed to get chunks of yardage on the ground.
To be a viable quarterback long-term, Daniels must do a better job handling pressure. He was sacked nine times on 123 dropbacks because the protection was either not set to handle the blitz or he could not feel the pressure on his back.
He completed 60 of 98 pass attempts for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions.
Preseason selection: Fernando Mendoza , Raiders
The running back position was more complicated than quarterback because each of the candidates has either missed time due to injury or is serving in a reserve role. Love leads all rookie running backs with 76 carries despite missing two games and is now actively dealing with an ankle injury that landed him on the injured reserve. His presence on the end-of-year All-Rookie team is very much in doubt.
Love shows good vision and does well breaking his feet down in space to leverage defenders. He is patient before making his move and has 11 receptions as well. Arizona's offensive line has left a lot to be desired. The Notre Dame product has been averaging 1.1 yards before contact this season, which is below average, according to TruMedia.
Las Vegas' Mike Washington Jr . has had some big runs on stretch plays to the boundary. San Francisco's Kaelon Black drew heavy consideration. Denver's Jonah Coleman has been a personal favorite, but the body of work is limited due to injury.
Preseason selection: Jeremiyah Love , Cardinals
Concepcion has the second-most receptions among rookie receivers but has nearly half of his receptions and 57.7% of his receiving yards over the past three games. It has taken some time to develop timing and chemistry with Deshaun Watson , who was errant on several passes in Concepcion's direction at the start of the season.
Among all rookie receivers, Concepcion ranks second in yards after the catch per reception (5.5), according to TruMedia. He is dynamic and elusive with the ball in his hands.
The Texas A&M product has 33 receptions for 352 yards.
KC Concepcion just has a different gear with the ball in his hands pic.twitter.com/bumtXpwWll
Preseason selection: K.C. Concepcion, Browns
Tate was the third choice, and the margins may be slimmer than one may expect of the leading rookie receiver. The No. 4 overall selection has four drops and three fumbles this season.
Tate has good size and the foot quickness to win out of the stem, but he generally has not been threatening downfield against man coverage. He was unavailable for Sunday's loss to the Bengals due to a shoulder injury; the first game of his career missed.
The Ohio State product leads all rookies in receptions (34) and receiving yards (413).
Preseason selection: Carnell Tate , Titans
Boston has slowed down a bit over the past month after his blistering start that led to some glamorous statistical and play-style comparisons. Most of his early season success was isolated to ball-winning downfield plays. In each of the first five games, he had a reception of at least 20 yards. In that metric, among rookies, he trails only his teammate, Concepcion, who has seven.
Boston is a classic X-receiver, but the Browns would be better served diversifying his usage as he becomes more comfortable transitioning to the NFL. The next step in Boston's growth is developing better chemistry with Watson and finishing plays. Boston has just one drop to his name, but there were a handful of others that could be classified as such. He is consistently open and a zone coverage merchant, but not always on the same page as his quarterback.
There are a variety of other pass catchers who deserve recognition, such as Omar Cooper Jr . ( Jets ), Germie Bernard (Steelers), Caleb Douglas ( Dolphins ), Antonio Williams ( Commanders ) and Malachi Fields ( Giants ).
Preseason selection: Denzel Boston , Browns
Sadiq has been a plus performer in both the pass and run games. He leads all rookie tight ends in receptions (17) and receiving yards (186). As a prospect, the ex-Oregon Duck was known for his play-making ability post-catch, and he has carried that trait into the league. Among all receivers and tight ends, Sadiq ranks second in yards after the catch per reception (6.0).
In the run game, he is a bulldog. He is constantly working and straining to sustain blocks and spring his teammates for bigger gains. At times, he could rein in that energy a bit better, but he has been a well-rounded asset for the AFC franchise.
In the preseason, Patriots tight end Eli Raridon was among those under consideration. He has been excellent for a rejuvenated New England team.
Preseason selection: Kenyon Sadiq , Jets
There have been a few rookies to moonlight as left tackles this season, but the possibilities boiled down to Kahlil Benson of the Chiefs , Jayden Williams of the Cardinals and Fano. Benson is a great story and incredibly valuable in the absence of former first-round pick Josh Simmons . However, Fano has a higher ceiling because of his athleticism.
Fano has a really natural feel for the game. He communicates and picks up exchanges well. He possesses the requisite foot quickness and ankle flexion to handle most of what is thrown at him. His issues are largely correctable, but his play strength still must improve.
Fano has been credited with two sacks and 18 pressures allowed on 311 pass-blocking snaps, according to TruMedia.
Preseason selection: Spencer Fano , Browns
Jacksonville's Emmanuel Pregnon and Proctor were candidates for different reasons. Pregnon has a better feel for the offense and consistently executes it well but does not possess Proctor's ceiling.
The former Alabama left tackle has allowed nine pressures and one sack in 186 pass-blocking snaps, according to TruMedia.
Preseason selection: Kadyn Proctor , Dolphins
A training camp injury to veteran Tyler Biadasz forced Slaughter into the starting lineup. Los Angeles' offensive woes can not be attributed to a single person, but the rookie has certainly been a flawed part of the line. TruMedia credits him with eight pressures and one sack allowed on 261 pass-blocking snaps, but more powerful interior players have given him fits with the bull rush. Slaughter has good foot mobility and can execute some of the blocks in space that have been asked of him.
Preseason selection: Jake Slaughter , Chargers
There was consideration to pencil in Ioane as the center given he spent some time there this season, which would allow Cleveland's Austin Barber to be the selection at right guard. Ioane and Barber have been the two best interior linemen this season. Baltimore intends to play the former at right guard, so he will align there in this exercise.
Although he is now dealing with an injury, TruMedia credits Ioane with seven pressures and one sack allowed on 210 pass-blocking snaps. Ioane plays with a sturdy base and looks for work when disengaged.
Preseason selection: Francis Mauigoa ,…

title: NFL Week 9 picks, best bets: Bears continue to surge in primetime, Vikings lose second straight vs. Bills
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 9 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
We've been on the wrong side of a couple of bad beats throughout the first half of the regular season, and Week 8 was no exception. One of my five locks last week was the Patriots covering a 7.5-point spread over the Dolphins in Miami. For a large chunk of the second half, we were well on our way to cashing. Then, in the blink of an eye, we were suddenly sweating it out.
After a 14-point third-quarter lead ballooned New England's lead to 11 and just four minutes remained in regulation, the Dolphins put together an eight-play, 84-yard touchdown drive to cut it within five. The gut punch was Malik Willis uncorking a 35-yard touchdown to Kevin Coleman Jr . to put them within the number.
Kevin Coleman Jr. scores and we have a one-score game in Miami NEvsMIA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4NjWuELca1
Even when all was thought to be lost, there was another opportunity for New England to extend the lead late after a botched onside kick by Miami. The Patriots reached the Dolphins' 38-yard line and faced a third-and-5. If they failed to convert, a meaningless field-goal attempt would've brought the lead to eight. Alas, Rhamondre Stevenson rushed for the necessary yardage to move the chains, Drake Maye knelt three times, and we came out losers. Pain.
While that bat beat put in through a torture chamber, it was a good slate for us overall. I was 3-2 ATS with my locks of the week, 8-6 ATS overall, and 10-4 on the moneyline. I'll look to keep that momentum rolling and try to avoid any more bad beats as our attention now pivots to Week 9. As always, we begin with my five locks of the week.
Note : Tennessee and Pittsburgh are on the bye in Week 9.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Bears look like bona fide Super Bowl contenders right now after rolling into Seattle and taking it to the defending champion Seahawks , with new defensive stud Jeffery Simmons showing out in his debut.
They head back home for another primetime matchup against a Bucs team that didn't complete a pass in a 16-0 win over the Falcons . Over the past two games, Tampa Bay's passing attack has completed 7 of 14 attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown. That might be good enough to lock in two wins against NFC South rivals, but they'll need to chuck it to keep pace with Caleb Williams and keep this newly dominant defense honest. I don't believe they will be able to, which sets up Chicago to win its fourth straight game.
The Bears are also 3-1 ATS at home this season.
Projected score : Bears 28, Buccaneers 20 The pick : Bears -6.5
Weather was a factor, but I did find it noteworthy that the Patriots struggled to fend off the Dolphins in last week's win in Miami. Sure, a divisional game will always be pesky, but it is sticking in the back of my head as I look towards this matchup with Green Bay.
I think Drake Maye, who leads the NFL in total yards and total touchdowns from Week 4 to Week 8, will have some trouble against this evolving Packers defense. Over the past five games, Green Bay is allowing just 14.6 points per game, which ranks third in the NFL. Meanwhile, Jordan Love is first in the NFL in passing yards entering Week 8 and first in completions of 20-plus air yards. He's also fourth in passing touchdowns, so New England's defense will have its hands full and is firmly on upset alert.
Projected score : Packers 23, Patriots 21 The pick : Packers +3
Jayden Daniels was pretty erratic with his throws on Sunday night, despite pulling out the 27-10 win over Philadelphia. For the game, he had an off-target rate of 17.2%, which was the third-highest in a single game in his career. That's alarming, particularly as Washington hosts a Rams team that is starting to gain some momentum.
This season, L.A. is allowing 301.1 total yards per game, which ranks fifth in the league. If Daniels continues to misfire, this Rams defense has shown it can shut down an opponent. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 0-5 following a win since the start of last season and own a -9.0 points-per-game differential over that stretch.
This could be a game where Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua feast, as Washington is currently giving up a 100.6 passer rating against this season, which ranks 25th in the league. I expect another prolific game from that duo as L.A. wins and covers.
Projected score : Rams 27, Commanders 21 The pick : Rams -5.5
At any moment, another star could be shipped out of Indy, which makes this line something we'll want to jump on with it below a touchdown. Yes, the Cowboys defense is horrid and just lost to Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals , but Indianapolis is lost right now. They were just blown out 42-7 by the Jaguars and are 2-13 over their past 15 games. This season, they are allowing 27.8 points per game, which is the third-highest in the NFL entering Week 9. That sets up this Cowboys offense to flirt with 30 points on the day.
If they get there, it's hard to imagine Daniel Jones keeping pace, even when accounting for Dallas' defense. Jones has an NFL-worst 68.7 passer rating this season and appears to be barely clinging to his starting job. Since Week 9 of last year, Jones is 3-10 as the starter with 13 total touchdowns and 20 turnovers. Meanwhile, I think Indy will continue to limit Jonathan Taylor , with trade rumors still swirling around him. Last week, he played a season-low 62.3% of the offensive snaps, which was less than the 67.2% offensive snaps he logged the week prior in Week 7. If Taylor is less of a factor, that only lowers the ceiling of the Indy offense and clears a path for Dallas to cover.
Projected score : Cowboys 30, Colts 17 The pick : Cowboys -6
The Vikings suffered their first loss of the season in Week 8, falling to the Lions in a game that further emphasized the clunky start Kyler Murray has had running the offense. It's largely been masked by the stellar play of the defense, but Minnesota's offense is averaging just 279.4 total yards per game, which is the fourth-lowest in the league. Their 20 points per game average ranks sixth-lowest.
That's unsustainable, especially against another high-octane offense like the Bills . Buffalo is averaging a league-best 33.3 points per game. While the Vikings defense will make it hard for them to maintain that average, they may not need to reach 30 to pull out the win on the road. Last week, Detroit scored 19 points in the winning effort, while going 1-for-3 in the red zone. Buffalo scores touchdowns on 70% of its red zone trips this season (fifth-highest). If they maintain that success and merely get north of 20 points, that could be too tall of a mountain for Murray and the Vikings offense to overcome.

title: Tyler Huntley out for season: Ravens lose top backup with Lamar Jackson already out, per report
summary: Baltimore will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday
full_text:
As the reeling Baltimore Ravens try to figure out whether Lamar Jackson's thumb injury will cost him the rest of the season, they got certainty on his backup. Tyler Huntley is in fact out for the remainder of 2026 due to a turf toe injury he suffered after relieving Jackson in Sunday's loss to the Bills , per ESPN's Adam Schefter .
The Ravens have been in scramble mode ever since the pair of quarterback injuries. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano , an undrafted rookie out of UConn, finished out Sunday's 36-10 blowout loss and will start Thursday against the Jaguars . Baltimore added Austin Reed , who was with the team in the preseason, to its practice squad and signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad earlier this week in an attempt to build some sort of depth on a short week. Reed has never taken a regular-season snap, and Slovis has taken five.
Huntley, 29, has spent six of his seven years with the Ravens after going undrafted in 2020. He has been a crucial depth piece, starting 14 games during his time in Baltimore, including three this year as Jackson dealt with an ankle injury. Huntley guided Baltimore to a win over the Falcons but lost to the Browns and Bengals before Jackson's short-lived return. He suffered the turf toe injury when Bills DT Ed Oliver landed on the back of his foot.
Ravens backup QB Tyler Huntley dealing with a toe injury. On the replay, you can see his right foot plant before continuing into extension, placing increased stress through the toe region. Turf toe is a concern here, involving injury to the plantar structures of the 1st MTP… pic.twitter.com/EIoipD8xyw
With more clarity on at least one quarterback's injury, the Ravens could look to make a trade ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with Tyson Bagent and Jacoby Brissett as potential options mentioned by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport earlier this week.
Baltimore is 4-4 on the season and has lost three straight games.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Week 9 QB Power Rankings: Familiar name returns to No. 1, Cam Ward crawls out of basement

full_text:
Quarterbacks are the most vital position in football. After all, they're the highest-paid players, and the past 13 NFL MVP award winners are, that's right, quarterbacks. While some quarterbacks are a byproduct of their offensive ecosystems, a select few elevate above their current circumstances to the ranks of the elite.
These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season. That's why some quarterbacks in this week's rankings rose as many as seven spots or fell as many as five. Not in a vacuum, Patrick Mahomes would remain No. 1 for the foreseeable future and so on. He hasn't been in the top spot for some weeks now, given his torn ACL and others playing better ahead of him. However, that isn't set in stone, and he could rise back to the top of the board as the 2026 season progresses. He made some steps forward this week.

title: Prisco's Week 9 NFL expert picks: Jaguars roll over Lamar Jackson-less Ravens, Cowboys rebound
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss
full_text:
The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday.
Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3.
As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take.
Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week.
Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16
The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain.
Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21
The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line.
Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20
The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game.
Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17
The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around.
This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff .
Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13
The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game.
Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14
The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late.
Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20
This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it.
Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24
The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense.
Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16
The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big.
Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17
This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it.
Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16
The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger.
Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13
The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it.
This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense.
Pick: Bills 21, Vikings 14

title: Cardinals trade updates: Sweat & Budda
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are trying to get back into the thick of things this year. Beating the Dallas Cowboys last weekend after being dominated for the first half is a sign that this roster still has a good degree of fight in it, and that the season is not lost. What is helping is that […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 01: Budda Baker #3 of the Arizona Cardinals exits the field after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are trying to get back into the thick of things this year. Beating the Dallas Cowboys last weekend after being dominated for the first half is a sign that this roster still has a good degree of fight in it, and that the season is not lost. What is helping is that this year, the other teams in the NFC West Division are also struggling, such as the Los Angeles Rams and the Seattle Seahawks. RELATED: BRISSETT TRADED TO THE RAVENS It is true that Arizona still resides at the bottom of the division with a 3-5-0 record, but unlike other years, they are now just one game out of second place. Usually, when teams begin their season badly, when the trade deadline rolls around in November, it is assumed that these horrid teams will begin trading off their best players, who just happen to be some of their most expensive athletes. Because the Cardinals began 2-5-0, they were tossed into this category. And even though the team is on a one-game winning streak, they remain on the “sellers” list, especially after the Jacoby Brissett trade. Here are two players that have been earmarked for being involved in a trade, and their updates. EDGE Josh Sweat For over a month, Sweat has been mentioned by just about every national and local media outlet as a potential trade. Last year, he had 12 sacks, 17 QB hits, and 28 pressures, among other stats. He was a menace on passing downs and proved his worth after being signed to a huge deal in free agency. If the Cardinals had sought out a trade partner during the offseason, Sweat would have brought a bounty of draft picks. But that was last year. His production this season has been subpar, with 3 sacks, 5 QB hits, and 9 pressures through eight games. Which means his trade value has lessened, even though the Cardinals have the same DC and the same defensive scheme as last year. However, it should be noted that Sweat has three sacks in his last five games. What is his update? For one, the franchise is admitting that Sweat is available before the trade deadline on November 10. But GM Monti Ossenfort has also stated that they are fine with keeping him and hope that his production will increase going into the second half of the schedule. Someone tell Andrew Berry Josh Sweat has 3 sacks in his last 5 games pic.twitter.com/EgAYQLFCPo — Mac🦬 (@tha_buffalo) November 3, 2026 And Arizona will most likely retain his services because Ossenfort isn’t letting Sweat go for cheap. Word is, the Cardinals have a high asking price, which will keep some teams in the probability category, while others will simply bow out. Sweat has stated that he would be amenable to a trade, or would be happy to stay put. The Cardinals have complete control over this situation. Considered dead, by coming back and beating Dallas the way they did, it is quite possible that a QB change will alter this offense going forward, and that Arizona isn’t interested in letting Sweat walk away. After all, every NFL club is always looking for a good pass rusher, and Sweat has two more years remaining on his contract. We will see this weekend against the Seahawks how this offense will react with QB Jacoby Brissett being relegated to the bench and Gardner Minshew elevated to the starting role. But this team may, or may not, be more competitive than once thought. Multiple clubs have reached out to Ossenfort so far, with the Cowboys the loudest voice. Other interested teams include the Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals. The San Francisco 49ers have also been mentioned, but the unwritten rule is that a club never trades within the division, and they try not to trade within the conference. Josh Sweat is open to a trade, per @Schultz_Report Multiple teams interested, but Cardinals asking price is believed to be high pic.twitter.com/kijVSsuGcB — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) November 3, 2026 Arizona has not divulged what their asking price is, but all along it has been estimated to be a Day 2 pick, meaning a second or third-round draft pick, with a fourth or fifth-round selection thrown in. The big question remains: Is it worth it to the Cardinals’ defense to suddenly be without their only productive pass rusher for a draft pick that isn’t going to help them at all this season? If things go well against Seattle, look for Ossenfort to stand pat on Sweat, then readdress a trade possibility in the offseason if his production doesn’t increase to last year’s level. Safety Budda Baker Nobody knows where the gossip began about Baker being on the trade market, but every year, his name appears. Maybe his agent starts the rumor. Baker has publicly stated that he is happy playing for the Cardinals organization, and that he likes the defensive scheme and gets along well with DC Nick Rallis. "I don't think Arizona wants to move on from Budda Baker.. He's meant so much to that franchise and he's such a baller" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/OZSjpcBo0k — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 2, 2026 The thinking in the organization at this point is that they are very content with Baker’s production, his tackling numbers, and his leadership in the locker room. The Cardinals are not actively seeking a trade unless they receive an offer that would blow the doors off. Which isn’t going to happen. Recently, on the “Pat McAfee Show,” NFL Insider Adam Schefter stated that Ossenfort has little to no interest in moving Baker.
author: Barry Shuck

title: Arizona Cardinals designate Isaiah Adams to return from injured reserve
summary: It has been a rough season with injuries once again for the Arizona Cardinals, but they could be getting at least one piece back. The team announced they have opened the 21 day practice window for Isaiah Adams, and the Cardinals desperately need help along the offensive line. From the team: The Arizona Cardinals Football […]
full_text: It has been a rough season with injuries once again for the Arizona Cardinals, but they could be getting at least one piece back. The team announced they have opened the 21 day practice window for Isaiah Adams, and the Cardinals desperately need help along the offensive line. From the team: The Arizona Cardinals Football Club today announced that the team has designated offensive lineman Isaiah Adams to return from the injured reserve list. Adams can begin practicing and the team can activate him to the 53-man roster at any time during the next 21 days or at the conclusion of the three-week period. In addition, the team has signed running back Jermar Jefferson and wide receiver James Proche II to the practice squad. The signings took place today at the Dignity Health Arizona Cardinals Training Center in Tempe, AZ. Jefferson (5-10, 215) returns to the Cardinals after he played two games with the team last season in addition to spending time on Arizona’s practice squad. In his career, Jefferson has appeared in 11 games (one start) with the Cardinals and Lions and has 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries to go along with five receptions for 33 yards. He entered the league with Detroit as a seventh-round pick (257 th overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft out of Oregon State. Proche (5-11, 193) is a seven-year NFL veteran who has played 71 games (three starts) in his career with Tennessee (2025), Cleveland (2023-24) and Baltimore (2020-22). In his career, he has 34 receptions for 364 yards to go along with 68 punt returns for 591 yards (8.7-yard avg.) and four kick returns for 60 yards. Proche entered the league with Baltimore as a sixth-round pick (201 st overall) in the 2020 NFL Draft from SMU. He was on the Browns practice squad earlier this season. Jefferson will wear jersey #37 and Proche will wear #18. The wide receiver position is obviously one of need as well, so the Arizona Cardinals added a couple of pieces there as well, but Adams is really the one to watch, and hopefully he can make it back on the field in the window.
author: Seth Cox

title: Cardinals Brissett traded to Baltimore
summary: Wow. How things change. And quickly, right? Four days ago, QB Jacoby Brissett was warming up on the field at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, home of the Dallas Cowboys. Today, he is a member of the Baltimore Ravens. On Wednesday, it was announced that Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort had traded Brissett to the Ravens. […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals walks off the field after the Denver Broncos defeated the Cardinals 30-16 at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wow. How things change. And quickly, right? Four days ago, QB Jacoby Brissett was warming up on the field at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, home of the Dallas Cowboys. Today, he is a member of the Baltimore Ravens. On Wednesday, it was announced that Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort had traded Brissett to the Ravens. Baltimore’s starting QB, Lamar Jackson, and his backup, Tyler Huntley, are both injured and landed on IR. The Ravens had undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, and UFL quarterback Austin Reed remaining. RELATED: CARDINALS BENCH BRISSETT IN WIN OVER COWBOYS Brissett was pulled early in the second half of the 33-30 win over the Cowboys, and his backup, veteran Gardner Minshew, was inserted. Suddenly, the offense came alive after Dallas had dominated for two quarters. Minshew orchestrated a late drive in regulation to tie the game, then led the game-winning drive in overtime that ended with a 42-yard Chad Ryland field goal for the win. Schefter: Jacoby Brissett to be traded to the Ravens. pic.twitter.com/HT4BU342r3 — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 4, 2026 The very next day, it was announced by Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur that Minshew would be the starting quarterback this week against the Seattle Seahawks, and his backup would become rookie Carson Beck. This meant that Brissett had gone from starter to QB3 in less than 24 hours. Brissett was mentioned as trade bait by several media outlets and Cardinals podcasts. That became true in a very short timespan. The details of the trade have not been released since the deal is not complete. It is assumed that Brissett would not dress or start at home against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The game is tomorrow night on Thursday Night Football , broadcast on Prime. The deal is announced as still pending, but will be finalized this weekend. He is a seasoned veteran with a low salary and should become a very good rental for the Ravens for the remainder of the season. Currently, Baltimore is 4-4-0 and listed last in the division. Brissett is heading back to a division he is quite familiar with, the AFC North. He played for the Cleveland Browns in 2022 and played the first 11 games while QB Deshaun Watson was on league suspension.

title: Bad weather can’t be the main cause of Falcons’ ugly defeat
summary: After the Falcons’ ugly loss in Tampa Bay, plenty of discussion focused on how the weather affected their performance. A nasty rainstorm affects every team’s play. Look no further than Baker Mayfield, who didn’t complete a pass on three attempts and fumbled multiple times. Instead of forcing a balanced attack, Tampa Bay solely relied on […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons hands off to Bijan Robinson #7 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Falcons’ ugly loss in Tampa Bay, plenty of discussion focused on how the weather affected their performance. A nasty rainstorm affects every team’s play. Look no further than Baker Mayfield, who didn’t complete a pass on three attempts and fumbled multiple times. Instead of forcing a balanced attack, Tampa Bay solely relied on the ground game and brutalized their opponent. They adapted to the conditions and used their strengths to break a divisional rival down in the trenches. The Falcons couldn’t move the ball efficiently on the ground or stop the run. That put the game in Michael Penix Jr.’s hands, and he proceeded to have the worst game of his career. Todd Bowles’ squad embraced the chaotic environment and flourished in it. Kevin Stefanski’s team was rattled in it and drowned in gruesome fashion. Much more went into that abysmal performance than a rainstorm preventing them from executing. A one-sided defeat stems from self-inflicted errors, personnel breakdowns, coaching miscues, and players not being good enough. That’s what the Falcons have to accept when assessing what went wrong. A quarterback’s miserable meltdown From not being able to push the ball downfield to having to adjust your footwork, a massive rainstorm will challenge how a signal caller operates in the pocket. What it shouldn’t change is how the quarterback reads the field and processes defensive looks, especially when he receives solid pass protection. Penix Jr. was completely discombobulated in the pocket, making numerous costly errors and misses. His inability to see Alex Anzalone on his first two interceptions was perplexing. The first turnover came from Anzalone dropping off the line of scrimmage into the short area of the field. The linebacker never tried blitzing into the C-gap. He went straight back into coverage and somehow capitalized on an errant Penix Jr. pass that was lofted into his hands. Penix Jr. didn’t see him there or on the next drive, where he tried to connect with Jahan Dotson down the seam. That throw went directly to Anzalone once again for another interception. The fourth-down interception to Jacob Parrish was the one excusable turnover, as it was a desperate heave in a collapsed pocket on a make-or-break play. There was no poor processing or decision-making. But that came back to haunt him on the final interception, where Zyon McCollum didn’t bite on the fake smoke screen. While the play design deserves criticism (more on that below), Penix Jr. used a pump fake before attempting to throw with anticipation, assuming McCollum would bite. The cornerback didn’t budge and capitalized on another appalling mistake from Penix Jr. Three of the four interceptions were squarely on the enigmatic quarterback. He had some ugly incompletions because he still doesn’t consistently throw the ball well in the intermediate middle area of the field. Bad weather will limit, not ruin, a quarterback’s ability to perform. Franchise quarterbacks have to prove they can overcome adversity and operate functionally in difficult circumstances. Penix Jr. failed to do that in a big divisional game. Overmatched in the trenches Mother Nature doesn’t impact how your linemen compete in the trenches. On both sides of the ball, the Falcons were mauled during long stretches. The undersized defensive front was bound to have issues against one of the league’s more physically imposing groups. Tampa Bay’s offensive line did its share of damage, but an overall team effort helped spring Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell into the open field. Chris Godwin and Payne Durham made multiple key pin and seal blocks to create space at the second level. As Tristian Wirfs and Cody Mauch imposed their will, the skill position players blocked like demons to disorient the Falcons’ attack front. Defensive linemen were getting erased in the run game. The starting rookie linebacker tandem struggled, particularly Harold Perkins Jr., who couldn’t get off his blocks and missed a few tackles. It was a humbling day for a unit missing size up front, as they didn’t receive much support on the back end, with defensive backs missing tackles all over the place. The offensive line was equally as humbled on the ground. My colleague Tre’Shon Diaz noted in his piece that Bijan Robinson averaged 2.6 yards per carry on 18 attempts if you remove his 30-yard gain. Most of his yards came from an extraordinary effort to keep his balance through a pile to produce an explosive play. Matthew Bergeron has played better in spurts, but he has failed to live up to the lofty contract extension he received this past summer. Ryan Neuzil’s physical limitations have become problematic against bigger fronts. Jake Matthews offers little as a run blocker at this point, while Jawan Taylor was repeatedly behind on his assignments. As much as the Falcons want to be fast and athletic in the trenches, the lack of sheer size and gap-moving power is glaring in these one-sided defeats. Short-yardage shortcomings Per The Athletic’s Josh Kendall, the Falcons faced ten third- and fourth-down plays of two yards or less. They gained a grand total of four yards on those plays. That includes not converting any of their 12 third downs. It was an appalling performance that requires some serious soul-searching. They can’t be solely reliant on Penix Jr. and Charlie Woerner to sneak to convert every time. They also need to understand the challenges facing Tampa Bay’s front. No matter how much you pride yourself on running the ball, you need in-game adjustments for your game plan against specific units. Tampa Bay has one of the league’s strongest run defenses. Calling runs that kept going directly toward Vita Vea was baffling. When the Falcons produced solid gains on the ground, it came from gap-scheme runs with offensive linemen pulling and other personnel making down blocks. They also had flashes of positive gains on stretch runs. It was nowhere near what Irving and Gainwell did, but it proved to be effective in spurts. You can’t call those runs often in short-yardage situations, but more variation is needed to attack a defense playing at a top-ten level. It nearly worked in the first quarter on a third-and-two when Kyle Pitts was open downfield on a deep crosser off play action. After coolly evading a blitzing Anzalone in the pocket, Penix Jr. had the space to hit Pitts for a likely touchdown. He sailed it well over his head with no Tampa Bay defender in sight. Although the execution wasn’t there, that type of clever, aggressive play calling could make the difference in solving these frustrating woes. Screens are becoming wasted plays What was supposed to be one of the offense’s schematic strengths is a genuine liability. Stefanski and Rees were praised for how well they utilized screens in Cleveland. The timing was on point. The execution was crisp. Offensive linemen and skill-position players handled their blocking assignments while defenders chased them downfield. Outside of Bijan Robinson’s opening-day touchdown against Pittsburgh, it’s hard to recall many significant screens. Opposing defenders are diagnosing them as soon as the ball is snapped. title: Week 8, 3 down and 3 down: No silver lining from the Monsoon Bowl
summary: The Atlanta Falcons played the role of Artax from The Neverending Story, and like Atreyu, Falcons fans’ cries and pleas went unanswered as they watched their team slowly drown in the swamp. There is no up this week; everyone sank in the pit. Here’s the Week 8, 3 down and 3 down. 3 down Michael […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers rushes in the first half against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons played the role of Artax from The Neverending Story , and like Atreyu, Falcons fans’ cries and pleas went unanswered as they watched their team slowly drown in the swamp. There is no up this week; everyone sank in the pit. Here’s the Week 8, 3 down and 3 down. 3 down Michael Penix Jr. This is what the worst version of Penix looks like. The slow starts have been there all season, but the turnovers have not. He’s a rhythm passer, but that’s a two-way street; once he gets off beat, he stays there. When he finds his groove, he is one of the more efficient passers out there. Yes, the game plan was poor and so was the weather, but that doesn’t mean you carelessly throw off your back foot, or throw into double/triple coverage. Everyone has bad games; I don’t expect Penix to look this bad again, but it’s up to him to make sure that doesn’t happen. Michael Panix Bowles packed the line and once again Penix struggled with these looks. Rat defender ate his lunch all day, he struggled when forced to move and, mechanics deteriorated as things got worse and he compounded his bad decisions. Worst game of his career. pic.twitter.com/Rsx9i3eVlg — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 2, 2026 Matthew Bergeron The guard received his extension based on his potential, and he isn’t living up to it. Unlike others on the line, he isn’t a lineman with a typical outside-zone build; he has the physical traits that should transfer to a gap or duo scheme, but the team hasn’t had much success running these concepts behind him. Of all the Falcons linemen, he is the one who doesn’t get to use the size excuse many have applied to the Buccaneers -Falcons mismatch, but he was routinely manhandled. If Bergeron can’t turn things around, he’ll be the first black eye on Cunningham’s resume, because no matter how this season goes, they are tied to him through the 2027 season . Run Defense The Falcons didn’t allow a single reception in this game, but they did allow 324 rushing yards. The rookie linebackers struggled all game, and the attacking scheme’s aggressive nature is being taken advantage of by gap schemes, and Jeff Ulbrich is out of answers. He’s increased the number of defensive line slants, a technique that essentially has his defenders line up in one gap and shoot into another, but it doesn’t really solve the problem. For starters, it’s a guessing game; the defense doesn’t know where the ball is going and is hoping to catch the offense off guard, but they aren’t. The other issue is that against a gap scheme, they block down most of the time, so even if you move into a new gap, the OL isn’t necessarily unprepared; they just need to play sound and pick up whoever shows up. Injuries to the front have definitely taken their toll on the defense, so the struggles are understandable. It is also worth noting that 229 of those 324 yards came after contact , and the weather definitely played a role in that statistic. Every Bucs explosive run – DL slants were ineffective, resulting in massive gaps and let the OL get to the 2nd level with ease – LBs struggled with their keys, lots of gap guessing. Cooked when the OL got hands on them – Horrific run fits from Watts – Poor tackling by everyone pic.twitter.com/jValXYFFkV — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 2, 2026 3 down (part 2) Run Offense Something’s gotta give. If you want to be treated like a winning team, you have to perform against good opponents, and the Falcons run game has been stuffed in a locker for four straight weeks. The reality is, they’re just not that good, and Bijan can’t cover up their poor blocking every week. Tommy Rees’ lack of confidence showed immediately in his decision to come out throwing in a monsoon. He isn’t putting forth a good enough effort to throw the run game away so early. After their best week with multiple tight end personnel groups, the young coordinator tried to do everything out of 11 personnel (3 WRs, 1 TE), which let Tampa Bay stay in nickel all game. He did implement more pulling concepts this week but did far less gap and inside zone. It feels like the team is just aimlessly throwing things at the wall and hoping it sticks, but nothing is. iOL was soft, Falcons couldn't get anything going either direction but struggled running left the most. Ran every concept in the book, nothing worked. OTs consistently lose at POA. Was a big fan of Josiah Trotter (45) last cycle and he lit the Falcons up, bulled the iOL pic.twitter.com/TI5f3UdoQL — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 3, 2026 Xavier Watts I highlighted Watts last week as someone who’s had an underwhelming second year, but I also pointed out that I was nitpicking a bit as he hasn’t truly been “bad.” That is not the case this week; Watts was awful. Just like Penix, that was his worst performance as a Falcon. His run fits were nightmarish, constantly misreading leverage and putting himself out of position. The open-field tackling was brutal and spurred many of the explosive runs. The young safety will get a lot more chances to play the pass next week, and let’s hope that helps him get some confidence back. Nick Folk Folk is cooked, washed, etc. The 41-year-old team captain will unfortunately not be the solution to the Falcons multi-year kicking struggles. Hard to use weather as an excuse when Chase McLaughlin posts a perfect day. The Falcons have no confidence in the kicker beyond 50, and we’re starting to see them not have any within 50. Folk signed a 2-year deal , but Atlanta can cut him without any financial drawbacks at the end of the season; back to the drawing board. It’ll take a while to get the mud out of those new red jerseys. The Falcons probably won’t play in a monsoon again this year, but that doesn’t mean there wasn’t plenty to learn from this outcome. Their process coming in was flawed, and they’ve now dropped to third place. Things won’t get easier as they are set to face the explosive Bengals offense in Spain.

Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Ravens are in an increasingly precarious position. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve for thumb surgery that could end his season – and who knows when there will be any clarity on his potential return? Tyler Huntley is likely out for the year with turf toe, leaving the 4-4 Ravens to start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano for the foreseeable future. Until Wednesday, when Eric DeCosta laid the foundation to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. Once finalized, the Ravens will have a new starter who has a better chance of keeping them in playoff contention. But how much better? Can the Ravens score enough points with Brissett under center to overcome an underperforming defense? Right now, that does not seem likely, leaving DeCosta with a series of tough decisions. He has already bought a center and a quarterback, but it may not make sense to invest even more draft capital into this season. But a surprising win against the Jaguars on Thursday night could inspire him to double down and roll the dice on Jackson returning for a playoff run. (History tells us that would be an unwise bet.) DeCosta should already be considering selling at the deadline, and a defeat on Thursday may push him further in that direction. Moving veteran players could recoup crucial draft capital heading into (another) offseason roster retool. For players on expiring deals, the Ravens will have to weigh the offers they receive against the potential for compensatory picks in 2028. So how should DeCosta approach the deadline? He’s already bought a quarterback – is there room for more? Or should he stand pat and maybe even sell players with an eye on the future? full_text: Rough shape is an understatement for the situation currently facing the Baltimore Ravens. Not only is superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson headed to injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, backup Tyler Huntley is also set to miss time with a toe injury. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will make his first NFL start on Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars with Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis next in line. The Jaguars are entering Week 9 with a 5-2 record and top-10 units on both sides of the ball. Their clearest weakness is their pass defense, providing a glimmer of hope for Fagnano’s NFL debut. But outscoring a Jacksonville offense that is facing a porous Baltimore defense feels exceedingly unlikely. Accordingly, the Ravens are 9.5-point home underdogs ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ), their biggest point spread in either direction this season. This is a pattern that is likely to continue as long as the Ravens are without Jackson. Their Week 10 matchup against the currently-winless Los Angeles Chargers will be an interesting test of the market’s confidence. Under John Harbaugh, Baltimore occasionally pulled off gutsy, unlikely wins with replacement players – even a few backup quarterbacks. Jesse Minter now has a similar opportunity. Can his underperforming defense shoulder enough of the burden to mitigate the likely offensive struggles? If not, this could be yet another ugly loss for the 2026 Ravens. title: AFC North Week 8 Recap: Steelers take the lead; Ravens lose Lamar Jackson
summary: Week 8 had major ramifications for the AFC North after Lamar Jackson suffered a potentially season-ending injury. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) The Pittsburgh Steelers sit atop the division now at 6-2 after a 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns. Pittsburgh dominated Cleveland on both sides of the ball on Sunday. The offense rushed for 200 yards […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens jogs across the field in a cap prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 8 had major ramifications for the AFC North after Lamar Jackson suffered a potentially season-ending injury. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) The Pittsburgh Steelers sit atop the division now at 6-2 after a 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns. Pittsburgh dominated Cleveland on both sides of the ball on Sunday. The offense rushed for 200 yards and three touchdowns while the defense sacked Deshaun Watson eight times and recovered two fumbles. Aaron Rodgers finished the game 13 of 25 for 172 yards and an interception. Jaylen Warren’s big season continued with 143 rushing yards on 17 carries while Darnell Washington led all pass catchers with 94 yards on three catches. Patrick Queen led the defense with 12 total tackles while also racking up 1.5 sacks and a pass defense. Keeanu Benton and Daylen Everette both recovered fumbles. Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) The Cincinnati Bengals outlasted the Tennessee Titans in a 43-36 shootout to improve to 5-2. Joe Burrow’s three interceptions on the day were offset by his five touchdown passes. He finished the game 38 of 48 for 462 yards. Tee Higgins was once again Burrow’s top target, catching 10 passes for 155 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Ja’Marr Chase had a monster day as well, with 141 yards and a touchdown on 11 catches. Chase Brown led the rushing attack with 55 yards on 12 carries while also losing a fumble. The Bengals allowed Cam Ward to throw for 304 yards and two touchdowns while also giving up 158 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe each had a sack on Ward, while Lawrence and Josh Newton both recovered fumbles. Cleveland Browns (5-3) The Browns ceded the division lead with a 27-6 loss to the Steelers. Deshaun Watson was placed in the concussion protocol on Tuesday following a game in which he was sacked eight times. Watson finished the game on Sunday with 27 completions on 39 attempts for 324 yards. The ground game was a non-factor for Cleveland as the offense racked up just 34 rushing yards on 15 carries. Harold Fannin Jr.’s 154 receiving yards on 10 catches led the team. Both Watson and Fannin lost fumbles. Jared Verse has yet to record a sack since joining the Browns as part of the Myles Garrett trade. Verse’s lack of impact was especially notable on Sunday after he spent the week trash-talking Pittsburgh. Adin Huntingon recorded Cleveland’s lone sack while Carson Schwesinger led the defense with 10 total tackles. Baltimore Ravens (4-4) The Baltimore Ravens dropped their third game in a row with a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. The biggest loss of the day for the Ravens, however, was undoubtedly at quarterback, as Lamar Jackson lasted just one play in his return from an ankle injury. On the play, Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could potentially end his season. Tyler Huntley then suffered a season-ending toe injury in replacement for Jackson, leading to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finishing the game under center. The three quarterbacks combined for less than 100 passing yards, an interception, and two lost fumbles. A trade for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett has since been announced and is expected to be finalized after Baltimore’s Thursday night game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Zay Flowers was completely blanked, catching zero of his five targets. Rashod Bateman’s 22 receiving yards led the team, while Derrick Henry totaled 53 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries. The Ravens’ defense held on for as long as they could reasonably be expected to, with little help from their offense. Roquan Smith had one of the best games of his season with 11 total tackles to go with two pass deflections and a forced fumble. Nnamdi Madubuike and Mike Green split the defense’s only sack on Josh Allen.

title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to the Jacoby Brissett trade
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, adding some much-needed quarterback depth after potential season-ending injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the move, and be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta I have long been a Jacoby Brissett […]
full_text: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) takes the field before they play the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, adding some much-needed quarterback depth after potential season-ending injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the move, and be sure to add yours in the comments section below! Nikhil Mehta I have long been a Jacoby Brissett fan. Turns out, so is Eric DeCosta! This is hardly a surprising trade considering the Ravens’ injury crisis at quarterback, and Brissett is exactly the type of bridge passer I expected the team to pick up. Look, we all like Joe Fagnano, but the undrafted rookie out of UConn simply is not ready to command an NFL offense. Fans will debate if the Ravens should even be trying to win games for the rest of the season, but this franchise was never going to throw in the towel. Brissett can provide a base level of play for as long as the Ravens need it. Keeping the team’s playoff hopes alive is another question entirely. Mark Myers This trade seemed likely on Sunday night, but became nailed on as soon as Arizona announced Brissett would drop to QB3 on their depth chart. Although his season has been much worse than 2025 (when he had a 23/8 TD/INT ratio), he can push the ball down the field and feed the Ravens’ weapons better than any of the current healthy options could. Compensation may take a while to be reported, but I suspect it won’t be anything above a 5th-round pick, maybe as low as a 6th-round pick going the other way. I’m just hoping this offense is watchable. Thankfully, Brissett’s debut is set to be against the Chargers. Maybe a win against Los Angeles in primetime can give the team a spark. Zach Canter I’m not a fan of this. My guess is this move means the Ravens brass is fairly confident Lamar Jackson will return this season and they want a veteran quarterback capable of keeping them within striking distance of a playoff spot. Otherwise, this truly makes no sense. In my opinion, even if Jackson is capable of coming back this year, I still think it makes no sense. This team is riddled with issues, front and center being the offensive line. While I still think it can be a good unit if they can get the desired starting five on the field, which has happened for less than a quarter of total eight games, it’s still a question mark. The defense is still highly inconsistent. Their coaching staff seems to be young and learning as they go, which is fine and makes sense. But none of this adds up to a Super Bowl contending team. I am of the belief that the Ravens should be selling tradeable pieces at the deadline (Humphrey, Stanley, Andrews, Henry, Campbell, Washington, etc), locked 100% in on figuring out the Lamar Jackson extension, and building towards a massive roster overhaul to give Jesse Minter a team in his vision for 2027. Even if this trade is for as little as a 6th round pick, I don’t love it. If it’s for a 5th or more, I absolutely hate it and we should call DeCosta’s priorities of the future into question, as well as his job. Dustin Cox The Ravens had to make a move to get another competent quarterback in the building and Brissett perhaps made the most sense of their options. Brissett can hopefully elevate the Ravens’ offense to watchable status, but I don’t expect him to move the needle very much in terms of winning games. If Lamar Jackson is able to come back at some point this season, then Brissett can hopefully keep the team afloat and in the playoff hunt, but my expectations for the rest of the season are about as low as they can get at this moment. Acquiring an established veteran like Brissett at least sends the message to players on the team that the season isn’t being punted on entirely. Kevin McNelis Jacoby Brissett provides more veteran leadership than you would have otherwise had in this QB room, and he has enough of an arm and a deep ball that he’s serviceable. Not great, certainly not elite, but serviceable, which is more than what we can say about the unknowns of UDFA and practice squad crew that the Ravens had otherwise. The concern now would be what Baltimore gave up to get him (which hasn’t been disclosed as of this writing) and whether they can keep him upright and healthy. If this deal ends up being much ado about nothing as they move through a tough portion of their schedule, they can say they tried. From a roster-building standpoint, we may end up at Draft time grumbling about winning some games that didn’t help them move up the board, but the front office will always prioritize trying to compete if they think things can be salvaged. What should the Ravens do at the trade deadline? | Baltimore Beatdown
