title: 5 Bears Takes: A Blockbuster, a Blowout, and Trade Deadline Thoughts
summary: It may have been 10 days since the Chicago Bears last played a game. Still, the front office kept things interesting on Thursday when they executed a blockbuster deal to bring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago ahead of next week’s trade deadline. With the added momentum of a two-game winning streak and a […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks guard Quenton Nelson (53) and Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (99) meet after the game at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It may have been 10 days since the Chicago Bears last played a game. Still, the front office kept things interesting on Thursday when they executed a blockbuster deal to bring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago ahead of next week’s trade deadline. With the added momentum of a two-game winning streak and a much-needed mini-bye week in the rearview mirror, a potential preview of the NFC Championship Game happened on Monday night in Seattle. Despite playing on the road, the Bears once again showed that they are one of the best teams in the league, moving to 6-2 on the season following a 34-17 dominating win in front of the 12s. Caleb Williams became the first quarterback in eight games this season to eclipse the 200-yard passing mark against the Seahawks defense. All in all, it was a great week for this team, and they’ve got just one more game until their Week 10 bye. Going 3-0 against the Falcons, Patriots, and Seahawks is extremely impressive. Before we turn the page on the crazy week that was, let’s relive the fun and look ahead to the trade deadline in under a week. All of that and more in Week 8’s installment of 10 Bears Takes. 1. On Thursday morning, general manager Ryan Poles swung for the fences, sending a pair of first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons– more on why this signals the Bears “going for it” in 2026 and what that means moving forward. If you’re like me, you were minding your own business on a rather ordinary Thursday morning when all of a sudden, the Twitter notifications came flying in. News broke that the Bears were sending their 2027 first- and fourth-round picks, plus a 2028 first-round pick, to the Titans for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Like usual, a trade of this magnitude sent shockwaves around the league, prompting all sorts of responses from analysts. Ultimately, Poles and his front office paid a high price for Simmons, and that’s hard to debate. On the flip side, they were in desperate need of an impact defensive lineman, and that’s exactly what the 29-year-old All-Pro provides. Another factor in this trade and the price paid is that Simmons recently signed a three-year extension, which means the Titans have already paid a chunk of his contract, helping the cap hits moving forward. Here’s how each year’s cap hit looks moving forward: 2026: $7.94 million 2027: $22.55 million (all guarantees and dead money run out after this season) 2028: $30.9 million 2029: $29.1 million 2030: $33.1 million The next year and a half come cheap, especially considering his production. Although the last three years of the deal become considerably more expensive, this is where the Bears are highly likely to exercise a restructure (or two) on top of adding void years to lower his cap hit. Simply put, Simmons is one of, if not the best, interior defensive linemen in the game. His 15.5 sacks since the start of last season are the most in the NFL, and he’s top of the league in sacks, tackles, pressure percentage, and disruption EPA for a defensive tackle. In addition to his great pass-rushing numbers, he’s very good against the run and has the versatility to be used all over the defensive line. Although the defensive line is far from “fixed,” adding an elite player like Simmons should have a similar trickle-down effect as it did when they traded for Khalil Mack in 2018. He’ll make everyone better around him, and should take most of the double teams off players like Montez Sweat and Austin Booker. This is a “multiplier” move that should be felt across the defense. More importantly, this big swing signals something clear: The Bears believe they are Super Bowl contenders and are operating as such. Cap space, both now and in the future, will always be a big talking point, but given how much flexibility they have with cuts and restructures next year, they are still in good shape for the next offseason. Obviously, missing their first-round picks for the next two years takes away some of the excitement on draft day and hurts their ability to add impact players through the draft; there was little chance they could find this type of impact player with either of their next two first-rounders. This move isn’t without risk, but given how the roster was built in previous offseasons, it was also a must. Finding elite defensive line talent isn’t easy, and this move guarantees production now and in the immediate future. 2. Giving up first-round picks should never be taken lightly, but in many ways, this is the Khalil Mack trade again, with much more certainty at quarterback and on the offensive side of the ball. Without going too far into the sore subject that was the 2018-2021 Chicago Bears, the decision to “go for it” with a big trade that cost multiple first-round picks is very similar. The good news is that this time around, they have a much more established quarterback situation, and Ben Johnson appears to be the real deal. Although that reduces some of the risk in a big trade like this, the history of deals involving multiple first-round picks typically doesn’t favor the team acquiring the superstar. In theory, the Bears would have been able to find their three technique of the future eventually, but you’d have to go back to the Akiem Hicks days for that to be a reality. Instead, the team has flailed around with different coaching staffs and the same disappointing results. Some might point to trading Gervon Dexter Sr. as a mistake, and while that might be true, it’s also worth mentioning that he wasn’t the fit for what Dennis Allen wants at defensive tackle. Sure, the two players have some similar numbers on paper, but there’s a chance that Simmons has been doing this at a high level for close to half a decade. There will always be inherent risk in a move like this, but if all goes well, both first-rounders they give up will be later in the round. Thus, the variance for those picks will be much higher than it would be if they were in the Top 10. Obviously, there’s a chance something goes horribly wrong, and they end up handing the Titans a Top 10-15 pick, but that’s the risk assessment when a deal like this is made. The reality is quite simple for this team. They’ve had multiple swings at fixing the issue and failed. Finding a star defensive lineman gets harder the later they go in the first round. Simmons is a guaranteed stud, and barring injury, should continue to produce at a high level for close to the life of his contract. This does increase the pressure on Poles and his front office to draft well on Day 2, but ultimately, the pressure was already there to a certain extent. Sometimes teams have to take risks to reach their goals, and for the Bears, this was a worthy swing. In terms of cap flexibility, the team will have plenty of restructure or extension options on players during the offseason, not to mention the multiple veteran players like Jaylon Johnson, Grady Jarrett, T.J. Edwards, and one, if not both, of Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo that could be cut before the start of next offseason. We already knew the defense would need an overhaul starting in March, but adding a player like Simmons helps with the heavy lifting needed in the coming months. For now, fans can enjoy what should be a drastically improved unit, and the front office and coaching staff can use the next 10-plus games to properly evaluate the veterans listed above. 3. Even following the Simmons trade, the Bears should still be active in their search for additional defensive help– how things could look over the next week leading up to the trade deadline. So far, all reports suggest that the Bears will continue to scour the market for additional help on the…

title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Falcons
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain, this week. The Buccaneers did not complete a pass during the game, and yet still won by double digits in a […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain, this week. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 victory against the Tennessee Titans, while the Falcons lost 16-0 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers did not complete a pass during the game, and yet still won by double digits in a rain-soaked contest. Even with that loss this past week, the 3-5 Falcons are not a team to take lightly. They have victories over the Packers, Saints, and the 49ers this season. They also have one-score losses against the Steelers, Ravens, and Bears. They will be getting back their best pass rusher, James Pearce Jr., this week also. He is coming off an 8-game suspension he served for violating the NFL’s conduct policy. Orlando Brown Jr. vs. James Pearce Jr. With the aforementioned Pearce coming off of his suspension, he is listed as the starter at right outside linebacker in the Falcons’ 3-4 defense. That means he is likely to face off against Orlando Brown Jr. this week. Brown struggled at times on Sunday when faced off against the speedier pass rush of Jacob Martin. He will see a similar test with the athletic Pearce this week. Orlando Brown Jr. allowed a season-high 6 pressures versus Tennessee. He was also credited with allowing a sack. Brown will have to play much better this week against Pearce. Last season Pearce produced at an elite level for a rookie. He finished the season with 45 pressures and 10.5 sacks for the Falcons. The Bengals will need to keep Pearce and the rest of a dynamic Falcons pass rush in check this week. Jacob Martin was giving Orlando Brown Jr. trouble on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/oGzLwiQXst — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Bijan Robinson vs. The Bengals Defense Slowing down Bijan Robinson is going to take a full team effort. While it will be up to everyone to try and limit him this week, I am specifically curious to see how Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., and Jordan Battle play. Those three players have struggled with missed tackles the last couple of seasons. Robinson is one of the most dynamic and elusive running backs in the league. He can make guys look absolutely silly out in space, and that trio will have to play sound football. If they don’t, we are going to see them all over the Bijan Robinson highlight reel. Bijan already has 780 rushing yards on the season. Toss in another 203 receiving yards, and he is about to eclipse 1,000 all-purpose yards already this season. The best running back in the league rushed for over 1,400 yards last season. He also finished the year with over 800 receiving yards. A player who can absolutely put the Falcons team on his back at times. If the Bengals’ effort against the run looks like it did on the long Tony Pollard touchdown run this past week, they are going to be in for a long day in Spain. Yeah, this shit was bad pic.twitter.com/ceoXlA5RzK — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Kyle Pitts vs. TBD I have no idea what the Bengals will plan on doing this week against Kyle Pitts at tight end. While Pitts hasn’t had the career many expected, he is still a dynamic receiving threat for the Falcons. Add in the fact that the Bengals cannot stop a tight end at all again this season, and Pitts could be in for a career game this week. The Bengals allowed Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger to grab eight receptions for 112 yards this past week against the Titans. I am never really sure what their plan for guarding tight ends is on a weekly basis. Jordan Battle made a couple of plays guarding tight ends, but most of the game we were just seeing guys completely wide open down the field at the position. I put it to be determined here because I don’t know why they won’t give Tacario Davis more of a chance to guard tight ends. I think that role would be DJ Ivey, but he has been thrust into starting at corner after the injury to Jalen Davis. Good play by Jordan Battle to force a Titans punt pic.twitter.com/DtHx0n7O9h — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Regardless of who ends up being responsible for guarding Kyle Pitts this week, I am fully expecting him to put up a hugely productive game. Dexter Lawrence vs. Ryan Neuzil Neuzil and the rest of the Falcons interior offensive line will be tasked with trying to stop the unstoppable in Bengals defensive tackle Lawrence this week. Lawrence is coming off a week with 7 tackles, a sack, and a fumble recovery. Lawrence is playing at an elite level this season, and now has 24 pressures and 5 sacks through his first 7 games of the year. Neuzil has allowed just 6 total pressures and 1 sack this season for Atlanta. However, Dexter Lawrence is a completely different animal to face. Neuzil will get help from Matthew Bergeron at left guard and Chris Lindstrom at right guard on Lawrence during this game, as well. Bergeron has allowed just 8 pressures with 0 sacks this season, while Lindstrom has allowed only 6 pressures and 1 sack. That interior offensive line has held up pretty well, but the Bengals are one of the toughest matchups to date for those guys. It should be a really fun matchup throughout the day. Dexter Lawrence with another dominant performance on Sunday. Lawrence is now up to 24 pressures and 5 sacks on the season. pic.twitter.com/fT8otsKIYF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026

title: NFL ranking of top 50 trade prospects is full of potential Bengals targets
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 as they prepare for their Week 9 game in Madrid, Spain, against the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons. They’re riding a two-game win streak, though the wins were ugly at times, and are very much in the mix to make a run at the AFC North title to host a playoff game […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 as they prepare for their Week 9 game in Madrid, Spain, against the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons. They’re riding a two-game win streak, though the wins were ugly at times, and are very much in the mix to make a run at the AFC North title to host a playoff game for the first time since 2023. Things aren’t all sunshine and rainbows, though. The Bengals are dealing with some injuries, and many analysts believe they’re aggressively pursuing an acquisition to help the team make a run. Considering they already traded the No. 10 overall selection in this year’s draft to the Giants for Dexter Lawrence, a rare mid-season trade from the Bengals would likely blow the collective minds of fans across the globe. Here are some of the players the Bengals could benefit from, in order from top to bottom on the list: No. 2: Jonathan Taylor, RB Colts Taylor is one of the best running backs in the league and has been for some time. Since he was drafted in 2020, Taylor has more scrimmage yards than all RBs except for Derrick Henry. He is the type of explosive player who could change an offense. After firing GM Chris Ballard, the Colts should be considering all options, including a full tear-down and rebuild. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August. Indianapolis would take on $10 million in dead money in 2027 if it traded Taylor, so the contract is not preventive. This would have made sense a couple of weeks ago, but there are issues in the secondary that can’t be ignored. Still, the Bengals do need to figure out how to fix their running game, because they’ll need it in December and January. No. 9: Josh Downs, WR Colts Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal, and he has developed into one of the better route runners in the league. He is predominantly a slot player, aligning inside on more than 74 percent of his career offensive snaps. The Colts signed receiver Alec Pierce to a four-year, $114 million extension in the offseason. Pierce has played 49 snaps this season while battling injuries. Downs is good, cheap and on an expiring deal. He would be a potentially valuable trade piece if interim GM Ed Dodds is tasked with bolstering the draft cupboard. Do the Bengals really need a wide receiver? No. But Downs could fit in nicely. He’s a true slot receiver, and he would immediately be the Bengals’ WR3, which is a spot currently held by TE1 Mike Gesicki. With some injuries at wide receiver, including to Andrei Iosivas, and the relative inexperience of everyone else, adding another talented receiver wouldn’t hurt. No. 11: Amani Hooker, Safety Titans Though Hooker is under contract through 2028, he does not have any fully guaranteed money on his deal after this season. He is a versatile safety who can fulfill multiple responsibilities — post safety, split-field safety, nickel, dime, underneath zone and man-to-man on tight ends and slot receivers. He is a strong tackler who can impact in the running game, and he has the instincts in zone coverage to feel routes and bait quarterbacks into throws. The Titans would take on $8.6 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Hooker. How crazy would it be for Hooking to pick Joe Burrow off three times in Week 8 just to join him a couple of weeks later? The Bengals have dealt with injuries at safety. Bryan Cook has missed a couple of games, as has Kyle Dugger, and Jordan Battle has been hit or miss (mostly miss). A trade for Hooker could shore up the secondary. No. 18: Amik Robertson, CB Commanders Robertson signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the Commanders in free agency. He has been one of the few bright spots from Peters’ offseason. Robertson does not have any fully guaranteed money on his deal in 2027. The Commanders would take on $3 million in dead money in 2027 if they trade him before the deadline. Robertson is a capable man coverage corner who could help a number of teams in the secondary. He can play inside and outside. Here’s really where the Bengals need some help, especially if DJ Turner is forced to miss some time. The cornerback position was pretty much an afterthought this offseason, and now they’re potentially going to pay the piper for it. If the Bengals do make a move, I predict it will be for a corner. No. 26: Riq Woolen, CB Eagles Woolen won a Super Bowl with the Seahawks last season. He then hit free agency and, rather surprisingly, a market did not materialize for him. Woolen ended up signing a one-year deal with the Eagles. Although he has given up two touchdowns, Woolen has played well in coverage down-to-down for Philadelphia. He was in tight coverage on the Parker Washington one-handed touchdown in the Eagles’ loss to the Jaguars in Week 5. The combination of size and speed will always make Woolen an intriguing piece. Another possibility at corner. He could join Boye Mafe, whom he won a Super Bowl with in Seattle. He could fill in for a starter on the outside should the need arise. That way the Bengals wouldn’t be forced to rely on Josh Newton, who reportedly spent much of the offseason in the doghouse. No. 28: Donte Jackson, CB Chargers Jackson is in the final year of a two-year free-agent deal he signed in 2025. He has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. Jackson is one of the most compelling defensive backs on this list. He is on an expiring deal. He is relatively cheap, so he is an option for teams tight against the cap. And he is an experienced veteran who can acclimate quickly to a variety of schemes, though a zone-heavy scheme would be the best fit. Jackson has 23 career interceptions, tied for fifth-most among active players. Same thing here. The Bengals could definitely use some help in the cornerback room. Even if Turner’s heel injury allows him to play this weekend, will it limit him? He’s required to be able to stay hip to hip with some of the best athletes in the world. If his foot hurts, will he be able to? No. 40: Nahshon Wright, CB Jets The Jets signed Wright to a one-year deal in free agency, and he has yet to play a defensive snap this season for coach Aaron Glenn. Wright should be a trade candidate even if the Jets win games over the next three weeks. He had five picks playing for the Chicago Bears in 2025. Wright lacks some burst and change-of-direction ability. But his ball production last season was very impressive. At 6-foot-4, he has receiver-like skills in 50-50 situations. The Bengals were actually listed as one of the best fits for Wright, who had a good 2025 season but is struggling to get on the field this year. He could be had for little and potentially make a major impact for Al Golden’s secondary. No. 48: Tony Pollard, RB Titans Pollard, who signed with the Titans in free agency in 2024, is on an expiring contract. He has been getting the bulk of the work in the Tennessee backfield over Spears. Pollard is a veteran doubles hitter with some vision. He is reliable in pass protection. Pollard has the potential to be a supplemental piece in a running back rotation. Pollard carried the ball 21 times for 117 yards and two touchdowns against the Bengals in Week 8. He might not be as flashy as Taylor or Saquon Barkley, but he would probably help. At least more than Tahj Brooks. There were obviously others, but these were just some that caught my eye. What trade targets from the list (and not on the list) are you most interested in for the Bengals before the Nov. 10 deadline?
author: Jason Garrison

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been floated in a couple of trade rumors ahead of November 10th’s trade deadline. A team that is 5-2 with Super Bowl aspirations could be aggressive ahead of the deadline if they think there is a player or players who could put them over the top. Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Bengals are one of a few teams “aggressively pursuing” Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, although no deal to any team seems imminent. The Cincinnati offense has been lighting it up in the passing game, but the running game has left much to be desired so far in 2026. With those rumors out there, former NFL great and current CBS broadcaster J.J. Watt is urging the Bengals to make the move. “I really do believe the Cincinnati Bengals make sense for a guy like him because of what their offense has in terms of the passing game and they just haven’t been able to get going on the ground,” Watt said during an appearance on CBS’ “Set Hut” show . As the Colts have started a fire sale following the firing of General Manager Chris Ballard, Taylor is widely expected to be moved before the deadline, but the Colts appear firm on getting top-tier value for him. Aside from the Dexter Lawrence II trade this offseason, the Bengals aren’t known for trading away draft capital. With the clear urgency in the locker room, though, the Bengals could surprise us once again. Former Bengal Cris Collinsworth also believes the Bengals should make the aggressive move. “Now with the defense and Dexter Lawrence comes in and Boye Mafe comes in, and the Bengals make moves that they’ve just never made, it’s right now, it’s this year, so go do it,” Collinsworth said on the PFF NFL Show . title: Bengals News: Should Jets RB Breece Hall be trade target for Cincinnati?
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been linked through insiders to be checking in on a possible trade for running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts, but another running back may be just as good of a target. The New York Jets may be looking to see what they can get for running back Breece Hall […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been linked through insiders to be checking in on a possible trade for running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts, but another running back may be just as good of a target. The New York Jets may be looking to see what they can get for running back Breece Hall as he gets healthy from a quad injury. Jason Buechler from Sports Illustrated also brought up a good point for Hall being a decent target for teams: Hall is in the first year of a three-year contract, so this is more than a rental. Hall could slot into the Bengals’ offense and take over the backfield immediately. With the Ohio team holding all its 2027 draft picks, including an extra third-rounder, New York could push for the Bengals’ second-round pick. While it is true that Hall and Taylor both have two years left on their contracts after this season (Hall has a couple void years attached to his), Hall’s overall cap hit and age are much closer to what Cincinnati would prefer to take on. Not to mention the team could cut ties very easily before the 2028 season and save roughly $12 million in cap space, according to Over The Cap . Taylor’s deal has a similar out, but his caph hit exceeds $20 million starting next season. The other thing here to consider is the cost. A third round pick could get this pick done for a player who is still well within their prime while also costing less money. Taylor is a wonderful player, but considering the Colts would like a multiple pick return which would seemingly need to include a second round pick, it makes that a hard pill to swallow. We are of course playing in the hypothetical space where the team had to choose one. I think a vast majority of fans would agree that adding a couple of players to the back seven would do worlds more to improve this team overall than a running back. Who Dey! summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are across the pond and in Spain right now for their Week 9 international game against the Atlanta Falcons. full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are across the pond and in Spain right now for their Week 9 international game against the Atlanta Falcons . Sitting at 5-2, the Bengals are primed for a run at the division, and they don’t want to drop a winnable game before they host the Steelers in Week 10. Unfortunately for the Bengals, they’re dealing with some injuries. They didn’t actually practice on Wednesday, but they did release a projection of who would have practiced if they did. Cornerback DJ Turner (heel), safety Kyle Dugger (quadricep), and edge rusher Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) were all listed as DNP as they’re dealing with injuries suffered against the Titans. Jonathan Allen was listed as DNP, but that was for a veteran rest day. The only other name on the injury report was Jordan Battle, who would have been limited had the Bengals practiced, with a hamstring injury. The Falcons had a walkthrough on Wednesday. They had more names on the injury report, but most of the guys on the list at least had a limited role in practice. Defensive back Billy Bowman (hamstring), wide receiver Beaux Collins, defensive end James Pearce Jr. and tackle Cameron Williams all practiced in full. Linebackers Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) were limited, while wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice. The Bengals and Falcons take the field on Sunday morning (at least for those of us in the States). Hopefully they’re much healthier Sunday than they are on Wednesday. title: Bengals Film Room: Dexter Lawrence shines in a forgettable day for the defense
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals had to force overtime in order to defeat the Tennessee Titans this past week. There were plenty of bad performances on both sides of the ball, including the Titans scoring 36 points on the day. That shouldn’t take away from just how dominant Dexter Lawrence was again. Lawrence finished with 5 run […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals had to force overtime in order to defeat the Tennessee Titans this past week. There were plenty of bad performances on both sides of the ball, including the Titans scoring 36 points on the day. That shouldn’t take away from just how dominant Dexter Lawrence was again. Lawrence finished with 5 run stops on the day, the most on the team. He was a force against the run all game long. One specific play in the first half, he was able to bring the ball carrier down by just using one arm. As with most plays, he certainly had an argument for a holding call here, but it didn’t even matter ultimately. I’ll just go ahead and make the play with one arm. You are a beast Dexter Lawrence. pic.twitter.com/076d8C1wrb — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Don’t let the defense giving up 36 points take away from how good Dexter Lawrence was again yesterday pic.twitter.com/zXXOU2qhrs — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Dexter Lawrence had 7 tackles yesterday, most of them were at or behind the line of scrimmage pic.twitter.com/17oQBEJv9q — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Dexter was credited with just 2 pressures on the day, which was his lowest mark of the season. However, one of those pressures led to the sack that ultimately forced overtime. If he doesn’t make that play, the Titans were getting close to field goal range for their kicker. Lawrence consistently faced double teams, as he does on a weekly basis. When they try to block him with one guy, it is almost guaranteed to end up with the lineman being pushed back into their own quarterback. My goodness Dexy pic.twitter.com/2ewv8g9s0s — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Dexter Lawrence for Defensive Player of the Year pic.twitter.com/jAIX4lgdqD — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Demetrius Knight Jr. was credited with the safety the Bengals forced during the second half, as he should have been, but Dexter Lawrence was also right there to help make the play if he didn’t. In a game that went to overtime, every play mattered. Dexter Lawrence was certainly in his share of pivotal plays all game long. Demetrius Knight and Dexter Lawrence with the safety pic.twitter.com/AtW2cKOkyh — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 At one point during the game, it seemed like we were even going to see a big man touchdown from Lawrence. After a strip sack by Boye Mafe, Lawrence recovered the fumble. He was tripped up after the recovery, but man, it is always a sight to behold when a big man gets rumbling up the field. Boye Mafe forces the fumble and Dexter Lawrence scoops it up for the turnover. I thought we were about to see an electric touchdown rumble for a moment… pic.twitter.com/vZTUsXTZiv — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Lawrence finished the game on Sunday with 2 pressures, a sack, the fumble recovery, 5 run stops, and 7 total tackles. He has been well worth the 10th overall draft pick that the Bengals gave up to acquire him via trade this season. I think he deserves to be in the conversation for the Defensive Player of the Year. While you always hate to give up 36 points in general, that is a game the Bengals would have lost the last few years. Dexter Lawrence making critical plays in critical moments was one of the differences compared to previous years.

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals needed overtime to defeat the seemingly hapless Tennessee Titans, just a week after blowing out the Baltimore Ravens. Here’s how the experts reacted. On Tuesday, GM Andrew Berry made seven moves related to the practice squad, along with waiving RB Audric Estime on Monday, which left the […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns start practice for Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints, the roster is going to get a lot of attention, especially given QB Deshaun Watson’s concussion protocol . On Tuesday, GM Andrew Berry made seven moves related to the practice squad , along with waiving RB Audric Estime on Monday , which left the Browns with an open roster spot on both their 53-man and practice units. Wednesday morning, Cleveland filled those two open roster spots. First, the Browns signed TE Carsen Ryan back from the practice squad. Ryan, a seventh-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft , was waived to make room for QB Dillon Gabriel before returning to Cleveland’s practice squad and being elevated for Week 8’s game. Ryan has played in seven games this season, with 85 snaps on special teams and two on offense. Second, the Browns also signed RB Hassan Haskins to fill the practice squad spot. As the team noted, Haskins has bounced around the league during his career: Haskins (6-2, 228) is in his fifth season out of Michigan. Originally drafted in the fourth round by Tennessee in 2022, Haskins has appeared in 44 career games with the Titans (2022) and Chargers (2024-25). He has spent time this season on New England’s practice squad. Haskins will wear No. 27. In total, Haskins has carried the ball 76 times for 229 yards, with two touchdowns. He’s also added 18 receptions for 119 yards and one touchdown.

full_text: From a Week 8 matchup that could have put the Cleveland Browns at the top of the AFC North and in prime position for the playoffs , to a Week 9 game that could include a change at quarterback and the team as underdogs against the 2-5 New Orleans Saints . Alongside Watson, three other starters will not be practicing on Wednesday: OL Austin Barber (Calf) DT Maliek Collins (Elbow) LB Quincy Williams (Hamstring) Given Collins and Williams’ veteran status, practice is less vital. Former Browns guard Wyatt Teller dealt with calf injuries quite often, with differing timelines for his ability to play. title: Browns preparing to start Shedeur Sanders at QB against Saints
summary: Wednesday morning, breaking news emerged on the Cleveland Browns’ quarterback situation as the team placed starter Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol. The team released the following statement: During the first quarter of Sunday’s game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit. The ATC spotted called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13: (L-R) Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns and Deshaun Watson #4 take the the field for warmups prior to the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wednesday morning, breaking news emerged on the Cleveland Browns’ quarterback situation as the team placed starter Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol. The team released the following statement: During the first quarter of Sunday’s game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit. The ATC spotted called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a gameday concussion evaluation. Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns’ next offensive series. As part of the protocol, the team’s medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared. On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol. This is the hit that resulted in a roughing the passer penalty on Pittsburgh, and led to Watson being pulled from the game for a few plays while Shedeur Sanders replaced him. As mentioned in the Browns’ statement above, Watson returned on the next series and played the remainder of the game in the team’s 27-6 loss. Deshaun Watson took a hit to the helmet and is likely getting checked for a head injury. Doesn’t seem like much so hopefully he can return to the game pic.twitter.com/YdUiiEOElP — Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT (@jmthrivept) November 1, 2026 Obviously, the biggest storyline for the Browns the remainder of the week will be whether he clears the protocol or not. Last week, right tackle Tytus Howard did not practice Wednesday-Friday while in the protocol, but then magically cleared it on Saturday and started. If Watson is out, then Sanders would start his first game of the 2026 NFL season. It’s certainly a unique situation for the Browns’ quarterback situation. At the start of the season, many fans wanted Sanders to start over Watson. However, Watson has led five game-winning drives in the team’s 5-3 start to the season, which has led to more fans at least tolerating watching him. The metrics still show he’s been a below average quarterback, though, so if Sanders indeed starts, he’ll have a chance to shift the narrative again to whether he should remain the team’s starter. It probably couldn’t come at a better time, too, because the Saints’ defense is among the worst in the NFL, and the Browns then return home for a four-game stretch.

title: What did the loss to the Steelers show about this Browns team?
summary: There was a lot on the line in the Cleveland Browns Week 8 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and it unfortunately did not go Cleveland’s way. It would’ve been a huge opportunity to assert their dominance in the AFC North, but the team instead fell to 5-3. It was never really close, and the final score of 27-6 was disappointing. One of the […]
full_text: There was a lot on the line in the Cleveland Browns Week 8 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and it unfortunately did not go Cleveland’s way . It would’ve been a huge opportunity to assert their dominance in the AFC North, but the team instead fell to 5-3. It was never really close, and the final score of 27-6 was disappointing. One of the biggest factors in the matchup was the Steelers’ ability to get pressure on Deshaun Watson . Watson struggled to escape Pittsburgh’s pass rush and was sacked eight times on the day. Taking that many sacks makes it incredibly difficult to get anything going offensively. The sacks weren’t entirely Watson’s fault. The offensive line really struggled in this matchup and showed their weaknesses. As many expected, the Browns’ defense struggled to stop the run in this game, allowing 200 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. Teams will continue to exploit this part of Cleveland’s defense if they don’t improve. AFC North opponents will always bring a physical style of play, and if the Browns want a chance to win the division, they will need to match that physicality on defense. full_text: The Cleveland Browns have changed their roster up a bit after losing to the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-6 in the rubber match on the road. Their practice squad saw activity on Tuesday. RELATED: BROWNS WAIVE RB AUDRIC ESTIME The Browns waived/released WR Bub Means, P Wes Pahl, OG Vershon Lee, and OT Andrew Coker from their practice squad. In corresponding moves, they signed WR Xavier Guillory, OG Austin Blaske, and OT Xavier Truss to the practice squad. This leaves one roster spot on the practice squad. Estime will not be filling that spot, as he was claimed by Cleveland’s Week 9 opponent, the New Orleans Saints. Guillory (6’-2”, 210 pounds) went undrafted in 2025 out of Arizona State, then signed with the Baltimore Ravens and was placed on their practice squad last year and this season until he was waived on October 13. He runs a 4.58 and has never been on a main roster. Blaske (6’-5”, 310 pounds) played for North Carolina and went undrafted this year. He then signed with the Los Angeles Rams and was a last-day cut, then signed to their practice squad. Truss (6’-7”, 320 pounds) played for Georgia, where he was part of two National Championship teams and went undrafted in 2025. He spent time with the Denver Broncos, New Orleans Saints, the Browns, and the Philadelphia Eagles. He has spent time on practice squads and played in seven NFL games while with the Saints. The Eagles waived him on October 27. Truss played for Cleveland head coach Todd Monken while with Georgia.

full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are coming off their first AFC North loss of the season. Overall, the Browns went down by 1.7 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 16.0 . Considering the magnitude of their loss to the Steelers, that’s not all-too-bad of a drop. Plus, Cleveland did split the season series with Pittsburgh, which could play a big factor down the road for divisional tiebreakers. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 17 (down 3 spots) The early success went bye-bye in the loss to the Steelers. They were dominated on both sides of the ball, which is not a good look. ESPN – No. 16 (no change) Best in-season trade acquisition ever: CB Tyson Campbell in 2025 In October 2025, the Browns traded Greg Newsome II to the Jaguars for Campbell, along with a swap of late-round picks, which gave two underperforming cornerbacks a change of scenery. In a man-based scheme that fits Campbell’s skill set, he has formed one of the NFL’s better cornerback duos with Denzel Ward. Since Campbell made his debut with Cleveland in Week 6 of the 2025 season, he is tied for the 15th-most pass breakups in the NFL (15). NFL.com – No. 15 (down 3 spots) The Browns received the reality check they needed in Pittsburgh on Sunday, getting bullied by the Steelers in all-too-predictable fashion. Deshaun Watson was sacked eight times behind an unpredictable offensive line, Cleveland wasted a monster day from Harold Fannin Jr., and its most important defenders were constantly seen chasing Steelers ball-carriers in vain. At 5-3, the Browns are still in a solid place and should benefit from a serving of humble pie. Pittsburgh smashed the entire dish in their face in Week 8. Sporting News – No. 16 (down 1 spot) The Browns are starting to spring more leaks in their run defense, but the bigger problem up front is their offensive line, which gave up eight sacks on Deshaun Watson and helped to produce only 34 rushing yards in Pittsburgh. Watson is on pace to be sacked an NFL-high 70 times, which would challenge the record set by fellow former Texan David Carr. Yahoo Sports – No. 16 (no change) Biggest need: A reality check Like the Raiders, it’s fun for a team that has had almost no success to start 5-2. An uncompetitive loss to the Steelers on Sunday should put the Browns in a more realistic mindset. They can’t keep living off last-minute wins, and their poor quarterback situation makes their level of success unsustainable. The five wins have already put the Browns in a bad spot to find a quarterback solution in 2027, but that’s a conversation for next offseason. The Browns can still be partial sellers without hurting their playoff hopes for this season. Receiver Jerry Jeudy is tradable and there are plenty of teams that could use him. Offensive tackle Dawand Jones, a backup who could provide depth elsewhere, can also be available. But with a promising young core, the Browns have to be careful to not get ahead of themselves despite a 5-3 record. Bleacher Report – No. 16 (down 4 spots) Days after Jared Verse’s comments about Pittsburgh, the Browns were comprehensively outplayed by their division rivals. Cleveland got outplayed, outcoached, and out-physicaled by the Steelers on Sunday while continuing a couple of alarming trends. The Browns fell behind early, again, and they committed more penalties (nine) than any playoff hopeful should. Considering how uncompetitive the Browns have looked in blowout losses to the Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars, it’s fair to wonder if they actually are a playoff-caliber team. It would be easier to take Cleveland seriously if it had at least one convincing victory on its resume. USA Today – No. 16 (down 1 spot) DE Jared Verse got taken down Sunday, but he’s still searching for his first sack eight games into his Browns career. title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Inconsistency looms as huge obstacle
summary: It’s one thing for a football team to be inconsistent from game to game. That can make it hard to accomplish much. Being wildly inconsistent within the same game is possibly even worse. We just saw the Dallas Cowboys wrest a stunning defeat from the jaws of what looked until halftime was going to be […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images It’s one thing for a football team to be inconsistent from game to game. That can make it hard to accomplish much. Being wildly inconsistent within the same game is possibly even worse. We just saw the Dallas Cowboys wrest a stunning defeat from the jaws of what looked until halftime was going to be a pretty decent win over their nemesis, the Arizona Cardinals. They dominated things before halftime, building a 17-3 lead. The offense wasn’t exactly crisp, but a couple of takeaways and some sacks let them put points up while keeping the Cards under control. But Arizona pulled Jacoby Brissett and put Gardiner Minshew in at QB, and suddenly they were an offensive juggernaut. Dallas still managed to add 13 points to their score, but could not stop the Cards from scoring TDs on four consecutive drives. Still, thanks to a missed extra point, the Cowboys had a chance to win it in overtime, only to see their offense continue a slump that started in the fourth quarter. This inconsistency now hangs over their heads as they visit the Indianapolis Colts next Sunday. Our Sean Martin and Tom Ryle discuss the unfortunate realities of this year’s Dallas team. Tom – It’s hard to process the abject failure we witnessed at AT&T Stadium. After bottling up the Arizona offense for the most part, the Cowboys’ defense just seemed to crumble once Minshew came in. What is really mystifying is how the most damage was done by running back Tyler Allgeier. Another bevy of missed tackles and bad defensive alignments let him run free. The defense had really been the main reason Dallas built a 14-point lead at half. Then it just fell apart. Meanwhile, their offense was also displaying its own version of inconsistency. After a good showing against the admittedly depleted Philadelphia Eagles, we once again saw multiple missed opportunities. The run game went back to sleep. A rash of sacks of Dak Prescott also played a big part. We are seeing evidence that he has to have a clean pocket to make the passing game work. Once that breaks down, things go off the rails. Now the chance for the first winning streak has been blown, they are facing another ‘must win’ game. The Colts do look very beatable. The challenge is that Dallas cannot play down to the level of the competition again. Sean – Our worst nightmare has been realized, as now it requires beating the San Francisco 49ers to get back-to-back wins, and still needing until mid-November to do so. The inconsistency really makes the fan experience hard to enjoy, we have to say at this point we’ve been conditioned under Brian Schottenheimer to just expect a letdown after each and every win. And here’s the crushing thing that goes with that too – even Schotty’s wins this season aren’t impressive. There were some things to like about how the team took a workmanlike attitude out of the Eagles win, instead of getting too high like usual, but clearly this somehow didn’t help them get up off the mat once hit with adversity at home against the Cardinals. That is ridiculous. Tom – I would choose ludicrous as my description. This is a team with veteran leadership that looks rudderless. And clearly the coaching staff is doing an enormously inept job. Although I will not tabulate any fetal barnyard fowl, I do think there is a better than even chance they will beat the Colts. Maybe by a comfortable margin, or just eking out a win. But as I said, that is hardly a given. And if they do manage to avoid an even bigger disappointment against 2-6 Indy, that, as you said, still leaves the NFCW-leading 49ers to face. Given how things have gone this season, the most likely scenario is that they will get a win at the Colts, then get totally embarrassed by San Francisco. That is another home game for Dallas, and they have only managed one win this season in their own house. Trying to find things to build hope on is very hard. Sean – This game was really a wild meltdown in three parts. Early on, it didn’t feel like the Cowboys had a lot of energy, but the score held at 17-3 for a while and there was some thought that maybe this would be a win stamped by the defense , which would be a welcome sight to say the least. Then it became just trying to hold on for dear life, to the point where even a win doesn’t bode all that well for seizing any momentum. My only thought at this point was that it is the Cardinals, these games are for whatever reason never easy, and let’s just get the win in the bank. Finally, the collapse was complete, and now there really is only one way to describe this upcoming Colts game as far as I’m concerned – two bad teams going at it. The Cowboys have zero quality wins and a list of bad losses that some head coaches don’t compile in multiple seasons on the job, yet Schottenheimer has five and room to add more before Thanksgiving here in year two. Tom – I for one am so tired of wasting talented players. I don’t know if it’s bad coaching, a failure to have a better supporting cast so the talent at the top is nullified, or maybe some kind of culture issue. Maybe some of all three, and things we just can’t figure out. I am getting an uneasy feeling that we are watching yet another season go down the drain. No, it’s not just a feeling. It’s a growing sense of inevitability. At least I came into this year without great hopes, believing it was always a long shot to make the playoffs with no real chance at going far. So I’m not disappointed as much as I’m just disgusted. Sean – Likewise Tom, my concern is about trying to get something out of this season that protects what’s hopefully the best possible future for this franchise, but that feels rocky right now. Doing virtually no work on one side of the ball (offense) in the offseason won’t be an option; by the time we slog our way through this latest wasted season, the offense is going to have concerns, question marks, and need to be shaken up. It could very well have a new head coach, offensive coordinator, or both on top of all that. The best path forward for the defense is likely still to get to a second season with the same coordinator in place, but is it too much to ask for the coordinator earning that chance to not give up 33 points to the Cardinals? This organization is going to have a hard time selling a year 12 for Dak Prescott being the one they finally use to get over the hump, and we don’t even know if that will include both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens remaining together. They sure didn’t seem interested in using this duo to their advantage against the Cardinals anyway. Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams will be a year older, and they’ve needed EDGE help since the start of this season, another thing that hurt them in this latest loss. Normally, the generic answer here would just be that seeing which players continue to play hard through adversity is always something a team can build off of. Right now though, that just feels like a play into the whole “culture build” that Schotty sold us a bill of goods on, and appeasing to a coach long term that doesn’t have a long term future here as far as any of the fan base is concerned. *Gulps* We might have to continue having the conversation that the best thing for this current 2026 team is to still try and win the NFC East, which physically makes me feel gross to even say.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys news: The lack of snaps for George Pickens explained
summary: If the Cowboys are going to find themselves in any kind of position to win a bad NFC East division, their defense has got to improve. Multiple players have spoken about the state of the unit, and the solutions don’t seem to be that difficult, but they have to put it all together on the […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If the Cowboys are going to find themselves in any kind of position to win a bad NFC East division, their defense has got to improve. Multiple players have spoken about the state of the unit, and the solutions don’t seem to be that difficult, but they have to put it all together on the field. One of the big topics around Dallas lately has been wide receiver George Pickens and his playing time, or lack thereof. There’s been speculation as to why this is, but it was recently cleared up by head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Brian Schottenheimer Explains George Pickens’ Lack of Snaps, Targets in Recent Cowboys Games – Mike Moraitis, SI.com The reduction of snaps for Pickens has been very noticeable over the last few weeks. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer breaks down why that’s been the case. “Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries,” Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. “He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game.” Schottenheimer added that it “would be poor coaching by me” to keep Pickens off the field for any reason. That checks out because Pickens was added to the injury report in Week 7 due to a shoulder issue and he remained on it through last week. Cowboys defense searching for answers after meltdown loss: ‘Execute on Sunday’ – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys defense has had trouble with consistency in 2026. According to defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, the solution is quite simple. In going back and watching the film, one thing stood out to the defenders on what did not happen: execution. “The biggest thing is execute,” defensive tackle Quinnen Williams said. “We got to execute. We haven’t been executing this whole season. We executed for three quarters and didn’t execute that last quarter, and the film says it all. We have to execute and stack days.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Cowboys injury updates: Dallas secondary might be extremely shorthanded again – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Its been a tough season on the injury front for the Cowboys secondary. When they face the Indianapolis Colts this Sunday, it could be slim pickings in terms of who is available in that area. It looks like those injuries could be a factor again. The Cowboys had 11 players who didn’t practice Wednesday or were limited due to injury. That included two starting defensive backs in corner Caleb Downs and safety P.J. Locke. Both suffered concussions in Sunday’s 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Schottenheimer said both Downs and Locke were still in concussion protocol as of Wednesday. Both were seen on the field during practice participating in workouts with helmets, but not drills. Wetzel: $17 billion Cowboys have a penny-pinching owner in Jerry Jones – Dan Wetzel, ESPN Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said earlier this week that he didn’t see any correlation between how much a team spends on a head coach and winning. That could be part of the reason why Dallas hasn’t won in such a long time. Or, as a coaching agent told NFL Network’s Jane Slater when asked how aggressive Jones had been in looking for a veteran coach after the 2024 season: “Jerry won’t pay $13M and up, and that’s the starting point.” Instead, Dallas promoted Schottenheimer, its own offensive coordinator and a longtime assistant. The Cowboys were the only team to interview him that year. Schottenheimer might prove to be a good coach despite his 10-14-1 start, but should the most valuable team on the planet be led by a guy who has to grow into the job? Shemar James explains mindset of Cowboys ‘urgent’ defense – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Dallas has had another shaky season defensively so far. With that said, linebacker Shemar James says the unit is eager to get things on track. “I feel there’s a sense of urgency every week, whether we win or lose, because every week is a dogfight,” James added. “I mean, we’re in a National Football League, so there’s not going to be a week that we have circled like, ‘Oh, we’re going to beat these guys.’ “You can’t take [a game] off. Every week, we have a sense of urgency to go out there and execute, and it just didn’t get done this weekend. And that’s why we have another week to go out there and prove to people that we’re the defense that we know we can be.”
author: Matthew Lenix

title: Cowboys have a chance to respond in Indianapolis
summary: The Cowboys suffered a painful 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona, but Sunday provides an immediate chance to respond. Indianapolis is 2-6, has lost four straight games, and is coming off a 42-7 defeat against Jacksonville. The Colts also appear to be looking toward the future after trading away two of their best veteran players. So […]
full_text: Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys suffered a painful 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona, but Sunday provides an immediate chance to respond. Indianapolis is 2-6, has lost four straight games, and is coming off a 42-7 defeat against Jacksonville. The Colts also appear to be looking toward the future after trading away two of their best veteran players. So basically Indianapolis is struggling badly and haven’t won since Week 4. Their four-game losing streak includes defeats of 34-22, 26-20, 16-10 and 42-7. Sunday’s 35-point loss to Jacksonville was their heaviest defeat in nearly four years and Jacksonville led the game 28-0 by halftime. Dallas may be frustrated after Arizona, but Indianapolis enters this game with even less momentum. Daniel Jones keeps giving opponents opportunities and has thrown only five touchdowns to nine interceptions this season along with being sacked 22 times. Over his last three games alone, he has thrown five interceptions and been sacked 13 times. Indianapolis ranks last in the NFL with a minus-11 turnover differential. Dallas is at minus-one. That is particularly encouraging after the Cowboys defense created two turnovers and five sacks against Arizona. Quinnen Williams had two sacks and has now recorded at least one in three straight games. DeMarvion Overshown also forced a fumble. The Colts have also just traded away two stars so their roster is weaker than it was a week ago. They traded eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco, both moves help Dallas. Nelson’s absence removes Indianapolis’ best offensive lineman just as the Cowboys pass rush finally showed some life. Buckner’s departure removes a defender who had four sacks through seven games and had been one of the Colts’ most disruptive players for years. As proof how important those players were to the team, Indianapolis just played its first game without both against Jacksonville. Indianapolis has already allowed 23 touchdowns and 2,748 yards this season. Opponents are averaging 5.7 yards per play and 4.9 yards per rushing attempt against the Colts. That gives Brian Schottenheimer options. The way Dallas lost to Arizona was incredibly frustrating, but there were signs of improvement before the fourth-quarter collapse. The Cowboys produced five sacks and two takeaways. Shemar James recorded his first NFL interception, Overshown forced a fumble, and Williams recorded two sacks. Dallas also held Arizona to only three points in the first half and carried a 14-3 lead into halftime. The challenge is making that defensive performance last four quarters. Against a Colts offense averaging only 19 points per game and struggling badly at quarterback, Dallas has an opportunity to do exactly that. History provides another positive. The last Cowboys-Colts game went very well for Dallas where they won 54-19 in 2022, scoring an incredible 33 points in the fourth quarter. Prescott threw three touchdowns, while the Dallas defense forced five turnovers, including three interceptions. It was another example of what can happen when Dallas forces Indianapolis into mistakes. That’s particularly relevant this week with the Colts carrying the worst turnover differential in football.
author: Mike Poland

title: Latest trade deadline rumors: George Pickens likely staying in Dallas
summary: Just one year ago today, the Dallas Cowboys shocked the world by moving part of their draft capital in the Micah Parsons trade for Quinnen Williams. A year later, Williams is signed to be in Dallas long-term and be a building block for the defense moving forward. The Cowboys didn’t have the same championship expectations […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just one year ago today, the Dallas Cowboys shocked the world by moving part of their draft capital in the Micah Parsons trade for Quinnen Williams. A year later, Williams is signed to be in Dallas long-term and be a building block for the defense moving forward. The Cowboys didn’t have the same championship expectations a year ago as they did entering 2026, and have severely disappointed with a 3-5 record through eight games. Could the Cowboys be buyers looking to capture whatever potential they have left to make the postseason, or could they deal a couple of players to restock on draft capital? Here is the latest buzz around the Cowboys with the deadline approaching next week: George Pickens should remain a Cowboy for 2026 Notice the wording of the headline. The expectation is that George Pickens will stay in Dallas for the rest of 2026. Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano of ESPN both get the sense that keeping Pickens in-house this year is something both parties want . Graziano: Staying in the NFC East, teams are wondering if the Cowboys would consider trading WR George Pickens if they suffer another loss this week and fall to 3-6. I do not get the sense that Dallas would consider such a move, but if it isn’t planning to sign Pickens to an extension next offseason, it would make sense to at least take the call. … Fowler: As Dan mentioned, Pickens’ name has circulated as a potential trade target in recent weeks as a result of Dallas’ 3-5 record, his 2027 free agency and the difficulty of keeping two high-profile receivers on the books. Pickens had four targets in Sunday’s loss to Arizona, fewer than backup tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford . But I’ve also been told Pickens remains content in Dallas and doesn’t want to be moved, nor does Dallas plan to trade him. Pickens, despite a decrease in production from a year ago (39-533-2 through eight games), still draws heavy coverage as a vertical threat and should eventually be in line for a deal in the Zay Flowers or Drake London range (around $35 million per year). The Cowboys have the star power to be a top-five offense in the NFL. They’ve fallen hard over the last few weeks, shifting between a run-first offense and a pass-first offense. On Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, Pickens’ involvement hit a new low when tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford had more targets than he did. So where do things stand for 2027? That remains to be seen, but the Cowboys have a big decision to make between two former Pittsburgh Steelers. No, not Broderick Jones, although it would be very Cowboys-like to sign him to an extension first. It’s between Joey Porter Jr. and Pickens. The feeling is that Dallas could apply the franchise tag on the wide receiver and then trade him before the draft. That’s a long way from the front office doing that, but for now, expect Pickens to see this year out with the Cowboys, hoping he can help them turn the corner to the playoffs in 2026. Surprise trade candidate for Dallas? The Cowboys still believe they have the pieces to be a playoff contender, and Jerry Jones was adamant in his Tuesday interview on 105.3 The Fan show, Shan & RJ, that he is not looking to be a seller at the trade deadline . So, could Dallas deal any of their players, and would anyone draw interest from other teams? Jeremy Fowler of ESPN mentioned one name that could be a trade candidate for Dallas—tight end Luke Schoonmaker. Yes, you read that correctly. There is some logic to Schoonmaker being a name to watch. The NFL is big on 13 personnel right now, where blocking tight ends are all the rage. Fowler mentions that teams are hunting for blocking tight ends. The Los Angeles Rams come to mind as a team that could be interested, considering they had to put Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. Schoonmaker has fallen to No. 3 on the tight end depth chart and is still a young player on an expiring contract. All benchmarks teams look for at this point in the year. That could net a very late-round draft pick for someone to take a flyer on a rental for a half season. He could still have some fans out there who liked him coming out of Michigan. The likelihood of it happening could be low, but as Fowler mentions, “I just don’t see Dallas moving key players at this point.”
author: Brandon_Loree

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Arizona loss, Cowboys defense, head coaching
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  Who deserves the majority of the blame for the collapse against Arizona? Mike – Brian Schottenheimer, and for me, it’s not even […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. Who deserves the majority of the blame for the collapse against Arizona? Mike – Brian Schottenheimer, and for me, it’s not even a debate. Christian Parker’s defense deserves criticism for the collapse, but Schottenheimer’s play-calling, poor game management and complete inability to close out games are becoming impossible to defend. What makes it worse is the complete lack of logic behind his rushing decisions. Dallas had been averaging 5.6 yards per carry running left compared with just 2.0 yards running right, yet on Javonte Williams’ 24 carries, only eight went to the left. How do you identify such an obvious advantage and then fail to exploit it? The frustrating part is that Denver had already handed Dallas a blueprint just one week earlier. Sean Payton exploited Arizona’s aggressive defense with a beautifully designed screen pass to the left (yes to the left), allowing RJ Harvey to race 52 yards for a touchdown. That was a perfect example of using creativity to get a running back into space. Schottenheimer had that evidence staring him in the face, yet showed little of the same imagination. For me, Schottenheimer’s biggest weakness is his conservatism when Dallas gets ahead. Instead of attacking opponents and putting games beyond reach, he becomes predictable, cautious and far too concerned with protecting a lead. Jorge – The person really at fault is Jerry Jones. He’s run this franchise somewhat like a despot running a small island nation with precious resources. Subsequently, a festering culture of losing has smoldered for decades, and losses like Sunday are commonplace, frankly. Even so, Schottenheimer is the guy with the headset on that players ultimately call coach, and his tenure in Dallas has been poor. It’s hard being a coach in Dallas given the circumstances with the Joneses, but man, just look at everybody that leaves this place once they land on stable ground. Sunday’s game was just another example of two wrongs not making a right with the dull duo of JJ and Schotty. Sean – Not to sound like a broken record, but we all might end up doing so thanks to not being able to look away from the obvious, but this one is on Schottenheimer to me. We went from Mike McCarthy is the right hire because he wants to work with Dak Prescott, and at the time Kellen Moore, to McCarthy gets to bring in his own OC and that being Schottenheimer, to Schotty is the man in charge and now can’t figure out how to get a first down with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens. Hell, the head man can’t even figure out how to get all three of these players on the field at the same time in this latest loss. It’s horror show stuff. Schottenheimer got the ultimate do-over card in year one when we all accepted the Eberflus defense was bad enough to not be able to fairly evaluate anything else, just to be as bad at calling an offense as Eberflus was at calling a defense in year two with the same personnel. Horror. Show. Tom – Not much to add, although I would add that the culture seems to be a real issue. This team just seems to have no real fight in it, and certainly does not seem to be working together. Now we have the Cowboys being treated as a laughingstock after blowing that game, and that is not going to help the morale. Maybe that falls back on the head coach, but you’d hope that some of the players would be trying to do something themselves to change the attitude. Dyllan – Players need to play. Coaches need to coach. Neither party involved did much of either in the second half. Coach Schottenheimer’s game management has proven to be abysmal this season, rearing its ugly head once again against Arizona. Players began missing tackles and committing drive-continuing penalties. Everything went from near perfect in the first half to a cataclysmic nightmare in the second. When that happens, the blame falls at the feet of every person involved. Tyler Allgeier finished with 147 rushing yards. Is the problem poor tackling, blown assignments, or simply a lack of physicality from Dallas? Mike – It’s all three, but for me, the biggest problem is poor defensive discipline and a complete lack of physicality. Players were losing their assignments, failing to maintain gap discipline, taking poor angles, and missing tackles. But what frustrates me most is how easily Arizona bullied Dallas at the line of scrimmage. There was no aggression, no accountability and very little resistance once Allgeier reached the second level. When it’s all three you have to look at Christian Parker to take responsibility for all this, and he’s sitting firmly on the hot seat already. Jorge – All of the above. Tackling has been an issue all year, and the lack of physicality has been a staple of the Dallas Cowboys defense even when they were recently good. Both go hand in hand; the same goes for the assignments. Christian Parker is failing as a DC, and the same issues have bubbled up all year. When you mix all three shortcomings into defensive performance, you get exactly what you saw on Sunday. The fact that the Cowboys defense isn’t okay at any of these three things is an indictment of Parker. Sean – I would include being out of position within the poor tackling category if I had to choose one of your buckets here, so tackling for me. Guys are expecting the first line of defense to make plays that they aren’t, which leads to the second level missing tackles, and then the third. There’s no swarming to the ball or visible effort to care about getting the guy with the ball on the ground before at least a positive gain every time. Tom – I heard someone during the SNF postgame talk about how none of the units on defense were really unified. They just seem to be playing the game in isolation, with no teamwork. The three levels of the defense have to support one another, and that is just not happening. Dyllan – Pre-snap alignment hurt them at times. Throwing shoulders instead of wrapping up occurred more than once. It looked like nobody wanted to take the bull by the horns in the second half and say, “enough is enough.” It’s troubling to see that against what’s supposed to be an inferior team. What does Brian Schottenheimer need to change about his late-game managemen t to be trusted to close out games when the Cowboys are ahead? Mike – Right now, I simply don’t trust Brian Schottenheimer to close out games when Dallas has a lead. He needs to understand that protecting a lead doesn’t mean abandoning what made the offense successful. Keep attacking defensive weaknesses and trust your playmakers. His clock management and play selection all need serious improvement. Good coaches know when to be aggressive and when to manage a game. Schottenheimer currently seems to confuse managing a lead with playing not to lose. Jorge – I hate to sound cliché, but he needs to coach to win the dang game. Too often he coaches not to lose, only to lose in the most enfeebling ways possible. Trust your playmakers, cut them loose, put your line in a position to succeed, give the defense different looks. He gets really cute with his play calls, overthinks the hell out of everything and worst of all, just shows no urgency whatsoever. He is the worst possible coach for this team with the DNA it has; he’s way too laid back, and it shows. Constantly taking opportunities, moments and plays for granted, I don’t think I’ve ever seen a coach so disinterested in winning and trying to get better. With that said, he has to give up playcalling, and he absolutely cannot be trusted to close out games. Sean – Again, like we’ve basically been saying for two years now, get the ball to your best players. Not to be a prisoner of the…
author: Mike Poland

title: Brian Schottenheimer report card: Out-coached again in another loss
summary: Do you remember when you were a kid and your parents always hounded you about how much better of a student you would be if you just applied yourself? No… just me? Well, for what feels like the 100th time this season, Brian Schottenheimer brought home a failing report card to his disappointed parents, and […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Do you remember when you were a kid and your parents always hounded you about how much better of a student you would be if you just applied yourself? No… just me? Well, for what feels like the 100th time this season, Brian Schottenheimer brought home a failing report card to his disappointed parents, and his lack of ability to properly understand how to attack his opponent based on tape is very concerning. Even after putting up 30 points in the Cowboys 33-30 loss, Schottenheimer (along with Christian Parker) was the clear problem for the Cowboys. Whether it’s failed challenges, ultra-conservativeness, questionable fourth-down play calls, extreme lack of creativity, or the stubbornness to establish the run, the Cowboys offense is consistently put on hard-mode week in-and-week out. The first half was filled with inefficient runs, setting the Cowboys up behind the chains and trying to convert on third-and-longs way too much. After torching the Philadelphia Eagles on the ground in week seven, the Cowboys were dedicated to replicating their running game success against the Cardinals, and they finished the game with 39 carriers for 93 yards (2.4 yards per carry). With the running game hurting them a ton in this game, the Cowboys relied on Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and Ryan Flournoy to carry the load. The only problem was the passing concepts looked eerily similar to how it did in Weeks 1-6. Very little motion, few bunch sets, and basic, static route concepts that make things extremely difficult for anyone to create separation in the passing game. With the run game setting them back, and the lack of modern day passing concepts making things very easy to defend, the Cowboys found themselves stalling out in the second half and blowing a two-possession lead with just four minutes to go in the game. The main concern with Schottenheimer (outside of everything else we’ve already touched on) is his inability to close games out as a play-caller. For his entire tenure at the head coach and play-caller for the Cowboys, Schottenheimer has called the game was too passive. His inability to understand how poor his defense has been for a year-and-a-half now has cost this football team wins. For a coach who has a $60-million dollar quarterback, two highly paid wide receivers, and an offensive line loaded with highly paid players and first-round picks, Schottenheimer puts more faith in his defense and special teams than he does his talented and highly-paid offense. The end of the first half field goal attempt was the first of many signs of this throughout the game. With 11-seconds left in the first half and a timeout in his back pocket, Schottenheimer elected to run the football for a minimal gain and send out Brandon Aubrey for a 61-yard field goal attempt. Aubrey, who has struggled mightily with the longer field goal attempts so far this season, missed the field goal, and the Cowboys carried a 14-3 game into half. Why not try to gain 10-15 yards with a timeout in your back pocket and the entire field at your disposal? The next drive that had a heavy weight on his grade was the Cowboys second to last drive in the fourth quarter. With the ball on the Cardinals 20-yard line up three points, the Cowboys ran Javonte Williams up the middle for no gain to get the Cardinals to burn their last time out, which was the right call. The next play call perfectly encases all of Schottenheimer’s warts as a play-caller. With the two-minute warning looming, the Cowboys were in a perfect position to go for the jugular. Instead, with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens standing on the sideline, Schottenheimer dialed up a slow developing play-action pass with everyone on the field and in the stadium knowing the Cowboys should and would be passing. The result? An L.J. Collier sack losing six yards. On 3rd-and-16, Schottenheimer did what he often does in less than ideal down and distances, runs Williams straight into a brickwall for a minimal gain. Brandon Aubrey came on to give the Cowboys a six-point lead with a minute to go and no timeouts for the Cardinals. In most instances, that’s enough to win the football game, but the Cowboys defense had other plans, as they often have in 2026. The decision to run play-action with Lamb and Pickens on the sideline, with a chance to ice the game was absolutely mind-boggling. Schottenheimer commented on his choice of personnel, pointing to a similar package earlier in the game on the Ryan Flournoy touchdown pass in the second quarter. I would certainly hope Schottenheimer understands the difference between a 3rd-and-1 in the first quarter of a 7-0 game and potentially the last play from scrimmage when the defense is forced to play aggressive to create negative plays from the offense, but who really knows right now. Play-Calling F Fourth-Down Decisions C I loved Schottenheimer’s decision to go for the fourth down on the opening drive of the game, but absolutely hated the play call and formation that got stuffed. Timeout Usage F Team Preparation F It was all pretty ugly, yet again. What grade would you give to Brian Schottenheimer on Sunday?
