title: Cowboys Week 9 opponent: A look at the 2026 Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Dallas Cowboys head to Indianapolis for a Week 9 matchup against a franchise, not unlike the Cowboys, that appears to be falling apart in real time. The Colts enter Sunday’s game at 2-6, riding a four-game losing streak after getting embarrassed 42-7 by the Jacksonville Jaguars. But the losing record is only part of […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys head to Indianapolis for a Week 9 matchup against a franchise, not unlike the Cowboys, that appears to be falling apart in real time. The Colts enter Sunday’s game at 2-6, riding a four-game losing streak after getting embarrassed 42-7 by the Jacksonville Jaguars. But the losing record is only part of the story. Indianapolis has already fired general manager Chris Ballard, traded away two of its biggest stars and opened the door to moving more players before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That could make the Colts a very different team by the time Dallas takes the field. Jonathan Taylor is drawing serious trade interest, wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, and quarterback Daniel Jones is coming off another miserable performance. For Dallas, this is a chance to take advantage of a team facing significant uncertainty. But the Cowboys are 3-5 themselves, and after blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead against Arizona, they can’t afford to overlook anyone. Daniel Jones is struggling, but Indianapolis is sticking with him The biggest question surrounding Indianapolis is what to do at quarterback. Daniel Jones was pulled during Sunday’s blowout loss to Jacksonville after throwing two interceptions, and the conversation immediately shifted to whether Anthony Richardson would get another opportunity to start. Steichen answered that question Monday, confirming that Jones will remain the starting quarterback for Week 9 against Dallas. Richardson entered the Jacksonville game late and completed both of his pass attempts for eight yards, but the coaching staff apparently believes Jones still gives the Colts their best chance to win. That is becoming a difficult argument to make. Through eight games, Jones has completed 162 of 268 passes for 1,542 yards, five touchdowns and nine interceptions. He has also been sacked 22 times and has a 68.7 passer rating. His 60.4% completion rate is a career low, and his five passing touchdowns are not a good sign for an offense that entered the season expecting to compete. Against Jacksonville, Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions before being replaced. The Colts managed just seven points, turned the ball over three times and never looked capable of making the game competitive. The offensive line has not helped. Indianapolis has allowed 22 sacks in eight games, and Quenton Nelson’s departure makes an already difficult situation even more complicated. Jones will work behind a reshuffled offensive line against a Dallas defense that desperately needs to generate pressure. Jonathan Taylor could be playing his final game in Indianapolis The biggest trade storyline in Indianapolis centers on running back Jonathan Taylor. One of the league’s most productive running backs is suddenly available, and the Colts are reportedly engaged in active discussions with multiple teams ahead of the trade deadline. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Colts are open to moving Taylor, with the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks among the teams that have shown interest. Taylor has been one of the few consistent bright spots for Indianapolis this season. Through eight games, he has rushed for 610 yards and eight touchdowns on 148 carries, averaging 4.1 yards per attempt. He has also added 21 receptions for 202 yards, giving him 812 yards from scrimmage. Most rush TD this season Josh Allen 9 Jonathan Taylor 8 Javonte Williams 8 Christian McCaffrey 8 3 players tied 7 pic.twitter.com/8LyyxYTY5f — PFF (@PFF) November 1, 2026 The numbers are impressive, especially considering how much the offense has struggled around him. Taylor entered Week 8 among the league leaders in rushing touchdowns and has been one of the Colts’ most dependable offensive weapons. However, his performance against Jacksonville reminded everyone that even an elite running back cannot carry an entire team. Taylor managed just 23 rushing yards on eight carries and added 24 receiving yards. He also fumbled during the blowout. Taylor has acknowledged the trade speculation but has not requested a move. He recently said he remains proud to wear the Colts uniform and is focused on controlling what he can control. Still, the organization has already shown that it is willing to move established players as it reshapes the roster. There is a legitimate argument for keeping Taylor as a centerpiece of the rebuild, particularly after signing him to a two-year, $44 million extension in August. But with Indianapolis sitting at 2-6 and already moving important veterans, a trade would not be surprising. Josh Downs wants out, and the Colts’ receiving corps is changing Taylor is not the only offensive player whose future in Indianapolis is uncertain. Wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, adding another layer to the Colts’ ongoing roster shake-up. Downs has been one of the team’s most productive receivers this season, leading Indianapolis with 30 receptions for 330 yards and one touchdown through eight games. He has become an important target for Jones, particularly in the short and intermediate passing game. Josh Downs is wide open ‼️ 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/w2M7uc1aW6 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 1, 2026 His request came after Indianapolis traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, two established leaders who were central to the team’s identity. Downs is entering the final year of his rookie contract, and with the Colts seemingly shifting toward the future, he could be another player moved before the deadline. Downs isn’t the only receiving option Dallas needs to consider. Veteran Keenan Allen has recorded 36 receptions for 325 yards and a touchdown, while second-year tight end Tyler Warren has added 34 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns. If Downs is still in the lineup Sunday, he will be an important underneath target for Jones. If he is traded, Indianapolis will have to rely even more heavily on Allen and Warren to provide consistency in the passing game. The Cowboys’ secondary remains one of the team’s biggest weaknesses, so even a struggling Indianapolis offense could find opportunities if Dallas allows receivers to work freely underneath as they have all year. The Colts’ defense has its own problems after trading DeForest Buckner The Colts’ defensive situation has changed dramatically following the trade of DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Buckner was one of the team’s most important defensive players, and his departure leaves a significant hole along the defensive line. Indianapolis has recorded 16 sacks and two interceptions through eight games, while opponents have accumulated 2,748 total yards. Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore and Buckner tied for the team lead with four sacks each before the trade, while edge rusher Laiatu Latu has two. Without Buckner, the Colts will need other players to take on larger responsibilities along the defensive front. That is a difficult adjustment for a team already struggling to stop opposing offenses. The Colts have allowed 1,054 rushing yards through eight games, averaging nearly 132 yards per contest. That ranks among the league’s weaker run defenses, and Buckner’s departure could make the challenge even greater, with Indianapolis also struggling to create turnovers this season. Indianapolis is in free fall, but Dallas cannot afford another letdown The Colts have lost four consecutive games with defeats to Pittsburgh, Tennessee, Minnesota and Jacksonville. Their latest loss was ugly: a 42-7 defeat in which Jacksonville averaged nearly seven yards per play, and Indianapolis struggled to produce anything offensively. The numbers paint a bleak picture. Indianapolis has scored just 15 offensive touchdowns through eight games, committed nine interceptions and has a minus-11 turnover ratio. The team has also allowed 2,748 yards while producing only 2,329 of its own. The…

title: Cowboys news: Jerry Jones likes the direction of his defense
summary: Before halftime, the Dallas Cowboys led the Arizona Cardinals 14-3, and Christian Parker’s defense played lights-out. Through it all, Jerry Jones said he still believes in his defense and sees the […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Before halftime, the Dallas Cowboys led the Arizona Cardinals 14-3, and Christian Parker’s defense played lights-out. Something changed in the second half, and the defense gave up four straight touchdown drives to end regulation, and the Cowboys lost in overtime. Through it all, Jerry Jones said he still believes in his defense and sees the unit trending in the right direction. Jerry Jones on Cowboys’ defense: ‘I like the way we’re trending’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys owner and general manager still believes in Christian Parker. “We’ve been changing,” Jones said. “We’ve changed out on our defense, we’ve changed out our coaching staff, complete coaching staff. We’ve changed out the majority of the players, really. And in today’s building of a team, you do it with a combination of draft, which draft picks have to have a little seasoning most of the time.” “And therein lies the inconsistency that we’re seeing, even within a game where we played so well in the first half and came back and didn’t play as well in the second half. That is a disappointment, but not a surprise… It does not call for massive, or not massive, it does not call for very succinct, important changes because I like the way we’re trending.” The Cowboys’ defense is turning 30-point games into losses. And jeopardizing jobs – Mac Engel, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Will the Cowboys’ continued disappointment cause a shake-up in the coaching staff at the end of the season? Jerry will not fire Schottenheimer during this season, but after it feels plausible. Schottenheimer is in the second year of a four-year contract, and while Jerry hates the idea of paying a coach to not coach, he will not want another year of what he’s currently watching. The problem remains the same as it has been for years. The defense under first-year, first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker continues to play at a level that is no longer bewildering but a state that will get people fired, most notably himself. Cowboys’ Brandon Aubrey problem is affecting them in more ways than one – Levi Dombro, The Landry Hat Brandon Aubrey hasn’t been the same clutch long-distance kicker this season. Although Aubrey’s kickoffs are undeniably the best in the league, which give Dallas better field position than any other team in the NFL, his field goals have been an issue. George Pickens Could Force the Cowboys to Trade Him – Michael Gallagher, Heavy on Cowboys The Cowboys would net some quality draft capital if they moved on from George Pickens. Pickens is playing on the one-year franchise tag ($27.3 million), and a second tag next offseason would cost Dallas about $32.8 million. That’s a problem. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is also playing without an extension and wants upward of $30 million per year — and the Cowboys only get one tag. An extension won’t be cheap either. Solak estimates Pickens would command north of $33 million per year, worryingly close to the $34 million CeeDee Lamb makes. Former Cowboys tight end Jason Witten was named the offensive coordinator and play caller for the remainder of the 2026 season by the University of Oklahoma. Witten was hired as the Sooners’ tight ends coach at the start of the year for his first collegiate coaching job, and now takes over the offense after Oklahoma’s decision to dismiss offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle.

title: How the Denver Broncos can beat the Carolina Panthers
summary: The Denver Broncos sit atop the AFC West with a 6-2 record. On Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina Panthers who are 3-4 and in first place of the NFC South for their Week 9 matchup. Denver has momentum entering the game being winners of four in a row, whilst Carolina has dropped back-to-back […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos sit atop the AFC West with a 6-2 record. On Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina Panthers who are 3-4 and in first place of the NFC South for their Week 9 matchup. Denver has momentum entering the game being winners of four in a row, whilst Carolina has dropped back-to-back games. Here are three ways I think the Broncos can earn their seventh victory of the season. Ride the running attack and give Jonah Coleman more opportunities Last season, Denver had an effective running game in the first half of the season. Unfortunately, it tapered off greatly after J.K. Dobbins was injured. This year, Denver has experienced the opposite. It’s been a relatively slow start for them establishing the run, but injuries have played a part in that this year too. While Denver’s current stable of backs isn’t completely 100-percent health-wise, I think there is a huge opportunity here to revitalize their run game on Sunday. Why? Because the Panthers have one of the worst run defenses in the National Football League. It’s clearly a giant weakness for the Carolina. They are allowing nearly 5 yards per carry. Moreover, they’ve been dreadful in four of seven games with respect to rushing yards. They gave up 291 on the ground to the Chicago Bears, 258 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 157 to the Atlanta Falcons, and 132 to the Cleveland Browns. I’d love to see a healthy dose of Jonah Coleman in this game. The rookie running back has looked good in his limited opportunities and deserves a majority of the carriers moving forward. It’s a road game, so dictating the pace of it will be essential, and enforcing a consistent rushing attack is key to that. Whether or not the Broncos will be buyers at the trade deadline remains to be seen. However, the more opportunities Coleman gets, the easier the evaluation process for him as a player gets. And in turn, would help answer whether or not the franchise needs to trade off quality draft capital to add to the room prior to November 10th. Rev up the pass rush and rattle Bryce Young Believe it or not, the Panthers enter Sunday’s matchup as a Top 10 offense in the National Football League. Quarterback Bryce Young has played a big part in that. He has thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and has just 5 interceptions thus far in his fourth season leading their offense. Young sported a few hot games to start the season. However, he has struggled recently. The former top-pick has 3 interceptions and just 2 touchdowns in their back-to-back losses. His accuracy has also experienced a big drop-off—completing less than 57-percent of passes the past three games. In 2025, Young was one of the least sacked quarterbacks in the NFL with just 27. In seven games, he has already been sacked 23 times. The crazy part? Eleven of those have come in the past two games alone. Knowing that, this seems like a prime week for Denver’s defensive trenches to rev up the pass rush. If they can rattle and get after Young early and often, they’ll have a great shot at winning. The Broncos have to start converting on third down The Broncos are a 6-2 football team despite struggling in many key areas. One major issue for them since Week 1 has been their inability to convert on third down. The Broncos are now dead last in the NFL with under a 30-percent conversion rate. It’s true Denver has faced some really good defenses. However, that isn’t an excuse for their poor play in this regard. This is arguably the biggest area the Broncos have to improve upon as they gear up for Sunday’s matchup—as well as the second half stretch of the season after their bye week. The Panthers have a bottom 5 third down defense in the NFL. Opposing teams are converting 46-percent of third downs against them each week. Head Coach Sean Payton, quarterback Bo Nix, and the rest of the offense need to find a way to sustain drives and move the field on third down. Last season, Courtland Sutton was the go-to guy if Denver needed to move the chains. Perhaps this weekend the Broncos make the savvy veteran their main target in the passing attack when they need a big play. He has been clutch through his career in that aspect. If not, who on offense can step up and be that player?

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Panthers and the rest of Week 9
summary: Welcome back to the ninth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. My Week 8 slate of predictions was my best thus far. I finished with a 12-2 record with my only losing picks being the Cowboys and Seahawks. Not too shabby! We’re basically at the halfway point of the season, so […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the ninth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. My Week 8 slate of predictions was my best thus far. I finished with a 12-2 record with my only losing picks being the Cowboys and Seahawks. Not too shabby! We’re basically at the halfway point of the season, so I thought I’d give a review of where I stand to date. Week 1: 11-5 Week 2: 10-6 Week 3: 9-7 Week 4: 8-8 Week 5: 10-5 Week 6: 7-7 Week 7: 9-5 Week 8: 12-2 Thus far, that’s 76 correct picks and 46 wrong picks. That’s good enough for 63-percent accuracy. However, that is still several points behind where I have been the past two seasons. This week there are 15 games with just the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans on their bye week. Jacksonville Jaguars at Baltimore Ravens — Thursday Night Football With Lamar Jackson likely out for the rest of the regular season due to a broken thumb and Tyler Huntley being on injured reserve, the Ravens will be starting Joe Fagnano against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football . However, they did strike a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals to keep their playoff hopes alive. That won’t matter this week, since he won’t be playing. Due to an unstable quarterback situation in Baltimore, I’ll be giving Jacksonville the edge here. Winner: Jaguars Cincinnati Bengals at Atlanta Falcons — Sunday (Morning Game) This will be an international affair taking place in Madrid, Spain. The Bengals are coming off an overtime win against the Titans. Meanwhile, the Falcons were shutout by the Buccaneers in a game where Tampa Bay didn’t even complete a pass to win. All things considered, I’ll be taking Cincinnati in this one. I think they will light up the scoreboard. Winner: Bengals Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints — Sunday (Early Game) The Browns are coming off a loss, and the Saints are fresh off their bye week with an extra week of rest and preparation. The key storyline to watch in this one is who starts at quarterback for Cleveland. Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol, which mean Shadeur Sanders could get the nod on Sunday. If so, I’m worried about Cleveland’s ability to get things done on offense. I’ll be taking the Saints at home in this one due to that. Winner: Saints New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs — Sunday (Early Game) Both of these teams are coming off Week 8 losses. I’m far more confident in Andy Reid and the Chiefs’ ability to bounce back from a loss at home as opposed to the Jets being able to find a way to win at Arrowhead. Sorry Jets fans, but I’m picking Kansas City in this one. But hey, you have three top ten picks currently in the 2027 NFL Draft. That’s something to look forward too—unless most of the top underclassmen at QB opt to go back to school. Winner: Chiefs Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders — Sunday (Early Game) Both these NFC teams earned wins in Week 8. The Rams have now pulled to 4-4 on the season and aren’t out of it yet. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 2-4-1 and a few games out of the lead in the NFC East. At the end of the day, I think the Rams are the much better team and will find a way to win on the road. It’s an absolute must to keep their playoff hopes alive in a tough NFC. Winner: Rams Dallas Cowboys at Indianapolis Colts — Sunday (Early Game) The Cowboys and Colts have certainly underwhelmed thus far. Both teams have failed to meet the expectations many fans and analysts had prior to the regular season. If Dallas wants to keep their playoff hopes and NFC East title chances alive, this is a must-win road game against the Colts who seem determined to acquire as much draft capital as possible to embark on a complete rebuild. I’ll be taking another road team and am picking Dallas. Winner: Cowboys Detroit Lions at Miami Dolphins — Sunday (Early Game) Each week, there seems to be a game I think is a surefire win that winds up backfiring on me. Looking at this week’s slate of games, this is about as close to an easy pick for a matchup I can find. I think the Lions roll on offense and cause a lot of problems for a Dolphins’ defense that is one of the worst in the NFL. Winner: Lions Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers — Sunday (Early Game) They haven’t been playing their best football, but the Broncos continue to find ways to win. They have a four-game winning streak and all the momentum heading into their Week 9 road matchup versus the Panthers. I think Denver’s offense will run the ball with authority and dictate the pace of the game to earn their seventh win of the season on Sunday. Winner: Broncos New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles — Sunday (Early Game) The Eagles have been an absolute flop this season and have lost six in a row. Meanwhile, the Giants have been one of the league’s surprise teams and lead the NFC East. It hasn’t always been pretty, but they’ve been finding ways to win and are pretty balanced on offense and defense. I’m getting a bit wild here picking road teams, but I like the Giants in this one. Winner: Giants Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Texans are a bad football team at 2-5. There is no doubt they have woefully underperformed expectations. Quite honestly, the only other team in AFC that has been more disappointing are the winless Chargers at 0-7. I expect the Texans to get back on track here and take care of business on the road since the Chargers are terrible. Winners: Texans Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Raiders are back to being a .500 ball cup. On the flip side, the 49ers had an extra week of preparation after their Week 7 loss to the Falcons to gameplan for the Raiders. I think that is going to make all the difference here. I just don’t see them dropping another game to an underdog. I’ll take Kyle Shanahan’s crew. Winner: 49ers Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This is one of my favorite matchups of Week 9. The Packers and Patriots are both 5-3 and coming off Week 8 victories. I feel they are evenly matched. It could definitely go either way, though I’ll be giving the Patriots the nod here because of their homefield advantage. Winner: Patriots Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Cardinals were able to shock the Cowboys last weekend. I honestly didn’t see that coming. Meanwhile, the Seahawks lost to the Bears in primetime—the other matchup I failed to get right last week. At 4-4, the Seahawks are starting to slip in the NFC West. They need this victory to get back on the right track. I’m confident they will pull out a victory at home. But Sam Darnold needs to perform better, and they have to start running the ball effectively. Winner: Seahawks Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears — Sunday Night Football The Buccaneers may have been able to pull off a win last weekend without completing a pass. However, they are going to have to be firing on all cylinders to keep up with a top-notch Chicago offense. I’m not sure that’s possible. Caleb Williams is really hitting his stride and playing well. I think Chicago won’t have any issues beating Tampa Bay at home. Winner: Bears Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings — Monday Night Football The Vikings were the last unbeaten team in the NFL until the Lions beat them last weekend. The Bills were able to obliterate the Ravens and are now 6-1 and the top team in the AFC. I’m excited to see how Brian Flores tries to combat Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense. That’ll be great to see in primetime. Though I remain confident Allen and the Bills can do enough to win on the road in Minneapolis. Winner: Bills

full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Alex Singleton #49 and Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrate after the final play of the game in their team's 28-24 win against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. He chimed in about the importance of their Week 9 matchup versus the Panthers and how Denver has gotten so good at being able to refocus after big wins. “It starts with Coach. Coach Payton is really good at that. He talks about every game in the NFL is an important game. There’s no such thing as a trap game because they’re all that way. They’re all must-wins. If you don’t play well, you’re going to end up messing around and getting beat,” stated Nix. “We know the importance of this week right before the Bye Week. We can’t go on a Bye early. This is a really important game for where we want to go. As captains and as leaders, it’s just all about practice. Details have to go up a notch, as if it isn’t already. More attention to detail, more communication. If you do everything a little bit more and maximize your time this week, I think we’ll be in a good spot.” The Broncos are the top team in the AFC West. They currently hold the second seed in the AFC playoff race thanks to performing better than the Pittsburgh Steelers, who are also 6-2, in conference games. Eight teams in the conference have at least five wins. For the first half of the season, I certainly didn’t imagine things being this close across the board. Nix is right. Denver’s Week 9 matchup is extremely important. Going into the bye riding a five-game winning streak and being 7-2 is a lot better than the alternative. Even though the Panthers are losers of two in a row and struggling on both sides of the ball, the Broncos can’t afford to underestimate them. They’ve proven to be a consistent offense that is Top 10 in many metrics. Carolina has a strong running game and quarterback Bryce Young has done a great job getting numerous players involved in the passing game. Denver’s defense will have to find a way to limit their impact. Meanwhile, the offense will have to continue to get better. We’ve seen some promise and flashes from Nix the past two games. Yet there is still much work to be done and plenty of room for improvement. He noted that getting better on third downs while continuing to maximize their opportunities in the red zone will be critical to achieve a victory on Sunday. If they can do that, Denver is going to be in a great position heading into their bye. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Bo Nix on the comebacks: ‘We have a lot of guys with a clutch gene’

full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos walks off the field after the 28-24 win against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have one 15 consecutive one score games. This is tied for the most all-time. Tying none other than Peyton Manning while he was with the Indianapolis Colts. Even more than that, Bo Nix is averaging a comeback and game winning drive at a rate far beyond anything seen in NFL history . He has the clutch gene. Clearly. When asked about his success, Nix believes it goes beyond just one person. He sees the whole team having that clutch gene and that is why they’ve been so successful. “I’ve always felt like I’ve wanted to feel like a clutch player,” Nix said on Wednesday. “It’s an important quality as a player when everybody’s looking at you and the pressure’s on. I don’t think you do it individually. If you look at our team in the last three years, we have had 15 game-winning drives. I just think we have a lot of guys with a clutch gene. We have a lot of guys that when the game’s on the line, will just find ways to go score. I’d much rather be known as the guy that wins games in the close ones than the guy that always looks great early and can win but doesn’t know how to close out the game. I’d much rather be clutch than the other way around.” He’s both right and wrong. You need the quarterback more than any other position to have the clutch gene. It feeds the rest. I think back to 2016 and how great that defense was and how clutch they were in 2015. Except, they were not quite clutch enough because the quarterback situation lost its mojo along the way without Peyton Manning’s aura around to spark the clutch. Tim Tebow had it. He was terrible at quarterbacking, but if the game was close everyone on that team believed clutch was going to manifest. It manifested because they all put in the plays to make it happen. It’s the same with these Broncos. Bo Nix is the driver. The team is the engine. Together they clutch the heck up week in and week out. Like John Elway’s years. Like Tim Tebow’s seven games. Like Peyton Manning’s 2015 run. The clutch is a team game, but it needs a quarterback that the players believe can make the magic happen if given the chance. Bo Nix is that guy too. I am enjoying this ride. Broncos daily recap Who needs picks when your offense is lacking? Every year that passes, I like having draft picks more and more. I fully understand that they are all essentially a roll of the dice, but I’d rather have a bunch of chances at improving the team than not. In general, I’m not normally about trading picks mid-season. Broncos at Panthers preview: Denver aims to avoid the “trap” The Broncos head east to face Carolina on Sunday. After a big win and brutal schedule to start, Denver can’t let up. Statistical dive into Denver Broncos record-tying 15th straight win in one-score games The Denver Broncos have now won 15 straight regular season games that were decided by one-score (8 or fewer points). This ties the 2007-2008 Peyton Manning-led Colts. Since the start of the 2025 season the Broncos are 16 and 2 in one-score games in the regular season (1-1 in the post-season). This is a big change from 2024 when the Broncos were 1-6 in one-score games. Potent quoatables Sean Payton On preparing a gameplan for a team that recently changed defensive coordinators “I think this: You go by all of the film you have. Really in that first quarter, there may be some things that we see that maybe have changed a little. [It’s] hard to change everything in a short period of time. They have a base front and coverage they like to play and then they have a sub package and then it’s really more of when they’re playing it. Then us being able to in the first quarter see if there’s something that’s different than we’ve seen on film.” On if the team is managing RB J.K. Dobbins’ workload “He’s a huge part of what we’re doing. So each week we look at—a lot of times who’s the back that’s in there with the hot hand. But he’s been fantastic. So to answer your question: No, that’s not a hot button topic with us here. It might be with you guys, but not with us. So we’re good. We’re good with the rotation.” On balancing RB J.K. Dobbins’ workload within a three-back rotation “Oh, we are paying attention to, yes, absolutely. Look, it’s always easy to work two (running backs) and it becomes more challenging when you’re trying to work three, but he’s doing a great job.” On the team’s sack total this season “All of that’s good. The pressures can lead to interceptions, the sacks can’t. So you’re looking each week, what quarterback are you defending? We’ve seen some mobile quarterbacks periodically. Maybe you get a quarterback that you know where they’re going to be in the pocket. So I think you have a rush plan based on the offense and who’s playing quarterback.” On if opposing offenses have adjusted to the team’s pass rush “Certainly the timing of when you want to throw the ball. There are some quarterbacks that are… Last week, it’s hard to sack [Chiefs QB] Patrick [Mahomes]. In other words, he’s seen the pressures, he’s seen the man… He’s got a good clock in his head. So those guys that process fast are difficult. Now fortunately for us, the last play of the game, we were able to get one. I think a lot of it is the offense and the QB. To answer your question, I’m sure there’s certain points of emphasis you make relative to the rhythm of your throws if you’re seeing a team that rushes the passer well.” On Panthers QB Bryce Young’s development “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing. It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” On how RB Jonah Coleman has impressed him despite missing time with an injury “We had those glimpses in the spring and in training camp and in the preseason. Atlanta, there’s a run, it just stood out to you. So the one thing that was unique about him is oftentimes you don’t get to see them in third down protection plans, but he was someone that we had quite a bit of tape on. Advanced protection plans, and he’s built to handle the blitz. It’s one thing to know who I have, but then also to be strong enough to do it. I would say that there were three backs—we just saw one of them that we really had visions for. Each one may be a little differently, but his versatility, to your point, that doesn’t always—you don’t get to stamp that with a lot of rookie backs that you feel like they’re going to develop into. We saw enough that we felt like he was going to be a good third down protecting back as well with the way he was built.” On if RB Jonah Coleman has exceeded his expectations in pass protection “Yeah, he’s got good ball skills. We caught him in the right pressure there. Yes, he’s very comfortable. He’s a different type [of] player than [RB] RJ [Harvey], but there were a lot of traits to like. More importantly, there was the exposure in an offense that sometimes the player just doesn’t have that exposure, so you can’t know for sure. I think we knew a little bit more with his tape.” On what allows QB Bo Nix to elevate his play when needed “I don’t know. I didn’t think he struggled. There’s certain…In Seattle, it was the opposite.” On QB Bo Nix’s ability to raise his level of play “I don’t have the answer. I know what you’re asking. I look at it internally myself like, ‘All right, let’s get going.’ I’ve said this before, I’ll let you know the week we don’t want to start fast, but it’s not this week. However, he was eligible to […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos runs onto the field prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to multiple reports, the Denver Broncos have designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from the injured reserve. The Broncos’ second-year wide receiver was back at practice today after suffering an ankle injury during the team’s loss to the 49ers and has been sidelined for the past four games. However, he was eligible to return this week, and today, Bryant was back at practice and has a chance to play in Sunday’s game vs. the Carolina Panthers. WR Pat Bryant (ankle) activated today from IR to practice.DT Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), CB Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) not present at Broncos practice today. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) November 4, 2026 Bryant was the star of training camp and was expected to have a large role in the Broncos’ offense this season, and before his injury, he was beginning to show signs of that. Through 4 games (left midway through the 4th game), Bryant has 9 receptions for 133 yards and 1 touchdown and was becoming one of the offense’s most dependable playmakers. Unfortunately, his ankle injury, which looked much worse than it ended up being, derailed the momentum he was beginning to build. However, if he does return this Sunday, he will join an offense that has shown signs of life over the past few weeks and is entering a pretty favorable stretch of games. So, if he is 100% and back to normal, he could provide a big boost to the Broncos’ passing game moving forward. As of this writing, we do not know if Bryant was a limited or full participant in today’s practice, but it sounds like he is trending towards returning this Sunday. The Broncos do have a bye week after Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers, so it’s possible they could hold off, but I do not think that’s the avenue they will take here. If Bryant does return this Sunday, he will return as the Broncos WR3 and rejoin starters Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton in the Broncos’ offense. After their big win vs. the Chiefs on Sunday, the Broncos sit at 6-2, at the top of the AFC West, and the current number 2 seed in the AFC. The addition of Bryant should give them a big second-half boost and hopefully help them win the AFC West and get the number one seed in the AFC for a second straight year.

full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Felix Anudike-Uzomah #91 of the Kansas City Chiefs tackles Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos in the fourth quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos are riding high. They’re on the heels of a massive win over the rival Kansas City Chiefs that puts them in first place in the AFC West. The 28-24 win over the Chiefs also puts Denver in the hunt for home-field advantage. Yes, it’s only eight games, but after the gauntlet the Broncos have faced, sitting at 6-2 and where they are is impressive. Now come the Carolina Panthers, who just got trucked on Thursday Night Football by the Green Bay Packers. As a result, the Panthers fired their defensive coordinator. Since Carolina plays in the NFC South, it leads the division at 3-4 and will be highly motivated to get back on track at home this Sunday. Denver is currently the -3-point road favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -118. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (273.0 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (92.6 YPG), 25th in passing offense (180.4 YPG), 22nd in scoring offense (21.5 points per game). Carolina : Ninth in total offense (363.7 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (102.0 YPG), fifth in passing offense (261.7 YPG), ninth in scoring offense (25.4 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-fifth in total defense (355.3 yards per game), 25th in rushing defense (127.9 YPG), 20th in passing defense (227.4 YPG), 11th in scoring defense (20.6 points per game). Carolina : Twenty-third in total defense (349.6 yards per game), 30th in rushing defense (140.7 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.9 YPG), 28th in scoring defense (27.6 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday’s game. Don’t fall into the “trap” Sean Payton owns the NFC South. Dating back to his New Orleans Saints days, he knows the division and how to beat these teams. However, the Broncos have historically struggled in the early games on the East Coast. On top of that, Denver is coming off a brutal stretch of games and is on the heels of a ginormous win. Not to mention, the bye is after this Sunday’s game. It’s natural to take the foot off the gas and think, “We got this.” In other words, the “trap game.” Don’t fall into that trap. It’s imperative for the Broncos to remain focused on the task at hand. Build on the win over Kansas City with the goal of playing a complete game. — Ian St. Clair Score more points than Carolina My advanced analytics came through once again. For the 6th time this season, the Broncos have scored more points than their opponent and won. Following this trend, if they do that this Sunday against the Panthers, they will improve to 7-2. — Scotty Payne Stop the run Scotty’s analytics are spot on. One of the best ways to ensure his analytics remain proven correct is to limit the Panthers’ ability to run the football. That forces Carolina into a one-dimensional attack and allows the defensive line to eventually pin its ears back and make Bryce Young as uncomfortable as the back of a Volkswagen. — Adam Malnati Keep feeding Jonah Coleman Good things happen when you run the ball effectively. We saw that for the Broncos in their past two victories. Last Sunday, rookie running back Jonah Coleman was solid on the ground for the Denver. He certainly deserves the majority of carries moving forward. The Panthers have one of the worst run defenses in the league and give up nearly 5 yards per carry. Why not pound the ball on the ground and keep giving Coleman a chance to prove himself even more? It seems like a great opportunity to see him shine. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday’s game?

title: Statistical dive into Denver Broncos record-tying 15th straight win in one-score games
summary: The Denver Broncos have now won 15 straight regular season games that were decided by one-score (8 or fewer points). This ties the 2007-2008 Peyton Manning-led Colts. full_text: The Denver Broncos have now won 15 straight regular season games that were decided by one-score (8 or fewer points). This ties the 2007-2008 Peyton Manning-led Colts. Since the start of the 2025 season the Broncos are 16 and 2 in one-score games in the regular season (1-1 in the post-season). This is a big change from 2024 when the Broncos were 1-6 in one-score games. The positive change for the Broncos in being able to win one-score games has coincided with Chiefs forgetting how to win one-score games. They were 11-0 in one-score games in 2024 and they have gone 3-10 since. As good as the Broncos have been in one-score games since the start of the 2025 regular season, the 49ers have had the same winning percentage, 0.889, just in half the games. They are 8-1. The two worst teams are the Chiefs and the Titans. Both have a 0.231 win percentage. Both in 13 games (3-10). Many of these one-score games have involved Bo Nix leading a fourth quarter comeback (4QC) and a game-winning drive (GWD). Both can only occur in the 4th quarter or overtime and can only happen in a win. If the QB leads a drive to take the lead and then the defense allows a GWD by the opposing QB, the Bronco QB does not get either. Bo Nix has now started 42 NFL games and has lead 12 4QC and 15 GWD. Those are the highest values for any QB at this point in his career in NFL history. Comparing Bo Nix to some other notable QBs at this same point (roughly) in their careers. pic.twitter.com/Nwh2pHX6i0 — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) November 2, 2026 The only QBs who are close is in 4QC are Tom Brady and Justin Herbert. Both have 10 in the first 3 starting seasons. Dak Prescott is the only one who is close in GWD. He had 14 in his first 48 starts (first 3 seasons). Tom Brady is the career leaded in 4QC with 46. He did that in 333 career starts. Bo has 12 in 42. Brady had one every 7.24 starts in his career. Bo has one every 3.50 starts. Brady also has the most GWD in his career with 58. He had one GWD every 5.74 starts. Nix has one every 2.80 starts. Bo’s numbers are best in history (min 32 GS) for both 4QC and GWD. Now some context, it takes a special set of circumstances to get either a 4QC or a GWD. There is some luck involved. The 3 and out drive for the FG after the interception in OT against the Seahawks gained 8 yards. But Bo Nix still got a GWD for that drive. That was luck and good, good defense. So a QB needs to be playing for a team with a good defense to get either. Tom Brady had this early in his career as Belicheat almost always had good to great defenses. QBs also need to be on a team with decent offense: good enough to keep the game at least close, but not good enough to win in blow-outs. By the same token, if the defense is inconsistent, the QB might be on the wrong side of blow-out losses. If the Bronco offense ever figures things out (they had four 3-and-outs last game), the opportunities for these two stats should go away because the Broncos will be playing with leads. That is what the Bronco defense is designed to be at its best – rushing the passer and defending against the pass with a lead. That didn’t work too well at the end of the last game, but when both starting safeties are out, it changes things. For historical context, as a rookie Nix had 3 4QC and 3 GWD. Last season he had 5 and 7. He already has 4 and 5 this season. However, the 5 GWD is not the most in the NFL. Somehow PFR is showing the Browns with 6 GWD when they only have 5 wins. That makes no sense until you realize that they credited two different QBs with a GWD (Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson) for the same game. I have never seen that before. The Broncos are currently 22nd in scoring at 21.5 ppg with a full 8 weeks of the season completed. The rushing offense is tied for 25th at 3.78 yards per carry (tied with Dallas). Although part of that is a result of just how ineffective JK Dobbins has been so far this season as a runner. His 3.26 yards per touch is tied for 3rd worst among RBs with 35 or more carries. Only Kendre Miller and Dameon Pierce have been worse this season. Contrast that with RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman who (aided by long catches) are near the top of the league in yards per touch for RBs. Comparing RBs Yds/Touch – for the Broncos it doesn't get much clearer as to who should be getting the ball. pic.twitter.com/geR6f6monu — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) November 2, 2026 The Broncos converted 2 of 11 third downs against the Chiefs and now sit at dead last in the NFL on 3rd down conversion rate at 29.7 percent. The Commanders are second worst at 31.9%. The Bengals have been the best so far this season at 52.9 percent. The 49ers at 50.0 percent exactly are second. Thankfully the Broncos have been able to convert on 5 of 6 4th downs, but 3rd down efficiency needs to improve or this team won’t make the playoffs. Jeremy Crawshaw is 4th in net yards per punt and he is tied for the league lead in punts downed inside the 10 at 10 (tied with Michael Dickson). He is also leading the league in “Inside the 10” points (trademarked) with 45. See below. For this a punter gets one point for a punt downed at 10, 2 for one downed at the 9, etc. While Crawshaw has yet to get one downed at the one or two this season, he has 10 of his 41 punts downed at or inside the 10. 41 punts is tied for most in the league (with the Eagles’ punter). The sack total for the defense sits at 23 after 8 games. They are 3 behind the league leading Steelers, but Kermit has always been hard to sack, so getting him twice last game is admirable. The Lions and Vikings are also ahead of the Broncos with 24 and 25 and they both have only played 7 games. The Bronco defense is looking to become the first team in NFL history to lead the NFL in sacks for three straight seasons.

full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 01: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) catches a pass in the corner of the end zone for a game-winning touchdown during the fourth quarter of a regular season NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions on November 1, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After a win, the Detroit Lions always release their own version of a “mic’d up” compilation from the game. Their “Sights and Sounds” videos are always worth your time, as they incorporate unique camera angles along with Dan Miller radio calls and mic’d up moments that you can’t get anywhere else. This week’s episode detailing the Detroit Lions’ 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings is can’t-miss. Obviously, it was an emotional game with Jack Campbell’s traumatic injury, and I think One Pride Productions does a good job covering that moment with grace and compassion while properly conveying the gravity and emotions of the moment. One other aspect of the game they uncovered was a moment of redemption that may have gone overlooked. This week, Lions receiver Jameson Williams was mic’d up, and it captured a couple of very interesting moments. Williams was involved in two extremely critical plays in the game. The first was his biggest mistake of the afternoon. It was the fourth quarter, and the Lions led 12-7. They had just gotten an emotional fourth-down stop on defense, and it was up to the offense to extend their lead and bleed some of the remaining 13 minutes of game time. Facing a third-and-inches, Jared Goff ran a QB sneak up the middle for a first down. But Williams had not properly reported as off the line of scrimmage, causing the refs to call illegal formation. Detroit would not convert the third-and-6, and they punted it back to Minnesota. As he was coming off the field, dejected, Williams was met with a coaching staff that had a message for him: “You owe us,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said. “I know, I know, I know,” Williams replied. The Vikings capitalized on Williams’ mistake, driving the length of the field to take the lead 15-12 with just under nine minutes remaining. That’s when Lions receivers coach Scottie Montgomery repeated the message to Williams. “You owe us,” Montgomery said. “Go back, make a play. I know the frustration. It [redacted] sucks. But we know you’re in. So stay in, okay?” “Yup,” Williams replied. What ensued was one of the Lions’ most impressive drives of the season. Detroit went 69 yards on just seven plays, led by five rushes for 57 yards—all of at least 9 yards. The cameras show Williams blocking is ass off the entire time. And on the first snap of Detroit’s goal-line offense, Jared Goff pulled the rug out from underneath the Vikings defense with a play-action pass to a wide-open Williams. As he sprinted toward the sideline following his game-winning catch, Williams reminded the staff of his redemption. Campbell: “Way to pay us back! That’s what I’m talking about!” Williams: “Hey! I owe you, don’t I? I owe you, don’t I?” Then, to Montgomery: Williams: “Hey! I owe you, don’t I? Montgomery: “Let’s go!” Williams: “I still owe you! I still owe you! Aw, yeah! Aw, yeah!” It’s a great moment caught on tape by the One Pride Production crew. You can watch the entire video below:

title: NFL trade deadline rumors: Lions, Bears could compete for same players
summary: The NFL trade deadline is coming soon (next Tuesday), and with such a tightly contested NFC North, there could be an arms race on the horizon. Currently the Minnesota Vikings lead the division at 6-1, but the 5-2 Detroit Lions and 6-2 Chicago Bears are close behind, and both teams are hunting to add more […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears and Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions shake hands following the game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is coming soon (next Tuesday), and with such a tightly contested NFC North, there could be an arms race on the horizon. Currently the Minnesota Vikings lead the division at 6-1, but the 5-2 Detroit Lions and 6-2 Chicago Bears are close behind, and both teams are hunting to add more talent before Tuesday’s deadline. In fact, according to ESPN insider Dan Graziano, both the Lions and Bears could be hunting for the same players. In one of his latest pieces for ESPN, Graziano said both the Lions and Bears have made calls about acquiring a cornerback. “The Bears made their big move for [Jeffery] Simmons, but they’re still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions,” Graziano wrote this week. “Detroit might also be in the market for help at linebacker, particularly in the wake of the terrible injury to mainstay Jack Campbell.” It’s no surprise to hear that the Lions are still searching for a cornerback. The team admitted they were in the market for Joey Porter Jr. before he was eventually traded to the Dallas Cowboys. And the Lions’ cornerback situation hasn’t really changed since. While D.J. Reed is certainly playing better as the team’s No. 1 cornerback in recent weeks, Detroit is still seeking a No. 2 cornerback while rotating through the likes of Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin, Khalil Dorsey, and Ennis Rakestraw. The Bears, who already made a big trade deadline move by sending two first-round picks and more to the Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, have also dealt with some issues in the secondary. No. 1 cornerback Jaylon Johnson is currently ranked 103rd out of 106 qualifying cornerbacks in PFF coverage grade (32.1), while CB2 Malik Muhammad isn’t faring much better (52.5, 78th). At this point, it isn’t clear which cornerbacks are available to acquire at the trade deadline. But some of the more commonly thrown around names are Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil, Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brent, and Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson. A month ago, we also compiled a list of defensive backs that the Lions could target at the trade deadline . We’ll see if either team can pull off a move with just days remaining before the deadline.

title: Discussion: Which Detroit Lions player needs to step up most in light of injuries?
summary: The Detroit Lions’ Wednesday injury report was as long as it’s been all season. On top of Jimmy Rolder being placed on injured reserve earlier this week, the following Lions players were estimated to not be able to practice: Additionally, these players were estimated to be limited in practice: That’s six Lions defenders and nine […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) smiles as he talks with linebacker Derrick Barnes (55) following Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions’ Wednesday injury report was as long as it’s been all season. On top of Jimmy Rolder being placed on injured reserve earlier this week , the following Lions players were estimated to not be able to practice: C Cade Mays (ankle) EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion) LB Jack Campbell (neck) CB D.J. Reed (hip) Additionally, these players were estimated to be limited in practice: RB Jacob Saylors (neck) WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) S Kerby Joseph (knee) S Brian Branch (concussion) That’s six Lions defenders and nine total players with their status up in the air this week. It’s far too early to declare any of these players definitively out this week (outside of Kerby Joseph— Dan Campbell already said he won’t play this week —and Jack Campbell), but there’s a pretty good likelihood the Lions will be missing at least a couple of these players. So today’s Question of the Day is: Which Lions players need to step up the most vs. the Dolphins? My answer: It feels like the answer has to come on defense. With Campbell and Rolder out, there will certainly be a ton of extra pressure on the linebacker room. Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske are the most likely starters for Detroit this week, and we’ve seen a lot of ups and downs from this group. The good news is that they all have plenty of experience on defense. The bad news is that none of them bring the consistent play-making ability of Campbell, nor the leadership of Detroit’s defensive captain. But relief can also come from a different position. Covering the middle of the field has been a challenge, and it’s not necessarily a strength of the current linebacking corps. This would be a huge week for the safeties to step up. While it’s unclear if Branch will be available this week, I’m really looking for Chuck Clark and Keith Abney to elevate their games. Abney has been up and down, as you’d expect from a rookie who made a midseason shift from cornerback to safety. But I’ve been pretty disappointed with how Clark has played. He was supposed to bring communication and discipline to the position, but mental errors have plagued the back end (admittedly, not all his fault). Malik Willis is not afraid to throw deep or utilize the middle of the field, so I’d love to see a clean game from the safeties to help out the ailing linebacker position. title: Lions promote LB Joe Bachie to active roster, sign two other LBs
summary: The Detroit Lions announced three linebacker-related roster transactions on Wednesday: signing Joe Bachie from the practice squad to the active roster, signing K.J. Britt from the Patriots’ practice squad to the active roster, and signing Owen Pappoe to the practice squad. No immediate roster moves were necessary, as the Lions previously opened two spots on […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Detroit Lions linebacker Joe Bachie (35) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions announced three linebacker-related roster transactions on Wednesday: signing Joe Bachie from the practice squad to the active roster, signing K.J. Britt from the Patriots’ practice squad to the active roster, and signing Owen Pappoe to the practice squad . No immediate roster moves were necessary, as the Lions previously opened two spots on their 53-man roster on Tuesday when they placed rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder on injured reserve and waived rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald. Bachie’s promotion from the practice squad opened a spot for Pappoe. Bachie joined the Lions in April and provided veteran experience throughout training camp at MIKE linebacker and on special teams. He performed well enough in the preseason to be firmly on the roster bubble, and while the Lions released him in cutdowns, they signed him back to the practice squad the next day. When it became clear Rolder couldn’t start the season due to injury, the Lions signed Bachie to the active roster for their first two games, then released him in late September and re-signed him to the practice squad. With Bachie operating as the team’s LB7, the injuries to Jack Campbell and Rolder have created a need for him to step into a larger role moving forward. While he will almost certainly be a fixture on special teams, his experience and positional versatility could put him at LB4 behind Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske, and Malcolm Rodriguez, the three presumed starters. As for Britt and Pappoe, it will likely take time for them to acclimate to the Lions’ defensive scheme. That said, Britt has plenty of special teams experience, and with the Lions’ preference to keep six linebackers active on game days, he could be active as soon as this Sunday against the Dolphins.

title: How Detroit Lions plan to channel Jack Campbell emotions into Dolphins prep
summary: The mental strain on this Detroit Lions team cannot be easy this week. Even with the great news that linebacker Jack Campbell has full movement in his lower body after a traumatic neck injury on Sunday, it’s natural for the entire locker room to have their attention divided between Campbell’s recovery and Sunday’s upcoming game […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions reacts during an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The mental strain on this Detroit Lions team cannot be easy this week. Even with the great news that linebacker Jack Campbell has full movement in his lower body after a traumatic neck injury on Sunday , it’s natural for the entire locker room to have their attention divided between Campbell’s recovery and Sunday’s upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins. Lions coach Dan Campbell isn’t running away from that difficult reality. “There’s no easy way to do this, but you also have to acknowledge it, and let’s talk about it and make sure we know,” Campbell said. “But I also know they’re not postponing this game. And I know the only way to honor Jack, we know the only way to really honor Jack and what he really wants is to make sure that we’re locked in and ready to go because otherwise what just kind of came about, then we’re throwing it away in a sense.” Like any other week, the Lions have mental health professionals in-house to help any players who may need support or just a person to talk to. Campbell indicated that there are players who have already utilized those resources this week. Lions coach Scottie Montgomery is taking a similar approach to Dan Campbell, noting that it’s impossible to ignore their “fallen leader.” “The key word is balance. The human in all of us—we play football, we coach football, but our first element is the human element,” Montgomery said. “It’s very difficult, of course, emotionally to be in a game like that, having a situation like that happen. And what we do have to talk about, we can’t ignore; we have had open dialogue. We do this with our players. Because we do have concern for our fallen leader. That’s exactly who he was; I don’t know any other way to say it.” But the Lions are hopeful they can turn that concern for Campbell into an on-field honoring of everything he represents. Campbell is one of the hardest-working players on the team, and they know one of the best ways to honor him is to attack the week as he would. “I think we owe it to him; we owe it to all of ourselves to make sure we’re locked in, and we make the most of this,” Campbell said. “And so, it’s balancing; you’re human and you know it, you want to acknowledge it. It’s a lot, but if that’s weighing that heavy and that’s where your mind’s at, it’s not going to be good going in this game, and that’s where you can get hurt as well.” “We’re honoring him by the way that we prepare. We’re preparing like he prepares,” Montgomery added. “That’s what we’re talking with each other about. As players, as coaches, we’re going to prepare like he prepares. We’re going to play like he plays. We’re going to do the things that he would have us do. […] There’s no way around anybody in that locker room not feeling a certain way about him. But that same feeling that causes pain, it causes us to pursue the excellence of what Jack would want us to do in this situation, and that’s go prepare and get ready to go down and play a good football team and play to a high level this weekend.“

I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong. Jack Campbell

title: 5 Lions vs. Dolphins thoughts after watching Miami’s loss to Patriots
summary: To turn the page from Week 8 to Week 9, I spent some time early this week watching the Miami Dolphins’ most recent game to see what’s in store for the Detroit Lions. Here are my five Lions vs. Dolphins thoughts after watching Miami’s 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots. Note: It’s worth mentioning […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) drops back to throw a pass during the first quarter against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect To turn the page from Week 8 to Week 9, I spent some time early this week watching the Miami Dolphins’ most recent game to see what’s in store for the Detroit Lions. Here are my five Lions vs. Dolphins thoughts after watching Miami’s 24-19 loss to the New England Patriots. Note: It’s worth mentioning that it was a very rainy day in Miami, particularly at the start and end of the game. Malik Willis holds onto the ball for a loooooong time There could be a lot of reasons for it, but Willis holds onto the ball way too long in the pocket. Per NFL Pro, Willis’ 3.05 average seconds to throw is third-longest in the league. Is it taking Willis too long to go through his progressions, is he too hesitant to trust his eyes, or is his young receiving corps just not getting open? It’s hard to say from my vantage point, but it certainly is an opportunity for the Lions to get home against Willis. Thus far, Willis has taken 21 sacks—the seventh most in the NFL—and the Dolphins have the second-highest sack rate in the NFL (10.3%). The Patriots got to Willis five times in the first half, before backing down a little in the second. This could be a big Tyleik Williams game Miami had an extremely hard time stopping Patriots nose tackle Cory Durden in this game. He set career highs in pressure (three), quarterback hits (three), and sacks (1.5). Prior to this game, Durden had never recorded a sack and only had two quarterback hits since starting his NFL career, coincidentally in Detroit, in 2023. Miami is particularly vulnerable on the right side of the line, where second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea is the 66th (out of 75) PFF-graded guard (47.9), and right tackle Austin Jackson is the lowest-graded tackle in football (44.6). Williams is having a strong start to his second season, remaining a force in the run game (Dolphins rank 21st in EPA/rush, 24th in success rate) while growing as a pass rusher. Obviously, look out for Alim McNeill, too, who is currently only behind Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen in PFF pressures from interior defenders (31). The Lions’ run game should find success Last week, the Lions found success pounding the rock right up the middle of the Vikings’ defense. That should be the game plan once again against the Dolphins. Rhamondre Stevenson toughed out 82 yards on 19 carries (4.3 YPC), as the Patriots produced a 45.2% success rate on the ground—ninth-highest of all Week 8 performances. For the year, Miami ranks 21st in EPA/rush allowed and 30th in success rate (43.9%). So they aren’t giving up a ton of explosive plays on the ground, but you can certainly grind them down. I would not be surprised to see another solid workload from Sione Vaki. But Miami does have some dudes on defense Miami’s defense as a whole won’t likely be up for the task against the Lions’ high-flying offense. The Dolphins rank 24th in points per game allowed (25.9) and 25th in yards per play allowed. However, there are a couple of players who are playing well and capable of game-changing plays. The first is edge rusher Josh Uche. While Uche only has two sacks this year (one against the Patriots), he’s produced PFF’s ninth-highest run defense grade among edge defenders (76.0). On the next level, rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez flashed against the Patriots. He had a teach-tape punchout and was second on the team with eight tackles. His rookie season has seen some ups and downs, but don’t be surprised if he makes a big play or two against the Lions. The game wasn’t as close as the score While the Dolphins only lost by five and they held a 10-point lead at halftime, this game did not feel like it was truly competitive between the teams. For one, the Patriots made a ton of mistakes in the first half. They fumbled inside their own red zone, missed a 40-yard field goal, and had a ton of untimely penalties (seven in total). In the second half, the Patriots dropped an easy interception, and they had a game-clinching pick erased by an away-from-the-play offsides penalty. And the Dolphins only made it close thanks to a prevent-defense touchdown with just over two minutes, because a Patriots defender fell down for an easy 35-yard touchdown. On a per play basis, the Patriots produced more yards per play (5.3 vs. 4.5), and had a much higher success rate (49.1% vs. 43.8%). If you take away garbage-time stats, the difference is even bigger in success rate (52.9% vs. 39.3%). Did we really get beat that bad? Comparing offensive success rates for NFL games in Week 8: pic.twitter.com/i4tQhlOtNa — Sam Hoppen (@SamHoppen) November 2, 2026 If the Lions can avoid making self-inflicted mistakes, they should be able to win comfortably, despite the fact that Miami has kept each of their last four games within a touchdown.

title: Mailbag: Could the Detroit Lions target a linebacker at NFL trade deadline?
summary: The NFL trade deadline is now less than a week away. If teams want to add talent via a trade, it must happen by 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. After that, the only talent acquisition can come via free agency or waivers. The Detroit Lions’ interest in a cornerback is no secret. The […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun (53) in action against the Carolina Panthers Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The NFL trade deadline is now less than a week away. If teams want to add talent via a trade, it must happen by 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10. After that, the only talent acquisition can come via free agency or waivers. The Detroit Lions’ interest in a cornerback is no secret. The team openly admitted they were involved in talks for Joey Porter Jr., although the Dallas Cowboys apparently outbid them. Cornerback sure seems like it’s still on the table, but could Detroit’s strategy shift after losing several players to injury on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings? With rookie Jimmy Rolder out for the year and All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell out indefinitely with a neck injury, suddenly linebacker seems like a pretty serious need. This week, the Lions have backfilled their depth chart with special teams pieces in KJ Britt and (reportedly) Owen Pappoe. But can they trust players like Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske to hold starting roles? Or do they need to make an aggressive move to raise the ceiling of the room and fortify the middle of the field? On this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast, we discuss the Lions’ options at the NFL trade deadline, and outline a couple of names we’d like to see the Lions consider. At the top of that list is undoubtedly Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. The 29-year-old All-Pro linebacker is on a very manageable contract for Detroit (salaries of $1.215M, $1.345M, and $1.39M from 2026-28, plus a $14 million option bonus in 2027). It makes a little less sense for the Eagles (over $16M in dead cap), but if the Lions could make it worth it with draft compensation, they could get a deal done. And with the Eagles 2-6—losers of six straight—forced to play Tanner McKee at quarterback, it may make sense to acquire as much draft captial as possible. Other linebacker options discussed: Buccaneers’ Alex Anzalone and Dolphins’ Jordyn Brooks. We also talk about whether the Lions’ strategy should change considering how competitive the NFC North is this year. Does it make sense to get in an arms race with the Chicago Bears after their acquisition of Jeffrey Simmons? Or is that actually a reason to pull back this year and wait for a time in which things feel more open? And we talk about a lot of topics beyond the trade deadline, including: How the Lions’ “sidecar” formation was the perfect antidote to Brian Flores Why didn’t Ennis Rakestraw play much vs. Minnesota? What’s with the Lions’ short-yardage issues? Is it actually better to have the 5th or 6th seed in the NFC rather than the No. 2 seed? Should the Lions consider extending Christian Mahogany this offseason? How many carries for Sione Vaki is the sweet spot? Check out the show below, or find us on your favorite podcasting platform by searching “Pride of Detroit.” As always, you can also catch the podcast on our YouTube page and Twitch channel . On this week’s show, we went through some more Movember shenanigans, including eating something called earthworm jerky. All available on the video portion only.

title: Packers-Patriots Preview: Christian Gonzalez defines New England’s defense
summary: Last week, the Carolina Panthers sat in split-safety coverages against the Green Bay Packers, forcing the team to run the football or take checkdown passes routinely — just like their matchup in 2025. While this didn’t stop the Packers’ offense, which still had a 100-yard receiver in Christian Watson despite his in-game trip to the […]
full_text: (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week, the Carolina Panthers sat in split-safety coverages against the Green Bay Packers, forcing the team to run the football or take checkdown passes routinely — just like their matchup in 2025. While this didn’t stop the Packers’ offense, which still had a 100-yard receiver in Christian Watson despite his in-game trip to the hospital for a rib injury, it did mean that the offense was a lot less explosive than it was in prior weeks. Don’t expect that same strategy from the New England Patriots this week, as it’s not really their identity to sit back and just let offense happen to them, hoping that the opposing team will trip up at some point. According to Next Gen Stats, the Patriots have sent max pressure (six or more pass rushers) with man coverage behind it 37 times already this season, the most in the league. On those looks, they’ve posted five sacks and allowed just 14 completions on 31 pass attempts (45 percent) for 123 yards (4.0 yards per attempt), with one interception and no touchdowns surrendered. The overall conversion rate on those players is 21.6 percent, which is the best mark in the league in these situations. In contrast, New England has only sent 13 of these “max pressure” looks out of zone in 2026, surrendering 9 of 13 in the air for 131 yards (10 yards per attempt) and a touchdown. In short, the Patriots’ man coverage looks have been better for them than zone coverage looks this year, especially when they’re trying to speed quarterbacks up. Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, their All-Pro defender, helps the team unlock that man coverage identity when so many other NFL teams are leaning out of the man coverage game. When Gonzalez has been on the field, the team has played man coverage on 39 percent of their defensive snaps, compared to just 29 percent when he’s not in the game. Packers quarterback Jordan Love has done his most damage this year against the blitz when he’s had either Christian Watson or Matthew Golden in one-on-one looks, but unlike a lot of the teams Green Bay has played this year, the Patriots are just as comfortable playing man as they are playing zone, even behind a blitz. Gonzalez travels, as he’s followed around specific receivers in man coverage at least 10 times in three separate games, a number that leads the NFL. For perspective, neither Watson nor Golden has been seen man coverage 10 times by a single defender in a single game this entire season. Something has to break here. This is going to be the most important matchup of Sunday’s game, by far. The only question is whether Gonzalez will travel with a receiver and which one of the Packers’ deep threats it will be.

title: Micah Parsons talks injury, recovery and timeline
summary: The Green Bay Packers opened up edge defender Micah Parsons’ 21-day practice window on Wednesday, which allows him to practice with the team for up to three weeks before he’s eventually brought up to the active roster. That 21-day window overlaps with the Packers’ bye week in Week 11, which means that Parsons should be […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers opened up edge defender Micah Parsons’ 21-day practice window on Wednesday, which allows him to practice with the team for up to three weeks before he’s eventually brought up to the active roster. That 21-day window overlaps with the Packers’ bye week in Week 11, which means that Parsons should be on the roster by the team’s Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve, but Parsons hesitated to commit to playing in that game. According to head coach Matt LaFleur, Parsons was only going to participate in individual drills on Wednesday. After practice today, Parsons spoke to the press and stated that he’s “excited for next week” when he can “actually practice.” Per Parsons, timelines jumped around for his recovery, as testing his leg — where he’s coming off a major knee injury — did not produce results beyond the common recovery. The edge rusher stated that he had full repairs to both his lateral and medial menisci in the same knee that suffered a torn ACL last season. Beyond of that, Parsons was essentially non-weight-bearing for two months, which is why the timeline for this recovery is pushing 11 months compared to the 9 months for Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft. Parsons also mentioned “Wisconsin” several times, likely a hint that the University of Wisconsin-Madison was involved in his recovery. The university has helped other players fix imbalances in their bodies in the past, including Watson and running back MarShawn Lloyd, two players who had been injury-prone before their trips southwest. The All-Pro said there were also times when he was unsure he would even be back on the field in November, but that his “knee feels great” at the moment. He also claimed that it’s “not realistic” for him to play 50 to 60 snaps when he does return back to games, as he’s still working himself into shape after missing training camp. You can find a full video of Parsons’ media availability below: One thing for sure, I promise myself this, and I will tell anyone that doesn’t believe or even my believers I’m gonna be great again!
