title: Patrick Mahomes says Chiefs aren’t afraid to call the quarterback sneak
summary: October 17, 2019. That was the last time Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a snap from under center and ran one of football’s most traditional plays: the QB sneak. After Mahomes converted the fourth-and-1 inside the Denver Broncos’ five-yard line, he stayed down on the field with a dislocated kneecap. The injury that […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images October 17, 2019. That was the last time Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a snap from under center and ran one of football’s most traditional plays: the QB sneak. After Mahomes converted the fourth-and-1 inside the Denver Broncos ’ five-yard line, he stayed down on the field with a dislocated kneecap. The injury that forced the Chiefs’ third-year superstar quarterback to miss the next two games looked much worse at first glance. Since then, Kansas City has gotten creative in short-yardage situations — even using tight ends to take the snap from under center — but Mahomes himself has not run the sneak. After excelling in those situations by handing off to former Chiefs running back Kareem Hunt last season, Kansas City’s effectiveness converting short-yardage downs has dwindled in 2026. Mahomes reflected on the drop-off during his press conference on Wednesday. “It’s something that we’ve been better at in the past years, but obviously this year, we haven’t been able to execute in those situations,” Mahomes acknowledged. “It always comes down to one guy here or there and just not being on the same page. I think that’s something that we have to continue to be more and more physical.” On the final drive against the Denver Broncos , a third-and-goal play from the one-yard line seemingly presented an opportunity for Mahomes to tuck the ball and get behind right guard Trey Smith in the A-gap. Instead, the called play in the huddle was run, a handoff that was blown up in the backfield. “The play call is what we called, and we want to execute that play,” Mahomes said on Wednesday. “They were able to stunt and kind of get people in position where Kenneth wasn’t able to get going downhill and score a touchdown.” Of course, the Chiefs couldn’t finish the drive, and the question of a sneak became a hot topic in the wake of the loss in Chiefs Kingdom. 3rd&goal run @SamMcDowell11 asked Andy about the DL not respecting a sneak by alignment: “We didn’t block it right on the right side there; we have to make sure we get our assignment right, but other than that, we’ve been pretty successful without sneaking it over time here.” pic.twitter.com/IpN1FIFcNb — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) November 2, 2026 On Monday, head coach Andy Reid told local media that the team has been “pretty successful without sneaking” during this golden era of Chiefs football. It was a polarizing comment, but it’s not a definitive statement about whether the team will run one. If it were up to the quarterback, any play-call is possible. “I’m going to do whatever it takes to win,” Mahomes said. “It’s not like I’m scared to go out there and put my body on the line, that’s kind of how I’ve played. It’s kind of gotten me in trouble sometimes, and then there are sometimes it has helped the team.” The two-time MVP should be trusted at the line of scrimmage to audible, but he knows it has to be the right time. “If I do call my own number, it’s got to work,” Mahomes said with a smile. He didn’t call his own number at the goal line in Denver, but he cited the play call as the reason. In similar situations, Kansas City may be more prepared for Mahomes to take it himself. “There have been quarterback sneaks in games that we have put in,” Mahomes shared. “We will alert and change at the line of scrimmage if they get in those Tite fronts. Obviously, that wasn’t the play in that situation of the game, but it’s not like we’re scared to call the quarterback sneak. It’s just something that we haven’t done; we’ve been able to execute with other things.” “So I don’t think coach Reid has put that on me,” Mahomes clarified. “But at the end of the day, if we can’t execute with the other things, I’m sure we’re going to have to make changes, and that’s something coach Reid is not afraid to do is make changes whenever needed.”
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs Mailbag: What to think of the Kingsley Suamataia mess?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! A frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos dropped the Chiefs to 5-2 and left fans wondering how seriously to panic. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds ahead of […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! A frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos dropped the Chiefs to 5-2 and left fans wondering how seriously to panic. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds ahead of hopefully a get-right opportunity against the New York Jets . Tomahawk0611 asks: Why didn’t left guard Kingsley Suamataia play yesterday? Has he been permanently benched? We saw Suamataia benched in Week 4 only to return to the starting lineup after the bye. I suspect that we will see him again in Week 9 against the Jets, but this has been a weird situation. I think it is fair to be frustrated with Reid’s cryptic responses, but what should be obvious is that the staff has made it clear to the player they are not happy about something. It is unclear whether that is tied to performance or practice habits. Whatever the problem, however, I don’t think fans are putting enough blame on Suamataia for how he is falling short of expectations. This is especially true considering one of the biggest fan criticisms from the past few seasons has been a perceived lack of accountability. The frustration with the staff and front office should be that they did not have a better backup plan than Mike Caliendo before deciding to hold the line on Suamataia. GoldenDomer asks: Is the QB sneak refusal an Andy Reid thing or Patrick Mahomes thing? It’s equally disappointing that Mahomes hasn’t just done it on his own at this point. Since the night in Denver that the world saw Mahomes’ kneecap put back into place on the field, the quarterback sneak has clearly not been an option for the Chiefs. We saw the team briefly use tight end Noah Gray — and Blake Bell before him — on the play. Unfortunately, teams quickly caught on. For fans, the obvious answer to short-yardage woes has been to re-sign running back Kareem Hunt. My solution would be to put backup quarterback Justin Fields into some third-and-1 and fourth-and-1 plays. Perhaps that means taking Mahomes off the field for a snap. Perhaps that has both quarterbacks on the field at the same time. Defenses accounting for Fields would likely pay bigger dividends for running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson in the crucial situations. Glorified KC asks: Why did the defense struggle so much in the fourth quarter? Did Sean Payton figure out a weakness to exploit? They went from allowing 0 first downs in the third quarter to allowing 15 points in the fourth. To be fair, the Chiefs are not the only team to have trouble putting the Broncos away late. Of Denver’s now six wins, they were trailing or tied entering the fourth quarter four times (with one of their other wins coming in overtime). I assumed that the Jacksonville Jaguars and Los Angeles Rams would put the Broncos away, only to see a similar story unfold that we saw Sunday. Reid put the defense in bad positions twice by punting on fourth-and-1, leading to a touchback, before having Harrison Butker miss a 54-yard field goal to start Denver’s final position at their own 44-yard line. I actually think Reid chose the wrong time to punt in either situation. On both of Denver’s touchdown drives, the Chiefs’ defense surrendered a massive play. One saw a 15-yard penalty added on, and the final drive saw a 50-yard play go to the five-yard line. The defense let Kansas City down. However, I would also put heavy blame on conservative offensive playcalling that yielded zero points in the final frame. Atypical Vagabond asks: Can the Chiefs stop beating themselves? There is no reason not to win with a 15 point lead… yet we certainly found a way to lose. There are two seasons that are coming to mind when I see how the last two weeks have gone. The first season I covered the Chiefs for Arrowhead Pride was 2021. That year, the Chiefs appeared to play undisciplined much of the season and had a predictable offense where almost anyone could tell what play was about to be called based on the formation. That season ended with an inexcusable loss in the AFC Championship game. The other season I am thinking of came in 2023, when Kansas City took an extended offensive slump almost to the playoffs, including an inept Christmas Day performance against the Raiders. We will remember that year ended with Kansas City’s third Super Bowl title in a five-season span. The past two games have been frustrating. However, I think we need to wait out the rest of the slate and judge the Chiefs on the whole of the season. That said, we need to see the team really focus on getting right over the next three weeks against a trio of seemingly lesser opponents. RunningFree asks: At what point will (local) media turn on Andy’s way of not providing meaningful answers no matter the question? If someone asked him if it rained during the game at Denver he might say something along the lines of: “We’ll go back, look at the tape, and see where we’re at. I’m not gonna get into all the details on that. You guys saw what happened out there. So, uh, we’ll just go from there.” Truthfully, I included this question because it really made me laugh. I do not know how much longer the 68-year-old Reid plans to continue coaching. But I don’t see him changing his tone with the media. Fans frequently vent frustration that beat writers are not asking tough enough questions when Reid is available, typically on Wednesdays, Fridays, and after games. I would counter that most of those writers know what topics Reid is likely to be more upfront about. It is hard to create content off of the coach’s nonanswers. Local media will continue to ask similar questions in press conferences. When we do get unflattering details around the team — such as what we have seen recently with tackle Josh Simmons — expect national media to continue breaking the news. Thank you for reading this week’s Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! We will be back after the Chiefs try to get back on track against the Jets. Keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to ask your questions.
author: Jared Sapp

title: The Good and the Bad from the Chiefs’ loss to Broncos
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second game of the season in Week 8, 28-24, to the Denver Broncos. Let’s look at one thing that went well and two things that didn’t from the game: The Good Emmett Johnson’s performance Rookie running back Emmett Johnson was the best player on the field for the Chiefs […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second game of the season in Week 8, 28-24, to the Denver Broncos . Let’s look at one thing that went well and two things that didn’t from the game: The Good Emmett Johnson’s performance Rookie running back Emmett Johnson was the best player on the field for the Chiefs against the Broncos. Johnson finished with five catches for 128 yards, including a 73-yard receiving touchdown. He only got one carry, but it went for 15 yards. Johnson’s long touchdown was a great design by head coach Andy Reid and staff. The Broncos love to blitz on third downs. They send their nickel on a blitz, hoping to keep Johnson in protection. Instead, the Chiefs have Johnson leak across the formation and run a wheel route. The Broncos screw this coverage up, as one of the defensive linemen, likely the defensive end, should drop and carry Johnson. Regardless, it’s still Johnson on a defensive end in a footrace, and Johnson is going to win that often. Andy Reid wanted to get Denver’s linebackers in space, and Johnson executed on those plays. The Broncos are in Quarters coverage here against the 2×2 formation for the Chiefs. The boundary cornerback is occupied by tight end Travis Kelce running a 12-yard in route and can’t turn back to the flat quickly enough. Wide receiver Rashee Rice runs an underneath route to occupy the backside linebacker, leaving the other linebacker responsible for covering Johnson in the flat because the coverage was flooded. He had no chance of stopping Johnson, easily getting around him for another explosive play. I really liked Johnson coming out of Nebraska due to his combination of agility and balance in the hole. This play is a good example of that. Johnson makes the defensive end miss in the hole after right tackle Jaylon Moore whiffs on a block, makes the linebacker miss inside, jukes the safety inside with a deceleration move, spins out of another arm tackle, and gains 15. These types of plays were all over his Nebraska film, and he can do that in the NFL as well. Johnson is now up to 237 receiving yards on the year. He’s been terrific on third downs this year, which is huge for spelling lead back Kenneth Walker. I would like to see Johnson get into the rotation for carries as well. The case against giving Johnson carries is that it takes Walker off the field, and Walker has a greater chance of getting explosives. However, giving Johnson more carries does save Walker and keep him fresher to get those plays. I would argue that the Chiefs should probably throw the ball less than they do now and feature Johnson and Walker more often in the run game. The Bad Andy Reid’s 3rd and 2 play call before the missed kick There’s been some consternation about Andy Reid’s playcalling in this game, but honestly, I think the Chiefs offense played about as well as you can hope. This team has two shaky tackles against a great Denver pass rush and one NFL wide receiver in Rice against Denver’s top-tier cornerbacks. Kansas City’s only options were attacking the Broncos’ bad linebackers in coverage, and they did that well. The run game didn’t go as well as you would hope, but they also had a backup left guard — a separate issue for the team. Denver was always going to stop the run better in this game than they did in Week 1, but the Chiefs’ passing game was legitimately good. That was a huge difference from Week 1, too, when the Chiefs’ passing game was terrible. That said, I didn’t like this third-and-2 call before Butker misses the kick. Chiefs are in 12 personnel and run a half rollout for Mahomes. Kelce is the #3 receiver and runs the corner clearout route, which doesn’t make sense to me. The play is designed for Jalen Royals and Xavier Worthy to win on whip routes. Royals and Worthy can’t win against man coverage at all and had zero chance of getting open. Wouldn’t it make more sense to have one of those two bad receivers run the pointless clearout route and let Kelce or even Rice have the underneath route? Why are we designing plays for Worthy or Royals? Mahomes should’ve thrown this ball away, but I don’t like limiting the field on third-and-2; mainly, designing the play for Royals or Worthy is bad. Worthy just does nothing on the field well anymore, and they need to replace him. Hopefully Royals’ snaps go down once Rice gets healthier. The Bad Chiefs defending the flats The Chiefs defense made me mad in this game. Once again, they had zero pass rush. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix did hit some nice downfield throws that weren’t always bad coverage. But the biggest issue was how badly the Chiefs defended the flats. Bo Nix is either a vertical or flat thrower. He does nothing else. This is the Chiefs’ fifth time facing Nix, and they didn’t seem to realize it. It started twice on the first drive: the first was a running back screen Alohi Gilman was late to close on, and the second was Cochrane completely lost on a bootleg. Gilman has to defend Jonah Coleman in the flat here and lets Coleman run past him, and he gets called for pass interference. The Broncos run a switch release to Waddle for a touchdown. Chris Rolland-Wallace and Nohl Williams botch the switch call, and Rolland-Wallace is way too late to recover on Waddle. The annoying part is the Chiefs messed this up again, this time off a bootleg. Jadon Canady thinks he’s running the clearout route, but Williams does too, making one of them way too slow in the flat. The Chiefs send a six-man pressure here with two to the running back side of the protection. The Broncos have six in protection and slide the right way. I believe Nick Bolton is green-dogging here, which means he blitzes if the back stays in protection; otherwise, he has him in coverage. Regardless, he gets lost on the play, and the blitz means everyone is behind the play when it goes for 51 yards.
author: Nate Christensen

title: Week 9 AP NFL Power Rankings: Broncos enter top 10 after divisional win
summary: Maybe you’re like me and the Kansas City Chiefs’ loss completely ruined your Sunday afternoon. I couldn’t bring myself to watch football anymore until halftime on Monday night. Yes, the “Sunday Night Football” matchup was horrible — Philadelphia Eagles versus Washington Commanders. But it could have been the 1972 Dolphins versus 2007 Patriots, and I […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maybe you’re like me and the Kansas City Chiefs ’ loss completely ruined your Sunday afternoon. I couldn’t bring myself to watch football anymore until halftime on Monday night. Yes, the “Sunday Night Football” matchup was horrible — Philadelphia Eagles versus Washington Commanders . But it could have been the 1972 Dolphins versus 2007 Patriots, and I wouldn’t have watched. The Chiefs left too bad a taste in my mouth. Hopefully the Chiefs have moved on, but I’m still working through my anger over that game. Regardless of the Chiefs’ clunker, this NFL season continues to be entertaining and unpredictable. No team is unbeaten in the league, and only one team remains winless. Preseason favorites such as the Los Angeles Rams or Seattle Seahawks are only .500. The Pittsburgh Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars are surprising first-place teams in their respective divisions. The Arrowhead Pride staff returned this week with the latest edition of the Power Rankings. This week’s rankings saw two new entrants in the top 10, while two new teams fell into the bottom 5. Biggest riser: Las Vegas Raiders +5 Biggest fallers: Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts -5 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. Buffalo Bills (1st) They could basically go on cruise control due to the Ravens’ quarterback injuries. 2. Chicago Bears (5th) A legit Super Bowl contender. They get more impressive by the week. Trading for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons solidifies one of the few holes on the roster. 3. San Francisco 49ers (3rd) I fully expect this team to be angry and return to form after their bye week following a head-scratching loss to the Falcons. 4. Minnesota Vikings (2nd) Their defense plays lights out. Their offense barely plays. 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (7th) They could potentially have this division wrapped up by Thanksgiving. A great team absolutely no one talks about. 6. Seattle Seahawks (4th) The Bears dropping 34 points on this defense is not what I wanted to see a week after the Chiefs couldn’t even get into the red zone. 7. Denver Broncos (11th) They may be in the top 10 of our rankings, but I don’t have a positive thing to say about this franchise at the moment. 8. Cincinnati Bengals (8th) Joe Burrow may be the current MVP frontrunner. 9. Kansas City Chiefs (6th) The worst vibes of any 5-2 team I can think of. 10. Detroit Lions (12th) A huge, gritty win for the Lions and their gritty head coach. 11. New England Patriots (9th) They almost blew it, but divisional games are always tough. A win is a win. 12. Pittsburgh Steelers (10th) This week’s matchup against the Bengals will tell me if the Steelers are for real or not. 13. Green Bay Packers (14th) If Micah Parsons comes back healthy, the NFC North race is the most interesting in football. 14. Los Angeles Rams (16th) Would Aaron Donald have come out of retirement had he known this team would only be .500 after Halloween? 15. New York Giants (17th) The surprising leaders of the NFC Least. 16. Cleveland Browns (15th) Not winning a single game in Pittsburgh since 2003 is objectively crazy. 17. Las Vegas Raiders (22nd) In my opinion, the Raiders are making the smart long-term play by keeping Fernando Mendoza on the bench and riding it out with Kirk Cousins. 18. Baltimore Ravens (13th) Some difficult conversations regarding Lamar Jackson’s long-term future in Baltimore will be happening soon. 19. Carolina Panthers (19th) The Chiefs may have been able to muster a sack against this offensive line. 20. Houston Texans (21st) We’ll see if they can dig themselves out of the hole they’ve created following their bye week. 21. Atlanta Falcons (18th) I repeat—your offense fields Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts—yet you look this anemic? 22. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (20th) I legitimately thought I was being trolled when a friend texted me the Bucs won without completing a pass. How is that possible? 23. Dallas Cowboys (23rd) This team invents hilarious ways to lose football games every week. 24. Washington Commanders (27th) Good job, Jayden Daniels! You won a football game! 25. New Orleans Saints (25th) The first fall guy: the Saints fired their run game coordinator this week. 26. Arizona Cardinals (29th) Spoiler alert! 27. New York Jets (28th) This week should one hundred percent be a “get right” game for the Chiefs. But I’m worried that won’t be the case. 28. Philadelphia Eagles (24th) When I looked ahead at the NFL schedule, I unfortunately saw a lot of Eagles’ games in primetime. 29. Tennessee Titans (31st) They had the Bengals right where I wanted them. Until they let them off the hook. 30. Miami Dolphins (30th) Ollie Gordon has been a good waiver wire addition to a couple of my fantasy teams. But he hurt his real team on Sunday. 31. Indianapolis Colts (26th) I remember the old “Suck for Luck” campaign. But (currently) without a first-round pick in 2027, they’re tanking without any real direction. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (32nd) It’s getting real bleak in Southern California.
author: Dakota Watson

title: Poor situational football dooms Chiefs’ offense against Denver
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second straight game, 28-24, against the Denver Broncos on Sunday, falling to 5-2. The loss propelled Denver to first place in the AFC West standings and should leave the Chiefs scratching their heads. The Chiefs offense was fairly productive all game, with big plays from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second straight game, 28-24, against the Denver Broncos on Sunday, falling to 5-2. The loss propelled Denver to first place in the AFC West standings and should leave the Chiefs scratching their heads. The Chiefs offense was fairly productive all game, with big plays from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and rookie running back Emmet Johnson. Heading into the fourth quarter, the Chiefs led 24-13, but ended the game with a punt, a missed field goal, and a turnover on downs in the final minutes. The Chiefs’ offense outgained Denver by nearly 100 yards, but lingering third-down issues and poor situational football led to critical failures in the game’s largest moments. First possession of the fourth quarter The fourth quarter started well for the Chiefs, with running back Kenneth Walker converting a third down and keeping the clock running. After gaining four yards on a zone-read look on first down, Mahomes barely missed Kelce on second down on a pass that would have put the Chiefs past midfield and in the driver’s seat. On the ensuing third down, Mahomes would go to Johnson, who had a monster game up to that point. This look is somewhere between an option and a rollout pass to Johnson. As it turned into a downfield pass, right tackle Jaylon Moore was deemed too far downfield, and officials called an illegal man downfield penalty; meanwhile, Johnson got as close as he could to a first down. It is hard to know the series of events on the field, but Johnson was ruled down about a foot short of a first, and then Denver head coach Sean Payton declined the penalty, making it fourth-and-1. No review of the play was made, but once Payton declined the penalty, this locked in his decision and would have given the Chiefs a chance to go for it on fourth down. The Chiefs punt unit quickly ran to the field, where the ball was booted into the end zone for a touchback. Nine plays later, the Broncos scored and converted a two-point conversion to cut the deficit to three with less than nine minutes to play. The decision to kick The Chiefs would start their next drive on a positive note as they looked to drive the ball and burn time off the clock. With just under four minutes to play, the Chiefs had picked up another first down, with Walker and Johnson both contributing against a tired-looking Denver defensive front. With the run game finally firing, and Denver on the ropes, the next set of Chiefs plays was baffling. The Chiefs ran a screen to Rashee Rice outside, which, in theory, would strain the legs of the already-tired defense, but Rice made a poor choice to cut back inside instead of following his blocks to the outside and was tackled for only a two-yard gain. On the next play, the Chiefs ran a similar look to Walker. The screen to Walker appears to have been meant to take the defense by surprise, but they quickly swarm around Walker and prevent a larger gain. The play still gained six yards, and it would open up a manageable third-and-two. The next play and ensuing decision would shape the end of the game. The Chiefs’ run game had been ineffective for most of the game, but Walker and Johnson had started to wear down the defense’s tired legs. The Chiefs came out of the gun needing two yards for a first, and they ran a rollout look, but the play quickly broke down. Walker is responsible for the first man off the line, but the edge rusher knocks him back, stopping the rollout. This disrupts Mahomes timing and prevents him from seeing Kelce flashing across the screen. With no one else open, Mahomes takes a costly sack, putting the Chiefs in a situation where going for it on fourth and short is no longer an option. Loyal Andy Reid trotted out Harrison Butker to attempt a 54-yard kick, and it ended up wide right. The Broncos got the ball back in prime field position and scored in two plays to take a four-point lead. The Chiefs got one more shot, and it came down to the red zone. Final drive A monster Johnson kickoff return put the Chiefs in business, and it took them four plays to set up a first-and-goal at the Denver four-yard line. After an eight-yard shovel pass, the Chiefs let the clock run from 1:05 to 35 seconds. A Walker run would move the ball to the one-yard line. Out of timeouts, Denver could only wait, but then the Chiefs used a timeout of their own. On their first crack from the one, the Chiefs went with an old favorite— the corndog —but Denver was ready. With nine seconds to play, the Chiefs tried to run the ball again with Walker, but Denver was ready. Denver’s defensive line pinches down, and a free runner comes through at the line to stuff Walker for no gain. On the next play, it appeared that the Chiefs had won, but a penalty on Moore wiped it away and set up a fourth-and-6. On the game’s final play, Mahomes would take a sack on a poorly designed look. The play was poorly protected, and none of the Chiefs’ receivers found any daylight againt the Broncos’ man coverage. The bottom line There is more than one reason that led to this loss, but the poor situational football was a large culprit for the offenses implosion late in the game. The Chiefs short yardage conversions have become an issue, and there is a path to succsuess, but it would involve the team doing something they have not done in over seven years. The quarterback sneak is one of the most efficient plays in the history of the game, and the Chies blatant refusal to do so has cost the team due to a freak accident. Even if the team decides to execute the plays with Mahomes on the sideline, backup quarterback Justin Fields should be more than capable of getting the job done. Justin Fields converting 3rd and 4th shorts (1-2) the last 3 years. Might be worth a shot for the Chiefs to try this option to solve the short yardage woes pic.twitter.com/FBtsan5lAB — Billy M (@BillyM_91) November 2, 2026 The run game was bottled up, but the decsion to run a rollout look leading to a sack was inexcusable, especially when there was a hot hand like Johnson ready to go. Running the ball takes comitment, but if the rock is pounded enough times it will eventually break. Relying on one of the worst reciever rooms in the NFL to produce consistently in key moments is not an option. The decsion to allow Butker kick, to only put the team up six points may be one of the worst of Reid’s career. The inability to score from the one yard line against a gassed defense with no timeouts, and relying on old tricks like “corndog” that half the field for a wizard like Mahomes can no longer be accpeted, especially when the main target runs out of bounds. Starting one of the worst interor offensvie lienmen in the NFL inexplicably for the second time this season can also no longer be tolerated, especially when his body of work provides no evidence he has earned a stating spot, and his backup this week did not play with little context from the organization. The 2026 Chiefs have the offensive talent to remain one of the leagues best units, and they showd what they are capable of multiple times through the course of the game. The key situations, and bad decisions on critical downs are what seperates them from a two game division lead, and the race they will be in with the Broncos the rest of the season. The wrongs can me made right, but a plan needs to be put in place for these short yardage situations, what to do with Butker, and how the offensive line will look. November is here, and as the schedule gets tougher, the games get bigger. It will be worth watching to see how the Chiefs perform as the pressure builds.
author: Caleb James

He has also been cleared to return to football after ankle surgery in August. Johnson had ankle surgery in August and served his six-game suspension while a free agent. He signed with the Tennessee Titans this offseason before he was suspended and suffered the ankle injury in late August. Six lessons from Week 8: Bears emerge as top-tier Super Bowl contenders, Chiefs must address glaring flaws | CBS Sports The Chiefs have multiple issues to fix, and the trade deadline must be the time to fix them In a vacuum, the Chiefs’ loss to the Broncos was just that: one loss. Yes, it was a disappointing one, given the chance to put a vice grip on the division, but it’s just one loss. In the big picture, this game revealed multiple significant issues — issues that will cost the Chiefs when a loss isn’t just a game lost, but a season lost. These are the three things I’m quite worried about: Andy Reid’s continued game mismanagement Short-yardage issues Absolutely no downfield presence Jets vs. Chiefs prediction: Odds, expert picks, QB matchup, injury update, betting trends, and stats | NBC Sports Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Around the NF L Bills release C.J. Gardner-Johnson after one-game spitting suspension | ESPN Garrett was the prize of the Rams’ offseason, when they traded Pro Bowl outside linebacker Jared Verse as well as first-, second- and third-round draft picks to the Cleveland Browns to land the two-time Defensive Player of the Year. Fresh off breaking the NFL’s single-season record with 23 sacks, Garrett arrived to the Rams and helped entice Aaron Donald to end his two-year retirement and return to play alongside him. The two have yet to share the line together in a game, as Donald missed the season opener while ramping up. That time is coming soon. When it does, the Rams will become the first team in NFL history to have two players with 100 career sacks and a 20-sack season on the same defensive line. New Cowboys Trade Rumors Reveal Plans for George Pickens Ahead of NFL Deadline | Bleacher Report The Dallas Cowboys are 3-5 and look nothing like a legitimate contender. George Pickens is playing on the franchise tag and may go elsewhere during the upcoming offseason. Logic dictates there could be a trade in the making before the NFL’s Nov. 10 deadline. But that doesn’t seem to be the case. “I was told there’s nothing here and that it is not happening,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported during an appearance on Tuesday’s episode of The Pat McAfee Show . “… As of right now, literally nothing there. … The way the Cowboys’ division is, it is wide open. I would be surprised to see them trading a playmaker.” Week 9 NFL MVP tracker: Can Caleb Williams join Joe Montana in making history? | NFL.com History says he’s a long shot simply because of those missed games. In the post NFL-AFL merger era (since 1970) in non-strike-shortened seasons, only one player has missed three games and still won the NFL MVP award: Joe Montana in 1989. “Joe Cool” battled through various injuries that season, missing Weeks 6, 8, and 15, and portions of others. Every single other MVP missed two or fewer tilts. Most missed zero. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Numbers Never Lie: 5 Chiefs stats to know from loss to Broncos A week after running just 12 plays from under center, a season-low mark, the Chiefs’ offense re-established its identity in Denver and tied the season-high number of 28 plays run from under center; the team matched it against the Miami Dolphins in Week 3. Patrick Mahomes also attempted the most passes from under center in any game this season, dropping back 14 times. However, Kansas City averaged just 4.5 yards per play from under center, the second-lowest rate of the year behind the poor showing in Seattle. It may not have been the most efficient game, but the offense looked much better than it did in Seattle, and getting back to what worked through the first five games of the year felt like a big factor in that. title: For the Rams, one player leaves as another enters?
summary: It is awful news that Jaylen Watson is out for the year, and you have to wish the player all the best. On the flip side, Myles Garrett is coming back for the Los Angeles Rams, right? Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 and he’s practicing this week, but no announcement has been made that […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 10: Jaylen Watson #35 and Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams are seen during a Los Angeles Rams NFL media availability at Marvel Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is awful news that Jaylen Watson is out for the year, and you have to wish the player all the best. On the flip side, Myles Garrett is coming back for the Los Angeles Rams, right? Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 and he’s practicing this week, but no announcement has been made that he’ll be playing this Sunday or next Sunday, but unless there is a setback, the expectation is that he will be playing. Eventually. For Watson, his season ends just as the Rams were hoping to really get their year rolling. Watson has been tremendous, but he’s been nursing a shoulder injury since earlier this year (at least since their game against the Denver Broncos), and at a certain point, it is better to shut a player down than risk further injury. It’s better for the player, and the Rams expect to have Watson another couple seasons, so let him heal. Still, the news is a bummer for the person, and for the team, to put it lightly. In other news Quentin Lake was talking some smack on Justin Herbert. So there’s that. Rams CB Jaylen Watson is out for season after shoulder surgery. Myles Garrett returns to practice (houstonchronicle) “But Watson missed a game earlier this season after dislocating his shoulder, and the two-time Super Bowl champion hurt that shoulder again in the Rams’ 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday. “That’s a big blow, a bummer for him,” McVay said. “He’s been such a stud for us. He wanted to be able to play through it, but just kind of understanding the totality of it all, it was recommended for him to get that surgery, and he’ll be on IR. He’s been awesome, and whenever he gets back next year, we’ll be better. He’s been everything and that much more that we’d hoped.” Rams CB Jaylen Watson is out for season after shoulder surgery. Myles Garrett returns to practice (houstonchronicle) “But Garrett was in practice with his teammates for the first time since his zero-tackle Rams debut in Australia nearly two months ago. The two-time AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year had knee surgery and missed seven games. McVay isn’t certain whether Garrett will be ready to play at Washington, saying the Rams will make that decision later in the week. Garrett will take about half of the practice reps on Wednesday to see how his body responds. “It’s exciting,” McVay said. “It’s great to be able to get him back out there. Just trying to stay in the moment, one day at a time.” Rams star safety cooks Justin Herbert for ‘throwing deli meat’ in Chargers loss (nypost) “I mean, [Herbert] was throwing deli meat out there. He’s seeing ghosts, I’m not going to lie,” Lake said with a laugh during his appearance on the “St. Brown Podcast.” “Bro, I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were getting a couple,” he added. Herbert has been the butt of many jokes this season — and for good reason. But it’s one thing for fans to roast Herbert about his mediocre performances. It’s another thing for one of his peers to do so on a podcast, where the whole world can hear about it.“ Rams lose Pro Bowl cornerback for the season with news of shoulder surgery (sports.yahoo) “”Unfortunately, Jaylen Watson has to get surgery on his shoulder. He will be out for the year. That’s a big one,” said Rams’ head coach Sean McVay on Wednesday afternoon. “He’s been such a stud for us. He wanted to be able to play through it, but just understanding the totality of it all and some of the different things, it was recommended that he get that surgery.” McVay added that Watson will be put on IR for the rest of the year. Watson aggravated the dislocated right shoulder he suffered against the Denver Broncos earlier this season during the Rams’ win against the Los Angeles Chargers this past weekend.“ With no-huddle offense working so well, could Rams use it more? (ramswire) “The numbers do not do the situation justice in terms of how much the offense benefited from going at a faster pace. With their no-huddle approach, the Rams ran five plays on their final drive of the half, going 66 yards, with Matthew Stafford throwing four completions on four attempts before Kyren Williams ran in the score. The Rams caught the Chargers struggling to organize defensively, with Tutu Atwell burning his defender for a 40-yard gain, setting the Rams up in the red zone. Before that drive, the Rams had five other drives, and they were awful. Three points, no first downs, and their only score came after an interception by Quentin Lake that set the Rams up in the red zone.“ Rams May Be Better Equipped to Overcome Jaylen Watson Injury Than Expected (si.com) “With Watson out, the Rams will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in his spot. While there is certainly a difference in being a rotational player and playing full time, the Rams have gotten good production out of Wallace and Forbes this season. “I think those guys have done really well,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Jimmy Lake has done such a great job really with those corners as a whole group. Josh has played a lot of snaps. I thought ‘E-Forbes’ really played well last week. Both of those guys have been tapped in. They’ve been ready to step up and it seems like there have been a lot of games that we’ve had our top corners get banged up and they’ve played a lot more.” Rams stars get emotional over Jaylen Watson’s devastating injury: ‘We’re going to do it for him’ (sports.yahoo) “Linebacker Byron Young went one step further, dedicating the remainder of the season to Watson, injured defensive tackle Poona Ford and the other teammates whose seasons have ended prematurely. “I hate to lose a guy like that, but we’re going to keep going,” Young said. “We’re going to do it for him.” Watson’s season is over, but his influence isn’t. Lake believes the veteran’s football intelligence and leadership can continue helping the secondary from the sidelines during his recovery.“ 3 things for the Rams to know about the Commanders (ramswire) “Washington may not win, but it won’t be for a lack of trying Washington’s effort level this season has been unreal, and for a team that has been struggling, there’s a reason why head coach Dan Quinn’s seat isn’t as hot as others in the NFL. The Commanders play with a passion and an attitude that goes above and beyond. It feels like there’s a real belief within the organization behind what they’re about, and if they can clean up their on-field operation – especially with penalties – they could turn the corner.“ Rams-Commanders injury report: McDuffie, Curl DNP to start Week 9 (ramswire) “The Rams released their first injury report of Week 9 on Wednesday and a total of 12 players were listed on it, five of them being non-participants. McDuffie did not practice, nor did Colby Parkinson, Kam Curl or Joe Cardona. McDuffie injured his back last week against the Chargers, Parkinson is still dealing with a rib injury and Curl picked up a foot injury. There is some good news, though. Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Ronnie Rivers were all designated to return and were back at practice. None of them have been activated from IR yet but it’s a good sign that they’re practicing again. Rivers was a full participant, and Garrett and Ferguson were both limited.“ Commanders dealing with injuries on defensive line ahead of matchup with Rams (nbcwashington) “Defensive linemen Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne were both placed on injured reserve, with their seasons likely both over, coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday. Kinlaw had knee surgery, while Payne has a foot injury. And yet, Washington’s defensive line has been a mostly consistent unit so far this year, even as the defense has had issues elsewhere through the course of two months. “I just think the mentality and…

title: Have faith in Josh Wallace
summary: In early 1916 Calvin Coolidge stood before the Massachusetts state senate and delivered an oration that would later follow him into the White House: “Have Faith in Massachusetts”. Not faith in some distant authority. Deciding to not leave the future up to an outside rescue. Instead, trusting in the people and the existing institutions. The […]
full_text: In early 1916 Calvin Coolidge stood before the Massachusetts state senate and delivered an oration that would later follow him into the White House: “Have Faith in Massachusetts” . Not faith in some distant authority. Deciding to not leave the future up to an outside rescue. Instead, trusting in the people and the existing institutions. The line has been flattened into a cliche over time, but the original point was concise and simple. Stop looking outward for a solution when the answer lies within the same building. The Los Angeles Rams are about to find out whether the same idea applies to their cornerback room. Prized free agent signing Jaylen Watson exited last Sunday’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers with a shoulder injury. He has now been ruled out for the remainder of the season . The secondary has been one of the more defined bright spots across the roster this year. Their future performance is no longer guaranteed. The question now is who steps into the void? And the Rams seem to be in good hands with Josh Wallace, who has played often recently due to both Watson and Trent McDuffie battling injuries. Wallace has not been asked to carry a starting role for long. He was an obvious weak point on the team filling in for Quentin Lake last season. It has been a different story so far in 2026. Across the NFL for corners with at least 20% of the maximum snaps to-date, Wallace currently ranks 10th at the position. That is effectively top five when you need at least two corners on the field at all times, and it’s typical for defenses to deploy three at a time more often than not. The unfortunate truth is that Wallace ranked eighth. McDuffie is second. Wallace may still be a step back, although in a situational role he has proven capable. But at least with the numbers we can go off of, Wallace has been stellar by any standard. Opposing quarterbacks have thrown the ball into his coverage 32 times this season, according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). Wallace has allowed 17 receptions for 126 yards (77 after the catch) without a touchdown, one interception, a pass breakup, and a passer rating of just 49.7. One area of concern for Wallace is the fact he’s been grabby. Officials have flagged him in coverage six times already this season. It’s an outcome worth monitoring as holds onto a starting job for the foreseeable future. For comparison, McDuffie has committed four penalties while Watson has just two. The silver lining to this data point is the fact we’ve already seen more of Wallace than either of McDuffie or Watson. He has sneakily played more often in coverage than both of LA’s blockbuster offseason additions. The fact we haven’t noticed should tell us all we need to know. Season to-date snap counts: McDuffie: 362 total; 200 in coverage Watson: 381; 214 Wallace: 377; 245 Coolidge’s argument in 1916 was not that his state was perfect. It was that Massachusetts already possessed the tools to handle its own adversity should it stop treating every difficulty as a crisis that required outside intervention. The Rams’ cornerback situation following Watson’s injury is far from perfect as well. With the trade deadline looming, the team must have faith in Wallace rather than parting with future draft resources in exchange for a short-term patch. Whether that trust is rewarded will be demonstrated in the coming weeks. Wallace will either handle his new starting role or he won’t. The Rams do not control that outcome. They do control whether or not he is given a chance as the solution. Have faith in Josh Wallace. Have faith not because the secondary is suddenly fixed by his presence but because the alternative is pretending the Rams’ were not prepared for this scenario. The answer may lie in-house this time.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams place Jaylen Watson on season-ending IR
summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without starting cornerback Jaylen Watson for the rest of the year after placing him on season-ending IR with a shoulder injury on Wednesday. The free agent signing who was added to fix one of the Rams’ biggest defensive weaknesses will have surgery on said shoulder and miss the rest […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams will be without starting cornerback Jaylen Watson for the rest of the year after placing him on season-ending IR with a shoulder injury on Wednesday. The free agent signing who was added to fix one of the Rams’ biggest defensive weaknesses will have surgery on said shoulder and miss the rest of 2026. Watson was injured in Week 8’s win over the L.A. Chargers, looking as though he was unable to even lift his arm after going down. In a season full of bad news for the Rams, the hits keep coming. 𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚: Rams’ CB Jaylen Watson will undergo shoulder surgery and miss the rest of the 2026 season. Big loss in the LA secondary. pic.twitter.com/Ib7jI1ynbI — JPA (@jasrifootball) November 4, 2026 The Rams signed Watson to a three-year, $51 million contract in the offseason and paired him with former Chiefs teammate Trent McDuffie to fix L.A.’s issues at cornerback from last season. Watson had 24 tackles and an interception over seven games prior to injury. The team will now need to turn to their reinforcements like Emmanuel Forbes for the foreseeable future. At least the Rams do hope to get back Myles Garrett soon , as he began practicing this week. The Rams have already lost Kobie Turner and Poona Ford to IR, while Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 and McDuffie has missed time as well. Aaron Donald has not played at 100% all weeks either. Matthew Stafford has elbow soreness and Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring. Terrance Ferguson just started practicing again. Is there a power station nearby and we don’t know about it? The Rams play the Commanders this Sunday, but without Watson.

title: NFL coaches on hot seat: Safe or  fire
summary: The NFL regular season is approaching its halfway point, and for some head coaches, the pressure to turn things around is becoming impossible to ignore. With playoff hopes fading for several teams, questions about leadership, accountability and the direction of struggling franchises are beginning to take center stage. The NFL’s coaching carousel is always one […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers watches fourth quarter game action against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL regular season is approaching its halfway point, and for some head coaches, the pressure to turn things around is becoming impossible to ignore. With playoff hopes fading for several teams, questions about leadership, accountability and the direction of struggling franchises are beginning to take center stage. The NFL’s coaching carousel is always one of the league’s biggest storylines, but the decisions made over the next several weeks could determine which coaches survive and which organizations decide it’s time for a change. Some coaches may still have enough time to salvage their seasons, while others are running out of opportunities to prove they’re the right person for the job. In this edition of “Safe or Fire,” we’ll evaluate coaches across the league whose seats are heating up, examining whether they deserve another opportunity or if their respective teams should begin looking elsewhere. Jim Harbaugh The Chargers are 0-7 and Harbaugh is 0-10 in his last 10 games. It’s been tough to watch this year especially as Los Angeles had playoff expectations (and favorable preseason Super Bowl odds). Herbert looks lost for a coach known for being a quarterback whisperer. The Chargers have not started 0-6 since 2000… When Jim Harbaugh was their quarterback 🤯 pic.twitter.com/F5ZDYfQOVo — Bussin' With The Boys (@BussinWTB) October 19, 2026 Verdict: Fired Aaron Glenn The Jets are 5-20 under Aaron Glenn. It’s almost a guarantee that a new head coach will be hired in 2027 with the team having three first round picks and likely to spend one on a new quarterback. Aaron Glenn also has seen him teams outscored significantly with under 2 minutes left in the first half. Stuff like that shows you are outcoached weekly. #Jets HC Aaron Glenn was asked today about the viral stat that New York has been outscored 107-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under his watch: “We're trying. We do a two-minute jog through on Wednesday and then we come back and we have a live two-minute on Thursday… https://t.co/I6NkEsLRfv pic.twitter.com/IiR6qynA54 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 26, 2026 Verdict: Fired Demeco Ryans There is no reason that the Houston Texans shouldn’t be succeeding this year. The Texans did not really lose anything on defense yet the Texans are 2-5 despite averaging 23.5 points per game (15th in NFL). It’s not the offense this time, it’s the defense. DeMeco Ryans taking accountability for the Texans 2-5 start: “It all starts with me first and foremost. As a competitor, we’re not getting the job done. Point blank, period. That’s it.” DeMeco also questioned whether the team is preparing the right way throughout the week,… pic.twitter.com/B56n8QdOrL — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) October 26, 2026 Verdict: Safe Shane Steichen The Colts getting blown out in Week 8 to the Jaguars will probably be the final nail in the coffin for Steichen’s tenure in Indianapolis. Chris Ballard was already fired mid-season. Steichen will probably finish the year but then he is gone. Verdict: Fired Robert Saleh The Titans are 1-7 in their first year with Saleh. They decided to trade away Jeffery Simmons because management likely sees this as a rebuild year and way to give Cam Ward a supporting cast. I think Saleh will get another year in 2027 since the team is focused on adding picks rather than winning now. Verdict: Safe Dan Quinn Washington had a fortunate run to the NFC Championship in 2024. But since then, Quinn’s Commanders are 7-16-1. Jayden Daniels needs an offensive minded coach to get his career on track. The disastrous ending against the New York Giants in Week 5 sums up Quinn’s last 24+ games. The Commanders will fire HC Dan Quinn if they do not start winning games soon, per @RapSheet He’s got the hottest seat out of any head coach in the league, it would appear. pic.twitter.com/gEOZ54Rb9p — JPA (@jasrifootball) October 26, 2026 Verdict: Fired Nick Sirianni Here’s the story on Sirianni. When the offensive coordinator is the scapegoat in 2025, there is no one else to blame now for the offensive woes. It falls squarely on Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts. Sirianni relied on a young and cheap roster in his first few seasons. But now players are getting paid and the team can’t hide Hurts’s limitations. IT IS TIME FOR THE PHILADELPHIA #EAGLES TO FIRE HEAD COACH NICK SIRIANNI. This entire season has been an absolute DISASTER for Philadelphia, and something needs to change: • Started 2-0 and have now lost FIVE straight games. • Embarrassed 38-21 by the division-rival Dallas… pic.twitter.com/9ovvxWcO2n — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 27, 2026 Verdict: Fired Todd Bowles Bowles is 38-38 in four plus seasons with the Buccaneers. With the NFC South being so weak, going .500 is pretty disappointing. Verdict: Fired Brian Schottenheimer Dallas has Texas sized expectations. With Brian Schottenheimer failing to address its defensive woes in two straight seasons, you wonder how patient Jerry Jones will be? The bad collapses in Week 3 and Week 8 are concerning along with a dud to a Bucs team without Baker Mayfield in Week 5. Verdict: Fired

title: Rams’ upcoming opponent trades former starting QB
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, guaranteeing that he won’t be the starter when the Los Angeles Rams face them next week. The Rams lost to Brissett’s Cardinals 18-16 just 17 days ago, but now Arizona is turning to Gardner Minshew for the rest of the season with Carson Beck […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals are trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, guaranteeing that he won’t be the starter when the Los Angeles Rams face them next week. The Rams lost to Brissett’s Cardinals 18-16 just 17 days ago, but now Arizona is turning to Gardner Minshew for the rest of the season with Carson Beck as the backup. The Ravens are in need of a quarterback after losing both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in a matter of one half of football. Baltimore will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday, but Brissett could be in line to start soon. Trade: The #Ravens are finalizing a trade for former #AZCardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, per me and @AdamSchefter , filling the void left by the injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler “Snoop” Huntley. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend. pic.twitter.com/RWhT1LQ2fc — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 4, 2026 It was only October 18 when Brissett helped the Cardinals upset the Rams and send L.A.’s season from a couple of understandable losses to good teams to losing to Arizona. Brissett struggled so badly against the Cowboys defense on Sunday that Mike LaFleur benched him for Minshew in the second half, and then Minshew led the Cardinals to an overtime win. Minshew will now be starting for his sixth career NFL team. The Cardinals had to give Brissett a raise this season — up to $21 million — because he wanted to be paid like a starter. Predictably, the team made yet another dumb mistake at the position and expected a career backup to help them win, which has not been the case at all. They should have traded Brissett before the season if he wanted a raise. Now the team turns to Minshew and he’s set to start against the Rams next weekend, after Arizona faces the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. The Seahawks also made a change at QB, announcing that Sam Darnold will be ruled out with a quad injury and Drew Lock will start against Arizona. The NFC West is changing fast.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: George Pickens would be a wild trade swing for Rams
summary: If the Los Angeles Rams really want to make a splash, they should call the Dallas Cowboys about George Pickens. The problem is the cost, while the upside is obvious. When guys like Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and Jeffrey Simmons are suddenly joining title contenders in your own conference, it feels underwhelming if the best […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images If the Los Angeles Rams really want to make a splash, they should call the Dallas Cowboys about George Pickens. The problem is the cost, while the upside is obvious. When guys like Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and Jeffrey Simmons are suddenly joining title contenders in your own conference, it feels underwhelming if the best option you have is to effectively promote from within , even if that’s more sensible. If the Rams want to maximize their aggressiveness (and their championship window), a swing for George Pickens would add major pop to this offense. If Les Snead can convince Jerry Jones to trade him, that is. The Cowboys have yet to concede that their season is lost or that Pickens isn’t part of their future despite a franchise tag. “I've also been told (George) Pickens remains content in Dallas and doesn't want to be moved, nor does Dallas plan to trade him.” – @JFowlerESPN — SleeperCowboys (@SleeperCowboys) November 4, 2026 Pickens is the only WR trade worth it There are plenty of good options when it comes to available wide receivers this year. Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars is the biggest name on the market, while Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts is a name that’s been gaining steam as that franchise goes into tank mode for the rest of the season. There are also some slightly less high-profile options, like the Cleveland Browns’ Jerry Jeudy . But if the Rams want to go all-in on the biggest move possible, like they did repeatedly all offseason, Pickens is as close as they can get to adding a truly transformative player. Pickens is on pace for what would be his third 1,000-yard season in his five-year career. He currently has 533 yards and a pair of touchdowns on 39 receptions this year. He’s been good for the Cowboys, whose offense (seventh in the NFL in scoring) is hardly the biggest reason behind their 3-5 record. 2025 George Pickens. pic.twitter.com/OVgrBFy2Vi — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) August 5, 2026 Their division, the NFC East, has also been a massive disappointment this year and is still wide open halfway through the season. Dallas certainly doesn’t have to move him. Still, speculation is increasing from a variety of outlets that Pickens could be trade bait ahead of next week’s deadline. Every team in the league that needs offensive help should be checking on his availability. ESPN’s Ben Solak believes that Dallas can’t afford Pickens next year and that a loss in Week 9 will force their hands : “I understand all of the reporting out of Dallas. The Cowboys don’t intend to move anyone, and they’re still competing for the NFC East in 2026. It would be out of character for Jones to move Pickens at this stage. But some things are so painfully obvious that I have to ignore the public PR and read between the lines. If Pickens and Dallas have no long-term future, why wait for the compensatory draft pick in 2028? Why go through all the necessary rigamarole to preserve that comp pick when they can get a guaranteed third-round pick in a trade now — and likely more! The Chiefs would do it. I’m calling my shot here: The Cowboys lose to the Colts in Week 9, and at 3-6, Pickens is frustrated enough that the Cowboys make a trade before next Tuesday.“ The Rams can’t afford to fall behind in the NFC arms race. Three other Super Bowl contenders in the conference have added All-Pro caliber talent in the last couple of weeks, including the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks in the NFC West, plus the Chicago Bears with their Jeffrey Simmons addition as well. The Rams, and other should-be contenders in the conference, for that matter, are only going to make their title quest more difficult if they wait this out. Compensation and salary cap fit are important considerations, per usual. They’re likely directly tied together in this hypothetical, too. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag, so he’s a free agent after the season ends. An acquiring team likely isn’t signing him to a long-term deal right away, which will lower the cost. Or just hear me out… #Rams fans want more than one catch for 15 yards a game out of their WR2. Call it greedy but Davante is injured, Puka has been playing injured, even Whittington was iffy to play this week. This is just thinking logical. Which is why we also wanted to draft a… https://t.co/Zcc0HdFsiv — JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) November 2, 2026 In order to make his cap hit fit into the Rams’ available space, they could also offer a better draft pick next year to entice the Cowboys to retain more of his salary, though that likely means L.A. would go into the spring with no picks on either Day 1 or Day 2 of the draft. This is a bold hypothetical, there’s no doubt about that. If it’s even remotely realistic, it will obviously also come with a hefty price. If the Rams are going to trade for any wide receiver though, I’d rather the player be worth the risk of a high draft pick than so safe that he doesn’t move the needle at all.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Rams try another change on special teams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams released Alex Bachman as they continue to try and figure out their special teams. They released Xavier Smith earlier this year. They’re currently using Brandon McManus for field goals and Joshua Karty for kickoffs. The Rams are trying to adjust their special teams. Are their changes working? Not yet because they […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 01: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Alex Bachman (11) returns a kickoff during the NFL game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on November 01, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams released Alex Bachman as they continue to try and figure out their special teams. They released Xavier Smith earlier this year. They’re currently using Brandon McManus for field goals and Joshua Karty for kickoffs. The Rams are trying to adjust their special teams. Are their changes working? Not yet because they keep making changes. So far, McManus has been perfect, but will he deliver in the clutch? How long will Karty be used for kickoffs? Who will be the next return man for L.A.? Will the Rams go with someone who will just catch or someone with upside on the return? So many questions for the special teams unit, but as of now, Bachman won’t be one of them, and the Rams are still trying to find answers. Rams Release Alex Bachman as Special Teams Overhaul Continues (si.com) “The Los Angeles Rams have made another change on special teams as they head into Week 9. On Tuesday, the Rams released wide receiver and kickoff/punt returner Alex Bachman. Over the past several weeks, the Rams have been working to make improvements to their special teams unit, and Bachman being released is the latest indication of that. Earlier this season, the Rams turned to Bachman after they released wide receiver Xavier Smith from the same role. While Bachman fielded punts without issue, he didn’t offer much as a returner. Among players with at least five punt returns this season, Bachman averaged just 5.2 yards per return, which ranked 31st. At some point, the Rams needed to raise the bar from ‘just fielding punts’. Bachman averaged just 22.9 yards per kick return, ranking 62nd out of 75 qualifying returners.“ A newly added name to the NFL trade deadline rumor mill is the perfect target for the Los Angeles Rams (sports.yahoo) “So allow me to throw a name out there. New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore makes a lot of sense as a potential addition for the Rams. Los Angeles lost defensive tackle Puna Ford for the rest of the season. Barmore could certainly help the Rams replace some of what they lost in the middle of their defense – and he’s reportedly available. Why Christian Barmore makes sense for the Los Angeles Rams Barmore is a disruptive presence up front, and he brings plenty of size to the position. We’ve seen the kind of impact a disruptive defensive interior group is capable of with Seattle’s deep playoff run last year. The Rams have Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, and Kobie Turner (injured reserve) – but Barmore is built a little differently. At 6-foot-5, 315 pounds, Barmore still has disruptive twitch in his game to complement to others on the Rams’ front.“ Ian Rapoport shares update on Myles Garrett’s outlook for Week 9 (ramswire) “McVay stopped short of saying Garrett will play against the Washington Commanders on Sunday afternoon, but he isn’t ruling it out, either. On Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network shared an update on Garrett and said that once he gets on the field, “it should all happen quick.” He added that “this week is in play” for Sunday’s game but the Rams will need to see how Garrett responds to the week of practice. Myles Garrett is an interesting one,” Rapoport said. “I thought he was coming back last week. Just didn’t get to a point where he could feel comfortable enough on the knee, so it was like, all right, don’t rush it, stretch run, be ready this week. What I don’t know – I was told when he gets on the field for practice that it should all happen quick, so I think this week is in play, but we need to see how he actually responds. I think it’s finally, after like two months, in a pretty good place.” ESPN analyst lays out hypothetical trade for Rams to acquire Colts WR (ramswire) “Josh Downs requested a trade from the Colts and could be dealt before next Tuesday’s deadline. ESPN’s Ben Solak predicted some trades that he thinks “might” happen based on fit and logic, not inside information. One of them was the Rams acquiring Downs and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Colts for a 2028 third-rounder.“ Patriots Quietly Make Move for Ex-Rams Linebacker Before Packers Game (sports.yahoo) “The Patriots are signing linebacker Elias Neal to their practice squad, less than a week after the Los Angeles Rams released him. The move was reported, by ESPN reporter Mike Reiss, who cited Neal’s agent, Sean Stellato. The Patriots had not officially announced the addition as of Tuesday afternoon. New England’s linebacker room leans on starters Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss, and Neal arrives with a résumé built almost entirely on special teams.“ Rams Get Matthew Stafford Update Amid ‘Interesting’ Myles Garrett Situation (heavy.com) “Despite the bottom-line positivity, Rapoport’s update on Stafford adds to the nebulous nature of the situation. Rams head coach Sean McVay did not provide much clarity following the reports. “He’s had some soreness there,” McVay told reporters on November 2. “I think he’d be better equipped, once you guys talk to him, to answer that. I can’t attest to stuff that I’m not necessarily aware of.” Rams boast hidden gem as LA heats up ahead of Commanders matchup (nypost) “Corum has been an overlooked piece for some time now, but the 25-year-old made sure he was remembered against the Chargers. During the first half, the crosstown rivals both looked willing to give the other a victory. Then, everything changed for the Rams in the third quarter when Corum’s 23-yard touchdown extended the lead to 17-9. The Michigan product tallied 73 yards on 11 carries against the Chargers and routinely made defenders miss. While Kyren Williams is the Rams’ primary running back, Corum has looked just as efficient — and at times better. Corum led the team in rushing yards, despite logging five fewer carries than Williams on Sunday.“ BEST PHOTOS: Blake Corum’s 23-yard touchdown, Wesley Bailey’s strip-sack & more | Best of the Rams’ Week 8 victory over the Chargers (therams.com) “The Los Angeles Rams hosted the Chargers at SoFi Stadium for a crosstown battle in Week 8. Browse through photos from the Rams’ 24-9 victory, including running back Blake Corum’s 23-yard touchdown, outside linebacker Wesley Bailey’s strip-sack, and more.” Rams cut PR Alex Bachman, place RB on IR and make 3 other roster moves (ramswire) “Bachman replaced Xavier Smith after he was waived, but he hasn’t exactly been an upgrade as a return specialist. He’s returned nine punts for 47 yards and 13 kickoffs for 298 yards, struggling to make defenders miss and pick up yardage. To take his place on the active roster, the Rams signed Cam Lampkin from the practice squad. Lampkin has been promoted from the practice squad twice but will now be a member of the 53-man roster. Nyzier Fourqurean was signed back to the practice squad after being released last week and running back Dean Connors was placed on injured reserve.“ Matthew Stafford’s Wife Kelly Demands Answers From NFL Over Rams Situation (si.com) “Los Angeles visits the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 15, before its Week 11 bye. However, because the Rams host the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25 — the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game — they’ll get just 10 days between games instead of the usual 14. Kelly Stafford is Not Happy With the NFL Scheduling On Tuesday, Kelly took to her Instagram story to call out the league for doing her husband’s team dirty with their bye week scheduling. “@NFL Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week,” Kelly wrote. “Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap.” Comment of the day: Feed post(s) of the day:
