title: Las Vegas Raiders playoff hopes depend on the defense
summary: It’s no secret that the Las Vegas Raiders offense is putting up numbers. At the midway point of the season, the Raiders currently sit at 9th in the conference standings. With a 4-4 overall record, ranking second in total points and sixth in points per game, the Raiders can be in the playoff mix, but […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret that the Las Vegas Raiders offense is putting up numbers. At the midway point of the season, the Raiders currently sit at 9th in the conference standings. With a 4-4 overall record, ranking second in total points and sixth in points per game, the Raiders can be in the playoff mix, but the defense must get better fast. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard must find a way to evolve or open his playbook. His Raiders defense ranks 31st in points allowed, 31st in rushing yards allowed, 30th in passing yards, 24th in passing yards per game and 30th in total yards. Ugly stretch Over the last five weeks of the season, the Raiders are allowing an average of 35.2 points per game. Four out of the five games they were been beaten by: the Kansas City Chiefs, the Super Bowl runner-ups New England PatriotsBecoming the 85’ Bears or the 00’ Ravens isn’t necessary or likely to happen. Getting opponents scoring down to 25 points per game will provide the proper offset to the offense’s production. Making winning much more obtainable consistently. The Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams. The good news is they were able to fly into New York and win a shootout against the Jets. However, the defense has put some ugly football on film and in a copycat league, they have been exposed over and over again. Surrendering 822 yards rushing during that stretch and nearly 164.4 yards per game. The seven rushing touchdowns allowed aren’t horrible, considering the yardage given. Defending the pass has been an issue at the line of scrimmage and the back end of the defense alike. In the last five games, the defense has produced eight sacks and 26 hits on the quarterback. A far cry from the Hellhounds, which started the season with 10 sacks in three games. Turnovers are supposed to come in bunches, and they most certainly did at the beginning of the season. Since week 3, however, the Raiders defense has only produced two forced fumbles and recoveries and three interceptions. Things to build on It hasn’t all been bad; there are definitely things the team can hang their hats on. Raiders’ defense has amassed 18 sacks and 36 tackles for loss, 6 interceptions, and 12 forced fumbles this season. Should they be able to improve on being T-2nd in turnover margin +5, T-6th in interceptions (6), T-1st In Fumbles (12), with their 13 total takeaways being 3rd best in the league, they can offset the tremendous amount of yards being given up. Not allowing drives to extend remains the biggest opportunity to make a difference. The Raiders are 21st in 3rd down conversion (41.7%), 20th in 4th down conversion (57.1%), 5th most in defensive penalties, 6th most in penalty yards and T-4th in first downs by penalty. Maxx Crosby ranks 3rd in the league in pressures (26), but his 3.0 sacks this year are average. Although Malcolm Koonce and Kwity Paye also have 3.0 sacks each, their pressure production of 10 and 9, respectively, leaves more to be desired. What needs to happen Playing less soft zone coverage and running more twists and stunts against basic fronts will help a bunch. Simplify things for the young defensive backs; allow them to make their mistakes and learn. Resume attacking aggressively. This personnel group is much better at attacking than they are at waiting for something to happen. Good things happened when Leonard pressed issues. Becoming the 85’ Bears or the 00’ Ravens isn’t necessary or likely to happen. Getting opponents scoring down to 25 points per game will provide the proper offset to the offense’s production. Making winning much more obtainable consistently. Lining up the Raiders to be able to capitalize on their offensive success and make a run at a wildcard berth in the second half of the season.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders release early-season TD machine Cody White
summary: A few weeks ago, wide receiver Cody White was the Las Vegas Raiders’ secret weapon. Now, he’s out of a job. The team released the veteran on Wednesday after as they needed room to activate reserve tight end Carter Runyon from the injured reserve. The Raiders had until Wednesday to either put Runyon on the […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images A few weeks ago, wide receiver Cody White was the Las Vegas Raiders’ secret weapon. Now, he’s out of a job. The team released the veteran on Wednesday after as they needed room to activate reserve tight end Carter Runyon from the injured reserve. The Raiders had until Wednesday to either put Runyon on the 53-man roster or shelve him for the rest of the season. Runyon was hurt in training camp and put on the injured reserve. The Raiders signed White to the practice squad in September, reuniting him with head coach Klint Kubiak. They won a Super Bowl ring together with the Seattle Seahawks last season. The Raiders elevated White from the practice squad for the first three games of the season before signing him to the 53-man roster when fellow receiver Jack Bech went on the injured reserve. Bech returned in Week 8. White’s first three receptions were touchdowns and he made some big plays on special teams. He ended up having eight catches for 112 yards and three touchdowns on 19 targets. His play time dwindled in Week 2 to two offensive snaps. If he clears waivers Thursday, the Raiders could sign him back to the practice squad. Runyon, an undrafted free agent in 2025, played in 13 games last season. He logged 206 snaps on special teams and 45 on offense. He is the Raiders’ fourth tight end with Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas. The Raiders have six wide receivers on the 53-man roster. To take White’s place on the game-day roster, the Raiders will likely choose between Runyon and receivers Dont’e Thornton and Malik Benson, who were both inactive in Week 8.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Raiders injury news: Darien Porter not practicing
summary: The 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders are beginning their practice week Wednesday to prepare for Sunday’s game at the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers and, has been the case for most of the season, appear to be close to full health. According to multiple reports, the only starter not on the practice field at the beginning of […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders are beginning their practice week Wednesday to prepare for Sunday’s game at the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers and, has been the case for most of the season, appear to be close to full health. According to multiple reports, the only starter not on the practice field at the beginning of Wednesday’s session was outside cornerback Darien Porter. That is not a surprise since Porter departed Sunday’s 38-33 win at the New York Jets on the first play from scrimmage with a groin injury. He did not return. Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Porter would be monitored as the week progressed. Kubiak said after practice Porter is progressing and the team is taking it “day-to-day.” If he can’t play Sunday, rookies Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses will likely rotate as they did against the Jets. The only other player not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice was reserve wide receiver Cody White. The team later announced it released White and activated tight end Carter Runyon from the injured reserve. Starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was on the field Wednesday. He played just 13 snaps Sunday because of a stinger. Meanwhile, for San Francisco, stars, running back Christian McCaffrey (hamstring and wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) didn’t practice Wednesday. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan said McCaffrey may practice Thursday. Standout defnesive end Nick Bosa (calf) returned to practice on a limited basis.

title: Raiders at the midway point
summary: We’re basically halfway into the 2025 NFL season (this 17-game thing messes with the math), so let’s take a quick review of the 4-4 Raiders and where they stand with nine games of the season remaining. Let’s review the past quarter of the season: Quick summary of the second quarter: It was rough sledding for […]
full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re basically halfway into the 2025 NFL season (this 17-game thing messes with the math), so let’s take a quick review of the 4-4 Raiders and where they stand with nine games of the season remaining. Let’s review the past quarter of the season: Quick summary of the second quarter: It was rough sledding for the Silver and Black after they started the season 3-0. After beating bad teams, the Raiders lost four straight games to solid teams. They salvaged their season with a comeback win at the lowly New York Jets in Week 8. Offensive MVP: Tight end Brock Bowers. He’s a superstar. He can’t be stopped as a tight end or a wide receiver. He had 25 receptions for 345 yards and three touchdowns in the past quarter. He is the Raiders’ best player. Defensive MVP: Linebacker Nakobe Dean just like the first quarter. The free-agent is flourishing in the middle of the Raiders’ defense. He has been described as the “glue” of the unit. The defense has had major issues, but Dean is a player. Rookie of the quarter: The Raiders’ rookie class, as a whole, hasn’t done much, but second-year pick Treydan Stukes has been a steady starter at safety. He gives up plays, but he also makes plays. He’ a solid player. Best surprise: Quarterback Kirk Cousins just keeps plugging along and putting up top-of-the-league stats at the age 38 in a season he was supposed to be a game manager and placeholder to Fernando Mendoza. Worst surprise: 2025 No. 6 overall pick, running back Ashton Jeanty may have just become a backup running back. Bold prediction for next quarter: The Raiders play at the San Francisco 49ers, host the Seattle Seahawks, play at the Denver Broncos and at the Cleveland Browns. They all have, at least, a 4-4 record. The Raiders will find a way to go 2-2 to be 6-6 to start the stretch run and still be in the playoff hunt.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Dylan Laube honored for TD kick return
summary: In an expected move, Las Vegas Raiders backup running back and returner Dylan Laube was named the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance in their 38-33 victory at the New York Jets on Sunday in Week 8. Laube, a third-year player, had a 95 yard kickoff return for a touchdown in […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In an expected move, Las Vegas Raiders backup running back and returner Dylan Laube was named the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance in their 38-33 victory at the New York Jets on Sunday in Week 8. Laube, a third-year player, had a 95 yard kickoff return for a touchdown in the second quarter of the Raiders’ victory. The Raiders may not have won the game and snap their four-game losing streak had Laube not returned the kick for the score. It was the first returned kick for a score in the NFL this season. It was the Raiders’ first kick return for a touchdown since wide receiver Jacoby Ford did it in 2011. Laube is leading the NFL in kick return average at 34.1 yards a return. It is 2.8 yards per return higher than any other returner in the league. Only 4 players have finished a season with a higher average with the most recent coming in 1970. The Raiders have won four games this season and this is their third player of the week honor. Rookie cornerback Zeke Masses won the Defensive Player of the Week award in Week 2 and tight end Brock Bowers won the Offensive Player of the Week award in Week 3. This is the first time a Raider has won the Special Teams Player of the Week since kicker won it in the 2021 season.

title: Was this a 1-game demotion for Ashton Jeanty?
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-33 win at the New York Jets on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick saw […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 01: Ashton Jeanty #2 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs the ball against the New York Jets during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium on November 01, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-33 win at the New York Jets on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers. Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick saw his play time and work load decrease dramatically. He played a career low 40 percent of the snaps, but more importantly, the Boise State product had just two carries as he saw rookie fourth-round pick Mike Washington get a whopping 25 carries. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the decision had nothing to so with Jeanty’s disparaging words about the Jets’ defense. We will see if Jeanty gets more work against the 49ers. But this was a major development. Jack Bech: The second-round pick returned from spending four games on the injured reserve with a broken forearm. He played 40 percent of the snaps, but was not targeted as a wide receiver. Darien Porter: The third-round pick injured his groin on the first play from scrimmage. His availability for Sunday’s game is unknown. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick was benched after he started two games at right guard, in favor of rookie Trey Zuhn. Kubiak indicated Zuhn will play against the 49ers. Rogers played two plays on offense and six on special teams. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense as usual, but he did log five snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, was activated from the injured reserve, but he was a healthy scratch. So, that’s not overly encouraging. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick suffered a stinger for the second time since Week 5. His availability for Sunday in unknown. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was inactive for the fifth time this season. It was a bit of a surprise since he had a forced fumble in Week 7 and the team had just waived Jonah Laulu. Meanwhile, rookie Tim Keenan, elevated from the practice squad, has been getting quality playing time the past two weeks. It leads to speculation that a Keenan-for-Pegues roster move could potentially be in play at some point. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 18 snaps on special teams, which is his norm. He didn’t play on defense, a week after he had three defensive snaps, his first defensive action of his career.

title: Raiders news: Quay Walker is all over the place
summary: Question: Where is Quay Walker lined up? Answer: Everywhere. The Las Vegas Raiders have moved the base linebacker all over the field in his first season since signing in free agency from the Green Bay Packers. According to NFL Researcher, Walker is one of three players in the NFL to get, at least, 50 snaps […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Question: Where is Quay Walker lined up? Answer: Everywhere. The Las Vegas Raiders have moved the base linebacker all over the field in his first season since signing in free agency from the Green Bay Packers. According to NFL Researcher, Walker is one of three players in the NFL to get, at least, 50 snaps on the defensive line, linebacker and in the secondary so far this season. title: Lions vs. Dolphins injury report: Jaylen Wright does not practice; Jack Campbell update
summary: The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions this weekend, hoping to bounce back after a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots last week. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Jaylen Wright #5 of the Miami Dolphins in action during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions this weekend, hoping to bounce back after a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots last week. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding a walkthrough rather than a full practice. Jaylen Wright does not practice The Dolphins’ second-string running back missed practice with a quadriceps injury. While Wright’s contributions on offense have been minimal this year, picking up just 41 yards on 22 carries, he has been strong as a kick returner, where he is averaging 27.6 yards per kick and has a long of 79 yards. If Wright is unable to play this weekend, rookie running back Kaytron Allen, the Washington Commanders’ sixth-round pick who Miami claimed off waivers last month, could be in line to backup Ollie Gordon II. Allen, however, was limited in practice with a quadriceps injury of his own. Kadyn Proctor practices Dolphins rookie guard Kadyn Proctor fully participated in Wednesday’s practice but remains in the league’s concussion protocol, according to head coach Jeff Hafley. “He is progressing in the protocol,” Hafley said. Jarrett Kingston, an August waiver claim from the Houston Texans for Miami, started in Proctor’s place last week. Good news from Detroit’s Jack Campbell The Lions’ All-Pro linebacker sustained an ugly injury against the Vikings after tackling tight end T.J. Hockenson. Caught in an awkward position, Campbell hit Hockenson and had his head compress back onto his neck. He fell to the turf and lay motionless before being carted off the field and taken to a hospital. Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, indicating that he is progressing well in his recovery from the injury ( via Pride of Detroit ) : My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong. Jack Campbell Campbell is on the injury report as a non-participant, as the Lions have not moved him to injured reserve yet, but none of that matters. It is just great news to hear that he has full lower-body movement and is progressing with his upper body. title: Miami Dolphins Fans: Your Game 8 Takeaways
summary: Following Sunday’s loss by our Miami Dolphins to the New England Patriots, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s fourth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the New England Patriots? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins throws a pass against the New England Patriots during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following Sunday’s loss by our Miami Dolphins to the New England Patriots, I asked the following question: What are your overall takeaways from this afternoon’s fourth game of the season between our Miami Dolphins and the New England Patriots? What are the positive and negative takeaways from this afternoon’s game, as they apply to the team overall and to individual units and/or players? Below are some of your answers and thoughts on the game- Miami7 has a few thoughts- Willis was up & down, inconsistent. I don’t understand why he didn’t try to utilize his legs at all – there were a couple opportunities. I also don’t understand why he’s under Center so much? Without a better understanding of exactly what NE was showing defensively, it just ‘seemed’ as though the offense ran smoother outta the gun. The pick was unfortunate but another was an easy one that was dropped. OL had a bad day. Brewer wasn’t himself & Savi gave up some whopper whiffs. Kingston was either overmatched or completely lost on a few. Paul’s been solid but is showing a 2 penalty per game penchant that’s getting to be too commonplace. As a whole they failed to open much running room. Chop & Uche played pretty well but the Interior DL was terrible. Grant is scarily just, not good at the point in the middle. I thought earlier this year that IDL was going to be a strength? Not so much…. Ollie’s Ollie and all that….love the fire – HATE THE FIRE!!! He’s got a big mouth. He’s immature. And HE’S COSTLY in an emotional way. He dances a fine line, but he’s a bit overreactive and kind of a punk, always needing to yap & be heard. He should sit to start the game vs Lions….except for the fact that Jaylen Wright STINKS! But, it IS a teaching -and-learning opportunity. The kid needs to grow up. That whiff non-sack from Chris Johnson was SO egregiously bad that it looked as if the fix was in or something? At least NE shanked the FG after, but that was really strange ‘looking’ – how he alligator armed a sure sack? The Safeties had another sporadic/up&down day. The down’s hurt more than the up’s provided. I thought time mgt. on our last TD drive was absolutely TERRIBLE. We were going to need 2 scores….quite possibly 2 TD scores! With a little over 10 minutes we’re huddling and walking back after plays, taking WAY too much time. I’m not saying go no huddle, but there should have been with much better rhythm/pace to save time AND keep NE on their heels a bit. We got beat by a better team. Had our chances but made costly mistakes at the most inopportune times. I don’t even understand how that non-1st down call for NE was overturned? I went to get a drink and came back & NE had the ball again? No angle I saw was conclusive to overturn? Guess I missed whatever they saw on review? Whatever – they fought/played hard. Made some mistakes that really cost em’. They were in the game the whole way – the 2 pt. conversion was a poorly designed play (they got some work to do there). FinsSince70 says it’s ”coming together.” Just got home and cleaned up. Soggy drive, tailgate and game. This team is coming together…they play with effort. I’m proud of what they are putting together I wish dolphins fans put in the same effort. Bunch of sellout fans give the opponents a homefield advantage. I hate it. We had a shot. They were in it till the end. On to Detroit. Dolphster says the negatives and positives are obvious. Kind of stating the obvious here, but the positive takeaway is that the team plays hard, doesn’t give up, and is showing toughness and improvement even if the record doesn’t reflect it. The negative takeaway is what everyone also already knows. The team is young, inexperienced, and will be digging out of the hole the previous regime put them in for a while. dedstrk is happy with the team’s week-over-week improvement. My takeaway is they played better than I thought they would. They have gotten better every week imo. That says a lot to me. phinette is happy they are not a Colts fan right now. As everyone has said, the team competes well and is improving on both sides of the ball. We just lack depth and elite playmakers. I sure feel better about our team than the Colts’ fans probably feel about their team right now. As always 🐬⬆️ Wildfin22 sees some bias in the refereeing. So Washington receiver was short but Patriots receiver made the LTG 🤣🤣 dolfan8181 is another who has some issues with the refs. get another stop on 4th down .. see raiders game for the refs to pull the okie doke.. im so sick of watching games being stolen its unreal Wildfin22 has lost the ability to believe any longer. Fair! Just can’t understand how we played so well in the first half. Then just downright stink up the field in the 3rd quarter.But I’m realizing that we just aren’t talented enough to beat any good teams.No matter how much they play hard or execute on offense. Sooner or later the lack of true talent will show up. Malik Willis just isn’t good enough but he’s also not experienced enough. This team may turn this around but this franchise has lost for so many seasons that I truly don’t believe in them turning things around. We are on the Cleveland Browns level losing season after season. But like I’ll always say until I die FINSUP!!🐬🐬 Dolphins84te says bring on the high draft picks. Glad we lost = higher draft pick. Second-half adjustments (or lack therof) are killing us again this season. I suspect that there’s never going to be a consensus, especially during a painful season like this one. I’m personally trying to take it in stride and watch how all the rookies are progressing. As always, thank you all for participating in our Phinsider Question Of The Day.

On Wednesday, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley gave good news when updating Proctor’s status during […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - OCTOBER 11: Miami Dolphins offensive tackle Kadyn Proctor (74) leaves the field following the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, October 11, 2026 at Hard Rcok Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins were without their starting left guard — rookie Kadyn Proctor — on Sunday in a loss against the visiting New England Patriots due to a concussion the player suffered the week prior against the New York Jets. On Wednesday, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley gave good news when updating Proctor’s status during his media availability. Proctor is in the final stages of the NFL’s concussion protocol and, as such, practiced Wednesday without a red, non-contact jersey. If all goes well, and Miami’s massive rookie remains symptom free following today’s session, he should clear the protocol by tomorrow and be available for Sunday’s home contest against the visiting Detroit Lions. Miami’s offensive line struggled against New England on Sunday — although Proctor’s replacement, Jarrett Kingston, played decently well for a second-string player. Starting right guard, Jonah Savaiinaea, and starting center, Aaron Brewer, struggled with the Patriots’ defensive tackles, however. With Proctor likely factoring back into the mix, the Dolphins will look to get back to playing bully-ball up front against Detroit this weekend. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the club continues preparation for this Sunday’s game against Jared Goff, Aidan Hutchinson, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jahmyr Gibbs and the rest of the star-studded Lions roster.

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: When Did 6-1 Become Not Good Enough?
summary: The team had their first loss and the consensus opinion appears to that it is all Kyler Murray’s fault. Even though he led the team in rushing, he still did not do enough in the passing game to extend drives and give the defense more rest. Fair enough. I said and will repeat, I doubt […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after catching a touchdown pass during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The team had their first loss and the consensus opinion appears to that it is all Kyler Murray’s fault. Even though he led the team in rushing, he still did not do enough in the passing game to extend drives and give the defense more rest. Fair enough. I said and will repeat, I doubt any defender is happy about giving up 164 rushing yards in the second half to the Lions. You cannot be a top defense and do that no matter how long you are out there. They were on the field for 16:56 seconds in the second half. The entire team had a 10 minute break at the start o the 4th quarter due to the unfortunate injury to Jack Campbell. Prayers up to Campbell. I hope he recovers well. So there really is no excuse to say they were tired. They just did not tackle well and I thought they kept trying to punch the ball out rather than getting the runner down. It was a tough loss for sure but the team is still 6-1 but you would not know it based on stories, tweets, comments, etc. You would think this team is the Chargers right now. Sheesh! It is all centered around Kyler Murray too. I do not think he is ever going to get a fair shake because he is not JJ McCarthy and is the reason they traded McCarthy. That is just how I am reading the tea leaves. Kurt Warner does a great job going over the Lions film reviewing Kyler Murray and some of the play designs and where he may have gone with the throw. It really is interesting and unbiased. He does say he is not a big fan of the progression read system (or something along those lines) because he said it is very difficult on QBs. If you watch this video, you will see that the play design is not the issue. He asks why is Kyler not throwing it sooner or to another location but says that may be due to how he is being told to do it. This ties in with the comments from Cousins and Darnold about the offense taking them about half the season to get a good grip on. It also ties in with the offensive players making comments along the lines of we are almost there. I think they could modify some things and, if it were me, I would want to bring Warner in to consult for a little bit. He made a comment about the defensive coverage/alignment where if he saw that then he would immediately look to the other side of the field. Call it an excuse or whatever but I do not see any trade or QB change coming unless Kyler truly is unable to go. I doubt his hammy is that sore since he was able to finish out the game although it was just one more short drive (3 and out if I am not mistaken). I have been wrong many times before especially when it comes to QBs but I just do not see a change making too much of a difference. Wentz could come in and complete more throws “on time” but he ain’t scrambling and they ain’t calling no roll outs for him. Those players Kyler made with his legs would be sacks for Wentz. Of course, then the discourse will be about the team not investing in the offensive line which is complete rubbish. They invested but you just may not like the players they invested in. Another video here with Matthew Coller is talking to Jeremiah Sirles about benching Murray. Sirles is not a fan unless he is injured. title: Patriots vs. Packers: Who has the edge in Week 9?
summary: This weekend will be one of celebration for the New England Patriots. On Saturday, former tight end Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the organization’s Hall of Fame, followed by an event honoring the 10-year anniversary of the club’s 2016 Super Bowl victory. Will the 2026 version of the team be able to add to […]
full_text: This weekend will be one of celebration for the New England Patriots. On Saturday, former tight end Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the organization’s Hall of Fame, followed by an event honoring the 10-year anniversary of the club’s 2016 Super Bowl victory. Will the 2026 version of the team be able to add to the good feelings against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday? The oddsmakers seem to believe so, and the statistical comparison also favors them in certain areas. However, a closer head-to-head look shows that a victory is not a guarantee. Passing game Patriots pass offense vs. Packers pass defense: This is probably the pick that has the biggest potential to come back to bite us. However, we are not entirely confident in New England’s passing offense against the Packers. Granted, Drake Maye has been fantastic since the calendar turned to October and Mack Hollins might be coming back from injured reserve to bolster a shorthanded receiver group, but this is not the Dolphins they are going up against: Green Bay has been disruptive in the front and opportunistic in the back, and has both the scheme and personnel — even without Micah Parsons — to challenge the Patriots’ weak spots and personnel shortcomings along the offensive line and at the skill positions. | Edge: Packers Patriots pass defense vs. Packers pass offense: New England’s passing defense has been very good when playing man-to-man coverage (-0.36 EPA/dropback; 3rd), but suspect whenever Zak Kuhr opted to switch to zone (0.23 EPA/dropback; 30th). Finding the balance is a challenge, as he said himself last week , but it should be easier to do so against the Packers: Jordan Love is not a threat as a runner, which should play into the Patriots’ hands. He also has three clear favorite targets in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft, meaning that if New England can limit their damage and put pressure on an injury-plagued offensive line, they should be able to keep the NFL’s passing yards leader in check. | Edge: Patriots Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Running game Patriots rushing offense vs. Packers run defense: Taking both teams’ production so far into account, this might be the Week 9 game with the least productive combined run games. Unsurprisingly, we are giving both defenses the edge. The first battle will see a New England offensive line that has had its issues blocking the run, particularly along the interior, go up against a generally stout run defense ranked in the top half of the league in yards per run (3.9) and EPA per run (-0.108). Rhamondre Stevenson has impressed so far as the clear RB1, but blocking consistency remains a concern. | Edge: Packers Patriots run defense vs. Packers rushing offense: You think the Patriots run game has been bad? The Packers have been abysmal moving the ball on the ground. Obviously, it did not help that Josh Jacobs has been limited to two games following a domestic violence incident that remains under investigation, but the main issue — just like in New England — has been the blocking. The right side of the offensive line in particular has struggled, which is no surprise given that is dealing with some of the same personnel problems that have plagued the Patriots through most of the season. New England’s run defense, meanwhile, has quietly developed into a solid unit ranking 14th in EPA per run (-0.104) and 10th in yards per attempt allowed (3.8). | Edge: Patriots Special teams The Packers have been slightly better than the Patriots returning kickoffs and punts, and in kickoff coverage, while New England enjoys a minor edge covering punts. What tips the scale the home team’s way in this one is the place kicking. Sure Andy Borregales has not set the world on fire in his second season as a pro, but his 88.2% combined success rate on field goals and extra points is still leaps and bounds better than Packers rookie Trey Smack’s 77.2% — the worst such number among regular kickers in the NFL so far this year. Add that Borregales has familiarity with the Gillette Stadium wind patterns, and he looks like the more trustworthy option come Sunday. | Edge: Patriots Coaching The Packers are an all-around solid teams that is doing the best with what it has available. The Patriots are in a similar boat, which is why both teams are 5-3 right now even though they have had to deal with some serious injuries over the first two months of the season. We are giving Mike Vrabel and company the smallest of edges, in part because their home record so far (3-0) is superior to Green Bay’s on the road (2-2) — a sign of a team’s abilities to adapt to travel and hostile environments. | Edge: Patriots Verdict Despite being slight favorites, the Patriots beating the Packers on Sunday is not a given. If they come out like they did last week versus Miami, they might find themselves in a hole bigger than 10 points — and possibly too big to overcome. There is reason to be optimistic that that will not be the case again, but the message is clear: Green Bay is well-equipped to take advantage of any potential slip-ups, and New England needs to be on top of its game from start to finish in order to move to 6-3 on the season.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots vs. Packers preview: Players to watch, stats, more for Week 9
summary: After back-to-back road games, the New England Patriots will be back at Gillette Stadium this week to take on a Green Bay Packers team that has played some successful football so far this season. At 5-3, they are currently in the NFC playoff picture and have shown themselves capable of winning both at home and […]
full_text: After back-to-back road games, the New England Patriots will be back at Gillette Stadium this week to take on a Green Bay Packers team that has played some successful football so far this season. At 5-3, they are currently in the NFC playoff picture and have shown themselves capable of winning both at home and on the road. What the Packers also have shown is that they are capable of winning despite facing serious personnel questions. Much like the Patriots, they have been hit hard and will be without starters or key reserves at wide receiver, along the offensive line, along the defensive line and at linebacker this Sunday. So, what can be expected in Week 9? Let’s find out. Packers key stats The Packers are a good football team, they just happen to play in what is the most competitive division in football right now. Despite a 5-3 record, they are in fourth place in the NFC North; they are, however, the current owners of the seventh playoff seed in the conference — same as their opponent this week, the Patriots. And that is not the only similarity between the two teams as a look at the key stats shows. Packers Patriots Record 5-3 (4th AFCN) 5-3 (2nd AFCE) Scoring diff. +7 (t-14th) +22 (13th) Points /game 21.4 (23rd) 23.0 (16th) Points allowed/game 20.5 (10th) 20.3 (9th) Off. yards/game 331.6 (18th) 367.3 (8th) Off. EPA/play 0.010 (17th) 0.057 (9th) Off. EPA/dropback 0.142 (12th) 0.214 (6th) Off. EPA/run -0.266 (32nd) -0.169 (25th) Def. yards/game 314.9 (10th) 309.9 (8th) Def. EPA/play -0.044 (7th) 0.011 (16th) Def. EPA/dropback -0.005 (10th) 0.081 (17th) Def. EPA/run -0.108 (11th) -0.104 (14th) Turnover diff. +4 (t-7th) -7 (31st) Giveaways 11 (t-19th) 15 (t-29th) Takeaways 15 (2nd) 8 (21st) Offensively, the Packers function mainly due to their passing game. They are ranked top-10 in attempts, yards, touchdowns and net yard per attempt; they barely rank outside in expected points added per game. Their run game, on the other hand, has been abysmal. They are not just 32nd in EPA per rush, but also in attempts, yards and yards per attempt — a direct result of their offensive line being in shambles: they have used 11 different linemen this year, with seven of them playing more than 100 snaps. Defensively, Green Bay has performed very well especially in one department: taking the ball away. No other unit in football has had a better percentage of drives ending in giveaways than the Packers’, which registers takeaways on 16.7% of opponents’ possessions. For comparison, the Patriots are giving the ball away at a rate of 17.9% — second-worst in the league. Packers 2026 season The Patriots and Packers have followed the same pattern so far this year. Both lost their season openers but came back with a win the following week only to lose again in Week 3. They then rattled off three straight victories before a defeat in Week 7 and subsequent win in Week 8. Week 1: 39-22 loss at Minnesota Vikings (0-1) Week 2: 20-17 OT win at New York Jets (1-1) Week 3: 35-14 loss vs. Atlanta Falcons (1-2) Week 4: 17-14 win at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-2) Week 5: 31-7 win vs. Chicago Bears (3-2) Week 6: 23-14 win vs. Dallas Cowboys (4-2) Week 7: 20-17 loss at Detroit Lions (4-3) Week 8: 27-19 win vs. Carolina Panthers (5-3) As for the games themselves, the Packers didn’t look overly impressive so far. They barely avoided going 0-3 by beating the moribund Jets in overtime, and registered one of their wins against a Bears team led by a pair of backup quarterbacks. That said, they still have the eighth-best strength of victory. Packers active roster Roster up-to-date as of Nov. 4, 5 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter Quarterback (2): Jordan Love* (10), Tyrod Taylor (6) Running back (4): Josh Jacobs* (8), MarShawn Lloyd (32), Pierre Strong Jr. (22), Kaleb Johnson (26) Wide receiver (6): Christian Watson* (9), Matthew Golden* (0), Savion Williams* (83), Bo Melton (16 | KR), J.Michael Sturdivant (87), Coleman Owen (13 | KR/PR) Tight end (4): Tucker Kraft* (85), Mark Redman (86), Josh Whyle (81), Jonnu Smith (18) Offensive tackle (3): Jordan Morgan* (77 | LT), Anthony Belton* (71 | RT), Mekhi Becton Sr. (74) Interior offensive line (8): Laken Tomlinson* (72 | LG), Sean Rhyan* (75 | C), Travis Glover* (79 | RG), Aaron Banks (65), John Williams (73), Kevin Zeitler (70), Jager Burton (52), Donovan Jennings (67) Interior defensive line (5): Karl Brooks* (94), Devonte Wyatt* (95), Chris McClellan (55), Anthony Campbell (93), Jordon Riley (97) Defensive edge (4): Lukas Van Ness* (90), Barryn Sorrell* (99), Dani Dennis-Sutton (51), Brenton Cox Jr. (57) Linebacker (5): Zaire Franklin* (44), Isaiah McDuffie* (58), Ty’ron Hopper (59), Nick Niemann (31), Kristian Welch (54) Cornerback (5): Keisean Nixon* (25), Brandon Cisse* (2), Carrington Valentine (24), Benjamin St-Juste (21), Kamal Haden (36) Safety (4): Evan Williams* (33), Xavier McKinney* (29), Javon Bullard* (7), Kitan Oladapo (27) Specialists (3): Trey Smack (28 | K), Daniel Whelan (19 | P/H), Matt Orzech (42 | LS) Through the first eight weeks of the season, no quarterback has attempted more passes or thrown for more yards than Jordan Love. The seventh-year man has gone 192-for-312 (61.5%) for 2,246 yards with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions so far. He also has scored a rushing touchdown and is ranked 12th in the NFL in EPA per play (0.150). The Packers putting the ball in Love’s hand is no surprise given their aforementioned struggles running the football behind an offensive line that has been a revolving door so far. One would assume the QB himself also has been impacted by this, but his 4.3% sack rate is still fairly low and the sixth-best in football. As a consequence, Love has been able to push the ball down the field: he is tied with Drake Maye and Geno Smith as the league leader in completions of 20-plus yards (17) and tied for third in average depth of target (9.8). Unfortunately for Love, his receiving corps has not held up its end of the bargain at times. A league-leading 23 of his passes have been dropped, resulting in the second-worst drop rate in the NFL (10.7%). And that is despite Green Bay having some talent at the receiving positions. Christian Watson (42/708/6) and Matthew Golden (43/619/4) are among the most productive wide receiver pairings in football, while tight end Tucker Kraft (35/350/3) has also been steadily involved. Behind those three, however, there is a significant drop-off in receiving production — the passing game runs through their connection with Love. The running game, meanwhile, doesn’t run a whole lot at all. Part of it is Josh Jacobs (32/75/1) missing six games on the commissioner’s exempt list due to domestic violence charges, part is neither him nor MarShawn Lloyd (57/149/2) being particularly effective behind Green Bay’s O-line. The outlook isn’t much better either: starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and No. 2 right guard Travis Glover (knee) were absent from practice on Wednesday , while nominal right guard Jacob Monk and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele are currently on injured reserve. Maybe some extra time coming off a mini-bye can help the unit find some chemistry, but the production on the ground so far has been poor. Defensively, star outside linebacker Micah Parsons remains on the physically unable to perform list even after returning to practice on Wednesday. In his place, Lukas Van Ness has been the top guy on the edge: his 28 quarterback pressures are leading the team, as are his 4.5 sacks. The Packers are about more than those two, with the other edges all being heavily involved in the rotation. On the interior, Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt and rookie Chris McClellan are the main three. With rotational DTs Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave on IR, they are hoarding snaps at the position. Green Bay’s injury questions also have hit the linebacker position: Edgerrin Cooper is out for the year, while Zaire Franklin has missed practice on Wednesday with a shin issue. If Franklin ends up…

title: Patriots set for measuring-stick opportunity against Packers
summary: The New England Patriots have a big opportunity ahead of themselves against one of the NFC’s top teams this Sunday when they welcome the Green Bay Packers to Gillette Stadium. At 5-3, both teams enter Sunday looking to keep pace in competitive divisions while strengthening their respective position in the playoff picture. For the Patriots, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 18: Kevin Byard III #31 of the New England Patriots yells prior to the NFL game against the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots have a big opportunity ahead of themselves against one of the NFC’s top teams this Sunday when they welcome the Green Bay Packers to Gillette Stadium. At 5-3, both teams enter Sunday looking to keep pace in competitive divisions while strengthening their respective position in the playoff picture. For the Patriots, it also presents a chance to prove they can compete against a quality opponent from the other conference. “This is a big game for us. This is a huge game,” captain Kevin Byard said. “To be real, we haven’t beat an NFC team just yet. This is going to be a huge challenge for us as a team. I almost want to say a measuring stick game.” The similarities between the two teams extend beyond their records, making Sunday’s matchup a significant test for a Patriots team looking to establish itself as a legitimate playoff contender. “Both these teams are trying to keep pace with the other teams in the division,” Byard said. “So, I think both coaches preaching the same thing. This is, I’m not going to call it a must win, but we need to get this win at home and we’ve been really good at home at Gillette, so we got to keep that going.” Quarterback Drake Maye sees it similarly. “For sure. It’s a playoff team from last year. A playoff team with a great defense, a really good offense, a good quarterback,” Maye said. “Then, for us, it’s another NFC North opponent that’s been someone that we don’t play very often, but has been historically, in the past couple years, a playoff football team. They’re good, they’ve beaten good teams, and they continue to show up every year. We’ve definitely got a challenge and a chance to see how we look.” Green Bay presents a difficult challenge on both sides of the ball. Despite an offense that ranks in the bottom 10 in points per game (21.4), the Packers have shown an ability to generate explosive plays through the air. They lead the league in pass plays of 20 or more yards, with quarterback Jordan Love continuing to push the ball downfield to explosive pass catchers in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel then noted that Green Bay’s defense has generated the second-most negative plays in the league, while a league-high 17% of its drives have ended in a turnover. While Byard stopped short of calling the game a must-win, outside linebacker Dre’Mont Jones made it clear that the Patriots understand the importance of continuing to stack victories. With 10 AFC teams currently holding at least four wins, there is little room for the Patriots to let opportunities slip away. “We need to win,” Jones said. “I mean, we got to win to stack up W’s in that column so we can figure out where we’re going to be when it comes January and February, hopefully.”
author: Brian Hines

title: What Mack Hollins, Greg Van Roten returning to practice means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots’ first practice of Week 9 saw the return of two starter-level contributors. Wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten made their comebacks after spending multiple weeks on injured reserve due to respective calf and thigh issues. Even though neither was able to participate in a full capacity […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ first practice of Week 9 saw the return of two starter-level contributors. Wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten made their comebacks after spending multiple weeks on injured reserve due to respective calf and thigh issues. Even though neither was able to participate in a full capacity on Wednesday, Hollins and Van Roten returning to practice is a positive step for the two of them and the team as a whole. Let’s assess what else it means from a big-picture perspective. Clock starts ticking At least in theory, returning to practice means that both Hollins and Van Roten are now eligible to play in this week’s game against the Green Bay Packers. They would have to be activated from injured reserve to the Patriots’ 53-man roster first, but that move could happen at any point now. Whether it will actually take place this week or not will be seen. The Patriots are in no rush, however: they have 21 days to make a call before the return window closes again and they would revert back to IR to end their season. The expected outcome is that the two return to the 53-man when all is said and done, potentially as early as this week. Wide receiver group trending up Last Sunday against the Miami Dolphins might have been the low point for the Patriots’ wide receiver group, at least personnel-wise. The Patriots were without three of their top four receivers, including Hollins, and had to rely on a starter trio of Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and DeMario Douglas. The group performed well — it caught a combined nine passes for 156 yards and two touchdowns — but a lack of depth forced recently-signed practice squad wideout Ryan Miller to be elevated as an emergency option. Hollins’ full return whether this week or at a later point will help address the issue. Before getting hurt in Week 4, he played 63% of New England’s offensive snaps this season and had caught 15 passes for 209 yards. The numbers were not particularly impressive, but the 33-year-old showed some chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye while also being able to be a contributor in the running game; his effective replacement, Chism, has been competitive in that latter area but is lacking Hollins’ size and power. The Patriots will get all of that back soon, which is an encouraging development for a depleted receiver group that also will be without Romeo Doubs (shoulder) for at least two more weeks. Given that A.J. Brown’s status is also up in the air (knee), Hollins’ pending return has the group trending up again. Starting questions at guard Even though the Patriots only signed him in August, Van Roten made the Patriots’ roster out of training camp as a top backup along the interior offensive line. As such, he entered the lineup when right guard Mike Onwenu fractured his ankle in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Van Roten’s time with the starters lasted only four quarters before he himself got hurt the next week in Jacksonville, but the Patriots do like what he offers. The question is whether that means he will return to the lineup at some point. Heading into this week’s game versus Green Bay, the starting guards project as Ben Brown and Matt Pryor. Van Roten would likely replace the latter, but there is an argument for the Patriots to prioritize stability over potential upside, at least this week and with the returnee still limited in practice. Ultimately, though, the goal would be for New England — assuming Onwenu is unable to return — to go back to an interior of left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, center Jared Wilson, and either Van Roten or Brown at right guard. Vera-Tucker will have to sit out two more games before being eligible to return after New England’s Week 11 bye. At that point, the other pieces will also have fallen into place. Follow-up moves TBD The Patriots currently have one open spot on their 53-man roster, and the assumption is that it will be used on one of Hollins or Van Roten either this week or at a subsequent point in time. That still leaves them in need of an extra spot, should they plan on bringing back of them back into the mix (and as mentioned above, that is the team’s intention). So, how can this roster spot be created? There are multiple ways, even if we exclude the possibility of another player getting hurt and sent to injured reserve. The Patriots could release a backup at the two respective positions, release a backup at another spot with comparatively good depth, or trade a player away ahead of next week’s deadline. New England releasing one of its wide receivers seems unlikely at this point, but the team could opt to pull the plug on Walter Rouse or Matt Pryor with the intention of retaining them via the practice squad. It also could look at the depth at running back (Lan Larison), tight end (Tanner Arkin) or cornerback (Channing Canada, Karon Prunty) to create that second opening. As far as trades are concerned, defensive tackle Christian Barmore has been mentioned as a candidate to be moved . So far, however, nothing has materialized. More return spots taken Every NFL team has the opportunity to return eight players from injured reserve during the regular season. With Hollins and Van Roten now designated to come back, the Patriots have used up four of those already; they previously brought back wide receiver A.J. Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant from IR. This means there are four spots left for what is a group currently consisting of seven players: FB Reggie Gilliam, WR Romeo Doubs, RG Mike Onwenu, LG Alijah Vera-Tucker, ED Quintayvious Hutchins, LB Khalil Jacobs, and S Dell Pettus. Whether or not Hollins or Van Roten actually are activated to the 53-man roster is immaterial to the designation. Their spots count regardless.

title: Patriots vs. Packers Wednesday injury report: Hunter Henry among four sidelined
summary: While the 21-day return windows opened for wide receiver Mack Hollins and guard Greg Van Roten, the New England Patriots practiced without an offensive captain on Wednesday. Hunter Henry was among four non-participants in Foxborough as Green Bay Packers work got underway. After sustaining a foot injury last weekend, the tight end stayed sidelined alongside […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Hunter Henry #85 of the New England Patriots lines up before a play during an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the 21-day return windows opened for wide receiver Mack Hollins and guard Greg Van Roten, the New England Patriots practiced without an offensive captain on Wednesday. Hunter Henry was among four non-participants in Foxborough as Green Bay Packers work got underway. After sustaining a foot injury last weekend, the tight end stayed sidelined alongside running back TreVeyon Henderson, wide receiver A.J. Brown and defensive tackle Christian Barmore. Here’s the first injury report ahead of Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium. DID NOT PARTICIPATE Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) WR A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) TE Hunter Henry (foot) DT Christian Barmore (illness) Packers TE Josh Whyle (concussion) OT Travis Glover (knee) C Sean Rhyan (ankle) LB Zaire Franklin (shin) Henry injured his foot before halftime last weekend against the Miami Dolphins. After heading to and from the locker room, the tenured tight end tested things out yet was ultimately downgraded to out in the final quarter. His outing spanned eight offensive snaps as well three catches for 30 yards. That sent rookies Eli Raridon and Tanner Arkin up the depth chart along with August waiver claim Cameron Latu. Elsewhere for New England’s 53-man roster, illnesses kept Henderson and Barmore away on Wednesday. The running back had been ruled out for the AFC East meeting at Hard Rock Stadium after missing three straight practices last week, while the defensive tackle started and split a sack. As for the No. 1 wide receiver, Brown missed back-to-back sessions before the road trip with a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that landed him on injured reserve in September. The three-time All-Pro was downgraded from questionable on the eve of the 4:25 p.m. ET divisional kickoff as DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III and standard elevation Ryan Miller made up the wideout room. LIMITED PARTICIPATION Patriots WR Mack Hollins (calf — IR return) OT Morgan Moses (foot) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) LB Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder, knee) LB Gabe Jacas (knee) CB Carlton Davis III (neck) S Kevin Byard III (chest) Packers RB Chris Brooks (ankle — IR return) WR Christian Watson (rib) G Aaron Banks (knee) LB Micah Parsons (knee — PUP return) CB Keisean Nixon (shoulder) Hollins landed on injured reserve due to a calf injury in early October, while a hamstring injury sent Van Roten to the same destination in late September. The 33-year-old wide receiver and the 36-year-old interior lineman returned to practice as limited participants on Wednesday. They were not alone in that group. Five members of the Patriots’ current active roster also went in a partial capacity. Count a rookie and a veteran outside linebacker among them because of knee and shoulder ailments. This campaign, the edge efforts of Jacas and Jones have netted 38 tackles, 12 quarterback hits, four sacks and an interception. Two starters in the New England secondary also continue to manage neck and chest injuries, respectively, but both outlasted the inactives list in Miami Gardens. FULL PARTICIPATION Patriots QB Drake Maye (right shoulder) Packers No players listed And then there was one full participant listed for the Patriots. Maye’s throwing shoulder has been on hand for 1,398 yards, 14 touchdowns and a pair of interceptions through the air over his past five starts. The Patriots quarterback has added three rushing touchdowns during that torrid stretch. And last Sunday, he began November by completing 80 percent of his pass attempts. Only one of those attempts hit the grass after halftime during the divisional visit as a 13-3 deficit became a 24-19 win.

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Elliott Davison #27 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After going through the NFL transaction wire unclaimed, Elliott Davison has circled back to the New England Patriots. The organization officially re-signed the safety to the practice squad on Wednesday. Davison, 24, was waived 48 hours prior on the heels of being a healthy scratch against the Miami Dolphins. The 6-foot, 190-pounder had been promoted to the 53-man roster in Foxborough midway through October following two standard elevations from the practice squad. Now, he takes the opposite route as the active safety depth chart moves forward with Kevin Byard III, Craig Woodson, Jaylen Reed, Mike Brown and Brenden Schooler. First joining the Patriots’ practice squad in September before being released and re-signed, Davison’s stay has included two tackles and one pass deflection through three games. The UTSA product stands with 10 snaps on defense and 57 snaps on special teams thus far in 2026. Undrafted in 2025, Davison spent the duration of his rookie season on the practice squad of the New Orleans Saints and remained in the NFC South on a futures contract in January. He was let go at the league’s cutdown deadline in August on his way to Gillette Stadium. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s 5-3 club stood with two open spots on the practice squad midway through the week. That was the case after losing linebacker K.J. Britt to the Detroit Lions, adding running back Terrell Jennings and linebacker Elias Neal, and also releasing wide receiver Cameron Dorner and offensive lineman Jake Kubas. The Green Bay Packers visit on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

title: Mike Vrabel addresses Patriots rumors ahead of NFL trade deadline
summary: A pair of New England Patriots veterans found themselves in trade rumors ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline. This week, defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis were mentioned as potential trade candidates by Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. According to Breer, trading either player would give New England an opportunity to add needed draft […]
full_text: A pair of New England Patriots veterans found themselves in trade rumors ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline . This week, defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis were mentioned as potential trade candidates by Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. According to Breer, trading either player would give New England an opportunity to add needed draft capital while getting younger. Speaking on Wednesday, head coach Mike Vrabel responded to the report. “I think sometimes national reports have the tendency to do that. I have not shared that information with anybody,” Vrabel said. “You know, this time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up. So we’re focused on trying to prepare for Green Bay, make the corrections from the game. I mean, this is business as normal here. So, I don’t know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not any conversations with me.” Davis, 29, has played in four games this season while dealing with a neck injury. When healthy, he has occupied his usual starting role opposite Christian Gonzalez, with Vrabel highlighting his physicality and competitiveness. Barmore, 27, has seen his playing time decrease slightly, playing just 50% of New England’s defensive snaps this season after logging 65% last year. The defensive tackle has been productive at times, recording 3.5 sacks, his highest total since 2023. Neither player has guaranteed money remaining on his contract beyond this season, making a potential trade a realistic possibility. However, would dealing away two defensive contributors make sense for a 5-3 Patriots team with aspirations of competing? “I don’t know. There’s probably a bunch of ways we can make this team better,” Vrabel responded. “You know, coach better, execute better, whether that’s [adding] guys on the streets or — there’s multiple ways. Again, we’d have these conversations each and every day.” Vrabel said he doesn’t feel the need to discuss trade rumors with players, instead keeping conversations centered on football and the team’s preparation. The NFL trade deadline is set for Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. With less than a week to finalize any moves, Vrabel’s focus remains on the present. “Right now, there’ll be another week before the trade deadline,” Vrabel said. “We’ll be leaving for Munich next week. We’re focused on today and how we get better and how we can run the ball better, how we can affect the quarterback. All these things that if we don’t do, it’s going to be tough.”

title: Robert Kraft among contributor nominees for Pro Football Hall of Fame class 2027
summary: New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft is once again in a position to enter the Pro Football Hall of Fame. As was announced on Wednesday, the 85-year-old is one of five contributors nominated for enshrinement in 2027. Alongside him, the contributor subcommittee also picked Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten from what […]
full_text: New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft is once again in a position to enter the Pro Football Hall of Fame. As was announced on Wednesday, the 85-year-old is one of five contributors nominated for enshrinement in 2027. Alongside him, the contributor subcommittee also picked Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten from what was originally a field of 42 candidates. Buying the Patriots in 1994 for $175 million, Kraft oversaw the franchise’s development from one of the least successful in football into the NFL’s model operation. With head coach Bill Belichick and quarterback Tom Brady leading the team’s football operations, New England won six Super Bowls — an unprecedented feat in the salary cap era. In total, the Patriots advanced to the Super Bowl 11 times in his 33 seasons as an owner. In addition, Kraft’s ownership included 20 AFC East titles, 23 playoff berths and only six losing seasons. In total, the Patriots have won a combined 65.6% of their games since he bought them in the mid-90s. Kraft furthermore has been none of the most influential owners in the league. A member of several NFL committees, including the broadcast and media committee, he played an integral role in ending the NFL’s 2011 lockout. Kraft being mentioned as a Hall of Fame candidate is therefore neither a surprise, nor a new development. He was a candidate for 14 straight seasons before being named a finalist for the first time in 2025. He came up short in the end, and it has been suggested that a series of scandals involving both his team and himself as well as some overeager lobbying on his behalf have hurt his candidacy. Still, his résumé speaks for itself, something Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel also said on Wednesday. “Just being able to buy the team and the success that they’ve had since he’s bought the team is really unprecedented,” Vrabel said during a press conference at Gillette Stadium. “I think the ability to grow this area, to grow what is Patriot Place and everything that surrounds this place — the success speaks for itself. I think he’s always continuing to grow the game. Having these conversations as a coach now with Robert about the media deals and the ability to grow the game, and trying to strengthen our relationship with the players and what’s best for the game of football. “Admittedly, he started out as a fan of the team and then obviously was able to buy it. I started out as a fan of the Browns, I didn’t end up buying the Browns, but I played in the NFL, so I guess we all have a dream. He certainly has done a lot, and the ability to keep it within his family — I appreciated the opportunity to come back here and work with familiar faces.” The contributor subcommittee will meet again on Nov. 17 to discuss Kraft and the four other nominees. One candidate will be selected to advance to the next round of voting by the full Hall of Fame Selection Committee. The 2027 Hall of Fame class will be announced in the lead-up to the Super Bowl in February.

Wide receiver Mack Hollins and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who remain […]
full_text: Update 4/11/2026: Mack Hollins, Greg Van Roten return to Patriots practice ahead of Packers game The New England Patriots started their preparation for the upcoming Week 9 game against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, and it involved two players returning to practice. Wide receiver Mack Hollins and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who remain on injured reserve, both participated in the first session of the week. Patriots are without Hunter Henry, Gabe Jacas, A.J. Brown, Morgan Moses, Dre’Mont Jones, Christian Barmore (illness) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) to start Wednesday’s practice. Mack Hollins (calf) and Greg Van Roten (thigh) officially returned. pic.twitter.com/EPPEuDd2uc — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) November 4, 2026 “Mack and GVR will return to play,” head coach Mike Vrabel said during a press conference on Wednesday. “Just want to get guys out there to practice. There’s only so much the trainers and strength coaches can do with them, so hopefully we can work those guys back in and see where they are here as we work through the week.” Whereas Hollins, whose return was previously reported, was placed on injured reserve after Week 4, Van Roten went to the injury list a week earlier. The summer pickup, who entered the starting lineup in Week 3 as an injury replacement for starting right guard Mike Onwenu, suffered a thigh injury in a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The 36-year-old had played 64 snaps for the Patriots before his injury. In his absence, Ben Brown and in-season. signing Matt Pryor took over the position between center Jared Wilson and right tackle Morgan Moses. New England has 21 days to activate him and Hollins to the 53-man roster, or else they will revert to injured reserve and miss the remainder of the season. Original story 11/4/2026: Mack Hollins to return to Patriots practice on Wednesday The New England Patriots’ depleted wide receiver group is about to receive a boost. Mack Hollins, who has missed the last four weeks on injured reserve, will make his return to practice on Wednesday. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Patriots will open his 21-day window to rejoin the active roster. Hollins, 33, was placed on injured reserve following New England’s Week 4 win over the Buffalo Bills due to a calf injury. Up until that point, he had played 63% of the team’s offensive snaps and been on the receiving end of 15 catches for 209 yards. His return to practice will be a big step for player and team alike. Hollins is not only a starter-caliber wide receiver and locker room leader for the Patriots, but also was part of a group of three wideouts who recently were forced to miss time. During last Sunday’s 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins, Hollins was joined on the sidelines by A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder; IR). In the three veterans’ absence, New England relied on a trio of Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and DeMario Douglas. The trio combined to catch nine passes for 156 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Week 8. The Patriots will host the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium this week. They will release their first injury report leading up to the Nov. 8 contest on Wednesday afternoon.

title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: Cleveland Browns
summary: The New Orleans Saints are returning to action after a bye week with more questions than they had to start the season. Now, this matchup with the Browns serves as a litmus test for the changes that were made during the bye, not just for the coaching staff but for the entire organization. This game […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints scrambles with the ball under pressure from Charlie Jones #89 of the New York Giants during the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are returning to action after a bye week with more questions than they had to start the season. Now, this matchup with the Browns serves as a litmus test for the changes that were made during the bye, not just for the coaching staff but for the entire organization. This game against the Browns is a really intriguing matchup for the offense because this defense is exactly what the Saints need to face right now. The Browns’ biggest weakness on defense is rushing yards allowed. Cleveland ranks 24th in rushing defense in the NFL, surrendering 126.9 yards per game and 4.68 yards per carry. Just last week against the Steelers, the Browns allowed 200 rushing yards. Everyone knows the Saints have had issues running the ball, and now, with C.J. Donaldson suffering an injury, that only compounds their rushing problems. But there may be some hope after all. The Saints have added Audric Estime back to the roster, claiming him off waivers. Estime showed a lot of promise at the end of last season, when the Saints were struggling to run the ball, and throughout the preseason. It caught a lot of people off guard when the Saints opted to release him before the season started, but he’s back now and will be a welcome addition come Sunday afternoon for an offense that is averaging only 86 rushing yards per game and ranks 28th in the NFL. Running the ball will be very important in this game because if the Saints become one-dimensional, it will play right into the hands of the Browns. Cleveland currently has the sixth-best defense against the pass, allowing only 196 yards per game. The Browns have been so successful in pass coverage because they have an elite interior pass rush. Mason Graham, Maliek Collins, and Adin Huntington have combined for 11 sacks. Quarterbacks cannot step up into the pocket against this defensive front, and there is consistent pressure off the edge from Isaiah McGuire, who has 3 sacks, and Jared Verse. Verse has 0 sacks right now, but he is still an edge rusher the Saints have to be aware of. The Saints are averaging only 229 passing yards per game, which ranks 14th in the NFL. If the Saints get into the red zone, they have to convert. Cleveland allows touchdowns on 73.9% of opponents’ red-zone opportunities, while the Saints are converting only 52.2% of theirs. While Jordyn Tyson is trying to make his way back onto the playing field, Chris Olave remains one of the best receivers in the league. Over the past few weeks, his production has dipped a bit because of the attention he receives, and this week will be no different. Kellen Moore will have to find creative ways to get him open because Olave will be matched up against Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell. The Browns’ cornerbacks are very physical, and Moore will have to find ways to counter that. To win this game, the Saints will have to run the ball against this weak run defense and keep the offense balanced. They have to commit to a decent number of rushing attempts. This will help slow down Cleveland’s pass rush. The Browns have 21 sacks, with 11 coming from the interior. Run at them and slow down their pass rush! The Saints have allowed 15 sacks so far this season, and Tyler Shough is already fighting through broken bones in his non-throwing hand. Run the ball, protect Tyler Shough, and get creative. Design plays that get your playmakers in space and work in concert with the running game. Use motions, shifts into different formations, and heavy run-action plays. Make this defense play with its eyes and not its instincts. Will the Saints come out of this game looking like they have improved, or will it just be more of the same? Hopefully, the changes that were made will lead to better results this week. How do you think the Saints’ offense will handle this Browns defense? Do you feel good about the changes that were made during the bye week?
