title: NFL predictions, Week 9: Lucky 13 for NY Giants vs. Philadelphia?
summary: The New York Giants have not beaten the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field in Philly since 2013. That’s 12 straight losses on the Eagles’ home turf. Can the Giants end that streak this Sunday? Read on to see how the Big Blue View staff sees Giants-Eagles and the rest of the Week 9 slate […]
full_text: The Giants and Eagles are vastly different teams than they were a year ago. | Getty Images The New York Giants have not beaten the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field in Philly since 2013. That’s 12 straight losses on the Eagles’ home turf. Can the Giants end that streak this Sunday? Read on to see how the Big Blue View staff sees Giants-Eagles and the rest of the Week 9 slate unfolding. Chris Pflum I think I’ll always be uneasy when the Giants go on the road to play the Eagles. Weird (and generally bad) things tend to happen to the Giants at the Linc. But dare I hope that some of the smoke from burning sage and the power of Danhausen lifting the curse on the Knicks leaked from Madison Square Garden over to the Giants’ facilities this summer? The Giants are favored over the Eagles on the road for the first time in recent memory, and John Harbaugh’s record coming off of bye weeks is impressive. Cam Skattebo’s hamstring is obviously a concern, and we have to respect the Eagles’ playmakers and their ability to generate explosives. That said, I also have to believe Andrew Thomas, Jermaine Eluemunor, and Abdul Carter getting a much-needed break will have a positive impact on their play. The Eagles were already struggling after the departures on their coaching staff, and fell into disarray with the retirement of Lane Johnson, the trade of Cam Jurgens, the loss of Jalen Hurts, and Saquon Barkley’s injuries. Those excuses, however, fall flat considering the Giants are also without their starting quarterback, their offensive tackles have been gutting their way through injuries, their best pass rusher and a starting defensive lineman are on the injured reserve, and they’ve been dealing with injuries in their backfield and secondary — but have held it together and persevered. I think I’ll always have a (at least) a kernel of concern when the Giants play in Philly. But this seems like a great week for a statement game. Winner: Giants Tony Del Genio This is a must-win game for the Giants. Not because they can’t win the NFC East if they don’t – this division is bad enough to revive memories of the 2020 “NFC Least.” It’s because we don’t know yet whether the Giants are frauds who’ve made a couple of plays late in games against bad teams, or a rising team that just has what it takes to win. The opening win over Dallas was impressive…but the Cowboys are a 3-5 disaster. The most recent win in Houston was impressive…but that team is now 2-5. In fact, the Giants haven’t yet even played, much less beaten, a team that is currently above .500. The Philadelphia Eagles are a train wreck this season, having lost many key players to retirement or injury and having parted ways with the best offensive line coach around, Jeff Stoutland. Still, that Eagles defense has Jalen Carter on the IDL, Zach Baun at linebacker, and quality defensive backs in Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. Most importantly they have defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, whose two-high safety zone defenses with post-snap rotation have confused many quarterbacks and limited explosive pass plays.Will J.J. McCarthy be able to read that defense and exploit it, or is this the week he throws three picks and comes back to Earth? The Eagles’ offense hasn’t really scared anyone this season. They traded A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith and Jalen Hurts are out, Saquon Barkley is playing injured, and the formerly fearsome offensive line is a shell of its former self with future HOFers Jason Kelce and Lane Johnson retired and the rest of them injured or playing poorly. The wild card is that Joe Milton III will make his first start at QB for them. The Giants saw a little of him as a Cowboy in the final game last season, and Jalin Hyatt will have fond memories of a QB who actually completed a deep pass to him for a TD in college. Milton has a rocket arm and is more mobile than predecessor Tanner McKee, but the Giants should be able to limit him, if they can produce an effective pass rush. That said, Dallas Goedert always hurts the Giants, and Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, and rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon can make plays. At The Linc, you never know. It’s been 13 years since the Giants won in Philly. There’s no excuse for them not to break that streak Sunday, and do so easily…unless they’re frauds. I’ll guess that they’re not. Winner: Giants Nick Falato The New York Giants enter the matchup riding momentum after their bye week, while the Philadelphia Eagles are mired in a six-game losing streak and rapidly falling toward the top of the 2027 NFL Draft order. The Giants defense is playing well, and the offense received a spark in Week 7 against Houston. Philadelphia’s offensive line struggles to protect Tanner McKee, who isn’t exactly fleet of foot. Philadelphia has averaged just over 14 points per game through this six-game losing streak. Philadelphia’s defense surrendered 27 points to Washington, 38 to Dallas, and 25 to the Carolina Panthers over their last three contests. It’s bleak in Philadelphia. The Giants have not won in Philadelphia since 2013 — a 15-7 Giants’ win where Josh Brown kicked five field goals, and Matt Barkley played for the Eagles. Eight of the Eagles’ 12 victories were one-possession games, and New York had some brutal losses at Lincoln Financial Field. But new circumstances have arrived, and the Giants have an opportunity to end a disturbing chapter in this rivalry. Giants should comfortably win, 30-13. Winner: Giants David Hartman The last time the Giants were favored at the Eagles was in 2009. The last time the Giants beat the Eagles in Philadelphia was in 2013. That’s a lot of history going against Big Blue as they travel to Philadelphia as 3-point favorites on Sunday. The Eagles are enduring a season from hell and after six straight losses, they sit at 2-6. They’ll be starting their third QB of the season when Joe Milton gets the first start of his career on Sunday. Milton has appeared in five NFL games, and his last game action came against the Giants at MetLife Stadium in Week 18 last season, in mop-up duty of a meaningless contest with the Cowboys. He’s a big guy with a big arm, and is a bit of an unknown quantity. For his career, he’s thrown two touchdown passes and two interceptions. Philadelphia is obviously hoping he can spark an anemic offense that’s mostly been without its star running back (who is quite familiar to New York fans), its top two receivers, and multiple first-string offensive linemen. J.J. McCarthy draws his second start for Big Blue, who should be well-rested off the bye. Philadelphia’s defense is still a capable unit, although it hasn’t played all that well, in part because the offense can’t sustain drives. If Philly has any chance to save its season, winning this game against the division leader is a must. I can see their defense giving maximum effort and posing problems for McCarthy, who I still don’t trust completely. This game scares me. The Giants are riding high after their big win over the Texans in Week 7 and Philadelphia is desperate. I also don’t have confidence in Dominic Zvada if the game comes down to him, which it might. I’ll give the G-Men the nod because they’re the better team at the moment, but it won’t be easy. Pick: Giants in a close one Valentine’s View I was asked during a podcast appearance this week whether I was picking the Giants to win. I said yes, with great trepidation. This is Philly we’re talking about, and whenever the Giants visit something always seems to go wrong. This, though, is the first time in a long while where these teams have met with the Giants having a clear upper hand. The New York Giants being favored to win in Philly? Who saw that coming when the season started? Good teams win games like this against struggling teams. I am going to trust that John Harbaugh and the Giants see the opportunity in front of them in the NFC East, and that they will take advantage Sunday of a team they should beat. Pick: Giants Giants…
author: David Fucillo

title: NY Giants cornerback Greg Newsome: Defense is ‘perfect scheme for me’
summary: The New York Giants secondary was widely looked at as one of team’s weaknesses coming into the 2026 season. The Giants were widely expected to make a splash to rebuild a unit that disappointed in 2025, but instead they merely brought in cornerback Greg Newsome II. Newsome II was a former first round pick by […]
full_text: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II intercepts a pass against the Arizona Cardinals. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants secondary was widely looked at as one of team’s weaknesses coming into the 2026 season. The Giants were widely expected to make a splash to rebuild a unit that disappointed in 2025, but instead they merely brought in cornerback Greg Newsome II. Newsome II was a former first round pick by the Browns, but his career stalled in Cleveland and he was traded by the Browns to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. So he was looked at as a flier at best when he signed a one-year deal with the Giants in the spring of 2026. At least that’s how the media at large viewed him. Newsome still saw himself as a first round corner and was willing to bet on himself if he could land in the right situation. Six games later, Newsome has signed a three-year, $46 million extension to make New York his home through the 2029 season. “I believed wholeheartedly after I signed a one-year,” he said on Wednesday. “I knew the type of person I was, first and foremost. And I knew what type of player I was and I knew that if I just get to the right place, that the money will take care of itself. I feel like when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted, you’re somewhere that you’re loved, everything else takes care of itself. So, I knew this would be the place.” He added that he was very intentional in wanting to come play for John Harbaugh and the New York Giants. “My first thing was fit,” Newsome said. “What coaches know me, and that was the biggest thing. I obviously played against Harbs a lot, so he knew what type of player I was, and I knew what type of coach he was. So, that was kind of my first thing, alright, fit. How did his defenses play in the past? Because that’s going to be kind of how the defense will be playing in New York.” From there, Newsome decided to bet on himself in big market. He knew a “Ravens” style defense would fit his skill set, and that the city would be a fit as well as the coach and system. “So, I figured, how about I sign in one year?” he added. “How about I come to New York and just play in front of a big media outlet? I feel like my personality will be able to show more in this city. So, that was kind of my thought process. “I think it starts from the top down,” he said when asked what makes the Giants such a great fit. “Starting obviously with ownership, just how they carry themselves. It goes down to the head coach and it keeps going down. So, just what Harbs (Head Coach John Harbaugh) has just instilled, just the toughness of how we’re going to play, things like that. And then, (Defensive Coordinator) Dennard (Wilson) has the perfect scheme for me. Being able to go challenge people, being aggressive and things like that. And just, man, just the ability to play with all 11 guys. We got some of the best players in the league, so they make my job a lot easier as well.” Speaking of the rest of the Giants’ defense, Newsome whole-heartedly believes in his teammates and their ability to be great. “I think the biggest thing with us was just proving ourselves right,” he said. “I said it from the first time [he spoke to the New York media] that we had the best secondary, and everybody was laughing. But I knew the talent that we had, and like I said in the beginning, it was just how tight we are as a room. When you got guys all competing essentially for the same job, sometimes it’s a lot of bad blood in that. But we really care for each other. We really want each other to succeed no matter who’s out there. So, I think the biggest thing, how we’ve been growing these past few weeks is just our communication. And I think it’s showing between these first seven games.” It has been showing itself. The Giants are third in passing yardage allowed, third in passing yards per game allowed, and second in yards per attempt allowed. “I think it’s just the same mindset we always have.” he said. Just to continue to go 1-0 each week, just get better on the little things and don’t become complacent.” The fit — people, teammates, and scheme — is everything. And Newsome made it clear that New York is where he wants to be, and he was willing to take less money to stay a Giant for the foreseeable future. “You obviously could play it [his one-year contract] out, maybe make a few more millions, continue to play well,” he said. “But for me, it’s not really about that. Once again, I chose this place because it just fits me. The coaches, my teammates, I just love being around these guys. So, when they approached us with a deal, it was a no-brainer. It wasn’t, ‘how about I play it out and maybe make a few more millions?’ Obviously, it would be great to have a few more but when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted and loved, the money, I’m getting good enough money that I’ll be secure for the rest of my life.”
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants news: Giants to face new Eagles QB, Cam Skattebo, Abdul Carter, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants get ready to face off against the Philadelphia Eagle this weekend. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants get ready to face off against the Philadelphia Eagle this weekend. Which NFL teams should be buyers, sellers or stand pat at the trade deadline? | The Athletic New York Giants: Buyers. It’s important to note that the Giants should be buyers only from the discount rack. A blockbuster trade for someone like Colts running back Jonathan Taylor that strips valuable early-round picks wouldn’t be prudent for a team still building. But a modest deal — say, a sixth-round pick for a veteran defensive tackle to upgrade their porous run defense — would make sense for a team with a clear path to its first NFC East title since 2011. They have plenty of injuries at the position, seem lukewarm at best on Cam Skattebo, but have a great chance to win a bad division. How much do the Giants want to pay for a running back? Jonathan Taylor is the dream, but he won’t be cheap. Perhaps Tony Pollard will be more reasonable, though he has played very well lately and that could increase the price. NFL Week 9 latest intel, buzz questions, and trade deadline news | ESPN.com Graziano: I covered the Vikings’ loss Sunday in Detroit a week after covering the Giants’ victory in Houston. Vikings people I spoke to were very happy for quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who thrived in his first start as a Giant after being traded away from the team that drafted him 10th in 2024. Minnesota coaches told me they believed McCarthy had matured significantly since the start of the 2026 offseason (the word “maturity” is also one the Giants’ coaches are using to praise McCarthy) and they were happy the team had been able to send him to a place where he had a chance to be successful. They also recognize they have a chance to look bad if McCarthy plays well for the Giants and Kyler Murray doesn’t get things going in Minnesota, but everyone agrees it was time for a scenery change. Inside the mind of a mindful quarterback now leading Giants | The Record At an early age, J.J. McCarthy gained tremendous inspiration from studying the mental approach of elite champions, business leaders and respected icons from all walks of life. When he got to IMG Academy in Florida for his senior year of high school, the teenage dream of one day becoming a quarterback who embodied all those qualities became more reality than fantasy. The Giants’ overlooked roster resource that has propelled their surge | New York Post It is the one constant for every NFL team to one degree or another. Players will get hurt. Starters will go down. Backups will have to play. An under-the-radar strength that has helped the Giants maintain first place: They have depth on their roster. That means injuries have not destroyed their chances and the coaching staff has options for starting spots. Malik Nabers, New York Giants (no change). Nabers and the Giants were on a bye in Week 8, with Nabers having put together four straight 100-yard receiving games, leading the NFL in receiving yards from Weeks 4 through 7. Neither player participated in practice Wednesday as the Giants prepared for Sunday’s gane against the Philadelphia Eagles. title: Eagles switching to QB Giants fans wanted when Jaxson Dart was injured
summary: It appears as though the Philadelphia Eagles are throwing a curveball at the New York Giants. The Eagles have decided to make a change at quarterback and are starting quarterback Joe Milton III, per a report from Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport. The report comes as the Giants have spent much of the last week […]
full_text: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III warms up | Getty Images It appears as though the Philadelphia Eagles are throwing a curveball at the New York Giants. The Eagles have decided to make a change at quarterback and are starting quarterback Joe Milton III, per a report from Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport . The report comes as the Giants have spent much of the last week since their upset win over the Houston Texans preparing for Tanner McKee. McKee has started the last three games for the Eagles and is 0-3 in that stretch, completing 63.2 percent of his passes with 2 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. The Eagles have lost their last three games by a combined 45-90. Milton III was originally drafted by the New England Patriots out of Tennessee in the 6th round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He was traded to the Dallas Cowboys in the spring of 2025, and the Eagles signed him off the Dallas practice squad on October 16th. Where McKee is a relatively immobile pocket passer, Milton is a massive (6-foot-5, 236-pound), athletic, and strong-armed quarterback. Milton has appeared in five games in 2024 and 2025, but only saw significant action in the Patriots’ 2024-2025 Week 18 win over the Buffalo Bills. Milton didn’t start, but finished that game 22 of 29 for 241 yards and a touchdown. It was a shockingly good performance, and one he has yet to replicate. While Milton possesses elite physical tools, he was heavily knocked for inconsistency and a lack of accuracy in college. He has enough arm strength to access all areas of the field, but completed just 38.6% of his passes beyond 10 yards downfield — despite Tennessee’s simplistic offense. He also rarely threw with anything like timing, touch, or anticipation and is much more of a “fastball only” passer. That said, Milton’s presence will force the Giants’ pass rush to be more disciplined. He’s a powerful and fast runner, which could hurt the Giants if they’re undisciplined in their rushes or allow him to break contain. It will be interesting to see how the Giants adapt to the sudden change at quarterback, and whether Milton can spark a listless Eagles’ offense.

title: NY Giants trade candidate: RB Derrick Henry
summary: Should the New York Giants, who are clearly big-game hunting in the running back market with the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, try to bring Derrick Henry to New York? Head coach John Harbaugh has said he would love for the Giants to have a “Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley situation” with the Giants. […]
full_text: Derrick Henry | Getty Images Should the New York Giants, who are clearly big-game hunting in the running back market with the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, try to bring Derrick Henry to New York? Head coach John Harbaugh has said he would love for the Giants to have a “Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley situation” with the Giants. Clearly, Harbaugh does not believe Cam Skattebo gives him that. The Baltimore Ravens’ season is falling apart. Baltimore is 4-4, last in the NFC North, and has lost its top two quarterbacks, Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntly (turf toe) for the season. The Ravens are going nowhere fast. Mike Florio said on PFT Live that Henry should be begging for a trade to the Giants. “If you’re Derrick Henry, are you showing up today and are you saying ‘Please trade me to the Giants’, or another contender … The season is going down the s——— for the Ravens right now. If I’m Henry and I’m looking at the calendar and I’m looking at the schedule and I’m looking at the situation and I’m thinking I’m not getting any younger and I’d kinda like to have a playoff run. “If I’m the Giants and I’m looking at Jonathan Taylor if I’m John Harbaugh I’m calling my former GM Eric DeCosta today and I’m saying ‘is there any way that Derrick Henry could be available’.” Why it would work Henry, 6-foot-3, 252 pounds, has been one of the pre-eminent running backs in football for a decade. He was the lynchpin of Harbaugh’s rushing attacks with the Ravens the past two seasons, and is the model power/bellcow/explosive running back for a Harbaugh offense. Henry is 32 with more than 3,000 touches in his career. That is a lot of mileage for a running back, and Henry is clearly past what is usually considered the expiration date for when backs are usually at their best. He gained more than 3,500 yards averaged more than 5 yards per carry the last two seasons with Harbaugh. Henry is averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry this year. Is that about Henry? Jackson barely playing? A new offense with a team that has now lost three straight games? Henry is signed through 2027, but has no guaranteed money next season.. He has three void years in his contract, but the Ravens would be responsible for those as dead money. As a rental, the Giants might not have to surrender as much draft capital for Henry as they would for Taylor. Harbaugh has clearly shown a willingness to pick up the phone and try to broker deals. His relationships with DeCosta and Baltimore owner Steve Bisciotti might help get this one done. Why it wouldn’t work There are only two reasons I can think of. Maybe Henry really is finally slowing down. It would be up to Harbaugh and the Giants’ pro personnel department to make that decision. The other would be that the Giants might choose not to go the rental route. [Article updated to reflect that Henry is under contract through the 2027 season].
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants trade deadline 2026: Missing picks complicating efforts to make deal
summary: The New York Giants are clearly pushing to make a big move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, which is now just six days away. The Giants’ efforts, though, are reportedly being hampered by their lack of draft capital. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Giants’ lack of fourth- and fifth-round […]
full_text: Jonathan Taylor | Getty Images The New York Giants are clearly pushing to make a big move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, which is now just six days away. The Giants’ efforts, though, are reportedly being hampered by their lack of draft capital. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Giants’ lack of fourth- and fifth-round selections in the 2027 NFL Draft is making it more difficult to put together viable packages for teams with players they may be willing to sell. Per Schultz, the Giants are countering that difficulty by “pushing for bigger names who would require higher picks—and seem open to doing that.” The Giants sent their fourth-round pick to the Cleveland Browns to move up and select wide receiver Malachi Fields in this year’s draft. They used their fifth-round pick to acquire quarterback J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending injury. The Giants are projected to receive a fourth-round compensatory pick in 2027. Since compensatory picks are not awarded until shortly before the draft, the Giants don’t yet possess that pick and cannot trade it. GM Joe Schoen addressed those moves during his bye week press conference. “Obviously you want to have as many picks as you can,” Schoen said. “But, again, we’re glad we have Malachi Fields. We’re glad we have J.J. So, the utilization of those draft picks that we gave up to get those two players, we’re happy we have them.” Head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that the Giants “always” want to improve the roster. He acknowledged the difficulty, though, of getting deals done. “Easier said than done,” Harbaugh said. “And it’s hard to find players that can make you better, because we have good players. Very good players. So, it’s got to be something that is a need, that fits your financial profile, that fits your price tag. “It’s not like we have a bunch of draft picks, either. We’re not loaded with 12 or 13 draft picks where we’ve got draft capital to burn. We don’t. So, we have to be smart shoppers that way.” Using 2028 picks is a possibility, with Harbaugh saying “it’s easier to put on the credit card.” The difficulty, of course, is that right now those have less value to teams who are selling.
author: Ed Valentine

title: 3 NY Giants-Eagles storylines for Week 9: Can New York handle prosperity?
summary: The New York Giants head to Lincoln Financial Field, a place that has been a house of horrors for the Giants more than a decade, to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The script has been flipped in 2026, with the Giants leading the division, while the reeling Eagles enter the game in last place […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images The New York Giants head to Lincoln Financial Field, a place that has been a house of horrors for the Giants more than a decade, to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The script has been flipped in 2026, with the Giants leading the division, while the reeling Eagles enter the game in last place in the NFC East with a six-game losing streak. Let’s look at some of this week’s storylines. Who’s the bully now? The Giants have not beaten the Eages at Lincoln Financial Field since a 15-7 victory on Nov. 27, 2013. The Eagles have won the NFC East title three of the last four seasons, appearing in two Super Bowls and winning one. The Giants went 11-38 from 2023-2025. Yet, at the midway point of this season we are living in an alternate reality. The Giants are leading the division at 4-2-1 and trying to make moves to improve their chances of reaching the playoffs. They are the betting favorite. The Eagles are trying to figure out what truck ran them over and whether or not Humpty Dumpty can be put back together again. It is an amazing turn of events. Question is, can and will the Giants handle their business? Good teams win games like this one. Who’s toting the rock? Tyrone Tracy is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Cam Skattebo did not practice on Monday due to his own hamstring injury, and head coach John Harbaugh said Skattebo will be “day to day up to the game.” As of this writing, the Giants have not completed a trade for Jonathan Taylor, Derrick Henry, Tony Pollard, Breece Hall , or any other running back. Najee Harris is somewhere looking for a new job. Devin Singletary , who has 18 carries this season, might be the last man standing from the Giants’ original backfield on Sunday. Gregory Desrosiers will be playing in his first NFL game after being signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad. Practice squad back Phil Mafah has five NFL carries. Eric Gray , released in cuts to the 53-man roster, was just re-signed to the practice squad. He has six fumbles in 81 career touches, hardly a confidence-inspring statistic. Can J.J. keep rolling? J.J. McCarthy has played five excellent quarters of football since replacing Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter of a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints. He has fans and media members alike conjuring McCarthy vs. Jaxson Dart scenarios regarding who will quarterback the Giants next season. There is a long way to go, though, and McCarthy has a lot to prove before putting the Giants into a situation where they would actually have to make such a decision. Can McCarthy continue to impress? Can he continue to look like a viable NFL starting quarterback? Can he continue to make the Minnesota Vikings silly for dumping him earlier this season in return for the bargain price of a fifth-round pick? That is to be determined. McCarthy is actually 7-4 as a starting quarterback with five consecutive victories. The common denominator in all of those games? Just like his national championship-winning career at Michigan, McCarthy was never asked to do too much in any of them. The Week 7 victory over Houston, when McCarthy went 20 of 28 passing was the most passes he has thrown in any winning effort as an NFL quarterback. The 252 yards passing was also a career-high. Only twice in his career has McCarthy been asked to throw 30 or more passes. In those two games, both losses, he has gone 36 of 74 (48.6% completions) with 2 touchdown passes and 4 interceptions. NFL teams will figure out how the Giants are using McCarthy, and how they are orienting their passing attack. Looking at McCarthy’s pass charts at NextGen Stats, it is clear he does not like to throw the ball in the middle of the field. Twenty-seven of his 28 passes against the Houston Texans were outside the hash marks, and most were outside the numbers. The charts from all 11 of his NFL starts tell the same story. What happens when teams start squeezing the Giants’ passing attack into the middle of the field, where McCarthy doesn’t want to be? What happens when they jam the box and force McCarthy to win games by throwing 35 or more times? McCarthy’s ability to navigate those things will tell us how much he has truly grown as an NFL quarterback.

title: Jalen Hurts provides “morale boost” by showing up to Eagles practice facility
summary: There have been few, if any, updates since the Eagles placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR as he deals with blood clots that traveled to his lungs. QB1 deserves his privacy and time to heal above all else, but the unknown surrounding how he’s doing, has been a dark cloud lingering over the city and […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images There have been few, if any, updates since the Eagles placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR as he deals with blood clots that traveled to his lungs. QB1 deserves his privacy and time to heal above all else, but the unknown surrounding how he’s doing, has been a dark cloud lingering over the city and fanbase. Thankfully, we finally get a bit of good news, with ESPN’s Tim McManus reporting that Hurts was at the Eagles practice facility on Wednesday, and even sat in on meetings. Eagles QB Jalen Hurts was at the practice facility today, per sources. He sat in on both the team meeting and other meetings. He did not address the team but his presence did provide a morale boost for some. Some players haven’t seen Hurts since he was placed on IR. — Tim McManus (@Tim_McManus) November 4, 2026 There had been early speculation that the quarterback would be allowed around the team, as his recovery would only limit him physically, but head coach Nick Sirianni wouldn’t comment on if Hurts had been, or planned to be, involved in the rest of the season. Earlier on Wednesday, Sirianni would only say that he’s seen Hurts and had been in constant communication with the quarterback, but wouldn’t say whether he was in the building. “ Q. Is there anything you can share with us about how QB Jalen Hurts is doing? Have you talked to him? Have you seen him, communicated with him? ( Reuben Frank ) Nick Sirianni: Of course, I’ve seen him, and I have no new update on anything. But of course, I’ve talked to him and am in constant communication with him and know he’s resting and recovering. I miss him like crazy. But nothing new on that front. I know he’s resting and recovering, and we’re all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery. Q. Has he been here? ( Jeff Neiburg ) Nick Sirianni: Yeah, like I said, no new information there on that.“ Players appreciate the lengths Sirianni will go to protect their privacy, and that carries more weight when talking about potentially life-threatening medical situations. BUT, now we know that Hurts is back in the building, and McManus reports that his presence brought a morale boost to his teammates — and it did the same for Eagles fans. That he’s well enough to be around the team, and also be in meetings to help turn things around, is a welcomed update from a situation that turned serious so quickly.

title: Tanner McKee benched: Joe Milton is the Eagles’ new starting quarterback
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are benching Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton III (that rhymes), according to reporting from ESPN. This news comes after the following exchange between Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni and reporters on Monday afternoon: QUESTION: What changes are you going to make this week and is a change at quarterback on […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Tanner McKee #16 and Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are benching Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton III (that rhymes), according to reporting from ESPN . This news comes after the following exchange between Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni and reporters on Monday afternoon: QUESTION: What changes are you going to make this week and is a change at quarterback on the table? Nick Sirianni: Tanner’s our guy. We’re not making any changes there. […] Lol. In case you’ve been living under a rock (I’m jealous), McKee has been filling in for Jalen Hurts, who is out for the season due to blood clots . McKee hasn’t been great. He is 0-3 as a starter this season with two touchdown to two interceptions and a 76.6 passer rating. In fairness, he wasn’t exactly helped by the coaching staff or the number of injuries to key offensive starters. But it’s not like the Eagles were exactly in love with McKee, who began the season as the team’s third quarterback behind veteran Andy Dalton at No. 2. The Eagles cut Dalton after he threw an interception on his sole pass attempt in relief of Hurts in Week 3. They had interest in bringing the 39-year-old back after Hurts’ outlook worsened … but he reportedly declined and decided to join the Atlanta Falcons instead. Dalton’s rejection led the Eagles to sign Milton away from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad in order to have more depth behind McKee. Milton was the emergency third quarterback behind McKee and rookie Cole Payton during his first game with the Eagles in Week 6. But then Milton moved ahead of Payton as McKee’s backup in Week 7. Milton, who is roughly two months older than the 26-year-old McKee, offers some intrigue. He can run around a bit more than the statuesque McKee, which could be important since the Eagles lead the NFL in unblocked pressures. Milton also has a big frame at 6’5”, 235 pounds (spider graph via Mockdraftable ): Here’s a look at his pre-draft scouting report via NFL.com : Rare physical specimen with the proverbial “arm talent to make all the NFL throws,” but he’s prevented from doing so by a lack of timing, accuracy and touch. Milton is gifted with a cannon for a right arm and can throw the ball as hard or as far as you want. His fastballs are often inaccurate and difficult to catch for moving targets, and he was wildly inconsistent locating his deep throws. He can elude pressure, extend plays and put jaw-dropping highlights on tape, but he’s never been able to mature his game from splashy to consistent. He’s primarily a single-side reader who struggles to improvise with his eyes. The physical ingredients could get him drafted on Day 3, but his lack of development over six seasons discourages his projection. Milton did indeed get selected on Day 3 of the 2024 NFL Draft; the New England Patriots selected him with a sixth-round pick (No. 193) overall. He saw him playing time in a Week 18 game as a rookie, completing 22 of 29 attempts for 241 yards (8.3 average), one touchdown pass, zero interceptions, and a 111.4 passer rating. He also logged 16 rushing yards for one touchdown and four first downs. The Patriots curiously traded Milton and a seventh-round pick to the Cowboys in exchange for a fifth-round pick during the 2025 offseason. Milton served as Dak Prescott’s backup last season and logged a mere 65.1 passer rating on 24 attempts through intermittent playing time. The Cowboys then brought in former Eagles quarterback Sam Howell to compete with Milton for the backup QB job during the 2026 offseason. Despite logging some impressive preseason numbers (67.4% completion, 3 TD to 0 INT, 118.2 passer rating), the Cowboys waived Milton and went with Howell instead. Dallas brought Milton back on their practice squad after he went unclaimed off waivers. Expectations for Milton in Philly should be kept in check. It’s certainly fun to think of him potentially being a diamond in a rough … or at least more aesthetically pleasing to watch than McKee has been. But there’s probably a reason it’s taken this set of circumstances for him to make his first NFL start in a league that’s desperate for good quarterback play. That being said, it feels like there’s now more reason to be excited to watch the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the New York Giants. At least there’s something new to see! (Until we get maybe get tired of watching him play, too.) Maybe this move gives this moribund team a spark? EVAN MOORE: “It’s at least intriguing to consider [Joe Milton over Tanner McKee.] And I realize he probably doesn’t know the offense […] NICK FOLES: “That might actually be a good thing that he doesn’t know the offense that well.” Via “The SZN” 💀💀💀 pic.twitter.com/iaVhbXsiGK — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) November 2, 2026 The Eagles began the 2026 season with four quarterbacks on the roster and none of those four are starting for them in Week 9. — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) November 4, 2026

title: Film Review: Eagles need their best defenders to start playing like their best defenders
summary: I wanted to see a response from the Eagles’ defense after last week. I don’t think we got much. The Commanders finished with 339 yards and averaged 5.9 yards per play. I didn’t come away from the film thinking this defense had improved significantly. Washington still had too many easy pockets and too many running […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jordan Davis #90 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field for halftime during the second quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images I wanted to see a response from the Eagles’ defense after last week. I don’t think we got much. The Commanders finished with 339 yards and averaged 5.9 yards per play. I didn’t come away from the film thinking this defense had improved significantly. Washington still had too many easy pockets and too many running lanes to exploit. In fact, I think the Eagles were fortunate the Commanders didn’t have a more explosive running back. The rushing numbers could have been worse. I know that sounds strange after allowing 135 yards at 5.2 yards per carry, but some of these gaps were enormous. A better back could have turned more of those opportunities into explosive plays. Unlike the offense, I can at least see Vic Fangio trying different things. There were heavier fronts, more man coverage, and more pressure. The problem is that the changes aren’t working consistently, either. And when even Quinyon Mitchell isn’t playing well, you know this defense is in serious trouble. Let’s get into it. Defense I don’t think the run defense bounced back. That is the starting point here. The Eagles used five-man fronts and sometimes put six defenders on the line, but the Commanders still created some huge rushing lanes. Jalen Carter had an inconsistent game, which we will get to, but Jordan Davis was disappointing again. When Davis is playing well, he can occupy space and keep the linebackers clean. When he isn’t, the whole run defense looks much more vulnerable. That has been the case for a while, and it is why his recent performances bother me so much. I know he’s likely hurt, but he is still out there, so I’m only judging what’s on the field. Eagles' Defense All22 Thread vs. Washington. 1) I don't think the run defense bounced back, and I think a good running back may have had some explosive runs against this front. Even with a 5-man front (and sometimes 6!), Washington seemed to create a lot of openings in the run… pic.twitter.com/SWtYnA7Qsc — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 3, 2026 This is third-and-1. Look at the space the Eagles create for the offense. Both defensive tackles slant in opposite directions, and the middle of the defense opens up. You are making a short-yardage conversion far easier than it needs to be. I don’t know whether these are called slants or whether the tackles have the freedom to react to the blocks in front of them. I don’t know the answer. But whatever the rule is, the result cannot be acceptable. If the movement is called, someone has to account for the space it creates. If players choose to go around blocks, they have to understand what they are leaving behind. Linebackers can’t do anything when offensive linemen climb directly onto them. Getting around a double team is only useful if you can affect the run. If you swim away from the point of attack and allow a blocker to climb cleanly, you have made life easier for the offense. Some of the up-front movement in this game was maddening. The Eagles’ slants are so hit-and-miss. If they slant the right way, it can work. But it feels so boom/bust. 2) This is on 3rd and 1! The double slant with both DTs going in opposite directions happened again, and it opened up these huge lanes in the middle of the defense. Are the players being coached to slant in opposite directions, or are they just allowed the freedom to choose… pic.twitter.com/4mubPYuqWo — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 3, 2026 I have criticized Andrew Mukuba plenty, and he made more poor plays in this game. But I want to give him credit for the way he kept playing. Some defenders on this team look passive right now. Mukuba was still flying toward the football and trying to make something happen. That matters to me when things are going badly. You can question the tackling technique here, but the forced fumble is all about effort. He flies downhill and knocks the ball out of Chig Okonkwo’s hands, and Zack Baun recovers it. The turnover gave the offense possession at the Commanders’ 26-yard line and set up the Eagles’ only touchdown. Whatever else I say about Mukuba, he helped create an opportunity to win this game. 3) I think Mukuba made a number of poor plays once again in this game, but I will give him credit for how he played. Some players on this defense are going through the motions and playing very passively. Whatever you think of Mukuba (and his tackle technique here!), he is… pic.twitter.com/ZcS3bp4LUE — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 3, 2026 This might be the worst slant of the game. Byron Young is already aligned with a significant gap between himself and Nolan Smith. He then slants inside and makes that space even bigger. Look at the right guard and right tackle. They can head straight to the second level without dealing with a defensive lineman first. How is this supposed to work? The Eagles end up with four defenders accounting for three gaps on one side of the formation, while the run goes the other way. With a better block from the right guard, this could have been a very long gain. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. makes an excellent play to limit the damage. Asking your linebacker to rescue a rep like this is a terrible way to live. This is also why I am reluctant to judge the linebackers purely by whether they get off blocks. Trotter has limitations when a big lineman gets into his frame, but look at how easily those linemen are reaching him. The defensive front has to give him a chance. 4) This has to be the worst slant of the game. Someone, explain what is going on. Byron Young is already lined up with a huge gap between himself and Nolan Smith. Then he makes it even wider by slanting inside. Look at the size of the gap! Look at the RG and RT! They can just… pic.twitter.com/HkbqCL0rRX — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 3, 2026 The run defense was bad, but the pass rush was equally frustrating. Fangio cannot consistently affect the quarterback with four rushers, and it is killing his defense. Here, the Eagles drop both edge defenders and bring a linebacker, changing where the rush comes from. It makes very little difference. Jayden Daniels gets a pocket that most quarterbacks would happily take all night. Daniels can easily see the field and deliver the football. You can ask the secondary to cover well, but you cannot keep giving an NFL quarterback this much comfort. The Eagles generated pressure on only 30.3% of dropbacks despite the higher blitz rate. At some point, someone has to beat a block. 5) The run defense was not good, but the pass rush was equally bad. Vic Fangio just can't win with 4, and it's killing his scheme. They drop both edge defenders here and send a LB, but nothing comes. You will not see many better pockets in the NFL. Look how easy this is for… pic.twitter.com/K8Sce69myq — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) November 3, 2026 The Commanders’ under-center outside zone caused problems, too. They used motion away from the run to pull Cooper DeJean out of the box and change the numbers for the run fit. That is a straightforward way to make a defender move before attacking the space he leaves, and the Eagles didn’t handle it well enough. Once again, watch the defensive line. All three interior defenders move left, and the run goes right. Look at the gap between Moro Ojomo and Arnold Ebiketie. The back has far too much room to work with. I know I sound like a broken record, but this looks like a fundamentally poor run defense. The Commanders ran outside successfully, especially from under center. Across all concepts, they gained 106 yards on 17 carries from under center, compared with 29 yards on nine shotgun runs. That difference fits what we are seeing here. 6) The Eagles had a real issue with under-center outside…

summary: There’s no argument the Philadelphia Eagles offense is bad. The 2026 unit is historically bad. The Eagles are 29th in the NFL in points per game (17.1) and 30th in points per drive (1.61). They’re 32nd in yards per game (265.3) and yards per play (4.4), far from the offensive juggernauts the franchise has posted […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts during the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s no argument the Philadelphia Eagles offense is bad. The 2026 unit is historically bad. The Eagles are 29th in the NFL in points per game (17.1) and 30th in points per drive (1.61). They’re 32nd in yards per game (265.3) and yards per play (4.4), far from the offensive juggernauts the franchise has posted this century — whether that would be from Andy Reid, Chip Kelly, Doug Pederson, or even Nick Sirianni. There has only been one Eagles team that has put up fewer points than the 2026 squad this century. The 2012 Eagles averaged just 16.6 points per game, and they ended up with a 4-12 record in what would be Reid’s last season. The 1.61 points per possession is also the lowest since 2012. The 265.3 yards per game is the lowest through eight games since 1999 (244.0), and that Eagles team started 1-7 before rallying to finish 5-11 (year one under Reid). The 4.42 yards per play is the lowest since 1999 (3.92), and only the 1998 offense was worse than those two (3.73). Those 1998 Eagles were an abomination. They were 30th out of 30 teams in points per game (10.1) and yards per game (261.7). That was the only time in franchise history the Eagles finished in the 30s in points and yards per game. If points per possession and yards per possession were measured in 1998, the Eagles would have been last in those categories too. The 2026 Eagles have the worst offense this century, and is the worst Eagles offense since 1998. That unit had Bobby Hoying start the seaosn before a rotating carousel of quarterbacks that included Rodney Peete and Koy Detmer. The Eagles went from Hoying to Peete before returning to Hoying and eventually Detmer. So how did the 2026 Eagles get to this point? How did they go from a top-10 offense, to middle of the back, to what they are now — all over the past year? There were quite a few contributing factors towards the Eagles offense reaching historically bad levels for the franchise. 1. Jeff Stoutland deciding not to return The Eagles offensive line was middle of the pack last season, the first time in the Nick Sirianni era the offensive line wasn’t a top-10 unit. Outside of Lane Johnson, all the other starters on the offensive line started 14+ games — so injuries didn’t play a factor in the mediocrity. Stoutland’s role as run-game coordinator also regressed, as Nick Sirianni and former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo began incorporating different run designs to the offense. With these changes in place, Stoutland reportedly wasn’t consulted about them as his title was in name only. With Stoutland not having a prominent voice as in years past, he decided to step aside after the 2025 season. Chris Kuper was hired as the offensive line coach, despite the Minnesota Vikings ranking 31st in sack rate (11.0%) and 27th in pressure rate allowed per dropback (39.8%) last season. The Vikings were 26th in sack rate (8.0%) and 29th in pressure rate (37.8%) from 2022 to 2025 under Kuper. The Eagles offensive line under Kuper this year? They are 24th in sack rate (7.9%) and 28th in pressure rate (42.7%). They were 19th in sack rate (6.7%) and 20th in pressure rate (35.4%) last year. 2. The Kevin Patullo hire, followed by Sean Mannion hire The Eagles were coming off a Super Bowl victory in the 2024 season, but offensive coordinator Kellen Moore was leaving after one season to take the New Orleans Saints head coaching job. Philadelphia didn’t have a deep opol of candidates for the offensive coordinator role since the Eagles played into February, so Patullo was promoted from passing game coordinator to offensive coordinator. Patullo was passing game coordinator for four seasons, and came over from the Indianapolis Colts with Nick Sirianni. His lone season as offensive coordinator was a disaster, as the scoring dropped from 27.2 points per game to 22.3 (seventh to 19th) and points per possession from 2.50 to 2.00 (eighth to 21st). Yards per game dropped from 367.2 to 3111.2 (seventh to 24th) and yards per play from 5.6 to 5.2 (11th to 19th). The Eagles went from 24.7% in three-and-out rate to 36.0% (21st to fourth). The offense got worse with Sean Mannion hired to replace Patullo, as the changes to the offensive scheme has made the unit worst. Injuries to the offense haven’t helped (Jordan Mailata is the only player to start every game), but the Eagles are historically bad on offense. To showcase Mannion’s struggles, look at the second half of games.The Eagles average 4.6 points per game and 3.9 yards per play (both 32nd in the NFL). The third quarter is even worse, ranking 32nd in points per game (1.6), yards per game (43.0), yards per carry (2.5), yards per play (3.1), and yards per attempt (4.0). The offense went from bad to worse. 3. Lane Johnson retiring Johnson’s sudden retirement played a factor in how this offense has performed, as the Eagles haven’t won a game since his sudden retirement after Week 4. The Eagles are 0-3 since Johnson retired, and 3-8 in games he’s missed since last season (including playoffs). The Eagles were 122-63-1 with Johnson in the lineup, a .659 win percentage (including postseason). They are 18-30 without him, a .375 win percentage. Johnson’s replacement at right tackle, Markel Bell, has had a rough start to his career. Bell has allowed five sacks in his three starts, and is tied for second amongst right tackles in most sacks allowed. He has allowed a 7.3% pressure rate per dropback this season — seventh-worst amongst right tackles in the NFL. Right tackle is a new position for Bell, and he wasn’t expected to play this year. Bell was expected to take over for Johnson after this season, just three years after moving up to FBS from Holmes Community College. The Eagles were going to have to adjust to life without Johnson at some point. This wasn’t expected to happen this season. 4. Jalen Hurts out for the season Any time a team loses their franchise quarterback hurts. What Jalen Hurts over the past month is way bigge rthan football. Hurts was discovered to have a having a superficial blood clot in his leg following the team’s trip to London, which was discovered before he played in the team’s Week 5 game against the Jaguars. An ultrasound in the middle of that week found the blood clot had moved to his lungs, which put Hurts on blood thinners and ruled him out for the season. The Eagles are 58-25 in games Hurts has started since he became the full-time starting quarterback in 2021, a .699 win percentage. Without Hurts, the Eagles are 3-7 in 10 games — a .300 win percentage. The Eagles passing game has struggled with Hurts, but he has found ways to win football games. They just aren’t getting that when Hurts isn’t on the field. In the three games Tanner McKee has started, the Eagles are 32nd in yards per play (4.2), 31st in yards per attempt (5.6), and 29th in offensive points per game (15.0). McKee has completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with 2 TD, 2 INT, and a 76.6 passer rating. He is 31st out of 32 qualified quarterbacks in yards per attempt (5.6) and 26th in passer rating. There is a massive drop off from Hurts to McKee, who couldn’t beat out Andy Dalton for the QB2 job this summer. 5. Failure to address TE position The Eagles didn’t have the depth at tight end in the 2025 season, despite Dallas Goedert having 11 touchdown catches. Goedert had 591 receiving yards and the rest of the tight ends had a combined 116. While the Eagles ranked 22nd in tight end receiving yards, they also had a significant hole in blocking at the position. The Eagles addressed the position by signing Johnny Mundt to a one-year contract as the blocking tight end and drafting Eli Stowers in the second round to be the TE2 behind Goedert. title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 9 Edition
summary: Now that Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni looks on before a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 9 POWER RANKINGS 1 – Chicago Bears (LW: 5) – The Bears going into Seattle and dominating the reigning Super Bowl champions was really impressive. This team looks like a force to be reckoned with, especially after adding Jeffery Simmons to their defense. Overall strong combination of talent and coaching. Feels like there are NFL teams mastering 4D chess while the Eagles are struggling with tic-tac-toe. https://t.co/kGjci7JymF — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) November 3, 2026 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – The 49ers had a solid bye with Seattle (NFC West threat) and Minnesota (No. 1 seed threat) losing. They’ll host a spunky Raiders team in Week 9. 3 – Buffalo Bills (Last Week: 3) – The Bills have lost one game this season and it was by three points to a division rival. As their conference’s only one-loss team, they have a navigable path to the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoff picture. 4 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 1) – Make that two straight losses for the Chiefs. This team needs some help ahead of the NFL trade deadline and they’ll probably make some moves to get it. 5 – Detroit Lions (LW: 7) – The Lions are the only NFC North team yet to lose a game in their very competitive division. They continue to be ravaged by injuries but they shouldn’t be slept on. 6 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 4) – The Vikings weren’t going to stay undefeated with how inept their offense has been. Their defense is going to make teams really earn wins over them, though. 7 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 9) – The Jags own the NFL’s best point differential at +85. The next closest team is the 49ers at +58. Jacksonville also ranks second in DVOA. They’re a real title contender. 8 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 6) – If the season ended today, which it doesn’t, the Seahawks would actually be on the outside looking in with seven teams ahead of them in the NFC playoff picture. This is still a good team but they’re not an elite team like they were last year. 9 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 8) – Despite being 12.5-point home favorites, the Bengals needed overtime to beat the lowly Titans. Not really ideal to allow Cam Ward to log the third-best passer rating of his career against your defense. 10 – New England Patriots (LW: 11) – It has not been a great vibes season for the Pats but they’re 4-1 in their last five games. Drake Maye has thrown 14 touchdowns to two interceptions for a 122.2 passer rating during that stretch. 11 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 12) – The Rams are benefiting from a softer part of their schedule. It also sounds like Myles Garrett could be back soon. Maybe they’ll make a run. 12 – Denver Broncos (LW: 13) – Unfortunately, Sean Payton is a pretty good coach. The Broncos are tied for the NFL’s best record against the spread this season, a sign that this team is outperforming their expectations. 13 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 15) – The Raiders broke their four-game losing streak with a thrilling win over the Jets. Very interested to see how they fare over their next three games: at San Francisco, vs. Seattle, at Denver. That stretch will be a litmus test for just how real this team is. 14 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 16) – The Packers are lacking a signature win over a good team this season. They’ve beaten lesser competition but have yet to come out on top against a big dog. (I’m not counting the Bears game that Tyson Bagent started.) 15 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 20) – Do we have to take the Steelers seriously? They’re currently the top team in the AFC North, though Cincy’s ceiling appears to be higher. 16 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 10) – Oof. The Ravens are taking a big fall here after losing both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injury. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano might start in Week 9 even though he’s banged up as well. Not looking good. 17 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 14) – The Dallas defense is a joke and Brian Schottenheimer is doing a bad job. That being said, Dak Prescott deserves more blame than he’s getting. The Cowboys actually got a stop in overtime after the Cardinals got the ball first. Only needing to move into Brandon Aubrey’s long field goal range while playing at home, Prescott oversaw a drive that netted -5 yards in three plays and resulted in a punt. That’s a gotta have it moment for the highest paid quarterback in the NFL and he came up extremely small in a huge spot. Hardly the first time! 18 – New York Giants (LW: 18) – The G-Men are returning from their bye as road betting favorites in Philly for the first time since 2009. New York is also looking to boost their roster with more talent ahead of the NFL trade deadline. They just might win the NFC East. 19 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 17) – The Browns had a chance to make people take them more seriously by beating the Steelers in Pittsburgh. They did not come close to making it happen. 20 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 22) – Obligatory mention of the Bucs winning in Week 8 despite not completing a pass. The Bucs are perhaps following the 2024 Eagles script of just running the hell out of the ball. Not a bad strategy if teams can’t stop it! 21 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 19) – Two of the three Panthers’ win this season have come against depth quarterbacks (Cooper Rush and Tanner McKee). They’re not scaring anybody. 22 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 21) – I continue to maintain that the Falcons are the NFL’s most unpredictable team on a weekly basis. They followed up an impressive Week 7 over the 49ers by losing to a team that couldn’t even complete a single pass against them. 23 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 27) – Minshew Mania is running wild on you, brother! The Cards are one win away from surpassing their 2026 projected win total (3.5 games) with nine games left to play. Props to Mike LaFleur for helping his team overachieve expectations. 24 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 23) – The Saints are returning from their bye to host the Sheuder Sanders-led Browns. We’ll see if Kellen Moore can make a run in a weak NFC South. 25 – Houston Texans (LW: 24) – The Texans are returning from their bye to play the Bolts in California. If Houston can’t win this game, stick a fork in them. 26 – Washington Commanders (LW: 28) – The Commanders didn’t exactly look amazing in a win over the Eagles but, hey, they bought some time to keep their season alive in a weak division. We’ll see if they can build on this victory with the Rams, Giants (massive game in the NFC East), and Bengals up next. 27 – Miami Dolphins (LW 29) – After losing their first three games by double digits, the Dolphins’ last four games have been decided by one possession (1-3 in that stretch). Progress? 28 – New York Jets (LW: 30) – The Jets aren’t good but they’ve at least played some entertaining games this season. 29 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 25) – The Eagles are pitiful. I have my doubts that Nick Sirianni is going to survive a failure this massive. If you look at all 27 Eagles teams that have played football this century, the 2026 offense ranks: 27th in points per game 27th in yards per game 27th in yards per play 27th in YPC 27th in 3-and-out percentage 27th in EPA per play 27th in success rate 27th in explosive play rate — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) November 3, 2026 30 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 31) – Taking the Bengals to overtime feels like a moral victory for this group. 31 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 26) – Tanking doesn’t do the Colts much good since they don’t their own their…

title: Eagles News: Moro Ojomo is drawing “real interest” ahead of the NFL trade deadline
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I just don’t believe the Eagles are seriously interested in paying Moro Ojomo after signing Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis to big-money contract extensions. Unless they move on from Carter or Davis … or plan to do so in the offseason. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo #97 waves to the fans during the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 4, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I just don’t believe the Eagles are seriously interested in paying Moro Ojomo after signing Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis to big-money contract extensions. Unless they move on from Carter or Davis … or plan to do so in the offseason. Seems to me like they’ll trade Ojomo ahead of the deadline. If there isn’t a great offer, they can just keep him and hope he factors in to their compensatory pick formula. Now, what can they get for him? Hard to say for sure. I think some might overstate his value considering he has zero sacks this season and only six in his career. But he’s better than those numbers would indicate. Maybe a third-round pick? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL Week 9 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips and trade deadline news – ESPN This could be for edge or interior help, in part because the Jaguars have versatile players such as Travon Walker who can play multiple spots up front. Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo is a person of interest here, though Philly is inclined to keep and potentially extend him. […] Speaking of Philadelphia, my sense is the Eagles could be trading some players but likely won’t engage in a rebuild. As one source pointed out, that’s not in the Eagles’ organizational DNA. We already know they aren’t trading running back Saquon Barkley. Look, let’s not be naive — general manager Howie Roseman will take advantage of good value if it’s there, and supporting players are surely on the radar. But dealing big names would be a mild surprise. Ojomo will be a test of the Eagles’ transitional state. There’s real interest in him (from Jacksonville and others). Whether Philly acts on that interest will tell a lot. Eagles thoughts: Nick Sirianni’s staff stays put, questions at QB and Moro Ojomo’s trade value – The Athletic Moro Ojomo is a fascinating player to watch during the next week leading up to the trade deadline. The Eagles don’t like letting talented homegrown defensive linemen out the door — and they’re feeling the pain of seeing Milton Williams and Josh Sweat go elsewhere — but it’s hard to see a scenario where Ojomo returns next season with Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis still on the roster. Sports Illustrated reported last week that the Eagles are telling teams they’re not interested in trading Ojomo and want to keep him, but will they pay three defensive tackles top-of-the-league money (assuming that’s what Ojomo commands on the open market)? They seem to have made their choice when they signed Carter and Davis. “Howie (Roseman) and (Jeffrey) Lurie mean so much to me for giving me this opportunity to play for this team,” Roseman said. “I think I was the 23rd DT picked up? If we could make it work, I love playing for the city; I love working hard for the city. I want to produce results for the city. I hate letting them down and being 2-5 like we are. … I mean, I don’t think any door is shut. I wouldn’t say that. You don’t know what the future holds.” It’s a nice thought. It doesn’t seem realistic. The Eagles would be smart to get compensation for Ojomo now, especially in what could be a seller’s market at defensive tackle. If they can land a third-round pick, it would be better than any potential compensatory pick in 2028. Perhaps they can find a way to get a second-round pick. Ojomo said he doesn’t know what will happen — “I just work here,” he said — but he has the talent to help a contending team down the stretch. It hasn’t shown in his statistics this year. I believe in the player, and he’s also a value-add in the locker room. The Eagles will miss him if he’s gone. It’s the reality of the NFL. “I like the way I started the season a little bit,” Ojomo said. “The last couple games being banged up and all that, I want to get back to kind of playing confident, fast. I think that ‘get off’ is one of the things I do at a really high level. That’s one of the things I want to kind of lock in on these next however many games.” Eagles-Commanders Film Review: The idea that Jalen Hurts was holding this offense back should be finished by now – BGN I’m struggling to get particularly angry about this offense anymore. There were times when watching the Eagles lose 27-10 to the Commanders bored me. We keep seeing players asked to do things that don’t suit them. Every week, I sit down hoping to see something different, and every week, it feels like I’m writing about the same problems. The Eagles scored their final points with 4:27 remaining in the first quarter. There was an awful lot of football left to sit through after that. The idea that Jalen Hurts was holding this offense back, and that everything would look dramatically different with a quarterback who preferred playing under center and throwing over the middle, should be finished by now. Tanner McKee hasn’t transformed anything. It’s the same offense, with the same limitations, and very little downfield passing game. That doesn’t mean Hurts was playing perfectly or that McKee has played well. He hasn’t. It means changing the quarterback was never going to solve all of this. Bowen: As the Eagles lurch further into the throes of disaster, shouldn’t somebody down there get at least a little upset about this?- PHLY Eagles I would not make a good NFL head coach or coordinator for many reasons. High on that list would be, I can’t imagine being at ground level of a disaster like we currently are experiencing with the Eagles, and not reacting with urgency, frustration, and alarm. The Eagles’ coordinators held their weekly media briefings Tuesday. I’m smart enough to know that the manner they convey to reporters doesn’t necessarily mirror their private reactions. They don’t want their players to think they are panicking. Even so, the matter-of-fact, “we just need to tweak this or that” patter at this point in the season is jarring to the ear. Six losses in a row? The last three by double figures? All to teams that currently have losing records? Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has been known to get acerbic when his players aren’t performing to his standards. Not this season, which is shaping up as the worst by far in Fangio’s three years with the Eagles. Vic seems a bit distant these days, almost sedated. When asked to comment on specific players, he either praises them, as he has done repeatedly when asked about Cooper DeJean’s uncharacteristic struggles, or refers to injuries they are working through. 2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Lions retain top spot, Colts fall without Quenton Nelson – PFF 22) EAGLES — Left guard Landon Dickerson had his best game of the season, amassing a 72.8 PFF grade in the Eagles’ loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday night. Having permitted nine pressures from 75 pass-blocking snaps in his previous two starts, he allowed just two on 44 snaps this week. However, the right side of the line was ineffective, with Tyler Steen and Markel Bell combining to give up eight pressures. In Roob’s Eagles Stats: A big pile of misery broken up by tiny encouraging blips – NBCSP The Eagles have had fewer than 350 yards of offense in all eight games so far this year, with a high of 341 at Tennessee. This is the first time in more than half a century they’ve opened a season with eight games under 350 net yards. Last time it happened was the first 11 games of the 1971 season, when their yardage high was 315 yards in a 37-14 loss to the Bengals in the season opener at Riverfront Stadium. title: Just how hard is the rest of the Steelers’ schedule?
summary: The Steelers are 6-2 and hold sole possession of the AFC North as they enter a Week 9 bye. But stop me if you’ve heard this one before: The second half of Pittsburgh’s schedule looks quite a bit harder than the first. Or does it? After facing the Falcons, Patriots, Bengals, Browns (twice), Colts, Buccaneers […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers are 6-2 and hold sole possession of the AFC North as they enter a Week 9 bye. But stop me if you’ve heard this one before: The second half of Pittsburgh’s schedule looks quite a bit harder than the first. Or does it? After facing the Falcons, Patriots, Bengals, Browns (twice), Colts, Buccaneers and Saints before the bye, Pittsburgh has played in four games where its opponent would have a winning record at midseason, losing to New England (now 5-3), defeating Cincinnati (now 5-2), and splitting its series with Cleveland (5-3). After the bye, the Steelers face the Bengals again, along with the Eagles (2-6), Broncos (6-2), Texans (2-5), Jaguars (5-2), Ravens (4-4; twice), Panthers (3-4) and Titans (1-7). At first glance, it’s a harder stretch than the first. The Jaguars, and maybe even the Broncos, are better than anyone the Steelers have played so far. The Panthers, despite their poor record, might be the best team in a hapless NFC South lineup. The Texans are 2-1 over the last three weeks despite a 0-4 start to the year, and we all know the Ravens will play the Steelers tough no matter the circumstances. But that group of teams looks weaker than it did before the season started, no? Of the Steelers’ final nine opponents, only three currently have winning records. (Although it’s worth mentioning two matchups against the currently-.500 Ravens). And if we compare the combined midseason winning percentages of the Steelers’ first eight opponents (0.484) to their last nine (0.471), it’s incredibly close. Similarly, while the Steelers didn’t face starting quarterbacks against the Falcons and Buccaneers earlier this season, they won’t either for the upcoming Eagles game ( likely Joe Milton under center ) and at least one of the Ravens games ( likely Jacoby Brissett until Lamar Jackson possibly returns ). Of course, there are far more factors in play than just records and starting quarterbacks — and it’s an unfortunate truth of football that all the teams mentioned in this article will likely have some new, meaningful injuries between now and Week 18. And while the Steelers have the same number of games in Pittsburgh (four) in each half of the season, it’s worth noting that the team’s next five matchups are outside of the usual 1 p.m. EST Sunday time slot. You could definitely argue the Steelers’ second-half schedule is going to be more difficult than the first; I probably would. But the difference isn’t as extreme as you might expect. That’s good news for the Steelers, who already have a 77% postseason probability per NFL.com , currently the AFC’s third seed at 6-2. Pittsburgh’s road to the playoffs remains a promising one entering the bye week.

full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Former Steelers cornerback Arthur Maulet is retiring at 33 years old, NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reported Wednesday evening. Physical NFL slot cornerback Arthur Maulet is retiring after 9 seasons. Maulet made his biggest impacts with Steelers, Jets and Ravens. Now curtain closes. pic.twitter.com/ihlUdyJSzv — Cameron Wolfe (@CameronWolfe) November 5, 2026 Maulet was an undrafted free agent in 2017 out of Memphis who started his college career at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Mississippi. In the NFL, the 5’9 cornerback played games for six different teams over his career. He recorded his most games played (33) and second-most games started (eight) with the Steelers over the 2021 and 2022 seasons after recording 11 total starts with the Jets in 2019 and 2020. Over his time in the black and gold, Maulet logged 106 total tackles, two sacks, seven tackles for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. title: Former Steelers RB Merril Hoge joins in praise of Mike McCarthy
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 and in prime position to win the AFC North in back-to-back seasons.  Aaron Rodgers has turned back the clock and is playing at a solid level, leading the Steelers offense to four consecutive victories. People didn’t know what to expect with Mike Tomlin out of the picture and Pittsburgh’s own Mike […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 and in prime position to win the AFC North in back-to-back seasons. Aaron Rodgers has turned back the clock and is playing at a solid level, leading the Steelers offense to four consecutive victories. People didn’t know what to expect with Mike Tomlin out of the picture and Pittsburgh’s own Mike McCarthy taking over. More of the same? A better-executed offense? The first losing season in over two decades? So far, so good. Apologies and credit where credit is due have been the main theme of the bye week for many in the media who were wrong, at least to this point, about the 6-2 team. NFL analyst and former offensive guard Damien Woody is surprised by how McCarthy has anchored the veteran team. “I have to admit, I did not envision the Pittsburgh Steelers playing as well as they’re playing so far as we approach the halfway point,” Woody said on The OG Football Show. “I got to give my flowers to Mike McCarthy.” The Steelers offense ranks 13th in total yards per game (351.8) and 14th in rushing (117.9). After years of failing to run the football, McCarthy and offensive line coach James Campen are delivering a legitimate running game. “Mike McCarthy has done a hell of a job,” Woody said. “People frown upon him, but all Mike McCarthy has done is win in Green Bay; he won in Dallas, and now in his first year in Pittsburgh he has them sitting atop the AFC North… Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers and company are pushing all the right buttons. The Pittsburgh Steelers, to me, are the absolute surprise so far.” Former Steeler and current broadcaster Merril Hoge believes the Super Bowl champion coach belongs in Canton for his decades of success in three cities. “If you took his resume and his credentials and stacked it up to Hall of Famers, it’s very similar and better in some ways,” Hoge said. “He gets no credit for that. Nobody thinks of him like that. But he can stack up against not only great ones that are still coaching today, but those that sit in the Hall.” The Steelers lead the NFL in sacks. Jaylen Warren is in contention for Offensive Player of the Year and holds more rushing yards than Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor, and Christian McCaffrey. Pittsburgh’s schedule will sharpen with games against Philadelphia, Denver, Houston, Jacksonville, and Baltimore (twice) coming up. The Steelers always have difficult battles against the Ravens and haven’t won in Philadelphia since 1965. The Steelers are exceeding expectations, and historically, 90% of teams that start 6-2 make the playoffs. Are the pieces coming together to make a playoff run for the first time in a full decade?
