title: Tom Brady says no one is stopping Aaron Rodgers, Steelers in the AFC North
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers enter their bye week with a 6-2 record sitting alone at the top of the AFC North. Their run game has been a large focal point, as they lead the NFL in EPA per rush since Week 3, and Jaylen Warren currently sits third in the league in scrimmage yards. The defense […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers enter their bye week with a 6-2 record sitting alone at the top of the AFC North. Their run game has been a large focal point, as they lead the NFL in EPA per rush since Week 3, and Jaylen Warren currently sits third in the league in scrimmage yards. The defense has been terrific, as well. Over Pittsburgh’s four-game win streak, their defense ranks third in the league in defensive success rate while allowing just 14.2 points per game. However, Tom Brady says that Aaron Rodgers also deserves a good amount of credit for the way that he’s played this season. “Aaron’s always been a very aggressive passer,” Brady said . “If something was open down the field, he’d cut it loose. I’ve been really impressed with Aaron this year because he was a very mobile quarterback for a long time. He could move in the pocket and buy a bunch of time. He doesn’t quite have that same elusiveness, and he’s really transitioned to becoming more of a pocket passer.“ Brady adds that Rodgers’ control has been impressive, and that he doesn’t see anyone stopping the Steelers in the AFC North. “He’s always been an incredible passer of the football, but now that he’s playing from the pocket, he’s totally in control. I think he’s got six interceptions this year, and five of them have been off the hands of his receivers or a Hail Mary. He’s making incredible decisions. He has always made great decisions, and that’s why that team’s first place in the AFC North, and I don’t see anyone stopping them in that division, either.” Pittsburgh will face the Cincinnati Bengals on the road in Week 10 after the Bengals return from Madrid where they’ll face the Atlanta Falcons in Week 9. title: Steelers’ jumbo offensive line is one of the best units in the league
summary: After trouncing the Cleveland Browns 27-6 at Acrisure Stadium on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers are one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Heading into their bye, the team is riding a four-game winning streak and starting to generate some national buzz after pundits mostly wrote them off as irrelevant over the summer and first […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After trouncing the Cleveland Browns 27-6 at Acrisure Stadium on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers are one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Heading into their bye, the team is riding a four-game winning streak and starting to generate some national buzz after pundits mostly wrote them off as irrelevant over the summer and first quarter of the season. Whether it’s talking to fellow fans or listening to the players conduct interviews, there’s an unmistakable energy and optimism surrounding this team that hasn’t been felt in quite some time. The vibes are thriving in Pittsburgh right now. But it wasn’t that long ago that the exact opposite was true. Following the Steelers October 1 loss to the Browns on Thursday Night Football, the Steelers felt lost. With a 2-2 record and both sides of the ball struggling to find any semblance of an identity, the fanbase was dejected. And judging by how players and coaches alike spoke this week about the trip home from Cleveland, they were doing some soul-searching of their own. Steelers DC Patrick Graham said the turning point for both the defense overall & himself in his role was the bus ride after the loss in CLE Oct 1 He reflected while listening to Amy Winehouse "She's depressed in the song; I'm depressed on that day" Steelers haven't lost since — Chris Adamski (@C_AdamskiTrib) November 2, 2026 @byjoeybray TJ Watt practically name dropped the “day of reflection” in postgame interviews yesterday after the game. pic.twitter.com/HnPlV296ob — Bob Nutting Burner (@nuttingsburner) November 3, 2026 T.J. Watt and the defense’s performance since that game are, of course, a crucial element in the winning streak the Steelers find themselves in. But what I want to examine further today is something that first began to emerge when the Steelers were overseas in Paris: the return of Pittsburgh’s formations utilizing six offensive linemen. Starting in Week 7 against the Saints, the Steelers have reintroduced their jumbo, 6 OL packages in earnest. This has been a welcome development since it was so effective for PIT a year ago. With these 6 OL packages, PIT is averaging +0.11 EPA/play — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 In 2025, the Steelers and then-offensive coordinator Arthur Smith began experimenting with jumbo packages that brought guard Spencer Anderson onto the field for some extra heft in the trenches. Not to disimilarly from the NBA, Anderson began to fill a “Sixth Man” role for the team, frequently joining the starting five linemen and tight end Darnell Washington up front. The strategy was easy enough to follow; in a league where defenses are trying to match up with high-flying passing attacks by using lighter linebackers and getting five or more defensive backs on the field, countering with bigger bodies presents an offensive the opportunity to overpower their opponents on the ground. With a coaching staff shakeup and Anderson initially opening the season as the starting right guard, the Steelers abandoned their trendy 2025 formation during the first month of the season. However, given how successful it was last year and how running the ball is clearly still their biggest strength, it shouldn’t be that surprising to see the Steelers re-exploring this wrinkle in their offense. Since Week 7, the Steelers have called 29 plays with Anderson on the field as a sixth lineman. Turns out, it’s not unlike riding a bike, because the team has picked it up right where they left it. Pittsburgh has used four different personnel groupings with jumbo, but they have heavily leaned into one grouping: 11 personnel (one running back, one tight end, two wide receivers) — 21 plays 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends, one receiver) – four plays 20 personnel (two running backs, zero tight ends, two wide receivers — three plays 22 personnel (two running backs, two tight ends, zero wide receivers) – one play The most effective and most used of these 6OL personnel packages has been 11P. PIT has 21 such plays. Per Sumer Sports, they are averaging: +0.12 EPA/pass (4 attempts) +0.25 EPA/rush. +0.22 EPA/play average. NFL average is +0.05 EPA/play — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 When you look at the stats above, you may be wondering what this exactly tells us. For those of you less familiar with the Expected Points Added (EPA) metric, it’s a stat that takes into account field position, as well as down and distance, and how many points years and years of historical data tell us we can expect from a given play based on those factors. Outperforming those expectations gets you a positive EPA, and underperforming generates negative EPA. Running plays, historically, are less likely to generate explosive plays than passing. Likewise, an offense is considered less likely to pick up a first down with a rushing attempt from second-and-long or third-and-long. That makes generating positive EPA on the ground much more difficult overall. Through eight weeks, only five offenses average a positive EPA per rush: Buffalo (+0.11), Kansas City (+0.11), Pittsburgh (+0.07), San Francisco (+0.07), and Jacksonville (+0.01). Consider that further. On 17 attempts, the Steelers are averaging more than three times as much EPA per rush from their jumbo 11 personnel package than they are this season overall. That highlights just how explosive they’ve been from these looks. Explosive gain for 29 yards against the Saints pic.twitter.com/ZFOXWfVGcf — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 Put in simpler terms, the Steelers have run the ball 24 times with six linemen on the field, whether that be with 11, 12, 20, or 22 personnel. Nine of those rushing attempts (37.5%) converted a first down or scored a touchdown. Nine of those plays also generated gains of at least five yards. Four runs (16.6%) went for 10 or more yards. Steelers left side obliterates the Saints, and PIT gets rookie RT Max Iheanachor on the move to clear out the LB in the middle. Anderson does a great job sealing off his man, and Washington and Bernard make the edge and CB freeze long enough for Warren to explode through the hole pic.twitter.com/8EvthOhXko — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 And it hasn’t mattered which player the Steelers have had in the backfield; both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle have been productive. Warren has 16 carries for 95 yards (5.9 YPC) and a score. Dowdle has turned eight carries into 35 yards (4.4 YPC) and a touchdown. PIT fans, remember when we dreaded any toss plays being called? No more. Here, three sets of double teams set the table, and Fautanu used a nifty move to box out his defender like it was basketball to open the lane for Dowdle to burst through for 16 yards pic.twitter.com/czQWAEkyfc — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 Another toss, this time for 5 yds Washington/Anderson with a double team that takes out a second defender with his own guy. Fautanu/Frazier climbing to the 2nd level. McCormick initially looks like he overshoots, but that was either a great sell job or an amazing recovery pic.twitter.com/K0au7tjrAA — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 This play was a fun one that saw Rodgers manipulate the defense with the threat of a pass, even though the Steelers have only a handful of passing attempts from these looks. A Rodgers pump fake gets the Saints' right side and LB (20) to react. Iheanachor makes the LB pay for the misstep, Anderson moves his man just enough, Washington sets an edge, & rookie WR Germie Bernard with a marvelous bit of blocking on the S to let Warren do the rest for 5 yds pic.twitter.com/5pMSX7REFw — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) November 2, 2026 Against the Saints in Paris, the Steelers ran the ball 12 times against one passing attempt out of these looks. In Week 8 against the Browns, they once again ran it 12 times. Here were five of the highlights: 1. Dowdle 9-yard TD Dowdle…

title: Seahawks-Cardinals injury report: Leonard Williams held out with stinger, Drew Lock still limited
summary: As the Seattle Seahawks prepare for a pivotal NFC West contest with the Arizona Cardinals, they’ll face a boatload of injuries, according to Wednesday’s estimated injury report. The Seahawks had six players miss practice with injury, including quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams. “Big Cat” was held out […]
full_text: As the Seattle Seahawks prepare for a pivotal NFC West contest with the Arizona Cardinals, they’ll face a boatload of injuries, according to Wednesday’s estimated injury report. The Seahawks had six players miss practice with injury, including quarterback Sam Darnold , left tackle Charles Cross and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams. “Big Cat” was held out with a stinger he suffered on Monday night against the Chicago Bears and would be a massive loss for the team, especially in the run game. Nose tackle Brandon Pili also did not practice with a back injury, leaving Seattle thin at the position and facing a red-hot running back in Tyler Allgeier. With Darnold out, Seahawks Mike Macdonald indicated that backup Drew Lock would start in his place . Lock has been battling an elbow injury for the last three weeks, was inactive in their last two games, and was once again limited in practice on Wednesday with a right elbow injury. If Lock can’t go, second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe would need to step in to make his first NFL start, which would be as entertaining as it would be stressful. Sticking with the offense, newly acquired star guard Quenton Nelson was limited by a knee injury, as was backup Anthony Bradford. With Josh Jones poised to start another week at left tackle, more offensive line injuries have to be the last thing Seahawks fans want to see. While wide receiver Rashid Shaheed was held out of practice and appears on track to miss his second straight game, his backup Tory Horton was a full go with a hand injury. Take the good news where you can get it! The report proves to be a mixed bag for the Seahawks defense as well. Edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who missed last week, was limited with an ankle injury, and Nick Emmanwori was a full participant with a shoulder injury. Those two returning to form in the lineup would be a massive boost for the “Dark Side” defense that is reeling from giving up 34 points on Monday. As for the Cardinals, breakout wide receiver Michael Wilson was limited in practice by rest and a rib injury, which could give him a chance to play on Sunday. Wilson broke two ribs and put up 111 yards and a touchdown on eight catches in Arizona’s win over the Dallas Cowboys last week. Defensive tackle Walter Nolen was also limited with an ankle injury. Arizona will likely be without running back Bam Knight, who would back up Allgeier, as he did not practice on Wednesday due to a concussion. The Cardinals held stars Budda Baker and Josh Sweat out of practice, but it was not injury-related. Humorously, the Cardinals held quarterback Jacoby Brissett out with “rest,” which apparently means getting shipped off to the Baltimore Ravens . Here is the full Seahawks report:

title: Seahawks sign former UFL MVP following Sam Darnold injury
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have a banged up quarterback room, and unlike the last time Sam Darnold was injured, they are adding another player to the roster. Prior to the start of Wednesday’s practice, the Seahawks signed former Nebraska and Kansas State quarterback Adrian Martinez, who was most recently with the San Francisco 49ers. This comes […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have a banged up quarterback room, and unlike the last time Sam Darnold was injured, they are adding another player to the roster. Prior to the start of Wednesday’s practice, the Seahawks signed former Nebraska and Kansas State quarterback Adrian Martinez , who was most recently with the San Francisco 49ers. This comes after Darnold was ruled out of Week 9 against the Arizona Cardinals due to a quad injury , in addition to a cracked rib suffered in Monday’s loss to the Chicago Bears. Drew Lock is slated to start, but he’s dealing with a right elbow injury that caused him to miss the last two games, and therefore Martinez joins the practice squad as some insurance. Martinez’s career highlight at the professional level was not in the NFL, but the UFL. As starting quarterback of the Birmingham Stallions, Martinez compiled a 6-1 record as a starter, throwing 15 touchdown passes and only 3 interceptions, while also rushing for over 500 yards and 3 more TDs. His performances earned him league MVP honors. In the 2024 UFL Championship against the San Antonio Brahmas, Martinez was named game MVP after throwing a touchdown to former Seahawks draft pick Gary Jennings Jr, while adding a couple of scores on the ground in a 25-0 victory. If Lock is still limited due to his elbow injury, it’s more likely than not that Martinez will be a game day elevation against the Cardinals this Sunday. Seattle also brought Jamie Sheriff back to the practice squad after his brief stint with the Los Angeles Rams. Wide receiver Malick Meiga and linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo were released to make room for Sheriff and Martinez.

title: Seahawks Week 9 national power rankings: Seattle falls out of the top 10
summary: Entering Week 8, the Seattle Seahawks moved back up the national power rankings after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs. However, now after losing by double digits to the Chicago Bears, they surely will drop back down. The question is by how much. Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher […]
full_text: Entering Week 8, the Seattle Seahawks moved back up the national power rankings after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs . However, now after losing by double digits to the Chicago Bears , they surely will drop back down. The question is by how much. Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (B/R), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. Let’s start with the two sites who were the most punitive of Seattle. Both CBS Sports and BR have dropped the Seahawks down six spots, out of the top 10. CBS Sports, which dropped Seattle from 8th to 14th best in the league stated that Sam Darnold “just doesn’t look right” . Meanwhile B/R, which dropped Seattle from 7th to 13th, note that their 4-4 record appropriately represents how the team has performed this year. B/R further notes that the domination over the Kansas City Chiefs “appears to be an aberration .” Not all national websites were as harsh on Seattle. PFT dropped Seattle only two spots, from 7th to 9th , noting that the Seahawks (or the Los Angeles Rams) very well may not make the playoffs this year. ESPN also dropped Seattle, from 5th to 8th . In their rankings this week, ESPN talks about the biggest trade acquisition teams have ever made. Their choice for Seattle was Marshawn Lynch. The highest ranking the Seahawks earned this week was from NFL.com who ranked Seattle 7th-best in the league , down three spots from last week. Adding to the concerns about the offense, NFL.com also noted that offensive coordinator, Brian Fleury may be on a job watch after the offensive performance against the Bears. Overall the national landscape were not gentle with their rankings of Seattle this week. This may be a culmination of the team losing three out of their last four games rather than a reaction to one loss to a strong Chicago Bears team. The offense continues to struggle, and if it continues, it is difficult to see the Seahawks make noise in the playoffs this year (that is if they even make it). Entering week 8, the average power rankings between the five polled sites was 5.8. Entering Week 9, that average has fallen all the way to 10.2. Next week the Seahawks have a chance to get back on track against the Arizona Cardinals.

title: Former Seahawks draft pick has become one of the NFL’s unlikely sack leaders
summary: One of the few bright spots on yet another very bad Tennessee Titans team is a former Seattle Seahawks pass rusher. Jacob Martin, a 2018 sixth-round pick who was famously part of the Jadeveon Clowney trade just prior to the 2019 regular season, has hung around in the NFL for nearly a decade. He’s been […]
full_text: One of the few bright spots on yet another very bad Tennessee Titans team is a former Seattle Seahawks pass rusher. Jacob Martin, a 2018 sixth-round pick who was famously part of the Jadeveon Clowney trade just prior to the 2019 regular season, has hung around in the NFL for nearly a decade. He’s been a rotational pass rusher with the Seahawks, Houston Texans, New York Jets, Denver Broncos, Indianapolis Colts, Washington Commanders, and now he finds himself in Nashville for his ninth season. It’s also his best season to date; one that has him as one of the NFL’s best at sacking the quarterback. After taking Joe Burrow down not once, not twice, but three times in Tennessee’s wild 43-36 overtime loss against the Cincinnati Bengals, Martin has already reached a career-high 6.5 sacks through eight games. Only T.J. Watt, Will Anderson, Chase Young, and Greg Rousseau have more sacks than Martin. So, the @Titans ' pass rush was going to fall off a cliff without Jeffery Simmons, right? Not if Jacob Martin had anything to say about it (and he had a LOT to say about it). pic.twitter.com/eWEZMryfp2 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 2, 2026 Titans pass rusher Jacob Martin was incredible today with 11 pressures, 6 pass rush wins and 3 sacks. He was destroying the left side of the Bengals offensive line, especially on blitzes On the 11 dropbacks Martin had a pressure the Bengals offense had a -0.60 EPA/dropback and a… pic.twitter.com/KM89hDoSSw — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 2, 2026 At 30 years old, Martin appears to be the definition of a late bloomer. He had 5.5 sacks last season with the Commanders, and as a starter on the Titans he’s putting up very impressive numbers under Robert Saleh. Martin leads the Titans with 21 pressures, his 7 quick pressures (which is a pressure within 2.5 seconds) puts him on pace to match if not surpass his previous career high of 16. He already has 14 QB hits, which is only four fewer than all of last season, and his tackles for loss is already at a career high. The only thing to note is his pressure rate of 11.4% is modest, but he’s turning his pressures into sacks, and his one-year, $9 million contract looks like it’ll parlay into a bigger deal next offseason … an offseason in which Seattle will likely be overhauling its edge rush unit. Meanwhile, fellow former Seahawk Boye Mafe recorded a strip-sack of Cam Ward in the same game, bringing his total to 5.5 on the season for the Bengals. His first season in Cincinnati is looking like one of the best of his career, and the Bengals should be in good shape to return to the playoffs given their remaining schedule. Good for both of them!

title: Seahawks Reacts Survey: Is Sam Darnold Seattle’s starting quarterback in 2027?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. It’s crazy to be talking about an important part of a Super Bowl champion being off the team completely just a short time later, but we […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. It’s crazy to be talking about an important part of a Super Bowl champion being off the team completely just a short time later, but we might be at that point with Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold. The NFC Championship Game brilliance seems like a distant memory given the horror show to start the 2026 season. Seattle’s offensive woes are not exclusively Darnold’s fault, but he certainly has a helping hand in this mess . We aren’t running another poll on benching Darnold this season. Heck, if Drew Lock is going to remain sidelined with his elbow injury, then you can shelve any fantasy about giving Lock any run. But we’re absolutely at the point where barring an amazing second half of the season, Darnold’s future as Seahawks starter should be called into question. The franchise QB he looked like for about 10 weeks last year and the playoff run has regressed back to something close to the worst version of himself, and that volatility doesn’t sound like a recipe for a massive contract extension. Darnold’s contract is up in 2027 , so he could play out the rest of his deal and have another “prove-it” moment, possibly with a different offensive coordinator (again). Alternatively, John Schneider pivots and starts looking for his next guy, whether that’s believing in Year 3 Jalen Milroe, re-signing Lock to essentially recreate the Darnold magic with someone else, trading for a quarterback, or drafting one. title: Seahawks bring in former Bengals starting guard for tryout
summary: The Seattle Seahawks had a few free agents brought in for a tryout this week, with one name standing out given his three years as a starting guard for the Cincinnati Bengals. Cordell Volson was drafted by Cincinnati in 2022, starting 48 games at left guard over three seasons. A difficult 2024 led to a […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks had a few free agents brought in for a tryout this week, with one name standing out given his three years as a starting guard for the Cincinnati Bengals. Cordell Volson was drafted by Cincinnati in 2022, starting 48 games at left guard over three seasons. A difficult 2024 led to a contract restructure before last season . He was waived/injured by the Bengals in 2025 after suffering a shoulder injury in preseason, and ultimately signed with the Tennessee Titans as a free agent this offseason. Volson didn’t make it past final roster cuts, with this play summing up his preseason. Oh that’s why Cordell Volson is now with the backups pic.twitter.com/5ZrfGHGfdC — Jordan Dajani (@JordanDajani) August 14, 2026 Volson was most recently with the Green Bay Packers practice squad in September before being released. On the 53-man roster, Seattle has Anthony Bradford and Beau Stephens as the backup guards to Grey Zabel and Quenton Nelson. There are no guards on the practice squad. As for the two tight end tryouts: Chase Curtis spent eight years in college between baseball and football, making him a 26-year-old rookie. He was unable to crack the New York Jets 53-man roster after five seasons at TCU. Kenny Fletcher went undrafted out of Rutgers and has spent time with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Indianapolis Colts. Ben Sims is the lone TE on Seattle’s practice squad.

title: How DeForest Buckner has already made impact in 1st week with team
summary: The San Francisco 49ers continued their reunion party last week, bringing back former Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts six years after trading him away. Buckner, 32, instantly comes into a starting role in San Francisco alongside Osa Odighizuwa, giving the team some more experience and a veteran presence for a […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on after the game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers continued their reunion party last week, bringing back former Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts six years after trading him away. Buckner, 32, instantly comes into a starting role in San Francisco alongside Osa Odighizuwa, giving the team some more experience and a veteran presence for a young room of defensive tackles. Buckner was quite productive in 2025, but was on a poor Colts team this season and was expected to be dealt. Naturally, with the need, the 49ers were a perfect fit, and the two sides were able to get a deal done for a fourth-round pick. Now, the defensive tackle will play in his first game with the 49ers since the 2019 Super Bowl against the Kansas City Chiefs, as the team hopes to not only make it back, but win their first championship since 1995. Though it’s been just a week, Buckner’s presence has already been felt in the locker room, according to his teammates. “Oh, it’s awesome,” running back Christian McCaffrey said of Buckner’s arrival. “I think just even in the walkthrough today, you look out there, you got Bosa, you got him out there, all these other [guys]. You’re like, okay, definitely gives you a little boost of confidence. So pumped he’s on our team.” Bosa praised the move, believing it’ll add some needed leadership to the defensive line group for the younger guys. “Yeah, 100%, [we feel a boost],” Bosa said of his former teammate. “I think we needed some leadership, not that we don’t have a couple good leaders in the D-line room, but a guy who’s played this scheme a lot, and we have some emerging young D-tackles, so it’s a perfect fit, really.” Fred Warner echoed the sentiment, noting the impact Buckner had on him back when the two played together for two seasons in 2018 and 2019. “It means everything,” Warner added. “It was special when I found out that we had an opportunity or really when we did get him. That was the guy when I came in as a rookie, I think he was in his 3rd year and he was what everything that we were looking for as a 49er. Just building the culture and the standard here. “He was that, you know, and I learned so much from him early on. And, you know, it was unfortunate, the business side of it, obviously having to be traded to the Colts, but it’s rare you get a second opportunity to come home, right? And so I know he’s excited. I’m excited. He looks phenomenal. And it helps when you have really talented players on the defensive line. It makes my job easier.” Could the 49ers continue to add on the defensive line now? Reports have said they’re still on the look for a pass-rusher, perhaps another veteran to help out a younger room. When speaking to reporters, head coach Kyle Shanahan said the team is still looking for moves that make sense, and a pass rusher might be one of the top needs remaining. While it’s a possibility, Bosa feels quite confident with how the room is stacking up right now. “Oh, I don’t know,” Bosa said when asked about the possibility of another addition. “Yeah, I don’t know. It seems like we’re pretty stacked. [Buckner’s] the blueprint and, and now we get to watch it in person.”

title: Kyle Shanahan speaks about potential trade additions and the Jauan Jennings trade situation
summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took the podium today after the team’s bye week, including a trade for former 49er DeForest Buckner, and the announcement that Brandon Aiyuk is filing for reinstatement and, if all goes well, will report to the team facility on Friday. 49ers fans were likely eager to hear the […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan took the podium today after the team’s bye week, including a trade for former 49er DeForest Buckner, and the announcement that Brandon Aiyuk is filing for reinstatement and, if all goes well, will report to the team facility on Friday. 49ers fans were likely eager to hear the status of potential returning players, including Nick Bosa, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and Demarcus Robinson. Bosa revealed he’s feeling good and ready to go, which is a good sign for his return on Sunday, while Evans, Samuel, and Christian McCaffrey didn’t practice today. The 21-day window for Robinson to return has been opened, but it remains to be seen if he’ll be ready against Las Vegas. The 49ers sent a fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for Buckner during the bye week, and Shanahan said “it was awesome” to add Buckner. The head coach continued by saying, “It’d be great to add someone else if that works out. We’re not counting on it, but it still would be great, still got time.” Obviously, teams won’t outright make their plans known, so this quote isn’t an indication of being satisfied with the players on the roster. It is very possible that the team is fine with the returning weapons and could stay put at the deadline, but there are six days between now and the trade deadline. A lot can change in that time, and Shanahan isn’t being definitive. Over the weekend, Fox Sports’ Jay Glazer reported that the Minnesota Vikings and 49ers had a trade in place for wide receiver Jauan Jennings. Glazer reported the Vikings asked for Jennings to speak to the head coach on a FaceTime call, but declined to even accept the call. Today, Shanahan gave a different version of the story, while acknowledging the team did have serious talks with Minnesota that bordered on being final. “We love Jauan,” Shanahan said. “We have such a good relationship with Jauan and know him real well, and we didn’t want to do it without talking to him first. So we had to agree on some things to at least make it close enough to be able to talk to him.” Shanahan also added that he did speak with Jennings on FaceTime and believed the conversation went well, but ultimately, the Vikings receiver was happy in Minnesota, and that put an end to the trade discussion.

title: The 49ers’ cap ramifications if/when they release Brandon Aiyuk
summary: Brandon Aiyuk finally applied for reinstatement. Aiyuk will report to the San Francisco 49ers facility this Friday, but Kyle Shanahan has a better chance of suiting up at wide receiver for the Niners than Aiyuk. The team will see if they can entice any team to trade for Aiyuk, but his offseason antics likely scared […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Aiyuk finally applied for reinstatement. Aiyuk will report to the San Francisco 49ers facility this Friday, but Kyle Shanahan has a better chance of suiting up at wide receiver for the Niners than Aiyuk. The team will see if they can entice any team to trade for Aiyuk, but his offseason antics likely scared off any potential suitors. That leaves a release as the inevitable outcome. There are still financial ramifications, even though Aiyuk’s salary guarantees were voided a year ago. Let’s walk through some of those ramifications. Aiyuk’s dead cap hit Per Spotrac : In 2026, the 49ers will need to take on $12,350,790 of dead cap, stemming from his 2024 signing bonus, his 2025 option bonus, & 1/5 of the 2026 option bonus – that wasn’t paid, but was still allocated as a cap charge this season. The 49ers will receive a $4.987M salary cap credit next March for this 2026 bonus charge. In 2027, the 49ers will need to take on $19,298,580 of dead cap, stemming from the 2024 signing bonus, and the 2025 option bonus allocations. It’s a total of $31,649,370, with AT LEAST $4,987,000 of it coming back next league year. I say that, because it’s 100% plausible to assume that the 49ers have already begun the process of filing paperwork to recoup as much of the 2024/2025 bonuses as possible. Just how much remains to be seen, and the timing of the salary void, the active/did not report list placement, etc…will further complicate that outcome, but it stands to reason that San Francisco will see an additional cap credit in the near future. According to Over the Cap, the 49ers are $31.54 million in the red for 2027. But that cap space also accounts for Aiyuk’s $40.47 million cap number. It remains to be seen what cap credit the 49ers can recoup to offset some of the dead money, or whether they’ve already exhausted all the relief. The 49ers have had no issues manipulating the salary cap by tinkering with contracts to move money around. We can expect more of the same this offseason, especially if they are hovering around little to no cap space.
author: Kyle Posey

title: What’s the most realistic splash the 49ers can make at the trade deadline?
summary: With the trade deadline nearing, there have been reports that the San Francisco 49ers are still looking to make moves after acquiring DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts last week. Notably, the 49ers are still interested in a wide receiver and a pass rusher. The pass rusher market has usually been there at the trade […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the trade deadline nearing, there have been reports that the San Francisco 49ers are still looking to make moves after acquiring DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts last week. Notably, the 49ers are still interested in a wide receiver and a pass rusher. The pass rusher market has usually been there at the trade deadline, and that should be the case again this year. It wouldn’t be a surprise if the 49ers looked for a minor move there, adding a veteran situational pass rusher to bolster their current group. But the receiver market is a bit different for a few reasons. There doesn’t seem to be a ton of flashy names available, with one, Garrett Wilson, already getting a ton of speculation that he won’t be traded. Additionally, the 49ers don’t need a run-of-the-mill receiver. They currently have Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and Christian Kirk all expected to practice in some capacity this week, while De’Zhaun Stribling is a few weeks away as well. That group could be what San Francisco rolls with going forward. It was reported that the 49ers were interested in Jauan Jennings, but that deal was nixed. Anyways, Jennings didn’t seem like the best fit, as the 49ers needed a true separator who could fill the Robinson or Stribling role that has been missing in the offense for weeks. But there is an outside-the-box wideout that the 49ers could target: Dallas Cowboys star George Pickens. Following their loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the Cowboys are 3-5. They do get the Colts this week, but face the 49ers after that. To end the year, they get the Titans, Eagles, Seahawks, Rams, Jaguars, Giants, and Commanders. But even if the Cowboys want to continue competing, they still could trade Pickens. Pickens had seen snap shares above 80 percent in every game but one over the first six weeks. But the last two? Those have dropped to 60 and 57 percent, with Ryan Flournoy seeing increased route participation. Pickens is coming off a career year in 2025 and is currently playing on the franchise tag. So, he’d be an impending free agent at 25 years old. When on the field, he’s been an excellent player and could be exactly what the 49ers want as a separator opposite Mike Evans. This trade could also allow him to play off the ball for the first time in his career, allowing him to move around the formation more and giving the Niners a true star receiver tandem. Now, a trade like this would always come down to cost, but if the 49ers only have to move a third-round pick and a Day 3 pick, it wouldn’t be a major issue at all, especially given that San Francisco can recoup a compensatory pick for Pickens in the offseason. The Niners and Cowboys made a deal back in the offseason for Osa Odighizuwa. That could happen again here with Pickens as an outside-the-box target that might make sense to move on both sides. Now, Ian Rapoport shared this week that the Cowboys are not expected to trade George Pickens, but Jerry Jones has said he’ll listen to deals on his players. So, that’s an option.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: What does ‘going for broke’ look like for the 49ers?
summary: ESPN went through each team in the NFL to determine what their trade deadline goal is, who could be on the move ahead of the deadline, and which player each team should target. The San Francisco 49ers have a 99.1% chance of making the playoffs. For the deadline portion, the theme discussed the Niners “going […]
full_text: Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN went through each team in the NFL to determine what their trade deadline goal is, who could be on the move ahead of the deadline, and which player each team should target. The San Francisco 49ers have a 99.1% chance of making the playoffs. For the deadline portion, the theme discussed the Niners “going all in” for this season: What is the deadline goal? Go for it. The 49ers have been hearing for years that their Super Bowl window is closing, yet they remain in the mix. This season, the Niners established it early with a winning start, but injuries along the defensive line and at receiver have made their needs obvious. They already acquired DT DeForest Buckner , but it would be a surprise if San Francisco didn’t, as OT Trent Williams told ESPN, “go for broke” with another meaningful addition (or two). — Nick Wagoner What does going for broke look like? Giving up a first-rounder for Maxx Crosby? He’s been elite, hasn’t missed a game, and would give the Niners an embarrassing amount of riches along the defensive line. Per Sumer Sports, only Will Anderson has more impact plays than Crosby at edge rusher this season. Going for broke means using future assets to win a chip this season. Fans, in my mind, have long overvalued draft picks. Before the season began, we were told the 2027 class is loaded with a handful of franchise quarterbacks. The college season is almost over, and none of those players have lived up to the hype. That might encourage the 49ers, or make it easier, to part ways with their picks this season. If you’re getting a player who other teams have to game plan for, then it’s a no-brainer. If that player helps you win today and is a part of your nucleus for the next few seasons, then what’s the hold up? No surprises for who ESPN selected as the player on the 49ers roster who could be traded over the next week: Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk . Be honest. You forgot he was still there, right? A ton of issues would need to be worked out, but it’s hard to imagine he just never plays again — especially because he just hired an agent . — Graziano Does including Aiyuk in a trade help you get a player you covet, or is all of Aiyuk’s value gone after he’s missed so much time? The 49ers getting a draft pick would feel like a win for them, but I’d use Aiyuk as a substitute for losing a potential pick, perhaps for the next player ESPN said the Niners should trade for: Who should they target? Jets WR Adonai Mitchell . It’s no secret that the 49ers are down bad at wide receiver. Mitchell has long flashed more promise than results, though we saw that promise Sunday when he recorded seven receptions for 142 yards and a touchdown. The Jets might be reluctant to part with Mitchell. But because they have Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr . and Kenyon Sadiq , it’s worth making a call. — Walder Adonai Mitchell was my favorite wide receiver in the 2024 NFL Draft. I had the Niners selecting him in just about every mock draft we did . I even said Mitchell was one of the top players in that draft . After a disappointing rookie campaign, the Colts shipped Mitchell to the Jets as part of a throw-in when they traded for Sauce Gardner. Michell has started to look the part. He missed a month, but he’s fresh off a game where he had 142 yards. Mitchell went over 60 receiving yards in the first two games. He’s a big body who can run and separate downfield. Mitchell is a walking big play. A quarter of his receptions are explosive plays. The Jets use him in the slot a little over 26% of the time, so he can move around the formation. He’s at his best on in-breaking routes. Best of all, he’s under contract for two more seasons and is only 24. We don’t know whether the wide receiver the 49ers drafted will ever play a full season. It might feel like the Niners are buying high after a big game, but Mitchell has always been talented. What does going for broke look like to you? Let us know in the comments below.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Why the 49ers roster construction has been a level above the rest of the NFL
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have not been the best drafters in the NFL during the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era, at least in recent years. And yet, they’ve found a way to remain perennial contenders, making a pair of Super Bowls and four NFC Championship Games over a nine-year run, and are currently Super […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers leaves the field after a win against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have not been the best drafters in the NFL during the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era, at least in recent years. And yet, they’ve found a way to remain perennial contenders, making a pair of Super Bowls and four NFC Championship Games over a nine-year run, and are currently Super Bowl favorites midway through the 2026 season. Overall, the 49ers have found a way to compete with top-loaded rosters, while also drafting well in certain years to keep good youth on the team. They’ve also made requisite trade deadline moves, been aggressive when the situation has called for it, and also benefitted from elite level coaching. In the NFL, we’ve seen some teams reach the top, but struggle to return. We’ve seen others remain in the playoff race year after year, but fail to reach that next level. The 49ers, though, have bounced back through hard years and have made the playoffs in five of the last seven years, with four of those appearances being to the NFC Championship Game and further. What’s been the secret to their success and roster construction? With the trade deadline coming up and another potential chance for the 49ers to improve their roster, I wanted to look at their past history under Lynch and Shanahan to see what separates them from the rest of the NFL. Initial foundation While many can fault the 49ers for some of their recent draft mistakes this decade, the 49ers built a very strong foundation of stars from their early draft successes. San Francisco got George Kittle and D.J. Jones in the fifth and sixth rounds of Kyle Shanahan’s first draft with the franchise back in 2017. In 2018, they added Fred Warner in the third round. And in 2019, they added Nick Bosa, Deebo Samuel, and Dre Greenlaw to the mix in the first, second, and fifth rounds. Right there, that’s a core of star players that help set the foundation for the 49ers, not only in the early years of the Shanahan era, but all the way to 2026. Kittle, Warner, Bosa, and Samuel ended up earning All-Pro awards. Greenlaw was a regular starter since his rookie year, forming one of the best linebacker tandems in the NFL. You follow up the strong drafting with quality trades from John Lynch for Jimmy Garoppolo and Trent Williams and even Emmanuel Sanders, and that’s what led to the 49ers’ first two NFC Championship Game appearances in 2019 and 2021. It’s rare that teams see that level of success, especially outside the first round, in the draft. Now, the 49ers weren’t close to perfect. They took Solomon Thomas and Reuben Foster in the first round in 2017, while Akhello Witherspoon, C.J. Beathard, and Joe Williams were their next three picks in the draft. In 2018, they took Dante Pettis in the second round and Tarvarius Moore in the third round. In 2019, they took Jalen Hurd in the third round and Mitch Wishnowsky in the fourth. There were a fair share of poor evals or draft misses, but the 49ers started their rebuild with a good foundation through the draft that set them straight going forward. Contract management Perhaps the biggest factor that sets the 49ers apart from other teams in the NFL is their contract strategy. The 49ers have dished out a ton of contracts near or at the top of position markets, like ones to Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Trent Williams, Nick Bosa, Arik Armstead, Charvarius Ward, and Fred Warner. They’ve been willing to pay up for their star talents, and those contracts have aged quite well for them, for the most part. Their mid-level extensions have also panned out well for the most part. Colton McKivitz’s three-year, $45 million deal is looking great already. When the 49ers initially signed Dre Greenlaw to a two-year deal worth under $10 million annually a few years back, that was a huge win. The biggest key is that the 49ers haven’t really been hurt as much by the contracts they’ve handed out. There have been a few poor contracts, such as Dee Ford and Brandon Aiyuk, but the 49ers have gotten out of those deals early. You could even loop Deebo Samuel, Javon Hargrave, or Jimmy Garoppolo’s contract into the mix as ones that were beneficial for the 49ers early on, but were ones they moved on from when they needed to. And the hits have been really good hits. Each of their extensions mentioned above has paid off. And their free-agent splashes have done really well as well. The Niners were early with Charvarius Ward and got high-level play out of him. Same with Richard Sherman a few years back. And this year, Mike Evans is looking like a huge hit. This has been where other teams have really struggled, be it to move off prior contracts or handing out bad ones in the first place. Nearly every team in the NFL has at least one of those on the books. The 49ers, on the other hand, have done a really good job of getting deals done early, while also getting out of them when they need to. Trades This is another key area that has separated the 49ers and led to a ton of their success. San Francisco has always been willing to flip capital for star players. They sent two draft picks for Trent Williams back in 2020. They traded for Christian McCaffrey at the deadline in 2022. They went after Chase Young the year after. San Francisco has made some major moves, as well as a ton of minor moves to position themselves well. They’ve also usually looked for multi-year value from their trades, which has worked wonders from a value perspective. Whether it was a small deadline move for Charles Omenihu or even the recent splash for DeForest Buckner, the 49ers have generally navigated the trade deadline well without overpaying with draft capital. Then, in the offseason, they’ve also been willing to make moves as well. These other avenues of improving the roster, be it contract management or trades, help offset when the 49ers whiff on draft picks. And the positives have come much more often than the negatives. Positional value I do think the 49ers have understood and captured positional value as well when handing out contracts. The Niners have generally shied away from paying defensive backs and offensive linemen marquee money, though they’re willing to hand out contracts to the right players. We’ve seen a ton of defensive back moves and contracts age quite poorly over the past few years, which have really hurt a number of teams aspiring to be contenders. The 49ers have instead prioritized other positions, such as defensive line and wide receiver. Overall, though, the total number of factors all contribute to why the 49ers have been able to build a sustainable roster construction model that has outlasted a ton of its NFL counterparts. So, even when they’re struggling to draft well, the foundation for roster building remains there and can be capitalized on in different ways.

Aiyuk has not featured in an NFL game since […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 20: Brandon Aiyuk #11 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up prior to the start of the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Levi's Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Aiyuk has turned in his paperwork to file for reinstatement, his new agent Drew Rosenhaus has said. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter , Aiyuk will report to the 49ers’ facility on Friday. “Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said, per Schefter. Aiyuk has not featured in an NFL game since suffering a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus in the 49ers’ loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on October 20, 2024. Aiyuk has remained on the reserve/left squad list this season, having initially been given that designation last December after he stopped showing up at the facility. The 49ers voided around $27 million in guaranteed money on Aiyuk’s contract in July last year after he failed to attend the required rehab sessions and team check-ins in the offseason. Aiyuk did not report to the 49ers’ training camp this July, leading to him being placed on the reserve/did not report list before being given the ‘left squad’ designation to start the season. The 2020 first-round pick was required to apply for reinstatement to the league to be able play again. Having done that, the 49ers are left with a decision, and a potentially tricky distraction ahead of their Week 9 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. It is now up to the 49ers to decide whether to keep Aiyuk, look to find a trade partner for him, or simply release him. Given the apparent breakdown in the relationship between Aiyuk and head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch, him staying on the team looks extremely unlikely. The 49ers, 6-1 and the current one seed in the NFC, do not need the sideshow of Aiyuk reintegrating with the team, despite the obvious talents that made him a star. The Washington Commanders have long been considered a likely trade partner. However, given his conduct over the past year, it remains to be seen if any team will be willing to give up any sort of draft capital to take a chance on Aiyuk. As such, the 49ers may be happy to just cut their losses and move on. Aiyuk was, at one point, the perfect Shanahan receiver and, from a talent perspective, would be ideal for a team dealing with injury issues at that spot. But, at this moment, with the promising position the 49ers enjoy and the baggage he brings, Aiyuk being anywhere near the team is the last thing they need.

title: How to win, how to lose: Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears week 9 game preview
summary: Anyone watch Monday Night Football? Wow, the Bears look good. Ben Johnson, Caleb Williams, and their Chicago Bears seem like they are on a collision course for a deep playoff run in 2026. So yes, the Bears are hot— Steaming, but so are the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay is coming off two-straight wins, three of their […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 17: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers attempts a pass during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Raymond James Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images Anyone watch Monday Night Football? Wow, the Bears look good. Ben Johnson, Caleb Williams, and their Chicago Bears seem like they are on a collision course for a deep playoff run in 2026. So yes, the Bears are hot— Steaming, but so are the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay is coming off two-straight wins, three of their last four and has seemingly found their new formula for offensive success. Will those good vibes and momentum carry over into the Chicago night on Sunday Night Football? “ Battles are won in the trenches, in the grit and grime of courageous determination. ” Charles R. Swindoll How can the Buccaneers win? Be the line they claim to be. The Chicago Bears are no joke and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will need to be all the way buttoned up to be able to stay with Chicago in this game. The Bears have a lot of things going for them in 2026, but their most recent addition may be the scariest. Chicago’s highly publicized trade for Jeffery Simmons opened some eyes when they made it. For those who haven’t seen may Titans’ games over the years, Monday night may have opened some more— Simmons is in the elite class of football players in the NFL and after spending years on a losing team, he looks motivated and rejuvenated. The trade for Simmons was an all-in move, the kind of move teams make when they have one goal on their mind— The Bears are a Super Bowl or bust team. The trade paid immediate dividends, Simmons’ first game with Chicago was a watch what I can do performance as he snared a team-leading six tackles (two for a loss) and a sack. For the Buccaneers, this game will be the game where their offensive line needs to prove the last two weeks true. Tampa’s season began horrifically, 0-4, a quarterback injury, and more importantly for the sake of this discussion, an offensive line that was woeful. Tampa Bay’s offensive line came into the season projected to be one of the strongest units on the team, perhaps in the league, depending on who you asked. Through the first four games, the Buccaneers allowed 20 sacks. Baker Mayfield spent most of those first four games running in circles behind the line of scrimmage like Fran Tarkenton, until he ran himself into an injury. In the four since, Tampa’s only surrendered seven sacks with five of the seven coming against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Tampa Bay will be and should be the underdog on Sunday. If there is any chance that an upset is in the cards they will need to protect their quarterback. Baker Mayfield is going to have to attempt more than three passes in this game to lead the team to victory and he will need to be upright to do so. Chicago has an absolute game-wrecker on their defense, he will make his plays— The Bucs can’t expect to wipe Jeffery Simmons out of the game, however, they cannot allow the game to devolve into what fans saw earlier in the season from this offensive line, Baker Mayfield, and the passing game. “ You can’t stop him, you can only hope to contain him .” Dan Patrick How can the Buccaneers lose? Lose contain of Caleb Williams. Caleb Williams might not be a truly great quarterback, though he does seem to be enroute to that status in short order, but he is a truly special athlete. No, he isn’t running 4.2 40’s or leaping 13’ in a broad jump but he is as all around dynamic as they come. One of the issues Tampa Bay might have is Williams simply does not throw interceptions. Caleb has missed some time this year, but he has only thrown one interception— Last year, just seven. Williams’ lack of interceptions isn’t even a Ben Johnson related statistic because dating back two years ago, pre their union, Williams tossed just six while throwing 20 touchdowns for a better than 3:1 touchdown to interception ratio. In his career (three years), Williams has thrown less interceptions than Baker Mayfield did in 2024—Turnovers may be off the table. Another key issue that Caleb Williams presents is his elite management of the pocket. Williams is not a runner, but he is quite mobile. He has a phenomenal ability to majestically glide up, back, or out of the pocket towards free space and away from danger . Todd Bowles and the Buccaneers’ defense will need to work tirelessly to mitigate that on Sunday night. Williams will dagger the Bucs with big plays off script if they let him. Bowles and the Bucs have been somewhat of mixed bag against mobile quarterbacks, different matchups bringing about different results, but Caleb Williams will represent a very unique challenge. Williams is not just looking to move around the pocket to buy time to throw— He isn’t just looking break out of the pocket so that he heave the ball down field on a broken play— He won’t be looking to run outside of contain so that he can scramble for yards to move the chains— Caleb Williams will be looking to do any and all of the above. He is special and he has proven that he can do each and every one of those things on any given play— Meaning, the Buccaneers must be dialed into the details on their rushes, sound in their tackling, and if they are caught lacking and take even just one snap off Williams could gash them for a game changing play. Todd Bowles’ defense has been reliably solid in 2026, as of late they’ve been exemplary. Sunday night’s game against Chicago will be a true test. Caleb Williams has the ability to put a defense on a poster, he and Ben Johnson have left a decent amount of carnation in their wake. Can Tampa Bay contain Caleb Williams and stay off his highlight reel?

title: Buccaneers at Bears: Initial injury report for Week 9
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers began preparations for their Week 9 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Wednesday, releasing their first injury report ahead of Sunday night’s game at Soldier Field. Tampa Bay listed eight players on the initial report, including three who did not participate in practice. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Kenny Gainwell #1 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers began preparations for their Week 9 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Wednesday, releasing their first injury report ahead of Sunday night’s game at Soldier Field. Tampa Bay listed eight players on the initial report, including three who did not participate in practice. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after missing the team’s previous two games, leaving his availability for Sunday uncertain. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) also did not practice and is expected to miss the matchup after suffering an MCL sprain in the Buccaneers’ Week 8 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts was the third player held out of practice, although his absence was listed as personal rather than injury-related. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited participants Wednesday. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), guard Cody Mauch (back) and tight end Cade Otton (thumb) participated fully. The Buccaneers are coming off a 16-0 shutout victory over Atlanta, their second consecutive win, and will look to continue that momentum against a Chicago team that enters the matchup at 6-2 following a Monday night victory over Seattle. Tampa Bay will have two more practice sessions before the team’s final injury report is released Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday’s contest. The Buccaneers and Bears are scheduled to kick off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.

title: Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone named NFC Defensive Player of the Week
summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week following his standout performance in the team’s 16-0 shutout victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8. The veteran linebacker played a key role in Tampa Bay’s defensive dominance on Sunday, intercepting Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. twice in […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Alex Anzalone #34 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrates after intercepting a pass in the first half against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week following his standout performance in the team’s 16-0 shutout victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8. The veteran linebacker played a key role in Tampa Bay’s defensive dominance on Sunday, intercepting Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. twice in the first quarter. Anzalone also finished the game with six tackles, including one for loss, helping the Buccaneers secure their second consecutive victory. Both interceptions came during Atlanta’s second and third offensive possessions, setting the tone for a Buccaneers defense that held the Falcons to just 224 total yards and forced four turnovers. Atlanta also failed to convert any of its 12 third-down opportunities. Anzalone became just the second NFL linebacker since 2000 to record two interceptions in the first quarter of a game, joining former Seattle Seahawks linebacker Lofa Tatupu, who accomplished the feat in 2007. The recognition marks the first NFC Defensive Player of the Week award of Anzalone’s 10-year NFL career and the first weekly award earned by a Buccaneers player this season. He is also the first Tampa Bay defender to receive the honor since outside linebacker Anthony Nelson in Week 8 of the 2025 season. Signed by Tampa Bay in March after five seasons with the Detroit Lions, Anzalone has recorded 42 tackles, one sack, three interceptions and three passes defensed through eight games this season. His three interceptions lead all NFL linebackers. The Buccaneers will look to build on their defensive momentum when they travel to Chicago to face the Bears on Sunday Night Football in Week 9.

title: 3 players the Titans should not trade before the deadline
summary: The NFL trade deadline is approximately five days away (Nov. 10). The Tennessee Titans are obviously sellers at the deadline following their stunning decision to trade superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for two first-round picks and an additional fourth-round selection. The Simmons trade poses a question: Who else will […]
full_text: Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard (20) carries the ball during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The NFL trade deadline is approximately five days away (Nov. 10). The Tennessee Titans are obviously sellers at the deadline following their stunning decision to trade superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for two first-round picks and an additional fourth-round selection. The Simmons trade poses a question: Who else will GM Mike Borgonzi look to trade before the deadline? We’ve identified three players Borgonzi should keep as opposed to trading away. RB Tony Pollard Tony Pollard is the player most linked to a trade following the Simmons departure. It’s easy to understand why. Pollard has been excellent in recent weeks, rushing for five touchdowns across the previous two contests, with back-to-back 100+ rushing yard performances. The former Memphis standout is on an expiring contract, but perhaps the Titans should consider re-signing him if his current form keeps up. DE Jacob Martin Jacob Martin is almost certain to draw trade interest around the league. Following his 3-sack performance versus the Cincinnati Bengals, the underrated veteran is now tied for fifth in sacks (6.5) in the entire league. Martin knows this Robert Saleh defense inside-out, and he’s signed through next campaign (2027), with a reasonable cap charge of $5.5 million. He’s outperforming his contract at a team-friendly number. CB Alontae Taylor The Alontae Taylor situation is unfortunate. The Titans clearly miscalculated his ability to play boundary cornerback when they signed him to a three-year, $58 million contract. They’ve reversed course and made him the league’s most expensive nickelback. He was also the backup nickel in Weeks 6-8 until Marcus Harris got injured versus the Bengals. The Titans probably won’t be able to trade him. They need to continue working on the best in-house solution.

title: Titans trade deadline 2026: Tracking every rumor
summary: The Tennessee Titans kicked off the 2026 NFL trade deadline with a huge trade, sending Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks. Titans GM Mike Borgonzi said he wasn’t planning on trading Simmons, but Bears GM Ryan Poiles came to him with an offer he couldn’t refuse. If Borgonzi can hit on […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - SEPTEMBER 27: Tony Pollard #20 of the Tennessee Titans runs during the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 27, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Tennessee Titans kicked off the 2026 NFL trade deadline with a huge trade, sending Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks. Titans GM Mike Borgonzi said he wasn’t planning on trading Simmons, but Bears GM Ryan Poiles came to him with an offer he couldn’t refuse. If Borgonzi can hit on those picks, and that’s a big IF, he can really rebuild the roster. Borgonzi should be listening to offers on pretty much anyone that he doesn’t think will be playing at their peak in 2029 because that is the first season the Titans are really going to have a chance to make a deep run in the playoffs. The names at the top of that list would be RB Tony Pollard and WR Calvin Ridley. Amani Hooker, who is coming off a 3-interception game, is a player teams are inquiring about, but at only 29, he is a guy who would still have value in 2029, but Borgonzi is apparently not interested in moving Hooker. Teams are reportedly calling about Pollard, but Borgonzi has declined to engage in those conversations, according to Mike Florio . Jeremy Fowler of ESPN says that Ridley is a backup target for teams that miss out on primary WR targets. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 3:00 Central. We will be keeping track of all of the rumors heading up to the deadline.

full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Jermaine Johnson II #11 of the Tennessee Titans looks on during the second half of the Week 3 preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is officially less than one week away (Nov. 10). The Tennessee Titans are obviously sellers at the deadline following their decision to trade star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for two first-round picks and an additional fourth-round selection. The Simmons trade poses a question: Who else will GM Mike Borgonzi look to trade before the deadline? We’ve identified three players Borgonzi should try moving for more draft capital. DE Jermaine Johnson II Jermaine Johnson has been fairly inconsistent as a pass rusher. The Titans acquired his fifth-year rookie contract option when they traded T’Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for him. That means Johnson is on an expiring contract. He’s a good NFL player who also sets hard edges as a run defender, but getting a draft pick back for an expiring contract would be a worthwhile move. His familiarity with Robert Saleh’s defense could keep him in Tennessee, but trading him would free up more snaps for Femi Oladejo and Keldric Faulk. LB Cody Barton Veteran linebacker Cody Barton has begun losing snaps to Cedric Gray in recent weeks. Most Titans fans are surprised it took this long. Gray and Anthony Hill Jr. are the future tandem for Coach Saleh’s defense. Barton is signed through 2027, which could make trading him a little complicated. He’s not on an expiring contract, but any postseason contending team searching for experienced linebacker help should have interest. RB Tyjae Spears Could the Titans receive anything in return for Tyjae Spears? It’s a question Mike Borgonzi should be asking. Tony Pollard has been exceptional in recent weeks and Spears is also on an expiring contract. He’s an athletic dual-threat back who is especially productive on passing downs. Perhaps there’s an offense in the market for another third-down playmaker.

summary: Watching Sunday’s ultimately decisive win against Tanner McKee and the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles, I couldn’t escape the feeling that there is the nucleus of a good football team, struggling to escape the grip of poor coaching and preparation. full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 1: Trey Amos #23 of the Washington Commanders breaks up a pass intended for Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter of an NFL football game at Northwest Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Watching Sunday’s ultimately decisive win against Tanner McKee and the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles, I couldn’t escape the feeling that there is the nucleus of a good football team, struggling to escape the grip of poor coaching and preparation. On this occasion, that team broke free toward the end of the first half to overcome a 7-point deficit and hand a 10-27 loss to their division rival, on the way to earning its second win in seven games. Will the Commanders be able to ride the momentum from the come-from-behind win to victory over the visiting LA Rams in Week 9? Who knows. But there was plenty to like, as well as plenty of areas for improvement, in the Commanders’ takedown of the dirty birds. On the positive side, the Week 8 victory featured the best coverage performance by the secondary this season as well as the best games in burgundy and gold by WR Treylon Burks, OLB Dorance Armstrong, NT Shy Tuttle and DE Charles Omenihu. Despite some lapses, the OL gave Jayden Daniels plenty of time in the pocket, and CB Trey Amos played a nearly perfect game of shutdown coverage. On the not so positive side, the team continues to start slow. It took nearly a full half of football to get the offense going and to stop committing penalties. In the first half, the Commanders committed 7 for 50 yards, compared to just 2 for 20 yards in the second half. If the Commanders can figure out how to start games like they started the second half against the Eagles, they will give themselves a chance to beat a better opponent in Week 9. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s have a look at where they lined up, who stepped up, who could have done better in the Commanders’ first divisional win of the season. Technicalities: Stats were sourced from the official NFL gamebook via NFLGSIS, Pro Football Reference (PFR), Pro Football Focus (PFF) and ESPN’s total QBR. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). Where differences in advanced stats result from judgment calls (eg. Coverage yards allowed, broken tackles) I have gone with a modified consensus approach. When there is fundamental disagreement between sources, the stats won’t be reported. Minor differences between sources that support the same conclusion are reported. If advanced stats are reported without attribution of source, it means there was consensus. As always, official NFL stats override conflicting data from other sources.
